text.ACTION: Rasler and Ashe's wedding. Click image for video.
Year 704 Old Valendian – Kingdom of Dalmasca – The Royal City of Rabanastre

It begins with a flock of snow white doves flying through the blue sky, followed by airships drifting over sweeping views of the royal capital, and glimpses of the bustling marketplace. A bell chimes merrily over the scenery. The view changes again to an extravagant wedding procession coming down a main boulevard, playing a joyous fanfare. The bride and groom stand next to each other, in a carriage making its way to their wedding ceremony, waving to the excited crowds around them - Prince Rasler of Nabradia and Princess Ashelia of Dalmasca. For a moment, they turn and share a shy smile with each other.
The scene changes again to the interior of a grand cathedral where a priest presides over their wedding.

text.Priest: In the name of the Father and in the presence of these Holy Relics, I hereby pronounce you man and wife from this time forth. May the blessings of the Gods light your path for all eternity. Faram.

text.ACTION: The two exchange a chaste kiss to seal their union. The bells toll and doves soar through the sky outside.

The scene changes, presumably to some days or even months later - a knight walks down the halls purposefully with his cape flowing behind him. His destination: the war room, where several people are having a somber discussion.

text.Knight: If, following this, Archadia should launch an attack by both land and air, our kingdom will stand little –

text.ACTION: He is interrupted as the knight, Basch, enters the room. All look up from the great map spread over the table - including King Raminas.

text.Basch: Nabudis has fallen.

text.ACTION: The shock is immediate.

text.Basch: I know not. I am sorry.

text.Knight: If Nabudis has indeed fallen ... it is only a matter of time before they reach the borders of Dalmasca. There is nothing to halt their advance.

text.ACTION: shaking his head

text.Basch: I will go.

text.Rasler: And I will go at his side.

text.ACTION: Raminas raises his eyebrows, but then nods in understanding.

The scene changes again as Rasler exits the room. A great force of airships, foot soldiers, and sentries mounted on chocobo all gather in front of the palace in Rabanastre. On the steps of the palace, the royal court is gathered, and Raminas presents Rasler with a sword.

text.Raminas: Galtea stand watch over your life.

text.ACTION: taking the sword reverently

He nods to Raminas, then looks to his right at Princess Ashe. Their eyes meet briefly, before he turns to his army and thrusts his sword in the air, shouting a battle cry. The army responds in kind. We see the airships departing before the scene changes once more.
The Dalmasca-Nabradia Border – Nalbina Fortress

In the night sky, a battle rages. Airships flying overhead shoot at each other, some of them going down in flames, some sent askew to be dashed against the paling, the shield, which surrounds the fortress. Armies struggle with each other on the ground, a fierce storm of swords and spears. In the melee, two soldiers mounted on chocobos meet briefly.
On a battlement above, Rasler and Basch, both on chocobo, are advancing as Basch shoots down enemies with a bow, and Rasler slashes at them with his sword.

text.Basch: The fortress is lost! We must withdraw!

text.ACTION: Rasler looks to the tallest structure in the fortress. In this same tower, a group of robed mages recites a spell in unison, apparently generating the paling.

text.Mages: Shield beyond sight, ne'er failing light –

text.ACTION: The group of mages hears a sound. They stop to see Imperial soldiers coming into the tower, and they are cut down by the Imperials' greatswords. As the magic fades, the paling begins to dissolve, like a paper being burned. The airships quickly fly in.

text.Basch: Then it's over!

text.Rasler: For my father. For my father!

text.ACTION: He moves to charge at the Imperials. Basch sees an Imperial archer across the way ready his bow and take aim at Rasler.

text.Basch: Lord Rasler!

text.ACTION: He hurriedly prepares his own bow and he and the Imperial archer shoot at the same time. The Imperial goes down first. Then the Imperial's arrow embeds itself deep in Rasler's chest, just beneath his collarbone, before Basch can reach him. Basch hurriedly jumps onto Rasler's chocobo as Rasler slumps over. A felled airship crashes into the chaos of soldiers below; Basch charges down the enemy, retreating; as he goes, we see the tower fall; only his panting breaths can be heard as the world goes silent, in slow motion.

The scene changes again; rain falls on a gloomy landscape. Then, inside a cathedral, the princess, Rasler's newlywed wife, in a black veil, with a somber expression. She kneels before the flower-lined casket where Rasler lies, while the priest speaks.

text.Priest: Blessings of the Great Father descend ... and guide your body's return to the earth. Great Father, guide your spirit's return ... to the Mother of All. There, you shall find peace. Faram.

text.ACTION: Outside, ravens gather amidst the puddles as an Imperial airship sails through the gray sky. As one of the raven's wings engulfs the screen, we see the title - FINAL FANTASY XII.

text.LOCATION: Excerpt from Memoirs of Mqs. Halim Ondore IV, Chapter 12: Of the Fall of Kingdoms

text.Ondore: The Death of Ld. Rasler Heios Nabradia was but one of many Tragedies to befall the Kingdom of Dalmasca.
The Air of Hope that had surrounded H.R.H. Princess Ashe's Wedding was now quite lost; Dalmasca had been set adrift, at the Mercy of History's restless Tides.
At this Time, two Great Empires struggled for Dominion over Ivalice; Archadia in the East, Rozarria, the west.
The Invasion of the Kingdom of Nabradia was Archadia's first Step in its westward March.
With Lord Rasler's beloved Homeland consumed by the Hell-Fires of War, it seemed clear that Archadia would soon mete out a like Fate to Dalmasca.
The Fall of the Fortress at Nalbina tolled the Destruction of the greater part of Dalmasca's Forces.
A Counter-Attack was mounted by the Order of the Knights of Dalmasca, ever Brave and Faithful, but against the martial Might of the Archadian Armies, they stood little Chance of Victory.
Indeed, their Defeat was to be absolute.
Soon thereafter, Archadia came forward offering Terms of Peace. Or, as one might rather put it, Terms of Dalmasca's Surrender.

Lord Raminas, King of Dalmasca – and my Dear Friend – had no Choice but to accept these Terms. It was, thus, only with Reluctance that He set out for Nalbina Fortress – now under Archadian Occupation – to affix His Seal to the Emperor's Treaty of Peace.
The King had scarce departed His Royal City of Rabanastre when the Remnants of the Order made their Return. And not a Moment too soon, for a terrible Revelation awaited them.
The Treaty would be signed with Steel and Writ in royal Blood.

text.ACTION: ~Memoirs of Mqs. Halim Ondore IV, Chapter 12: Of the Fall of Kingdoms
The next scene begins from the point of view of someone apparently being roused from unconsciousness. Vision is dark and blurry, and the voices are distorted.

text.Basch: You, there. Can you hear me?

text.Vossler: It's as I feared. They're slowing us down.

text.Basch: Do not say that. Not all of us are here for love of battle. He fights to defend his homeland. Your name?

text.Reks: Reks, sir. My name is Reks.

text.Basch: Good. Reks. You bore a few cuts, but you are still whole. Well, can you stand?

text.ACTION: As Basch holds out his hand, vision clears up and the sound becomes perfectly audible again. The setting is a fortress at night. A label in the bottom right corner gives us specifics.
Nalbina Fortress – North Ward

text.Basch: Think you can fight?
How old are you, Reks?
Young. Family?

text.Reks: My brother is all I have left, sir. He's two years younger than I, living in Rabanastre.

text.Basch: So young. You're barely old enough to be a man. You shouldn't be forced to wield a sword.

text.Reks: No, sir. I want to fight. For my homeland, and for my parents.

text.Vossler: Time, Basch. Save the discussion for later. We must reach the King before they act, or all our efforts will be in vain.

text.Basch: I'm aware of the situation.

text.ACTION: Imperial soldiers emerge.

text.Basch: Vossler, go ahead! I will handle this rabble.

text.ACTION: Vossler gestures to Basch.

text.Vossler: Godspeed.

text.ACTION: Vossler runs off with his detachment. Basch draws his sword and easily cuts through the five or six Imperials that lunge at him. Reks appears to be dazed by the action.

text.Basch: Steady, Reks. Keep your wits about you and you'll make it.

text.ACTION: to all

text.Basch: We move!
You must always be mindful of your surroundings. Use the right analog stick to look around. It's a useful way to spot Imperials. Go on, give it a try.

text.ACTION: Move the right analog stick...

text.Basch: Use the left analog stick to move, Reks. Tilt it slightly to walk, and further to run. You can walk, yes? Come, stand before me.

text.ACTION: Tutorial: Use the left analog stick to approach Basch.

text.Basch: Do you see the marker above my head? That's a Talk Icon. You can talk to any character showing one of these. To talk to someone, approach them and press X. Try talking to your friend by the gate.

text.ACTION: Tutorial: Approach the Dalmascan by the gate and press x to talk to him.
If you talk to Basch again first, he'll simply repeat his instructions.

text.Dalmascan: Life is worth too much to throw away, Reks. Do what you can, but don't try to be a hero. Save the hero stories for your brother once we're back in Rabanastre. Just listen to the Captain and we'll get through this.

text.Basch: We'll enter the fortress through this gate. We must go.

text.ACTION: Tutorial: Go to the iron gate.

text.Dalmascan: Listen to Captain Basch, Reks. We're heading in through the gate.

text.Basch: We'll enter the fortress through this gate. We must go.

text.ACTION: When you approach the gate and the marker appears above your head ...

text.Basch: See the marker above your head? That's called an Action Icon. One of these will appear when you approach a door, a switch, an item, or the like. To learn more about what you've found, walk closer and the icon will change. Then press X. Now, try opening the gate.

text.ACTION: Tutorial: Approach the iron gate and press X.

text.Dalmascan: Open the gate like the captain says, Reks.

text.ACTION: Talk to Basch, and he will simply repeat his last instructions again.
After opening the gate ...

text.Basch: It is time. We will drive back any Imperials standing between us and the King. Dalmasca's future hangs in the balance. Stay focused on the foes before you, Reks. I will watch rearward.
You can open the Party Menu by pressing triangle. From the Party Menu you can examine your equipment and inventory.

text.ACTION: The pair spots an oncoming Imperial, and the conversation transitions to a battle tutorial.

text.Basch: That red line is a hostile target line. Take heed – you're being targeted. When a foe targets you, the line is red. When you target a foe, the line is blue. If you see a red line, look for foes at once. If they are not readily apparent, use the right analog stick to look around. When you've found them, press X to open the Battle Menu. Once you've selected Attack and targeted a foe, close distance using the left analog stick. You'll automatically attack until your foe is defeated. You can change targets or actions at any time. If your HP falls, press x and select Items from the Battle Menu, then use a potion. After using an item, you will automatically resume your previous action. There is no need to input your commands again. You can do it, Reks. Show me!

text.ACTION: After defeating the Imperial and crossing to the center of the bridge ...
The party stops in the middle of the bridge. Basch looks up to the sky.
A small aircraft flies down to the bridge where Basch, Reks, and co. stand.
After defeating Air Cutter Remora ...
Basch finishes it off with his Quickening, Fulminating Darkness, leaving the Air Cutter sputtering and sparking.

text.Tonberry Pilot: Antlion, this is Tonberry! My engines are hit! She'll not hold much longer!

text.Antlion: We receive you, Tonberry. You've leave to retire. Well fought.

text.ACTION: The smoking, short-circuiting Tonberry finally swoops away.
Just before you leave the area, Basch will stop you ...

text.Basch: There is no simple way through the fortress – the Minimap at the top right of your screen may not be enough to gain your bearings. Should you lose your way, consult your Location Map by pressing Select. This will bring up the map of the fortress we gave you before we set out.

text.ACTION: If you are playing Zodiac Age on the PS4, the dialogue changes slightly:

text.Basch: There is no simple way through the fortress – the Minimap at the top right of your screen may not be enough to gain your bearings. Should you lose your way, consult your Location Map by pressing the touch pad button. If you still find yourself at a loss, pressing the L3 button will allow you to view the Location Map as you move. Navigate your way through as you see fit.
Vossler. Where are you?

text.Reks: What if Captain Azelas has fallen?

text.Basch: Don't talk such nonsense! Vossler's laughed in the face of Death far too many times to stop now! Men like him don't die in places like this. We must make haste to reach the King. We will take him to safety.
He'll agree to an unconditional surrender. They wouldn't dare touch him until the wax on his seal is dry.

text.Reks: But if we arrive after he's signed the treaty –

text.Basch: Wait.

text.ACTION: pause

text.Basch: Quickly, Reks!

Ahead we will face many Imperials, but we need not fight them all. Oftimes retreat is the wiser course. Should the need arise, press and hold R2 to run from your foes. There is no shame in fleeing from a battle that serves no purpose.

text.ACTION: Upon approaching the blue crystal ...

text.Basch: This is a save crystal, Reks. You can save your progress by approaching a save crystal and pressing X. Touching one of these crystals will also fully restore your HP and MP. Though you will gradually recover MP as you move about, it can take time. Do not miss this opportunity to refresh yourself and your allies. There is more I would tell you, but we've no time. Heed the lessons of the battlefield and you will do well. Come – we must reach His Majesty before it's too late!

text.LOCATION: Signed with Steel and Writ in Royal Blood

text.ACTION: Imperial soldiers find them once more.

text.Imperial: Intruders! Don't let them escape!

text.Reks: Sir! We have little time! You must go to the king! I'll handle these!

text.Basch: Fight well.

text.ACTION: Basch leaves.
After defeating the Imperials and moving to the red X on your map ...
Reks sees the King sitting hunched over in his chair, lifeless.
When Reks turns around, Basch is there – and sticks a knife in his gut.

text.Reks: Captain, why? Our King – What have you done?

text.ACTION: Basch retracts the knife and walks away slowly.

text.Gabranth: The King intended all along to sell Dalmasca to the Empire. His Majesty was a traitor.

text.ACTION: Reks turns to Basch, and then collapses to the ground. Imperials rush into the room.

text.Vayne: Seize the insurgent!

text.Imperial: M'lord!

text.ACTION: Reks's vision fades in and out, but he sees Basch, kneeling on the ground, his arms restrained by Imperial soldiers, and someone else standing before him.

text.Vayne: Well, so much for peaceful negotiations.

text.Gabranth: We'll never surrender to you! We are not cattle to be sold by a traitor-king!

text.Vayne: But the war is over, my dear captain. You have lost. Dalmasca is the property of the Empire, now. And to think, we intended to let you keep some of your sovereignty, out of respect. But now you've gone and ruined that. Haven't you, Captain?

text.Gabranth: We will never bow to you!

text.Vayne: And the people of Dalmasca will hate you for it. Take the Captain away.

text.ACTION: Reks's vision finally fails him as he loses consciousness, leaving behind one last thought.

text.LOCATION: Excerpt from Memoirs of Mqs. Halim Ondore IV, Chapter 13. The Province of Allies

text.Ondore: Pretenses of Peace left by the Wayside, the Archadian Forces resumed their Advance toward Rabanastre. Dalmasca's Doom had been decided.
To make Resistance would serve no end. With this foremost in my Thoughts, I, to the People of Dalmasca:
"Sons and Daughters of Dalmasca, I bid you lay down your Arms. Raise Songs of Prayer in their Stead. Prayer for His Majesty King Raminas, ever merciful. A Man devoted wholly to Peace.
"Prayer, too, for the noble Princess Ashe, who, wrought with Grief at her Kingdom's defeat, has taken her own Life.
"Know also that Capt. Basch fon Ronsenburg, for Incitement of Sedition and the Assassination of H.R.M. King Raminas, has been found Guilty of High Treason and put to his Death.
"They who at this late Hour choose still the Sword are cut of the same Cloth as the Capt.: Traitors who would lead Dalmasca to her Ruin."
Dalmasca's Surrender without Terms was soon to follow.

text.ACTION: ~Memoirs of Mqs. Halim Ondore IV, Chapter 13. The Province of Allies
A young man with a dagger confronts a few unnervingly large rats in what looks to be a sewer. A younger kid yells down to him from a higher level.

text.Kytes: Vaan! Hurry it up or they'll find us!

text.Vaan: I know, I know! Just a little more. You keep an eye out for me up there, Kytes.

text.ACTION: Kytes runs off, presumably to return to his position as lookout.

text.Vaan: One ... two ... three more. Right. Time to clean house.

text.ACTION: After defeating the rats ...

text.Kytes: Wow, Vaan. You got 'em all yourself? Guess I know who to call when something big comes along!

text.Vaan: Hey, it's good practice for the desert. I'm ready for anything now. That's enough for today. You should get back to Migelo's place, Kytes. Aren't you running errands for him?

text.Kytes: Oops! Heh. Totally forgot. You should come, Vaan. He's busy today. Might have some work for you to do, too.

text.Vaan: I got other "work" to do. Hey, lock this place up for me, will you? If Migelo finds out we've been down here, he'll tan our hides.

text.ACTION: The Royal City of Rabanastre -- Year 706 Old Valendian, Two Years After the Fall of Dalmasca
The scene changes to a stall in the bazaar where a merchant is confronted by two Imperial soldiers.

text.Imperial: Huh? What'd you say?

text.ACTION: grabbing the merchant by the collar

text.Imperial: What? Haven't paid?

text.Peddler: On second thought, please, sir. Take it. It is a gift.

text.Imperial 2: Leave the poor sod be. We don't want trouble today.

text.ACTION: letting him go

text.Imperial: Your luck, peddler.

text.ACTION: Vaan suddenly comes through, bumping into one of the Imperials as he passes by.

text.Vaan: Sorry!

text.Imperial: What? My pouch! It's gone!

text.ACTION: The two Imperials take off running after Vaan. Their path is blocked by market-goers, particularly a seeq, and a bangaa who stops to talk to him.

text.Imperial: Get out of the way!

text.ACTION: They don't seem to hear him. One of the Imperials throws their hands up.
The scene changes to another part of the city, where Vaan, with the Imperial's pouch in hand, stops to catch his breath. Someone snatches up the pouch.

text.Vaan: Hey, that's mine!

text.ACTION: He turns to see a girl his age holding the pouch, eyebrow raised. Her expression changes to a frown, her hands on her hips.

text.Penelo: What do you mean, "yours"? You've been stealing again. What happens if they catch you?

text.ACTION: he turns and paces while she lectures him

text.Penelo: We need you to be there for us, Vaan. You're no good to anyone if you're locked away in a dungeon!

text.Vaan: Oh, what, am I the leader now? We're orphans. The first thing you learn is you gotta look out for yourself. C'mon, Penelo. You know it as well as I do ...

text.ACTION: he turns to see her rifling through the pouch

text.Vaan: Hey, you give that back! What do you think you're doing?

text.Penelo: I thought this money was the people of Dalmasca's property. The Imperials stole it from us, so it's only fair that we take it back. It's our duty as Dalmascans. Well, wasn't that what you said?

text.Vaan: Yeah, but, I never said anything about taking it back from me!

text.Penelo: This is for that bread you took the other day. Just because I help Migelo out every now and then ... it doesn't mean that you get to eat for free, too, you know.

text.Vaan: I know that. You think I like living like this?

text.ACTION: A shadow passes over them and they look up to see an airship passing over in the sky above them.

text.Vaan: One of these days, I'll fly an airship of my own. I'll be a sky pirate, free to go where I will.

text.ACTION: Penelo smiles fondly before starting to walk away.

text.Penelo: Well, be careful. You'll never fly anything if you're rotting in a dungeon!

text.ACTION: she stops and turns again, remembering something

text.Penelo: Oh, Migelo had some errands that need doing. He wanted you to drop by his place. It might be a good idea to lend a hand.

text.Rabanastran (man in green shorts East En: You getting into trouble with the Imperials again, Vaan? Well, try and be careful. If not for your own sake, then for Migelo and Penelo, okay?

text.ACTION: If you approach the bazaar entrance ...

text.Vaan: I should probably make myself scarce right about now.

text.Lonely Boy: There sure are a lot of Imperials out today. They think they're so great, but I hate 'em.

text.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): Hey, mister. You wanna hear about the history of Rabanastre? It won't cost ya much ... What? I gotta eat, too, ya know. Let's see ... 1 gil oughta do it.

CHOICE.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): Okay, so two years back, Rabanastre lost the war with the Empire. That's when all the guards came and made us live under the city. The Empire has one person who runs the city and everything. He's called a consul. The new consul's comin' today, that's why there's so many guards. Kind of short, huh ... Don't worry, I'll try and find some new things to add for next time!

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink and tan EE): You can cut the tension with a knife out here on the streets today. Guards at every corner ... I can hardly stand it. If anyone asks, I said nothing. Nothing. Understood?

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq pacing about): That Migelo's made quite a name for himself, what with that sundries shop of his and all. There's one bangaa a fella could take after.

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa EE): I was just down at Migelo's Sundries ... that Migelo's comin' and goin' so, I'm half afraid he's gonna wear the door off its hinges!

text.Vexed Father: They've closed all the stairs to Lowtown. Can you believe that? I don't care how important today is, this is absurd!

text.Imperial: No traffic in or out of Lowtown until the Lord Consul's assumed his post. No exceptions.

text.Wistful Bangaa: Only been two years since Princess Ashe took her own life, but it seems like Rabanastre's been in the Empire forever ... uh, not that I'm complainin'.

text.Rabanastran (man in turban and brown sho: It's sweltering, even here in the shade. Maybe I'll head up to the Sandsea and get something to drink.

text.Imperial: Step back. Now! I haven't finished interrogating these two yet.

text.ACTION: (Yugri's Magicks (sign)) -Parties interested in the working of magicks, inquire within. Those seeking disquisition on the concoction of love philtres, look elsewhere.
If you try to enter any shops or leave east end any other way than the bazaar entrance ...

text.Vaan: I should really go see Migelo first.

text.Johm: Oh, Vaan, how ya doin'? Lots of people out today. Thought I may try out some of those "tricks" you showed me, heh heh.

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq outside Sandsea): Innocently walkin' past the Sandsea I was, when a sudden thirst seized me. But I ain't a-goin' in! Got to save my gil ...

text.Penelo: Migelo seemed like he was in a hurry. He's probably still at the shop ... better not keep him waiting too long.

text.ACTION: (Batahn's Technicks (sign)) -Technicks for all occasions! For the discerning warrior who trusts his own body and mind rather than a smithy's lifeless steel.

text.Rabanastran (man in green shorts East En: Migelo? Feting the new consul? Migelo this, Migelo that ... it's all I ever hear these days.

text.ACTION: (Panamis's Protectives (sign)) -Peace of body and mind – that's what you get when you buy quality armor. Step inside, and allow us to outfit you from head to toe.

text.Town Gossip: There's a nervous energy running through the whole city today. With the new consul coming, I suppose it's to be expected.

text.ACTION: (Amal's Weaponry (sign)) -In the market for a weapon? Look no further! Whether novice or knight, Amal knows just what you need ... even if you don't!

text.Bucco: Everyone sure seems busy today. You, Kytes, Penelo ... Me? Don't worry, I've got my own work to keep me busy. Heh heh. I'm gonna be so rich that – I know! I'll be rich enough to buy an airship! You can ride it anytime you want, Vaan!

text.Migelo: Ah, Vaan, I was waiting.

text.Vaan: Penelo said you needed something?

text.Migelo: Ah! Had me some packages supposed to be arriving by courier in the morning. Perhaps he ran into some trouble out in the desert. Now I've no foodstuffs to prepare for the banquet tonight!

text.Vaan: So you want me to find this courier? Hey, no problem!

text.Migelo: No problem? The desert teems with trouble. I'd be sending you to an early grave, m'boy. No, I've arranged for some replacement goods from Tomaj over at the Sandsea.

text.Vaan: So, you want me to go to the tavern to pick 'em up.

text.Migelo: Actually, I asked Kytes to do that. Wouldn't you know he's gone missing on me, too. Bah. I can't leave my shop and I've Penelo on another chore at the moment, you see. I want you to run over to the Sandsea and fetch Kytes back! What do you say?

text.Vaan: Sounds wild.

text.Migelo: It's easy work, and you'll thank me for it someday.

text.Rabanastran (tan seeq): Came to the East End to do some shopping ... But there are so many shops, I don't know where to begin.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa chatting with: My friend here says there are 14,264 cobblestones in the Southern Plaza 'round the corner, not including the tiles in the fountain. But even with the stones by the city gates ... 'Course, he could be countin' the flagstones, too. That would be another matter altogether.

text.ACTION: For more on this guy, see the Side Quests doc.

text.Imperial: Do anything suspicious, we'll lock you up so fast your head'll spin. Don't think we'll let you off 'cause you're young, neither.

text.ACTION: If you make for the Southern Plaza ...

text.Rabanastran (tan seeq): None of my business, I know, but Migelo did ask you to go to the Sandsea, didn't he? It's just that it's not that way, so ... Oh, never mind me.

text.ACTION: (Migelo's Sundries (sign)) -Newly refurbished and open for business! Everything's changed ... except our low prices!

text.Rabanastran (man in green shorts near Pa: Been some time since I was last in the Sandsea. Say hello to Tomaj for me, would you?

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq by bazaar entranc: Couple of guards were after someone, but looks like they gave up and went back to their post. Mebbe the parade's startin' soon?

text.Rabanastran (woman leaning against colum: Watch your purse if you're headed down to the bazaar. The place is thick with thieves. I suppose you know all about that, though. Ha ha.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink headscarf): Always provide for a supply of restoratives before starting a journey abroad. A potion's ability to instantly rejuvenate health is priceless.

text.Rabanastran (orange seeq): Hrmph. I don't know if it's because of the Consul or not, but things are just a little too on edge around here for my liking. If he thinks tightening his grip on the city will help, he's got another thing comin'. People will only resent him the more.

text.Rabanastran (man in green and blue talki: Always have more of a thing on hand than you plan to use, that's my philosophy. Better than running out of something when you really need it.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, green, and t: I was hoping to come across a bargain or two in honor of the new consul's arrival, but no such luck.

text.Migelo: Well? Have you found Kytes yet? Bah! I don't know what I'm going to do with the lot of you ... Oh, I'm grateful for your help. You work hard – when you want to. But lately you don't seem to want to, do you? What was it that set me off complaining? Ah, yes. Kytes. Go find Kytes! He should be at the Sandsea. Hurry now! Time's a-wasting!

text.Shop Clerk (Migelo's): Welcome to Migelo's Sundries! How might I be of service?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa in green vest): Some weapons are good for range, some strike quickly. Find a weapon that suits your needs, and stick with that.

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq walking about): Sure, we call 'em all "monsters", but not all are created equal. Plenty will keep to their business, if you keep to yours. 'Course, if you go pickin' a fight, don't surprised if'n they fight back. (snort)

text.Sherral: Don't mind me, boy. Just inspecting the weapons. Have to be sure nothing inappropriate is making its way to the average citizen, am I right?

text.Novice Adventurer: So many weapons, so little gil ...

text.Wise Moogle: Pish! What about all those pelts and fangs from the monsters you've killed? You know, the loot, kupo! That's worth plenty of gil!

text.Novice Adventurer: I know, I know. But it seems such a waste to just sell it all ...

text.Wise Moogle: Nonsense! You're only making things harder for yourself, kupo. Why line your purse with loot, when you could line it with gil instead? But there's more to it than that. The more loot you sell, the more bazaar goods you're like to come across. Bazaar goods can be anything from sets of items at discounted prices to rare pieces of equipment you won't see anywhere else, kupo.

text.Novice Adventurer: So what if I'm out on a hunt and I need to sell something? Do I have to keep selling my loot to the same shop to buy these bazaar goods?

text.Wise Moogle: You've got it all wrong, kupo! Where you sell makes no difference. All the shops will have the same bazaar goods available for you. They have a special arrangement, you see, so you can check any shop you like when you want to know which bazaar goods are in stock, kupo!

text.Novice Adventurer: Hmm. What'll they think of next?
Here's my plan. Once I find some bazaar goods I really like, I'm gonna buy as much as I can.

text.Wise Moogle: Oh, no no no. I'm afraid it doesn't work that way, kupo. Once you purchase a bazaar good, it won't be on sale any longer.

text.Novice Adventurer: What if I sell more loot? If the same bazaar good appears again, I can buy it again, right?

text.Wise Moogle: That's right, kupo. If you keep selling the loot you find, the same bazaar goods could come up for sale again. Then, of course, you can buy them again!

text.Amal: Might I interest the young master in some weapons?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Journeyman: Got to have proper protection before striking out looking for adventure. But be sure to pick armor that's right for you. That means finding a piece you have the license to equip. Having armor you can't wear is no better than having no armor at all!

text.Rabanastran (man browsing curio): I'm hoping this new consul can really make things better in Rabanastre. I'm ready to put war and suffering behind me.

text.Lively Bangaa: Woman asked me for some advice on choosing the right piece of armor. Thought I'd give her the lecture.

text.Panamis: We've many fine armors to choose from. If you see a piece you like, there's no time to buy like the present!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue pants): Things certainly are bustling over at Migelo's. I hear he's in charge of preparations for the Consul's fete.

text.Earnest Seeq: As I understands it, walkin' 'round can restore spent magickal energies ... but I can't for the life of me understand why! Magicks is a fickle mistress ...

text.Rabanastran (man in green & brown shorts: If you plan to dabble in magick, you'll need to be wary of elementals. They won't normally bother you, but they're sensitive to magicks. When they sense the working of magicks nearby, they react by attacking the caster with magicks of their own. And they're frightfully powerful.

text.Yugri: I'm sorry, we're still getting the shop in order. Please call again soon!

text.Rabanastran (man chatting with another m: Technicks are skills that let you do things no magicks can. Stealing treasures from your foes, stanching wounds ... You should give 'em a try.

text.Seasoned Adventurer: Want a word of advice from an old adventurer, boy? Don't squander your gil on technicks you've not got the license to use yet. Best to earn your licenses out fightin' first, then come buy what you need.

text.Rabanastran (man kneeling in front of sh: When it comes to technicks, no adventurer worth his salt would leave home without Libra. If you plan on fighting monsters, it's a must. Libra lets you see how tough your foe is before you fight, so you can decide if you're an even match. It will also show you a foe's weaknesses. But it won't work on every monster out there. Particularly difficult foes are immune to Libra. And there is ... another secret as well.

Hm? The other secret? Well ... all right. I'll let you in on it. But don't go spreading it around, okay? Libra is great, but there is some information you can only see without Libra. When you target a foe without using Libra, its name will appear red, yellow, or blue. The color tells you how strong your opponent is. Foes whose names are red are very powerful. Foes whose names are yellow will put up a fight. Foes whose names are blue should make easy prey.

text.Rabanastran (woman talking to red bangaa: I'm really looking forward to the parade for the new consul. If they're going to all this trouble, he must really be someone important.

text.Batahn: I am Batahn, and this is my technick shop. We are still preparing for today's business. Why don't you try back in a little while?

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with moogle): Still learning your way around the battlefield? It can help to set goals for yourself. Say, going from hunting rats to wolves. And if you really want to set your sights high, you should pay a visit to the notice board over in the Sandsea.

text.Imperial (pacing north side of fountain: The south and west gates are closed. If you've business outside the city, show a writ at the east gate. And be quick – she'll be closed soon.

text.Desert Merchant: I made it in from the Estersand just before they closed the gates. But they still haven't stopped with their questions ... My friend is still outside exchangin' words with the guards. If the parade starts, who knows how long he'll be stuck out there.

text.Imperial (pacing east side of fountain): Not long before the Consul's appointment ceremony begins. The south and west gates've been closed as part of the heightened watch.

text.Imperial (at the eastgate): What's this? No one passes through the gate without papers, boy. Off with you!

text.Imperial (standing in northwest corner): Do you always talk to strangers this way? Best learn to mind your place, churl.

text.Imperial (pacing west side of fountain): This gate's already closed! I bloody hate dealing with crowds ...

text.Imperial (pacing outside west gate): It's gettin' on for two years Dalmasca's been a province of the Empire. You'd think people would learn to accept it.

text.Imperial (halfway down stairs to south g: His Excellency the Consul is worried the heightened watch will make the smallfolk uneasy. Be thankful he's such a considerate man.

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa on balcony): I reckon this is one of the best views down into Lowtown you'll find from the city streets.

text.Merchant (tan seeq to side of stairs): Heh. Up to your usual "work", boy? The watch are out in force today – best not to try your luck. You'll not be picking any pockets from a dungeon, heh.

text.Merchant (green bangaa): Welcome! Welcome to the Muthru Bazaar! Finest goods in all Rabanastre! Deals not to be missed!

text.Trader: I've come across the Estersand to stock up on a few things. Always find the most unusual goods here in the Muthru Bazaar. A merchant's paradise! Speaking of the Estersand, I'm lucky I made it through when I did. Some red-pated beastie's been causin' trouble ... I might've been killed!

text.Merchant (blue seeq at top of steps): Spices! Authentic Bancour spices! Whaddaya say? Care for a pinch or two?

text.Gatsly: Business has been slow these days. I've been looking for something new to sell – you know, try and turn things around. If I don't come up with something soon, I may have to close shop. I've no time to be worrying about parades and banquets.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink and tan MB): The Imperials give us leave to manage the bazaar with some measure of freedom. It's in their own interest, really. Without places like this for people to let off steam, tension would boil over onto the streets.

text.Clan Provisioner: Heh, heh. Have all sorts of goodies for sale, lad. Hee, hee. But none for you. Hah, hah. Members only, here!

text.Merchant (tan bangaa in blindfold): Migelo played his hand well. Not everyone is lucky enough to be the provisioner for the Consul's fete. I've got some catchin' up to do!

text.Traveler (Muthru): I never imagined Rabanastre to be so delightful! A bustling center of trade and commerce, with just a hint of the exotic.

text.Headhunter: Hey there, boy. Got the lowdown on any good marks to be huntin'? Haven't had a chance to check the board over in the Sandsea today.

text.Busy Messenger: I'm runnin' an errand for the boss. Why go straight back, though, when I can take my time? Sometimes I do it just to annoy him, heh.

text.Rabanastran (man in white, yellow, and b: I've heard mention of some easy way to move around the city, but whatever it is, it's closed on account of the heavy guard for the ceremony.

text.Reks's Friend: Hey there, Vaan. Glad to see you're all right. You may want to think twice before picking any more Imperial pockets, though. You always were raisin' some kind o' trouble. I remember Reks was always fussin' at you about one thing or the other. Ah, those were the days ...

text.Rabanastran (green-horned tan seeq): Not many Imperials 'round here: just the way I likes it. Always walkin' about like their night soil smells better an' the rest of ours. The Knights of Dalmasca ... They knew how to treat a person with respect.

text.Patient Bangaa: The Imperials've sealed off all the gates leadin' out of the city. It's put my friend here in a foul mood. He won't shut up about it.

text.Swarthy Bangaa: You'd never know it to look at me, but I used to be a sky pirate. I worked and worked, and finally had enough money to buy me a beaten up old airship. Nothin' up t' then had put a bigger smile on me face. Ah ...

text.Troubled Woman: I saw you pick the pouch of that Imperial. I won't judge you for doing what you must, but you're asking for trouble. Reks would tell you the same.

text.Rabanastran (woman in red, pink, and blu: I do hope the parade drums up some business. I've just come from the bazaar, but I can scarcely afford a thing.

text.Bungling Hunter: Listen, churl, you get into trouble, do it proper, like. Make a name for yourself. I want the bounty on your head to be worth the trouble! Har!

text.Clan Watch: You want in? Out with it, then! Hah! You don't even have one! You'll no' be gettin' in without, boy. Off with ya!

text.ACTION: (??? (sign)) -(You're not sure what this sign is for.)

text.Imperial: Not now, boy, I'm on duty. Peddle your wares elsewhere, eh?

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on west sid: They're holding a banquet in the palace after the parade is over. Delicacies and delectables the likes of us'll never taste, boy.

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: They're locking the city down tight. Which suits me fine. I'm happy to stay right here. Don't believe me? Head down to the gates and see for yourself!

text.Traveler (North End): Isn't Rabanastre marvelous? Fascinating in ways wholly different from Archades. I've even taken to the local fashion!

text.Imperial: Don't worry, lad. I know the watch has been a bit rough today, but things should get back to normal soon enough once the parade is over.
We're on heightened watch until the Consul's inauguration ceremony is complete. Parts of the city are off limits for the duration.

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on east sid: There are those who care little for the Empire. No doubt they are the reason behind the show of Imperial force today.

text.Dispirited Woman: I haven't the slightest interest in the Imperial Parade. It will only remind me of the Princess's wedding to Prince Rasler ... I didn't have the clearest view of them then, but I could tell how happy they were. If only things had turned out differently ...

text.Imperial: No loitering! Can't keep watch with the likes of you standing 'round. We're under strict orders to arrest suspicious characters, boy.

text.Rabanastran (dark brown bangaa in black: First the parade, then the fete. This consul must be an important man.

text.Riby: Can't turn around without running into an Imperial today. Times like this, it's best to just keep your head down and stay outta trouble.

text.Rabanastran (man in white turban and bro: Oh, Vaan, it's you. Even two years later, sometimes I look at you and see Reks.

text.Tough Knight: The most important thing in a fight? A level head on your shoulders. Beasts great and small roam abroad. Be sure you know which you face before charging into battle.

text.ACTION: (Yamoora's Gambits (sign)) -"A mind without instruction can no more bear fruit than can a field without cultivation."

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, yellow, and: I was just out for a little stroll and these Imperials yell at me for no reason at all. Is such a heavy guard needed for the consul's arrival?

text.Rabanastran (woman in green and pink NE): I hear there's a resistance group planning something against the Imperials. But if you ask me, things aren't so bad the way they are now.

text.Imperial: All traffic with Lowtown is suspended until the new consul reaches the palace.

text.Helpful Man: Such a grand city ... Why, even the locals must need a map to find their way! Go ahead, look at your map. There's no shame in it!

text.Greenhorn: This is my first time in Yamoora's. I thought it was time I learned what all the fuss was about. Gotta say, I'm a bit nervous ...

text.Lord Vain: Looks like you've wandered into the gambit shop by mistake, boy! A great tool for leading a party of adventurers, which I can't help but see you lack. See, with a good set of gambits, you don't have t' shout out instructions left and right in a battle. First, you need a party, though. (snort)

text.Adept Adventurer: I walk the Way of the Gambit. Seek me out when the Way is open to you. I will lead you down its path.

text.Yamoora: Sorry, still gettin' the shop in order. It'll be a while yet, so you may want to try back later.

text.Vaan: There you are, Kytes. Stop loafing around!

text.Kytes: Look, Vaan, look! This is it! This is why Migelo's courier didn't get here on time!

text.Vaan: "Creature spotted in the Estersand." What is that thing?

text.Tomaj: Ah, Vaan. Migelo send you, too, did he? He's a busy man these days, that Migelo, if I dare say so myself. I don't envy him the work, though. Not a bit. Quite an affair, throwing a banquet to welcome the Imperials, eh?

text.Vaan: Welcoming? We should be – ah, whatever. Say, Tomaj, what's this?

text.Tomaj: Ah, don't remind me. Got some nastiness out there in the Estersand what's stopping our couriers ... and that means shortages all around. Thought I'd put up a bill ... offer a reward to anyone who can knock that nasty back in its place.

text.Vaan: Now that's work. Sounds ten times better than running errands for Migelo.

text.Kytes: That's right! Vaan, you should give it a shot!

text.Vaan: And you should be getting back to Migelo. Now, Kytes. He was waiting for you.

text.Kytes: Oh! Right, right.

text.Tomaj: So here's how it works. People post bills here on the notice board when they have a monster they need taken care of. Headhunters track people, right? Well, hunters track monsters. The monster you're hunting is called your mark. Here's the bill I posted for the Rogue Tomato, the mark I've petitioned to have hunted. Do you want to hear all the details?

CHOICE.Tomaj: Let's start with accepting hunts. You can't just take a look at the board, then go running off to hunt the mark. You'll miss out on the bounty. You gotta talk to the person who posted the bill - the petitioner - first. Let him know you're going on the hunt. So, take this Rogue Tomato bill, for example. I posted it, so I'm the petitioner. You have to come talk to me. Let's call that step "done," okay? Once your agreement's in place, the petitioner will tell you how to find the mark. Then you hunt it, report back, and claim the bounty. Oh, and I'll give you something to help keep track of your hunts: a clan primer. Use it to refresh your memory about hunts you've accepted.

CHOICE.ACTION: Clan Primer has been added to the Party Menu.

CHOICE.Tomaj: Go ahead and take this, while you're at it. Just a little something to commemorate your first hunt.

CHOICE.Vaan: No, I think I got it.

CHOICE.Tomaj: All right, but I'll be expecting you to take care of that Rogue Tomato for me. Oh, and I'll give you something to help keep track of your hunts: a clan primer. Use it to refresh your memory about hunts you've accepted.
Go ahead and take this, while you're at it. Just a little something to commemorate your first hunt.

Hmm, looks like you can't equip that yet. Know why? You don't have the license for it. Think of licenses as mile posts, marking your progress as your combat skills improve. Swords, bows, black magicks, white magicks ... none of it does you a lick of good until you have the license to use it. Same goes for that armlet. Tomaj, how can I equip this great treasure you've bestowed on me, you ask? Easy: learn by doing. Let's give it a try.
You can acquire a new license anytime you like from the Party Menu. First, decide whose licenses you want to examine. I don't see anyone else here, so it looks like that means you, Vaan.
This is the license board. The license board shows which licenses you already have, as well as some new ones waiting to be obtained. Licenses you've acquired are marked with a star.

Looks like right now you can equip Leather Clothing, Leather Caps, and Mythril Swords, and you have the technick to Steal from your foes. Heh, still a little wet behind the ears. We all have to start somewhere, though. The more licenses you have, the more equipment you'll be able to use, and the more abilities you'll have to choose from.

But a license alone isn't enough. Did you notice how Mythril Blade was darkened? That's because you don't have one in your inventory. You'll need to buy magicks from a magick shop, and arms from a smithy before you'll be able to put those licenses to use. It doesn't matter which you get first, magicks and equipment, or the license to use them, so long as you have both. You can use any magicks and technicks in your possession as soon as you acquire the necessary license. But you'll have to equip weapons and armor before they'll do you any good. Got it?

All right, let's take a look at that number in the top left. These are your license points. You spend these points to acquire new licenses. You can acquire any license that's next to one you already have, but only if you have enough license points.
Ah, this should do! Why don't you try obtaining this license now? Select the license and press X. Then you'll have the Accessories 1 license.

Now you shouldn't have any trouble equipping that orrachea armlet I gave you. Just don't forget to equip it, okay? You probably noticed already, but when you obtained that license, several new ones appeared on the board.

You don't have enough license points to obtain any more now, but take down a few monsters and you'll have the points before you know it. Don't be in a hurry to spend all your points, though. Think about which licenses you really need, or you might regret it later. Oh, let me show you one thing while I'm at it. Go ahead and press □.

That list shows all of the actions you can take during battle. It can definitely come in handy. Well, if you can remember all that, you shouldn't have any trouble taking down a mark or two on your own.

CHOICE.ACTION: Licenses has been added to the Party Menu.

CHOICE.Tomaj: I'd say you're ready to hunt that mark for me. Oh, you'll be needing this to leave the city. Just show it to the watch at the gate.

CHOICE.ACTION: You obtain a Writ of Transit!

CHOICE.Tomaj: The east gate's the one you'll want to head out. Once you've taken care of that mark for me, let me know. Your work won't go unrewarded.

text.Tavernmaster: How are you, Vaan? That creature in the desert has us chasing after supplies from dawn till dusk. Someone better do something, and quick.

text.Rabanastran (man sitting with woman): I hear there's a mark out in the Estersand. 'Course, the Imperials are too busy securing the city to worry over troubles beyond her walls.

text.Tomaj: Hi, Vaan. Something I can help you with?

CHOICE.Tomaj: Marks are monsters that a petitioner posts a bill to have hunted. Successfully hunting marks will earn you a small bounty. See that notice board over on the wall? That's where you can go to see what bills have been posted. It all starts there. But just looking at the bill isn't enough. You have to go talk to the petitioner and accept the hunt before setting out. The bill will always tell you where to find the petitioner. Once you've accepted the hunt, you're ready to track down the mark using the information given to you by the petitioner. If you're able to defeat the mark, report back to the petitioner. That completes the hunt, and you should receive your bounty. Simple, right? The best way to learn is by doing. Hunt a few marks on your own and you'll have it down in no time.

Ah, Vaan. I meant to tell you: this isn't the only notice board you'll find. Most cities – even some villages – have their own board. The good news is, all of the notice boards have the same bills. So you can go to the closest board without worrying about checking them all.

Each and every battle-related ability has a license that entitles you to use it. Say you want to cast the white magick "Cure." You have to obtain the license for it first. The same is true of equipment. Even the most devastating weapon won't do you any good if you don't have the license to equip it. The licenses you have determine how you can fight, so think before you choose.

Ah, Vaan. I meant to tell you: this isn't the only notice board you'll find. Most cities – even some villages – have their own board. The good news is, all of the notice boards have the same bills. So you can go to the closest board without worrying about checking them all.

You'll never find that Rogue Tomato standing around in here. The Imperials have started locking down the gates for the parade, but you ought to be able to get out if you show them that writ I gave you. Just talk to the watch by the east gate in the Southern Plaza. You shouldn't have any trouble.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa at bar with To: A parade to install this new consul? Fie! They're just lookin' fer an excuse to flaunt their might. Well, let the fools strut, I say!

text.Barkeep (woman leaning against wall by d: Have you seen how many guards they've stationed in the Southern Plaza? I suppose it makes sense ... That is where the city gates are. If you find yourself by Migelo's, you should take a look. Not every day you see that many Imperials in one place.

text.Barkeep (man standing near foot of stair: I heard you could still leave the city through the east gate, but when I tried to pass, I was turned away. Turns out they're only letting through people on business for the fete. Would it kill them to bend the rules? I hope they didn't hear that ...

text.Barkeep (woman on balcony): I'm sorry, but the balcony is reserved for members of the Imperial watch. Or so they've decided, at least. They're nothing more than two-bit sellswords, if you ask me.

text.Sotted Imperial: Who gave you leave to come up here, boy? The balcony's reserved for the Imperial watch, you hear?

text.Clan Watch: Ah, so you've got your Primer, so you have. Well? What're you standin' about out here for? In with ya! Can't quite recall your face. Are you new? Might want to pay special heed to what the folks inside have to say. Well, are you goin' in or not?

CHOICE.ACTION: You're let in to the Clan Hall.

text.ACTION: The Clan Hall

text.Monid: What are you lookin' at? This ain't no place for children! Him? He's an exception. His parents were both hunters. And they were friends of mine to boot. That is, until they set out on a hunt for this one most notorious mark ... But I'll avenge them, be sure of it! I've been keeping an ear to the ground, listening for any sign of that mark ever since. That's what this place is all about. A deadly serious business, this, not to be taken lightly, you hear?
You've got much and more to learn, and you can start with this: stay out of my way! I'd as soon kill you as look at you, so don't be trying my patience.

text.Bansat: New member, are you? M' name's Bansat. I'm a hunter here in Clan Centurio. Pleased to meet ya.
Getting the feel for battle? You can never have too much practice.

text.Clan Member (moogle with green pom-pom w: Are you new here, kupo? My advice for you: always be sure to check for the latest bills. Never know when a new one might be posted, kupo. No matter the notice board you check, the bills will be the same. So go to the nearest one, and you're set, kupo!

text.Clan Member (woman in pink watching prac: So, Tomaj recommended you to the clan, did he? I bet he pretended he didn't even know about the clan hall. If he had told you where it was, he'd be in trouble. Finding the clan hall is one of the tests to join the clan. Where you go from here is up to you.

text.Clan Member (man sitting on steps talkin: Hmph. You look like you barely know which end of the sword goes in the monster. Don't do anything to hurt the Clan ... or yourself.

text.Clan Member (green bangaa talking to red: What have we here? A newcomer, eh? Montblanc's the founder of our clan, so be sure to show him the proper respect. Our job's to travel about accepting hunts from the boards, gathering news about marks that need to be dealt with right away, elite marks, and the like.

text.Ma'kenroh: A new clan member? Hrgm ... I am Ma'kenroh. A pleasure, I'm sure. Unlike our other members, I cannot participate in hunts. My specialty lies in the collection of information. If you have a question about one of your marks, ask. I will tell you what I know.

Hello. How does this day find you? Hunting the Rogue Tomato? Hrgm ... Find it in the Dalmasca Estersand. Leave by the east gate, head to the northeast. Now, go. Oh, about your clan rank ... When you've defeated 2 marks and accumulated 700 clan points, you will gain a rank. Now, go.

text.Krjn: Yes? What is it you need? I am Krjn, a hunter of Clan Centurio. To know my boundaries did I join the clan. It is a wellspring of information about powerful marks.
If you sense danger, be cautious. Flight, too, has its place in battle.

text.Montblanc: Kupo-po? Yours is a new face! Are you a hunter? Welcome to our clan hall! I'm Montblanc, founder of Clan Centurio. It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance, kupo! Our clan has a very strict entrance examination. We should begin yours at once ... And, you pass. Moogles are quick to make up their minds, kupo.

Here in the clan hall you'll hear about especially dangerous marks you won't find posted on any board, the moment they rear their ugly heads! Well, I'll get on with filing the necessary clan membership certificates. I'll be finished in no time flat, kupo! Kupo! I nearly forgot! Now that you're a member, you can make purchases from our clan shop in the Muthru Bazaar. Be sure to stop by, kupo! Happy hunting!

How fares the hunt, kupo? All your membership papers are in order, kupo. Allow me to give you this to commemorate your joining the guild! I'll have a little something for you each time you attain a new clan rank, kupo.
Keep up the splendid work, kupo!
Kupo-po? I'm sorry, but I don't have any hunts to tell you about at the moment, kupo.
How fares the hunt, kupo? Kupo-po? I'm sorry, but I don't have any hunts to tell you about at the moment, kupo.

text.Clan Watch: Well, what do you think of the clan? A nice enough lot, if you ask me.

text.ACTION: (This is a sign for Clan Centurio, but only clan members would know it as such.)

text.Clan Provisioner: Heh, heh. Heard the boss gave you the okay. But it's not that simple, lad. We've got strict rules you gotta abide by here. The things I can sell you depend on your clan rank. You want a crack at the good stuff, best raise your rank. I doubt you'll be disappointed! Didn't mean to talk yer ear off! Go on and take a look at what we have ... for your rank, of course.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Clan Provisioner: Step right up, lad! Let's see, for your rank, our goods look something like this. Holler if you see something that takes your fancy.

text.ACTION: shop menu

After the initial meeting, the dialogue in the Clan Hall changes depending not on story progression, but on your progression in hunts and clan ranking. The only way story affects what goes on in the Clan Hall is when Montblanc has rewards for boss battles only completed through progressing the story. Clan Hall dialogue and the Clan Primer will therefore be documented in the Clan Primer doc from here on out.

text.Yugri: Welcome to Yugri's Magicks. How may I help you?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Batahn: Welcome to Batahn's! We've a fine selection of technicks. I'm sure you'll find something to your liking!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (man in green shorts near Pa: Heading out to the desert? Mind the guards in the Southern Plaza on your way. They're ill-tempered enough when they're not busy closing the gates.

text.Penelo: Did you finish the chores Migelo set you to already?

text.Migelo: Oh, Kytes is back – he's been on tenterhooks ever since he walked in the door. Well, so long as he's not up to any mischief ...

text.Kytes: What's wrong, Vaan? Aren't you going to go get that Rogue Tomato? You better hurry up before the ceremony starts. You won't be able to get back into the city!

text.Desert Merchant: I made it in from the Estersand just before they closed the gates, but my friend was stopped before he could get through. Could you take him something for me?

CHOICE.Desert Merchant: Excellent. You should find him just outside the east gate – a bangaa, like myself. And don't go sellin' that to pocket the gil for yourself, y'hear?

text.Desert Merchant: My friend's just outside the east gate. Can't miss 'im.

text.Imperial (at the eastgate): You there! Let's see some papers, boy. No public passage on account of the Lord Consul's parade.

text.Vaan: Oh, gee, that's too bad. You see, it just so happens that your provisioner for the fete tonight ... he sent me to pick up a few choice morsels for the, uh, Consul's dining pleasure. He wants 'em quick. I got the writ of transit right here. See? Signed: Migelo. I'd just hate to see the Consul upset because his food wasn't ready on time. And I'd sure hate to see him take it out on you.

text.Imperial (at the eastgate): The Lord Consul is a great man ... and not one to take offense at such trifling ... matters ...

text.ACTION: The Imperial looks to the other soldiers, who have gathered around him. Pressured, he concedes.

text.Imperial (at the eastgate): Move along, boy. Wouldn't do to keep the Consul waiting. Right! Gates are closed after this!

text.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): Your eyes not working, boy? You want to pass, you queue up with everyone else. Any arguments, speak to the guard at the back of the queue.

text.Waiting Bangaa: Once the gates close, they'll not be letting anyone through. No exceptions. I'm getting in while the gettin's good. You trying to push in? Best be rethinkin' that move, mate. You want inside, you get in line behind me, understand?

text.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): Not many more people comin' along now. Once we get this lot taken care of, that should just about do it, I'd say. What about you? Lookin' to get inside?

CHOICE.Vaan: Yeah, let me get in line.

CHOICE.ACTION: The Imperial will make room for you in the line, and people will begin filing in one by one from the line. Soon enough it'll be your turn; talk to the Imperial at the head of the line.

CHOICE.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): The watch inside notified me. Foodstuffs for the banquet wasn't it? Well, do you need to pass?
I don't see any foodstuffs on you. Still have work to do, eh? Well, be about your business. Go on now.

CHOICE.ACTION: The gate will open and you will automatically go back to the Southern Plaza on the other side of the gate.

CHOICE.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): Right. No foodstuffs on you yet. Leastwise none I can make out. Best hurry about your business. Gates'll close and stay closed 'fore long.

text.Man in Queue: They're inspecting everyone before letting people through. You're gonna have to stand in line if you want in. Not that the line is moving ...

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, pink, and gr: The inspection line's grown a good deal shorter, and hardly anyone's leaving the city now. I imagine these people will be the last through. I suppose I should be heading in myself. Wouldn't do to be shut out here, would it?

text.Erstwhile Adventurer: Cannae pass through the gates till they finish goin' over ma belongin's. Risked life an' limb crossin' the desert to be treated like this! Bah! On yer way out o' the city, are ye? There's a tomato beastie runnin' amok on a bluff close by. Don't get yerself into nae bother, d'ye hear?

text.Hapless Merchant: My companion and I arrived together, but they singled out my goods for inspection. I've been held up here all day! You came from the city, yes? Did a bangaa merchant happen to give you an item to deliver?

CHOICE.Hapless Merchant: Well, what do you know! My thanks, boy. Helped me out of a tight spot, you have. Heading into the desert, are you? Best watch yourself out there. Get into any fights, just be sure to keep well healed, hear me? Mind your wounds or the next blow you take could be your last. Had myself caught by the tail a time or two out there, let me tell you.
Right, of course not. Thanks anyway.

text.Hapless Merchant: Thanks for your help, boy. This won't get me into the city any sooner, but it should help pass the time. Mind what I told you about traveling the desert. Tend to your wounds or you'll soon be feeding the wolves, heh.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, pink, and gr: They've closed the chocobo stables for the day on account of the Consul's arrival. Speaking of which, shouldn't the ceremony be starting soon? I wonder if we can still get back in the city. Or have they closed the gates?

text.Rabanastran (woman in white speaking wit: I had no idea they'd be closing the gates. I was worried we may not make it into the city. But it looks like we've arrived just in time.

text.Imperial (at the eastgate): You again ... Well, are you going through or not?

CHOICE.Imperial (at the eastgate): The gate won't be open much longer. Hurry back, or you'll have to wait for the parade to finish.

CHOICE.ACTION: The gate opens and you automatically find yourself in the Eastgate area on the other side.

CHOICE.Imperial (at the eastgate): Then what you botherin' me for!? Now, step aside!

text.ACTION: The Dalmasca Estersand

text.Unlucky Merchant: That's my chocobo just over there. Has a fondness for shiny things – buries everything it can get its beak on. The most recent victim? All the gil I made in Rabanastre! And now they've got the road to the Nebra blocked off ... This just isn't my day.

text.Wise Elder: Huntin' the Rogue Tomato? Well, well. Looks like we have a fledgling clan member, am I right? But you've missed the mark, so to speak. Heh heh. The mark you're after is in The Stepping, back the way you came. Go and give it another look, eh?

text.Energetic Child: Pretty hot, huh? 100 gil if you wanna rest!

CHOICE.Vaan: It is pretty hot out here ...

CHOICE.Energetic Child: Heh heh, thanks mister! C'mon in!

CHOICE.ACTION: After a brief fade out and back in ...

CHOICE.Energetic Child: If you need to get in outta the sun, lemme know!

text.Dantro: Hi there. Name's Dantro. I'm on watch here. You come hoping to go to Nalbina? Sorry to tell ya, but the road's not open. Hey, don't blame me. You're not the only one put out by it, either. I've been waitin' forever for my replacement to come.

text.Desert Wayfarer (woman sitting on crate): My father said he didn't mind paying, but maybe I ought to pitch in a little too. Chocobos don't come cheap, and with all these delays ... I hope he can afford it.

text.Desert Wayfarer (man near chocobo speaki: I hired a chocobo, but for what? They've got the whole blasted desert blocked off!

text.Imperial Watch: No one's allowed through 'less they're on official business. Leastwise not until the Lord Consul's appointment ceremony is complete.

text.Arryl: You stuck here too? I came from the village up ahead, and now I can't get back. Him? Don't worry about him. He won't bite or nothin'. He's practically family! Cute, huh?

text.ACTION: After defeating the Rogue Tomato, there is an automatic cutscene.
Vaan spots a few red flowers growing nearby.

text.Vaan: Galbana lilies?
Never thought I'd see them growing out here.

text.ACTION: Vaan squats down to pick the flowers.

text.Vaan: This'll make a nice souvenir. Time to call it a day.

text.ACTION: You obtain a handful of Galbana Lilies!

text.Rabanastran (woman in white speaking wit: This is an outrage! I thought we'd make it in with time to spare, but they closed the gates before they finished inspecting our things!

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, pink, and gr: I just don't see why they won't let me through. I'm a citizen same as anyone else, aren't I?

text.Erstwhile Adventurer: So just as they're finishin' their inspection, what do I see but the gates closin' before ma very eyes! A wee bit dodgy, wouldn't ye say?

text.Hapless Merchant: Urgh. They wouldn't let me through! Nothing to do now but wait until the ceremony's over.

text.Kytes: Ah, Vaan! I guess I'm not the only one who got locked out of the city! I told Penelo about the mark you were going after, and I guess I got her worrying. So the two of us headed out here to find you. As soon as I stepped out, the guards closed the gates and things got crazy. I haven't been able to find her since.

text.Imperial 2: This gate's closed till the ceremony's over, do you hear?

text.Vaan: Now what?

text.ACTION: Vaan is forced to stand aside as a pair of highly decorated chocobos is escorted through.
gate begins opening

text.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): All right, out of the way!

text.Vaan: Wait a second! How come you let these chocobos through the gate and not us?

text.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): What of it? This here is a pedigreed parader, boy. Costs tens of thousands of gil, this one did. A prettier price than a hundred of you provincials would fetch. Keep your distance! We don't want the chocobos stinking of peasant.

text.Vaan: What did you say?

text.ACTION: shoves Vaan out of the way
Vaan notices he dropped his Galbana lilies when he was shoved, and the chocobos are now trampling over them.

text.Vaan: That does it.

text.Migelo: Ho, ho! A fine, fine chocobo you have there. Yes! Tchita Downs stock, if I'm not mistaken. Change the soil, change the chocobo, am I right?

text.ACTION: Migelo comes through the gate, chatting up the Imperial and holding a jar of wine. Penelo ducks in behind him, taking Vaan by the arm.

text.Migelo: Yes, yes. Different soil means different bouquet, too. Take a Dalmascan Barose wine, eh? It may lack the flavor and depth of some of your Archadian wines ... but it has a certain strength of character. It's not bad, really, once you get used to it. Care for some, sirs? There's more than enough for all to cool their throats, of course.

text.ACTION: The Imperial takes the jar from Migelo imperiously (of course).

text.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): You, let these carts through and then we close this gate as ordered.

text.ACTION: aside

text.Imperial (Outside Eastgate): My mail's choked with this sand.

text.ACTION: Migelo bows, and then turns to Vaan and Penelo.

text.Migelo: Don't give me a scare like that. You're lucky that ended where it did.

text.Penelo: Right. Now's our chance to go through.

text.ACTION: Bells peal from within the city.

text.Migelo: Ah, the ceremony'll be starting soon. I'd best be hurrying.

text.Penelo: Okay, well –

text.ACTION: Vaan takes off running suddenly.

text.Penelo: Vaan! Wait!

text.ACTION: Penelo starts after him.

text.Penelo: What is it? Vaan?

text.ACTION: The new consul Vayne Solidor's speech. Click for video.

text.Imperial: We will have order! I give you your new consul his Imperial Highness Lord Vayne Solidor, Commandant of the Archadian Empire's Western Arm –

text.ACTION: noticing Vayne has stepped forward

text.Imperial: Your Excellency!

text.ACTION: Vayne ascends the dais to speak.

text.Vayne: People of Rabanastre! Is it with hatred you look upon your consul? With hatred you look upon the Empire?

There was little point in asking. But know this – I harbor no idle hopes of frustrating that hatred, nor shall I ask your fealty. That is the due of your fallen king, and rightly so. King Raminas loved his people. Strove to bring you peace. His was a rule worthy of your devotion. Even now, he remains among you, protecting you. His ardor for the peace and weal of Dalmasca falters not. I would ask only that you do your king honor. Together, let us embrace this peace His Majesty would surely desire. Two years now divide us from war's bitter end, yet still its shadow looms over all, stifling the infant peace, a pall only you may cast off. Achieve but this one thing, and your hatred of me, and the Empire, will grieve me not! I will stand fast! I will endure your hatred! Suffer your slings and arrows! I will defend Dalmasca! Here I will pay my debts, I swear it now. Though King Raminas and Lady Ashe be gone, they stand ever at the side of their people. In honoring peace, you do honor to their memory, and to Dalmasca. What I ask, I ask plain. My hopes now rest with you.

text.ACTION: The audience, somewhat stunned and reluctant, breaks into applause as Vayne bows.

text.Imperial: Is Rabanastre to your liking, my lord?

text.Vayne: It is magnificent! Take this cathedral, for instance. Elegant, yet whimsical in its execution. A stunning example of Galtean architecture. I hope Lord Gramis might one day look upon it himself.

text.Imperial: The patron of this evening's banquet, may it please Your Excellency.

text.Migelo: I am Migelo, Your Highness.

text.ACTION: bowing, on one knee

text.Migelo: It is truly a profound honor to make the acquaintance ... of our future emperor, Highness. The people of Rabanastre join me in welcoming –

text.Vayne: That's enough of "Highness." Though indeed I am our emperor's son, I am no prince. Archadia's emperor is freely chosen by her people. I am but an elected official and nothing more.

text.ACTION: looking down

text.Migelo: I meant no disrespect.

text.Vayne: Now that I think on it ... I would not have you address me as Lord Consul, for that matter. Henceforth, I am a citizen of Rabanastre. Why don't you call me Vayne?

text.Migelo: Eh, I could not. That would not be right.

text.Vayne: You are overly fond of formalities. I've just the remedy for that. Tonight you will join me, and we shall drink until you call me by name.

text.ACTION: Vayne pats him on the back before departing. Migelo gives one last bow. Vaan and Penelo comment on the scene from their stoop a ways away.

text.Vaan: How can he stand to bow to him like that?

text.Penelo: Vaan, you just do not get it, do you. He's not doing it because he wants to. You know what would happen if he didn't?

text.Vaan: I know. It's just –

text.Penelo: So, what would you do different?

text.Vaan: I don't know. Well, I'd do something.

text.ACTION: The scene fades.

text.Penelo: Vaan?
Vaan! You haven't heard a single word I've said, have you.

text.ACTION: We see Vaan and Penelo back at the same spot in the East End where they were earlier.

text.Penelo: This place has changed so much. It's like it's not even Rabanastre anymore. Like the Empire is swallowing it whole.

text.Vaan: Hey, Penelo. That fete tonight. You think they'll let us in?

text.Penelo: Are you crazy? It's in the palace, and we don't have an invitation, if you hadn't noticed.

text.Vaan: So ... how are we getting in?

text.Penelo: As if I'd know. Why not ask Migelo to get you in? Or go see Old Dalan in Lowtown. Why the sudden interest, Vaan?

text.Vaan: I told you! I'm going to take back what's ours! Give back to Dalmasca. C'mon, what do you think? If I find something, and it fetches a good price, how 'bout I, uh ... I buy you all dinner!

text.Penelo: Oh please! You know as well as I do the first thing you'd buy is an airship! All hail Vaan, sky pirate of Dalmasca! It's got a nice ring to it! Stay outta trouble!

text.ACTION: Penelo waves goodbye and runs off.

text.Vaan: Hmm. An airship. I dunno. Maybe. But not through Migelo. Time to pay Old Dalan a visit.

text.ACTION: A bangaa with a hammer slung over his shoulder passes by Vaan as he leaves, and goes around the corner to meet a green bangaa in black armor and with several piercings dictating to another bangaa.
You are now free to enter Lowtown and leave Rabanastre.
