text.Rabanastran (woman in red, pink, and blu: If I could find a way to curry favor with Lord Vayne, I'd need never worry about money again.

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on west sid: They'll be starting that fete in the palace soon. Ah, the food they'll have ... What I wouldn't give for just a taste!

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: I can finally go home to Lowtown now! Maybe I'll pay Old Dalan a visit. He's always got a tall tale or two to tell.

text.Traveler (North End): Under Vayne's rule, Rabanastre will flourish as never before. I'm sure of it! I may even consider moving here myself!

text.Imperial (North End): The ceremony's over. You're free to move about Lowtown and pass through the city gates.

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on east sid: So the ceremony ended without incident, eh? Good! I don't care much for the Empire, but I care even less for trouble.

text.Dispirited Woman: Vayne invaded Nalbina ... Basch wouldn't accept surrender and killed the King ... Enemies of Dalmasca both, in my book.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa): The Empire wouldn't send someone like Vayne just anywhere. No, this says something about Dalmasca's importance to the Empire.

text.Riby: I didn't understand a word of that speech, but I'll get Old Dalan to explain it to me. There's no one knows more than he does!

text.Rabanastran (man in white turban and bro: That new consul – he looks like some kind of general to me. Which means he was probably involved in the attack on Nalbina. Why would they send someone like him to rule us?

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, yellow, and: I can never find my way to Lowtown when I need to. There should be a stairway around here somewhere ...

text.Rabanastran (woman in white with hat): The guards are letting people into Lowtown again, but I still can't find the stairs! My map shows a stairway over by the gambit shop, but I can't make head nor tail of it.

text.Greenhorn: This is my first time in Yamoora's. I was just getting an explanation about gambits from this kid here. It's all about efficiency, he says.

text.Adept Adventurer: Did I watch the parade? Does a forest watch the ocean? Parades are nothing to one traveling the Way of the Gambit. Seek me out when the Way of the Gambit is open to you. I will lead you down its path.

text.Johm: This new, uh, consul ... He's one of the ones that attacked Dalmasca, isn't he? Why'd it have to be someone like him ... ?

text.Rabanastran (man in turban and brown sho: I wish there were some way to sneak into that fete tonight. Wouldn't mind gettin' my hands on some of them eatables, eh?

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq pacing about): This is a big night for Migelo. He's in charge of the preparations for the fete, isn't he? Let's hope it goes off without a hitch.

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa EE): I'd heard they were bringing in one of these "highborn" to be the new consul, but the son of the Emperor himself? Never expected that!

text.Rabanastran (woman in green and pink EE): At last, we can finally go back to Lowtown. I've had enough of these Imperials and their meaningless rules! I'm sorry, I've let my tongue get the better of me.

text.Wistful Bangaa: At least this new consul seems better than the last. 'Course, the King and Princess, they ... oh, forget I said anythin'.

text.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): So Lowtown's the place where most of us people in Rabanastre live. There are stairs down to Lowtown here in the East End, and, uh ... Oh yeah! The North End and Southgate, too! Hmm, I may need to get some better material if I expect people to keep coming, huh. Maybe I'll go talk to Old Dalan and see if he has any good stories I can ... borrow.

text.Lonely Boy: I sure feel sorry for all the people what got forced to move down to Lowtown.

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: So, whaddaya think? Will Migelo be able to call this new consul by his first name tonight? Honestly, I don't think he has it in him.

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq by bazaar entranc: Sure, the parade was fun, but it wasn't that hearty belly laugh kind o' fun. You get me?

text.Rabanastran (man in green shorts near Pa: We're nothing but servants groveling at the feet of the Empire ... Seeing Migelo at the ceremony today was enough to remind me of that.

text.Town Gossip: Quite a parade, wasn't it? I always feel a little sad when something like that ends ...

text.Bucco: Hey, Vaan. I saw you and Penelo together during the parade. You sly dog ...

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa chatting with: My friend here says there are 22,505 cobblestones in the Southern Plaza 'round the corner, not including the tiles in the fountain. But even with the stones by the city gates ... 'Course, he could be countin' the flagstones, too. That would be another matter altogether.

text.Imperial: The Consul's appointment ceremony may be over, but our regular watch will continue as before. Mind how you behave, churl.

text.Rabanastran (woman talking to red bangaa: The parade was wonderful, don't you think? Just hearing the Consul speak, you could tell he's a man of power and influence.

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with moogle): I hear you hunted down the Rogue Tomato and even made it over to the clan hall. Coming along fast, kid.

text.Gatsly: I'm at my wit's end. If that shipment doesn't get through ... I don't know what I'll do. There has to be a hunter out there who'll do it ...

text.Rabanastran (man sitting with woman): I saw you lookin' at the notice board a while back. How did your hunt go? Well, I'm glad to hear it! You started your next hunt yet? Let me know how it turns out!

text.Barkeep (woman leaning against wall by d: Never hurts to keep a close eye on the notice board. At worst, you can look over your current hunts, and at best, you may find a new one!

text.Tavernmaster: How are things with you, Vaan? With all the food and drink orders for the fete, I can't complain, heh heh.

text.Tomaj: Ah, Vaan! Defeated that Rogue Tomato, did you? I was worried you might not be ready just yet, but you did a fine job of it! Here. Your bounty for completing the hunt.

text.ACTION: Red & Rotten in the Desert: 300 gil, x2 Potion, x1 Teleport Stone

text.Tomaj: Oh, I hear you stopped by the clan hall. You're one shrewd customer. I'm sure you heard all manner of things from the other hunters, but just take your time to ease into it and you'll do fine.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa at bar with To: 'Course I didn't watch the parade. What's the point in watchin' the Imperials march about, proud as they please?

text.Barkeep (man standing near foot of stair: Now that the gates are open again, I went to collect some goods, but I, uh, encountered a slight difficulty. Entirely my own fault. I was supposed to go to Giza Plains, but I left by the east gate instead of the south gate. (sigh) What a waste of time.

text.Sotted Imperial: Just who do you think you are? The balcony is reserved for the Imperial watch. You can toast the new consul from downstairs, boy.

text.ACTION: I'm studying magick so I can protect myself, if I must. It's not that I don't trust the new consul, but we each have a duty to keep our city safe.

text.Merchant (tan seeq to side of stairs): Up to your usual "work", boy? Best not test your luck. The watch may be more lax, but if they bump into a cutpurse ... they do it hard, heh.

text.Trader: I've come 'cross the Estersand to stock up on a few things. Now I hear some beast's appeared out there attacking desert wayfarers. You defeated the creature? Really? You must be tougher than you look. Well, guess there's no need to worry about the trip back now, is there.

text.Rabanastran (woman sitting in Gatsly's s: My husband spent almost every last gil we had on a shipment of new goods for the shop, hoping to keep the customers coming. But there's a creature wandering the desert that's been keeping traders from getting through to the city. My husband's been so worried that something will happen to our shipment, he's practically boarded himself up in the tavern.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink and tan MB): The Bazaar is one of the few places in Rabanastre where people can go to let off steam. Hopefully, the new consul won't do anything to change that.

text.Traveler (Muthru): I never imagined Rabanastre to be so delightful! And with Lord Vayne ruling the city, it's sure to prosper as never before!

text.Headhunter: I was hunting the Rogue Tomato, but someone else got to it first. Don't know who, but I'm none too happy 'bout it.

text.Busy Messenger: I'm runnin' an errand for the boss. He works us like dogs, that Montbla – er, boss.

text.Rabanastran (man in white, yellow, and b: I've heard people talking about some easy way to move around the city. You'd think it would be running now that the guard is back to normal ...

text.Patient Bangaa: The parade's really bringin' 'em out, innit? Put my friend here in a foul mood. Says he don't care to be pushed, pulled, and or pressed.

text.Troubled Woman: I didn't go to the ceremony. I just stayed here, thinking about how things used to be ...

text.Lively Bangaa: We're talking about this new consul. He seems a not-so-bad fellow, well-informed and capable.

text.Rabanastran (man browsing curio): The Consul has gotten off on the right foot. I've high expectations of him.

text.Panamis: Interest you in a piece of armor? If there's aught to your liking, I'll have it brought 'round. But don't dawdle, I've plans for the evening.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Sherral: Fortunately, His Excellency the Consul has arrived without incident. Naturally, I kept up my weapons inspection throughout the ceremony. A moment of weakness or indiscretion can undo a lifetime's work. History's replete with examples of such. Our duty is to enforce the law unerringly.

text.Amal: Welcome, welcome! I'll be closing the store early tonight ... Special circumstances, you know. Heh, heh. Should be quite an evening, yes.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink headscarf): Don't the Imperials have better things to spend money on than parades? How about putting some meat in our stewpots for starters?

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, green, and t: Migelo was really groveling at the ceremony. Embarrassing it was, yes, but you get the feeling he was only doing what he had to do. There are times to wear your pride, and there are times to swallow it. The trick is recognizing which is which.

text.Penelo: Migelo's out getting ready for the fete. Do you think he'll really call the new consul by his first name? I think he'd sooner die.

text.Rabanastran (orange seeq): Hrmph. This consul sounds a mite better than the last. 'Course, I won't believe it till I see it.

text.Rabanastran (man talking to red bangaa): Let's see, what is it you've got bubbling away in that head of yours ... Maybe you're planning to sneak into the fete tonight, eh? Ha ha! Of course you aren't! Even you wouldn't do something as foolhardy as that.

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa speaking with wo: Glad the watch has finally let up. Was gettin' so you couldn't turn 'round without your tail bumpin' an Imperial. Er, better watch my tongue ...

text.Rabanastran (boy squatting down and hugg: There were too many guards at the parade ... All those fat purses, and no chance to swipe 'em! I feel like I was the one who was robbed!

text.Imperial (Southern Plaza): There were rumors about a group of insurgents plottin' an attack, but we kept the peace good 'n' proper. The city gates, the stairs to Lowtown – you can come 'n' go as you like now.

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants with his: My boy and I just watched the parade ... it's all he'll talk about now. We saw the wedding parade two years ago, but he was too young to remember.

text.Rabanastran (boy with his father in the: That parade was the best thing I ever saw! I wanna be in a parade, too!

text.Lovestruck Man: I can't believe the Consul is the Emperor's son! Imagine, someone like that in Rabanastre ... I hope he's the right man to help the city move forward.

text.Cartographers' Guild: Would you like to buy a map, kupo?

text.ACTION: maps of Giza, Estersand, Westersand

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa in red vest): They've got the aerodrome at Westgate closed special for all the Imperials returnin' to Archadia.

text.Cotze: What are they doin' holdin' a parade? Nothing these Imperials do makes any sense to me ...

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue and green on so: That Vayne sure must be rich to throw a parade like that. I hope I, uh, "bump" into him on the street one of these days. Heh, heh.

text.Bright-eyed Boy: Chocobos are my favorite animal. Big, yellow ... what's not to like? I sure hope I get to ride one someday!

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: He was orphaned during the war, so I took him in. At first, he wouldn't say a word. He'd just cry, and cry. But I think that's finally behind him now. The orphans in this town are many. I only pray we never face such a war again.
I'm glad that parade is over. We can finally come and go as we please again.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Southga: You ever been to the village out on Giza Plains? It's just a ways off to the south of here. They raise some kind of big ol' roly-poly birds down there.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Westgat: Hey, Vaan, how's it goin'? Not so good for me ... It's hard to "work" with all these guards around. Maybe we can make up for it at the fete tonight!

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: If you're headed out west, take care. The Westersand is not so forgiving as the Estersand. I wouldn't be surprised to see some of the creatures lurking out there show up as marks. Keep your guard up, even near the city.

text.Hapless Merchant: Thanks for your help, boy. What for? For delivering that package from my friend, that's what for! Good work with the gates, too. Heh. Say, if you're heading back out into the desert, there's a camp not far from here. If you need a safe place to rest, you'd do well to stop by.

text.Rabanastran (woman in white speaking wit: That sure was lucky, getting in just in time to see the parade. I'll have to thank that nice old bangaa if I get the chance. Now if I can just find a way to go to the fete tonight ... There must be some way to sneak inside.

text.ACTION: For dialogue with Gurdy, see "Side Quests - Random Switch-Ups and Curiosities".

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, pink, and gr: Good for you, standing up to the Imperials the way you did! It's about time someone gave them what for! So, you have business outside the city today? There are dangers abroad. You might consider hiring a chocobo.

text.Erstwhile Adventurer: See those chocobos just over there? I wanted to hire one, but that floatin' moogle runnin' the stables wouldnae hear of it. Says, "Someone of your proportions may do better afoot, kupo." Aye, I've got a foot for that kupo, an' don't you doubt it.

I'm sure they'd let you ride on o' their precious chocobos. Hmph. Well, if ye do hire one, here's some friendly advice: A chocobo can sprint every now and again, but they'll soon tire. And they'll not let ye ride 'em long, so be sure to make the most o' yer time.

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa SG): A pity all the city's gates don't have their own passage down to Lowtown, don't you think?

text.Imperial: What, never seen a guard standing watch over a gate crystal before, boy? Very powerful, these. One touch can make you feel like new. And if you're fortunate enough to have a teleport stone, you can even teleport to any other gate crystal you've ever been to.

text.Weather Eye: I was headed to Giza Plains to take a look at those dark crystals they have ... all fine and good, until a group of monsters decided to take a look at me! Lucky that nomad village down south is as close as it is. I ducked in there and just barely managed to give those monsters the slip.

text.Chocobo Aficionado: If you go for a chocobo ride, just remember not to get yourself carried away. Can't ride forever ... Be careful, or you'll end up walking home. And don't forget that a chocobo can't just sprint all the live long day. Gotta pace the poor things. Do right by your chocobo, it'll do right by you!

text.Rabanastran (man in blue speaking to gro: Heading out into Giza Plains? Be sure you go prepared!

text.Reluctant Adventurer: A group of travelers headin' back to Archades by way of the aerodrome kept glancin' over at me ... as though they'd never seen a bangaa! Bah! Sure, I'd heard the Empire wasn't known for its tolerance of others, but hearin's one thing, and feelin' it first hand another!

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: Times I wish I could just ride off on a chocobo and never come back. Too bad the poor things tire so easily, eh?

text.Imperial: Archadian citizens and their guests only inside the aerodrome today. Sorry, but I'll have to ask you to leave.

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with group): They've closed the aerodrome today to all but Archadian citizens returning home. Does it bother me? Ha! After two years of this treatment, I've grown more than accustomed to it.

text.Adventurer: The Dalmasca Westersand can be harsh, boy. Get a good sandstorm stirred up, you can't hardly see your hand in front of your face! What's worse, elementals favor the storms, and you don't wanna tangle with one of those. So be sure to mind the weather 'fore headin' out.

text.Unlucky Merchant: That's my chocobo just over there. Has a fondness for shiny things – buries everything it can get its beak on. The most recent victim? All the gil I made in Rabanastre! At least they've opened up the road to the Nebra. I've lost profits to make up.

text.Wise Elder: This is just a nameless outpost on the road between Rabanastre and Nalbina. Whichever you're headed for, you've not far to go, m'boy.

text.Dantro: Now that the ceremony for the new consul's over, they've finally opened up the road to the Nebra. The village still hasn't sent out my replacement, though. How long do they expect me to stand watch here, anyway?

text.Desert Wayfarer (woman sitting on crate): The Imperials have lifted the blockade on the road, but the sun, I think it's gotten to my father. We may need to rest here a while. Chocobos don't come cheap, and with all these delays ... I hope he can afford it.

text.Arryl: I better get back to the village before they start worrying. Long as we stick together, we'll be okay. Him? Don't worry about him. He won't bite or nothin'. He's practically family!

text.Village Elder: Good day to you, traveler. We've little to offer aside from the river herself. You're welcome to rest along her banks, as you like.

text.Villager (old man stooping in shade besi: What's keeping the menfolk on the north bank, eh? I can't stand watch on my own here forever. What if brigands made for the village? We wouldn't stand a chance!

text.Cartographers' Guild: Wouldn't do for a member of the guild to get lost, would it, kupo. But it's easy to lose one's way in the desert ... a map is a must, kupo! Would you like to buy a map, kupo?

text.ACTION: Select a map to purchase.
Dalmasca Estersand 50
Cancel

text.Villager (woman in green, pink, and tan: My husband's been gone to the north bank for three days, and I've not heard word from him. Would it kill him to send a message?

text.Villager (old man sitting near fire): Our village straddles the River Nebra. We offer desert travelers passage across, but for a small fee. The ferry has crossed to the north shore. I worry it is too long gone, but there's little for us to do but wait.

text.Villager (woman in pink, blue, and red s: Arryl and Nathyl couldn't be truer friends. That wolf is like a brother to him. They run around playing from dawn to dusk.

text.Villager (woman standing at door of far: Shh! Quiet. We've a sick traveler sleeping just inside – collapsed not far from the village. Quite ill, quite ill. I've tried everything to bring the fever down, but nothing's worked.

text.Unlucky Merchant: That's my chocobo just over there. Has a fondness for shiny things – buries everything it can get its beak on. The most recent victim? All the gil I made in Rabanastre! Down on my luck, you might say. Buy somethin' and help me out. Whaddaya say?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Unlucky Merchant: How much longer we gonna have to wait for the ferry to start running again?

text.Tchigri: Sorry, the ferry's not runnin' right now. My dad took the boat across to the north bank, but he hasn't come back. What's takin' so long?

text.Ada: The Nebra is one of the greatest rivers in Dalmasca. She carries strange gifts, for those with eyes to look. Discarded trinkets, lost coin purses ... even messages in bottles have I found on my daily walks of her banks.

text.Portentous Provisions: I work to earn money to buy my daughter medicine. Please, buy something.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Imperial: Imperial army's engaged in a sweep of the Mosphoran Highwaste. No civilians allowed. You'll have to turn back.

text.Nalbinite: Many of our young men died defending their homeland in the war two years ago. Right here at Nalbina Fortress, they were slain. ... So too the King and Lord Rasler. Yet now this place is a base for the Archadian armies. They have gathered labor to fortify the town in preparation for Rozarrian attack.

text.Itinerant Hand (light blue seeq sitting: Come to help fortify the fortress? The wages aren't bad, aye, but it's hard work. 'Specially for someone as slim as yourself. Still they come. I've been working here since the beginning, so I've seen 'em all.

text.Merchant (Jajim Bazaar): We first opened shop in Nabudis ... And lost all but our lives when the Empire turned our home to dust. Good thing we'd the sense to evacuate! Me and my bangaa associate, he managed to get the shop open again. Now we do good business, selling to the Empire!

text.ACTION: (Magickery Banner (sign)) -Moved here from the lost city of Nabudis. Magicks you'll find nowhere else!

Mysterious Magicks: Come one, come all! Magicks straight from the lost city of Nabudis! I've got the connections that make lesser magickers green, no magick necessary! Take a look at my wares! They speak for themselves!
shop menu

text.Itinerant Hand (black bangaa with tattoo: Fun to check out the stalls between jobs. Peddlers making all sorts of outlandish claims. "My simples would cure Emperor Gramis himself!"

text.Itinerant Hand (man slouching on the gro: Say, you know of the baknamy? A violent, greedy lot, them. I hear they've made the Nabreus Deadlands their territory. That deathland is a fitting place for their ilk.

text.ACTION: (Technickery Banner (sign)) -I said my technicks were good. I never said they were safe. Interested? Take a look.

text.Troublesome Technicks: Eh heh heh ... I got lots o' things here ... none of which I'm at leave to talk about in public, if you know what I mean. Eh heh heh ... No?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Itinerant Hand (man speaking to woman in: It's tough work, under tough eyes. Pah. Food and break time's all I have to look forward to.

text.Nalbinite (bangaa): They say a horrible creature that lost a war with the gods lurks even now in the Mosphoran Highwaste. 'Tis a local legend.

text.ACTION: (Gambitry Banner (sign)) -Takes a little getting used to, but once you've tried these gambits, you'll never look back!

text.Morning Star Gambits: Say there, you know 'bout gambits? Well, see, they're like ... well, they're here. Take a look. ... Sorry, I'd best brush up on my wares 'fore I cry them. Come back later and I'll give it another try, eh?

text.Itinerant Hand (man walking between stal: You heard of the Barheim Passage? Legend says you can hear the eerie cry of a woman from the depths of that accursed place. Boss Burrogh knew this and still he went, that crazy bangaa ... He's down there now, scavenging for junk to restore and sell.

text.Imperial (pacing around near entrance): I've heard rumors of the creatures that lurk in the lands about Nalbina. Children's' tales, compared to the legendary fiends of Archadia! For instance, did you know that a great palace lies buried deep within the earth to the south of the capital? Well, within that palace ... ... there sleeps a terrible wyrm! Frightening, isn't it? And if it really exists ... there's a fight best avoided. Let sleeping wyrms lie, as they say!

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him before he flops onto the ground

CHOICE.Jovy: I-I'm a new recruit here, so I gotta work hard, or, or else they won't (snort) feed me! Bu hweeeeeeee!

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him lying on the ground

CHOICE.Jovy: (snort squeal sniff) M-my hero, he's g-gone ... Bu hweeeeeeeee!

text.Imperial (interrogating man off to the s: You report any shops you see selling stolen goods, son. ... I didn't join the army for this bloody drudgery. What happened to glory? I'm part of Lord Vayne's Western Armada, here to protect the homeland from the reaching arms of Rozarria, and I'm patrolling street stalls! Should've taken that Rabanastre posting when I had the chance ...

text.Sharp-eyed Man: Hold, there! No further, boy. Leave the sweating to the stonemasons, eh?

text.ACTION: (Armorer Banner (sign)) -The oldest shop of its kind in Nalbina! Offering you protectives with the best service tradition and experience can offer!

text.Antiqued Armors: Longest serving merchant in Nalbina, right here! Loved for years, and business's never been better! Take a look!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Imperial (pacing around near entrance): Headed for the aerodrome? Begging your pardon, but we're expecting a fleet arrival today. No civilian use of the facility allowed.

text.ACTION: (Smithery Banner (sign)) -Come and see our most impressive range of hand-picked, top-quality weapons!
Weapons of War: The Imperials have taken a liking to our shop. Business is great! Care for a weapon or two?
shop menu

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him by himself

CHOICE.Stonemason? (hume): We didn't come here as no stonemasons. We came to rescue one of our friends stuck in the dungeons! But ... my stupid seeq buddy got mistaken for a worker ... and here we are.

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him by himself

CHOICE.Stonemason? (seeq): A friend of mine's kept in the dungeons here, so me and my buddy came to help him ... 'Cept my buddy looked so needy, they thought he was a stonemason and put him to work! Now what do I do?

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him walking with his buddy

CHOICE.Stonemason? (hume): Listen here, swinesnout, it's your stupid fault we got mistaken for stonemasons. And no, it's not making us better people, okay? Gah!

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him walking with his buddy

CHOICE.Stonemason? (seeq): Hmph. We got mistaken for stonemasons on account of my buddy's grim appearance, that's why. Now we gotta work out here ...

text.Imperial?: I was complaining to that fellow over there about how rough I had it, and he gave me this suit of armor to put on ... It's hot, it's heavy, people are yelling at me ... All right, I get it, I get it! It's tough being an Imperial. Now can I please take this off?

text.Box Merchant: What? Don't know what kind of shop I'm running? Well ... truth be told, I'm a little unclear on that myself. I sell ... boxes? Yeah. Boxes. I pick up boxes no one needs, and I sell 'em. What? It's a living. (snort)

text.Nutsy: I'm just a traveling moogle, trying to scrape by. I should be here while the Dry holds, kupo. But the monsters during the Rains are too scary! The Dry should last a while longer, but take care during the Rains, kupo. Those big lightning balls don't mess around. Would you like to buy a map, kupo?

text.ACTION: Select a map to purchase.
Giza Plains 30
Cancel

text.Tott: Hey there. We don't see many travelers through here. If there's somethin' you're lookin' for, you should talk to our elder. She's over by the tent.

text.Arjie: Well, hello! The wary traveler never passes the chance to restock his supplies.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Arjie: The children still work, even in this heat. I guess I should try to follow their example.

text.Camina: I'm in charge of seeing all the herbs and roots we gather in the plain are properly dried and stored. We use charms made from the herbs to keep the monsters away while we're out. Used a whole lot during the Rains, so we need t' pick more!

text.Roaklo: Sorry, but could you come back later? Gotta finish work, or I can't play!

text.Nanau: You've come from the city? Our village may be small, but you are welcome here. Our village moves with the seasons. When the Rains come, Giza fills with water, so we cannot stay.

text.Masyua: Have you come to see the dark crystals? Not everyone takes well to the heat of the Giza Plains. We don't have much to offer, but you're welcome to rest here, if you like. These dark crystals absorb the light of the sun, until they shine with a brilliant light. People are always surprised just how bright they are.

text.Jinn: Most of us out here work at makin' sunstones or raisin' cockatrices. We won't get much work done once the Rains come. Gotta make the best of the Dry now!

text.Lesina: The men are off on their business, while we women mind the village. Even the children do their part. They make their mistakes, of course, but they learn from them!

text.Terra: I heard wild cockatrices can roll real fast. But these ones don't roll around at all ... You think they're just lazy?

text.Dania: Don't worry, they won't bite! These cockatrices are as tame as can be. Aren't they just the fluffiest, cutest things you've ever seen?

text.ACTION: (It stares at you with beady eyes ... )
(It looks like it wants to tell you something. Then again, maybe not.)
(It doesn't shy at your approach. It seems tame.)
(It looks like it has an itch on its back.)
(It looks like it wants to be left alone.)
(It looks hungry.)

text.Elder Brunoa: It can get quite hot here in Giza, but it's not all that bad if you can find a nice spot in the shade. Take care before heading out to the plains. Our children don't leave without making the proper preparations. Neither should you.
Don't go out to the plains unprepared. Speak with Arjie before you go if there's anything you need.

text.Filo: Arr, Vaan! Did ya go see the parade? Me? Are you kidding? Won't ever become a sky pirate watchin' parades. Gotta keep trainin'!
Today we're trainin' to hunt treasure! I'm gonna hide, and you have to find me. I'll be somewhere down in the South Sprawl. Hop to it, mateys! Last one to find me's a buckethead!

text.Deadbeat: Lowtown ... yeah, I like Lowtown. You got your North Sprawl in the north, and ... what was down south? Oh, right, the South Sprawl. That Old Dalan down there is somethin' else. Get him talkin', there's no tellin' when he'll stop.

text.ACTION: Private Residence: The door is tightly shut.

text.Rabanastran (woman in white): See that house on the corner? Well ... it's empty now. You see, the man who'd been living there recently passed away. He had fled from Nabudis during the war, the poor dear. If I'm not mistaken, that seeq laughing in the shop just across the way was his landlord.

text.Demented Merchant: You've come to make a purchase ... yes? Oh, my apologies. My store has no ware fit for children, I'm afraid.

text.Impoverished Man: Back before the war, I led a fine life up in the city. But I refused to bow my head to the Imperials, so they took everything I had and forced me to live here in Lowtown.

text.Milha: My husband died protecting me and my son during the war. I'm only glad that I survived. Not for myself, but for our child. No one should have to grow up alone in a world like this.

text.Rabanastran (man sitting against wall ac: Migelo keeps all the provisions for his shop over there in Storehouse 5. You shouldn't be pokin' around in there. It's locked for a reason, y'know.

text.Fussbudget: No fair! No fair doesn't even – Aww! She got tossed into the air at the parade! I wanna be tossed in the air too!

text.ACTION: Storehouse No. 5: The door is locked.

text.Kytes: Hey, Vaan. You need inside again?

CHOICE.ACTION: You're let in to the Garamsythe Waterway.

text.Kytes: If you say so.

Hey, Vaan. You here for some more rat hunting? The door's open and ready to go. I still can't get that door on the left open, though. Old Dalan said it led someplace really important ... can't wait to see what's inside!

text.Traveling Merchant (North Sprawl): Business's been mighty slow. Help me out and buy somethin', would ya?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Dalmascan Patriot: A new Imperial Consul? What difference does it make? I don't care if they send the Emperor himself, Rabanastre belongs to Dalmasca.

text.Cynical Boy: "City's off limits till further notice!" That's all they said before lockin' us down here. No explanation, nothin'. Little while ago I heard it was 'cause there was a parade for some important person from the Empire. What did they think we'd try to do?

text.Rabanastran (seeq sitting next to boy): Breaks me heart, all these poor orphans. It's a hard life for them. Try 'n' keep it under your hat, but there's a band o' folks workin' to free Dalmasca right here in Lowtown. Still, if it means war, I'll pass.

text.Careful Listener: The grown-ups told me all about how come we have to live underground. You wanna hear?

CHOICE.Careful Listener: They told me we all used to live above ground. My house was up there, too! But I don't remember. But then there was that war against the Empire two years ago, and Dalmasca lost. So that made us be under control of the Empire, too. Then when the Imperials come to Rabanastre, they ordered everybody to move down here. The Imperials let us do what we want, I guess, they just won't let us live where we want. Something about keepin' their control on us. You wanna hear the rest?

But it's not totally impossible to live up in the city, even for us Dalmascans. It just takes a whole lotta money. Way more than I got ... It's not all bad in Lowtown, though. At least there aren't any Imperials down here. Hmm ... maybe they stay out just so we'll think it's better down here than it is. I mean, if somethin' happens, it's a lot easier for them to round us all up if we're already rounded up. It makes sense, doesn't it? The grown-ups say I'm just bein' pair annoyed, whatever that means. Sorry for talkin' so much. I done listened to everybody to learn all that!

text.ACTION: end conversation

text.Careful Listener: Aww, and I done did my best listenin' ever to find all that out. Oh well, maybe next time.

text.Laughing Seeq: What's so funny? Oh, I was just thinkin' back on the Consul's speech, see. So many sweet words, I'm like to get a toothache. (snort) Hah!

text.Demented Merchant: Come in! Come in! I've many fine blades on display. Forged each and every one m'self! Look them over ... but they're not for sale!

text.Kindly Girl: The South Sprawl is at the bottom of the map, and the North Sprawl is at the top. That's how maps always are, y'know.

text.Watchful Seeq: This poor fellow here lost his son in the war. He's built up so much hatred over the years, not tellin' what he might do.

text.Furious Bangaa: Fie and pah! Blast those Imperials! Headin' up to the city, I was – the right of any proper Dalmascan – when ... SLAM! Gates shut in my face! I can't fathom what it is they expected us to do had we gotten up there ... Must be hidin' away the rubbish lest we offend the good Consul's nose.

text.Wandering Woman: Excuse me, do you think you could tell me where Old Dalan's house is? Of course, the South Sprawl. I never have a map when I need one. Just keep heading down this passage, right?

text.Water-watcher: Didya know this water all comes from a biiig river in the Dalmasca Estersand? It runs right through Lowtown on down into the sewers. I heard there are ghosts livin' down in those sewers, too – waaay deep inside in real hard-to-get-to places.

text.Vexed Father: I got stuck up in the city when the Imperials sealed off Lowtown. Which would be fine, if it hadn't meant my daughter missing the parade. She's been throwin' a fit, goin' on about how it's not fair I got to see it but she didn't . She's got to understand, we have to do what the Imperials say.

text.Rabanastran (tan seeq wandering open eas: Wasn't easy convertin' Lowtown into someplace livable. (snort) I remember when it was nothin' more than a maze of storehouses. Just look at these hangin' rugs, for example. May not be much, but they help make the place a little more homey.

text.Well-spoken Boy: Grown-ups never cease to amaze me. When we first moved down to Lowtown, they said they couldn't live in such a place. Now they pay it no mind. I don't know if they're just being brave, or strong ... Or maybe they've just given up.

text.Angry Woman: Angry? Of course I'm angry. Isn't it obvious? Living down here the past two years, watched by guards whenever I go to the city ... Sure, they let you move up there if you have the gil for it, but who has that kinda coin? I'm not sure how much more of this I can stand.

text.Demented Merchant: Time was, I had a shop up in the city. Look what they've driven me to. Breaks my heart to think about it.

text.Layabout (South Sprawl): Yeah, I'm takin' my time, but I'm almost there anyway. Filo's just up ahead. I'll win easy.
I'm tired of training. I hate lettin' Filo down, but I don't really care about winning anyway. So I'll just wait here until I lose ... But what if everyone decides to give up?

text.Guileless Girl: Sometimes I play down in the alley in front of Old Dalan's, but I ain't supposed to go up to Southgate. Nope.

text.Guileful Boy: I don't care how great they say this new consul is. They can't fool me. I ain't gonna sit back while they turn us into the Empire!

text.Resigned Boy: If the Empire's protecting us now, how come we had to fight them before? It doesn't make any sense to me.

text.Frustrated Man: Been thinkin' of headin' up to Nalbina, try and find a new job with the reconstruction. The pay's good, but it's hard work.

text.Somber Woman: My daughter won't talk to me 'less we come to some out-of-the-way place like this. Says it's not right to the kids what lost their moms. Did the Empire invade so we would be forced to live like this?

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: The shops around here have had trouble keeping goods stocked since the war. These days, the only merchant with much of anything is over in the courtyard.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, blue and gre: The children just love listening to Old Dalan's stories. You can practically follow the sound of their laughter to his doorstep.

text.Rabanastran (man in blue and green sitti: (sigh) No money, no job ... I'm bored to tears.

text.Traveling Merchant (South Sprawl): Ain't hardly sold nothin' today. Can't expect the likes of these to put up hard gil, though. Ah well, go on, have a look.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Samal: Fighting against the Empire is all well and good, but it's not enough. You've got to find something more to live for. A dream to follow. I don't know what kind of world he'll grow up in, but so long as there are people who follow their dreams, it can't be all that bad.

text.Awestruck Girl: See that man squattin' down talkin' over there? They say he used to be a sky pirate! Don't know if he was a for-real one or a for-fake one, though.

text.Friendly Boy: I feel sorry for that guy sellin' stuff in the courtyard. No one ever buys from him. I won't let that happen to me. I'm gonna be rich!

text.Ex-Adventurer: You ever find yourself down in the sewers, watch yourself, boy. They're crawlin' with creatures. You especially want to watch out for elementals. Don't linger in any one place too long and you should be able to avoid 'em.

text.Resolute Boy: Who do these Imperials think they are, keepin' us from goin' where we wanna? Ya know whose fault all this is? That Basch, that's who! Dirty traitor ...

text.Well-spoken Girl: Do you think dreams really can come true? Or are they just a way for us to escape our troubles? The other day this scary-looking man told me we'd be taking our kingdom back soon. If that's really true, then maybe it's okay for me to dream, too.

text.Rabanastran (man in green, red, and blue: You ever wish there were more ways to get up to the city? Sometimes I feel claustrophobic down here.

text.Patient Boy: Vaan, is that you? Can't remember the last time I saw you down here to visit Old Dalan.

text.Filo: Arr, Vaan! Here to see Old Dalan? I'm just waitin' for my friends – er, mates – to show up. What's takin' them so long?

text.Jolly Seeq: Old Dalan was tellin' me how this place was once a great storehouse. That explains the passage up to Southgate. Back when they were movin' freight and caravans from Giza Plains through Southgate they must have needed doors this large to pass through. Pity this is the only one that still works.

text.Old Dalan: Ahh, if it isn't Vaan Ratsbane. Come for a tip on how to skewer something bigger and in armor? By the east gate?

text.Vaan: What, you already heard about that?

text.Old Dalan: Wise I may not be, but well-informed I am.

text.Vaan: They'll get what's coming to them someday, believe me. But that's not why I'm here.

text.Old Dalan: Do tell!

text.Vaan: I want to know how to sneak into the palace. They've got to have some great stuff in there! Thought I'd partake.

text.Old Dalan: Not one to mince words, are you, boy. The Empire protects what's hers. That means the palace and all the treasures inside.

text.Vaan: That's why I'm gonna do it! To take back what's ours!

text.Old Dalan: So our champion of the sewers aspires to noble action. Admirable. Perhaps I can help you. Ah, now that I think on it, there was a rumor, yes. A secret passageway into the palace vaults, a door, and a magicked stone to open the way.

text.Vaan: That's it! This is exactly why I came to talk to you first, Dalan. So ... where's this, uh, magicked stone?

text.Old Dalan: Eh? Oh, I've had it for years. If I can remember where I've tucked it away ...

text.Vaan: I've heard all I need. So this, uh, Crescent Stone. Can I have it? Then I can find that secret passage into the palace, right?

text.Old Dalan: Not much of a listener, are you ... The Crescent Stone has lost its magicks. Without the power of a sunstone, it will be of little use.

text.Vaan: Right. So where can I get one of these sunstones?

text.Old Dalan: You seek Giza Plains. Speak with the nomads there. You will find your sunstone. Leave by Southgate and continue south. Their village is not far. There are like to be beasts on the plains, so be careful, m'boy.

text.Vaan: You don't have to worry about me. I'll be back before you know it.

text.Old Dalan: I need that sunstone, Vaan. You should start by talking to the nomads on the Giza Plains. If you leave by Southgate, their village is not far.

text.Rabanastran (woman at left): You may want to talk with the moogle from the Cartographers' Guild in the Southern Plaza before you leave for Giza. It can't hurt to have a map.

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): You goin' to Giza Plains? Be careful!

text.Vaan: Let's see, Giza Plains ... Hang a right here, and I'm practically at Southgate. This'll be easy.

text.Filo: Arr, Vaan! Welcome to the Buccaneer's Brigade! Come to tell us more stories about bein' sky pirates? This scurvy bunch would rather hear about bein' sky pirates than train for it. Maybe they need some trainin' on walkin' the plank ...

text.Fidget: Filo's had us trainin' real hard. Bein' a sky pirate's a lot more work than I thought.

text.Layabout (South Sprawl): Bein' a sky pirate? Nothin' to it! You just fly all over the place in your airship. So how come there aren't as many real sky pirates anymore? These days, most of them what say they're sky pirates are just a buncha thieves. Not me. I'm gonna be a real sky pirate! Yarr!

text.Camina: Those two must've gotten into a fight again, no doubt about it. That Jinn ... always getting into trouble!

text.Terra: But this time Roaklo was with them, too. I wonder what's going on?
Roaklo, Tott, and Jinn went out onto the plain, but Jinn still hasn't come back. To tell the truth, I'm a bit worried.

text.Camina: Something's up, but Roaklo and Tott aren't talking. They don't have to, though. It's written all over their faces.

text.Elder Brunoa: You've a troubled look, child. What's the matter? Ah, come from Rabanastre seeking a sunstone, have you? As you might have guessed from the name, sunstones contain the power of the sun. You'll often find them used as a source of heat or light. Here we leave all things sunstone to Masyua. You should be able to find her near the dark crystal. Do you see the large black stone behind my tent? That is a dark crystal. You'll not be able to find them outside Giza Plains. The dark surfaces of the crystal drink in the light of the sun.
You need a sunstone, yes? Best speak with Masyua about that. She should be just behind my tent.

text.Masyua: Have you come to see the dark crystals? Not everyone takes well to the heat of the Giza Plains. ... Ah, so it is a sunstone you seek! You've come to the right place. They can only be made here in Giza. They're quite valuable, though, so we can't go handing them out to just anyone who happens to wander through our camp. You see, we make and sell sunstones to earn the money we need to survive. Still, perhaps we can come to some arrangement ... Would you hear my offer?

CHOICE.Masyua: The making of sunstones is a chore we give to the children of our camp. They roam the plains, traveling from dark crystal to dark crystal, drawing the light from the crystals into shadestones. One of these children, Jinn, has not yet returned. He left carrying our supply of shadestones. If you'll find Jinn for me and tell him to come back to the camp, you may take one of the sunstones he's made in return. Some of the children said they might have seen him to the south of the camp. You may want to speak with them yourself before leaving. Please, find Jinn and tell him to return at once.

CHOICE.ACTION: After this, the next scene in blue will automatically begin.

CHOICE.Masyua: Of course. Our troubles need not concern you.

text.Masyua: Seems you haven't given up on finding a sunstone just yet. But as I said, we do not part with the fruits of our labors lightly. If you are serious, then hear my offer.

CHOICE.Masyua: The making of sunstones is a chore we give to the children of our camp. They roam the plains, traveling from dark crystal to dark crystal, drawing the light from the crystals into shadestones. One of these children, Jinn, has not yet returned. He left carrying our supply of shadestones. If you'll find Jinn for me and tell him to come back to the camp, you may take one of the sunstones he's made in return. Some of the children said they might have seen him to the south of the camp. You may want to speak with them yourself before leaving. Please, find Jinn and tell him to return at once.

CHOICE.ACTION: After this, the next scene in blue will automatically begin.

text.Vaan: Penelo? What are you doing here?

text.Penelo: I could ask you the same! Though the answer's pretty clear: no good.

text.Vaan: What? I'm being good.

text.Penelo: Hmm. Is that right? So, then, you wouldn't mind if I, say, tagged along, would you? Oh, don't worry. Migelo's busy with preparations for the fete up at the palace. Why, I'm free for the whole day. Well? Let's get going!

text.ACTION: Penelo joins the party!

text.Camina: Guess what! I saw Jinn off in the south part of the plains – in the Crystal Glade. He was right by a small crystal. I asked if he wanted to come back to camp with me, but he said he still had some work to finish up. The Crystal Glade is to the south of our village. Just head out into Giza Plains and wind your way south. We take breaks in the glade, since monsters seem to stay away from it. I was a little worried because Jinn looked like he might have been hurt, but I was afraid to push him too hard to come back. Now I'm wondering if I did the right thing.

I saw Jinn in the Crystal Glade. We take breaks in the glade sometimes, since monsters seem to stay away from it. The Crystal Glade is to the south of our village. Just head out into Giza Plains and wind your way south.

text.Tott: We all went out to make some sunstones, but Jinn still hasn't come back to camp. It's the first time he's been out on the plains since the end of the Rains. Maybe he got a touch of wanderlust.

text.Roaklo: Jinn still isn't back? Masyua's gonna let us have it for sure. I knew he shouldn't have – nothing. Never mind. Well, ya see, Jinn and Tott kinda got in a fight. Then while they were busy fighting, a werewolf came along and ... I hope he's okay.

text.Masyua: Please, find Jinn and tell him to return to camp. One of the children, Camina, saw him. You should speak with her before leaving. And be careful – werewolves stalk the southern plains. If you see one approaching, run. It would make short work of you.

text.Terra: Sure, I know Jinn. Brunoa was complimenting the sunstones he made, and I think it made Tott jealous. I just don't get it. Why can't they just get along with each other?

text.Penelo: Hey, Vaan. Let me give you these before we go. There are all sorts of monsters out there, so you can never be too careful!

text.ACTION: You obtain 3 Potions!
You obtain 2 tufts of Phoenix Down!

text.Penelo: So far you've been traveling by yourself, but now that I'm here we can travel as a party. You can give commands to allies in your party just like you've been doing for yourself up to now. I'll make my own decisions about what to do, too, but you can also give me specific commands and I'll take care of those first. Got it?

text.ACTION: You can now change leaders and issue party commands!

text.Penelo: Oh, one more thing! If you don't want me to fight on my own, you can always turn my gambits off. With my gambits turned off, I won't do anything until you give the word. You should really think about using gambits for yourself, you know. They can make managing a battle a lot easier.

text.ACTION: Gambits has been added to the battle menu.

text.Penelo: Well, you ready to go?

text.ACTION: When you exit by either the east or west ways ...

text.Penelo: Vaan, wasn't Jinn supposed to be somewhere to the south of the village? If we work our way around, we should find him!

text.Jinn: Yeah, my name's Jinn ... What's it to ya? Masyua wants me to come back to the village, huh? Hmm, that could be a problem. Let's see ... maybe my leg's better now. Nope, no good – still hurts. I tripped running from some monsters ... guess I pulled something. I'm never gonna get any sunstones made like this. I just needed to make one more to be finished for today. I didn't want to head back short, so I thought I'd give my leg a rest and try again. Why are you out here looking for me, anyhow?

CHOICE.Jinn: So you need a sunstone, huh? Well, if Masyua doesn't mind, I'll give you a shadestone. But I'm still not sure I can walk yet – you'll have to turn it into a sunstone, okay? Don't worry, I'll tell you how. You do know that we use dark crystals and shadestones to make sunstones, right?

There's your shadestone. As for the dark crystals, you'll find them all over Giza Plains. This stone right here beside me is one of the smaller ones. The bigger crystals have something inside that soaks up sunlight and shines really bright.
See that one over there? If you take that shadestone I just gave you and bring it near one of those shining dark crystals, it will absorb the energy from it.

There are four shining dark crystals in Giza right now. If you have trouble finding 'em, just stop and scan the horizon. There's no way to tell how much energy you can draw from any one crystal without trying. You shouldn't need to use all four, though.

This gauge will show you how much energy the shadestone's absorbed. When it's full, you'll have yourself a sunstone! Once you've made the sunstone, bring it to me. I'll make sure it's up to snuff. I'll go ahead and mark the dark crystals on your map, too. See you back here when you're done!
If I go back without all my sunstones, everyone's going to make fun of me. But this leg won't be getting better in a hurry ...

text.Jinn: I know, I know. They want me to go back to the village. But I'm not heading back until I'm done here. And my leg still hurts, besides. How come you're so interested?

CHOICE.Jinn: So you need a sunstone, huh? Well, if Masyua doesn't mind, I'll give you a shadestone. But I'm still not sure I can walk yet – you'll have to turn it into a sunstone, okay? Don't worry, I'll tell you how. You do know that we use dark crystals and shadestones to make sunstones, right?

If I go back without all my sunstones, everyone's going to make fun of me. But this leg won't be getting better in a hurry ...

text.Jinn: Be careful about wandering too far south. There are werewolves down there, and you don't wanna mess with them. That's how – Well, it's a long story. The important thing is that you remember how to make the sunstone. Take the shadestone I gave you and put it near the shining crystals. As soon as the energy gauge is full, the sunstone'll be ready! I already marked down all the dark crystals on your map. When you've made the sunstone, bring it here and I'll take a look at it.
As soon as the gauge is full, the sunstone'll be ready! I'll be waiting right here for ya. And watch out for those werewolves to the south!

text.LOCATION: Toam Hills, Starfall Fields, Warrior's Wash, Giza's North Bank

text.ACTION: Dark Crystal: The dark crystal radiates a brilliant light.
Hold the shadestone up to the crystal.
The shadestone will absorb some amount of energy from the crystal.
Do nothing.
After the second time absorbing light from the dark crystal ...

text.Vaan: Not bad. Maybe this won't take so long after all.

text.Penelo: So this is what the kids on Giza Plains do to make their way ... Maybe one of them will take you on as an apprentice.

text.Vaan: Yeah, yeah. Let's just find the next crystal, okay?

text.ACTION: After the gauge reaches 100%...

text.Vaan: That's that. Nothing to it!

text.Penelo: Let's take it back to Jinn and see what he says. I hope we did it right.

text.Vaan: Sure, let's go.

text.ACTION: You obtain a sunstone!
Now, you'll automatically go back to the Crystal Glade.

text.Jinn: Hey, you've got a sunstone! Let's take a look. Hmm, seems okay to me. Not bad for city folk. So here's what happened. Masyua's always warning us to stay away from the werewolves, right? Well, a bunch of us decided we'd have a little contest – see who's the bravest. It started out as a lark, but Tott said that none of us kids living on the plains should be scared of monsters ... I guess I got carried away. Don't let any of the grown-ups know, though, okay?
Anyway ... my leg's feeling better now. Let's head back to the village. I'll race ya – try and keep up!

text.ACTION: The scene will automatically change back to the Nomad Village.

text.Masyua: Jinn made it back home safe and sound. He is a good boy, but how his mind wanders! He never thinks of the worry it causes me! I'm sorry if he was any trouble. Please, take these with my thanks.

text.ACTION: You obtain 50 gil!

text.Masyua: Jinn gave you a sunstone, yes? I hope it may be of some help to you.

Has the sunstone been of use? Jinn makes very high quality stones – they always fetch a good price. You're fortunate you came when you did: the crystals do not always shine. Many have come seeking sunstones only to leave empty-handed.
There is much work to be had on the plains. When light returns to the crystals, you might try your hand at making sunstones.

text.Jinn: I expected Masyua to get a little upset, but it seems like I really worried her. She was even madder than I thought she'd be. She just stood there, all quiet. Really had me scared! Heh.

text.Elder Brunoa: I'm glad to see you were able to find a sunstone for yourself. Heading back to Rabanastre soon, then? Come visit us whenever you like. We will be here until the coming of the Rains.

text.Terra: Jinn isn't originally from here, you know. Brunoa brought him from Rabanastre. She says he's another orphan of the war. But here we're all treated the same, so what difference should it make? Maybe it still bothers him. Or maybe it bothers me ...

text.Camina: Can you believe it? Tott and Roaklo left Jinn to fend off that werewolf by himself! Those little – they're such ... cowards!

text.Tott: Worried? About Jinn? Not me. Nobody knows Giza Plains better than we do. Gotta make these sunstones fast, and they gotta be good, too. That's what Masyua says. I guess she knows what she's talkin' about.

text.Roaklo: Jinn and Tott started fighting near one of the crystals. We were all caught up with the fight, and that's when the werewolf came. We got split up while we were trying to get away ... Shoulda been more careful, I know. Now I have my sister mad at me, and Masyua, too! I think they're going a bit too hard on me.

text.ACTION: Approaching Dalan's place triggers a brief scene ...

text.Penelo: Hey Vaan?

text.ACTION: Vaan turns to Penelo behind him.

text.Penelo: It's been a long time since we did anything together. Too long. I had a really good time. Well, I should probably get back to the store. Actually, I was kind of supposed to be watching the place for Migelo. And, Vaan – Try to stay out of trouble. For me? I don't know what I'd do if you weren't here. If something happened to you.

text.Vaan: I'm not going anywhere. Okay?

text.Penelo: That's what I wanted to hear. See ya later.

text.ACTION: after she leaves

text.Vaan: Sorry, Penelo.

text.ACTION: Penelo leaves the party.

text.Rabanastran (woman at left): You get the sunstone for Dalan? I imagine that wasn't easy to come by. Sunstones, gate crystals, skystones ... there's magicite all around us, if you stop to think about it.

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): Dalan found that rock he was lookin' for. For some old rock, he sure was happy about it.

text.Old Dalan: Oh ho! So you've got a sunstone, have you? Hand it over, m'boy, and I'll use it to give the Crescent Stone back its magicks like I promised.

Now you'll be wanting to know how to sneak into the palace, eh? First you go to Storehouse 5. You know the one. Two doors she has. Now the right takes Vaan Ratsbane to his territorial hunting grounds in the sewerbottom ... But that's not the way you'll go. No, you'll take the left door, down into the Garamsythe Waterway. The waterway leads to a stair, the stair to the palace cellars. That's your way in. But don't go counting your gil just yet, m'boy. Getting into the palace was the easy part. The way into the treasury is carefully hidden. That's where this Crescent Stone comes in. The magicks it bears can open the hidden door to the treasury, you see. Listen, Vaan, for the words I shall speak are most important, and not to be forgotten. Do you understand? "The signet yearns for sunstone's strength, to light the clouded way." Once in the palace, you'll find the signet tile. Very important. Give to it the sun's power, and it will light your path. Very well. Oh, a warning: be aware that if you're caught ... you'll spend the rest of your short life rotting in the Nalbina dungeons. So, look sharp, m'boy. And don't go running off before you're ready. Plans freshly hatched have a habit of tumbling from the nest ... straight into the hunter's stewpot.

text.ACTION: You obtain the Crescent Stone!

text.Old Dalan: Need to hear the way in once more, do you?

CHOICE.Old Dalan: First you go to Storehouse 5 – you know the one. Two doors she has. The right takes you to your territorial hunting grounds in the sewerbottom, but you'll take the left door, down into the Garamsythe Waterway. Give to it the sun's power, and it will light your path.

CHOICE.Vaan: No, I think I've got it.

CHOICE.Old Dalan: Be careful, m'boy. Go getting yourself in trouble, and the ones who care about you also suffer. Think of that before you do anything rash.

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): Don't tell me you don't know where Storehouse 5 is? Over in the North Sprawl? Kytes is always up to something in there.

text.ACTION: Leaving Dalan's place triggers another brief cutscene ...
Beneath Rabanastre – The Garamsythe Waterway
An armored man is approached by other more crudely armed men.

text.Man: Squads 3 through 6 are in place. They stand ready. So far the Imperials haven't noticed a thing.

text.Vossler: Then go now and hurry the others. By nightfall, we must ensure all our men are in place.

text.ACTION: The men give a "sir" and depart, leaving the armored man to turn around to face a young lady in a pink skirt who now emerges from behind a pillar. We don't see her face.

text.Layabout (South Sprawl): Filo's always fussin' at me to be more like Kytes ... Hmph. I say everybody oughta be himself.

text.Fidget: Kytes loves helpin' ya out, Vaan. It's like the closer you are to a sky pirate, the closer he feels to being one too ... or something.

text.Filo: Arr, Vaan! That door what Kytes could never open? He finally figured it out! He come lookin' for ya to let ya know, but since he couldn't find ya, he went back up to the storehouse to wait for ya there.

text.Fussbudget: Hey, Kytes finally got that other door in the storehouse open. I think he's waitin' inside for ya, Vaan.

text.ACTION: When you open the door to Storehouse 5 you see ...

text.Kytes: Hey, Vaan! I finally worked out how to get the door on the left side open! I hope there's somethin' in there besides rats ... I wanted you to go in first, so I waited for you to come before openin' it. Well, that's one of the reasons I waited ... Thing is, I'm gonna need some special tools to open the door ... Gonna need you to go fetch 'em for me. I know, I know. Not the most exciting thing to do, is it? Heh, heh. I'm just messin' with ya. I've got everything I need ready to go! Hang on while I open it ...
Hmm, let's see ... Yeah, that should do it ... Huh?
Ungh. Urgh. Angh! Hrooph!
It's open! Now we've got a whole 'nother place to explore! Oh, and I almost forgot. Take these with ya before you go. No tellin' what's down there ... might come in handy.

text.ACTION: You obtain 2 Potions!
You obtain 4 phials of Eye Drops!

text.Kytes: Don't know what kind of monsters are down there, but nothin' you can't handle, I bet. Let me know what ya find!

text.Fussbudget: So Kytes finally got that door open, huh?

text.Vaan: The palace should be right up these stairs.
Won't be easy getting out. Am I ready for this?

text.ACTION: The Royal Palace of Rabanastre

Nighttime. Fireworks burst over the palace as Imperials patrol the gardens. A hoverbike comes flying in, unnoticed by the guards. The driver, a viera in black armor, brakes to a halt, and a man with gun in hand jumps off with a smirk.

text.Vaan: I've made it this far ... I'm not going back empty-handed.

text.Palace Servant (one of two women chattin: I've not seen you around. Were you hired especially for the fete tonight? Then you should be waiting over by the stairs. Down the corridor to the end.

text.Palace Servant (woman in white, yellow,: They were smart to keep most of the soldiers out of the palace for the fete. Who could eat with all those people in armor standing around?

text.Palace Servant (one of two men chatting: In times past, when the royal house flourished, a court painter gifted two signets to the King: one of a hawk, the other of a lion. While neither became the official seal of our kingdom, the King liked them, and so placed them in the halls of the palace. You can see the actual articles here on the floor above.

text.Palace Servant (man in brown pants & whi: Did you see the parade for the new consul? I had to work! Missed the whole thing ... Come to think of it, I missed the Lady Ashe's wedding parade, too ...

text.Palace Servant (red bangaa chatting with: I hope that fete gets done with quick. There's something I want to see on the upper floor.

text.ACTION: When you approach the other end of the cellar corridor where the Imperials stand before a group of servants ...

text.Imperial: Have you gathered up all of the occasionals? ... Good. You'll be on clean-up duty when the fete's over. Wait here until we're ready for you. No one goes to the upper floor until we give the order. Step out of line and you will be punished.

text.Palace Servant (man in green, red, and b: We'll let you know what to do shortly. Just a little longer, please.

text.Palace Servant (black bangaa in red vest: I'm having myself a little exploration 'round the palace. Lots of interesting things in here ... and guards to make sure I don't take 'em.

text.Palace Servant (woman in blue, yellow an: I thought I'd be able to see Lord Vayne, but they have me on clean-up. Too bad, eh?

text.Palace Servant (man in blue shorts and h: When I told my friend I'd be helping at the fete this morning, she got jealous and spent all afternoon trying to think of a way to sneak in. Hah! As though she even could!

text.ACTION: If you approach the guard at foot of stairs ...

He turns to see the statue of a goddess-like figure, whose face has opened to reveal a hollow space where a glowing stone is hidden. text.Balthier: Quite a performance.

text.Vaan: Who are you?

text.Balthier: I play the leading man, who else?

text.Vaan: No, you won't. I found it. It's mine.

text.Vaan: What's going on?

text.ACTION: Suddenly, an explosive ball of fire touches down nearby. We see a vaguely familiar young woman with sword in hand in the fray, looking up at the newly arrived, massive airship looming overhead. The man reappears behind Vaan, but he's looking up at the airship, too.

text.Balthier: The Ifrit, eh? Impeccable timing. If I didn't know any better, I'd say they were waiting all along.

text.ACTION: Vaan glances at him, then bolts as the Ifrit continues firing on the battle below.

text.Balthier: Stop running!

text.ACTION: As Vaan is being chased by the man, suddenly the viera appears on the hoverbike in front of him, blocking his path.

text.Balthier: End of the line! You have something that belongs to me.

text.ACTION: As they confront each other, Imperials run out on the promenade and spot them.

text.Imperial: More this way!

text.Balthier: Fran! Let's move!

text.ACTION: He begins running toward Vaan and the viera. He grabs Vaan as he is running and carries him to the edge of the promenade, where he pushes him.

text.Balthier: Off with you!

text.ACTION: As, Vaan falls, the man jumps after him. For a moment they are obscured by the smoke of Ifrit's fire. Then we see the man has landed on the back of the hover bike with the viera; he holds Vaan by the wrist, as he dangles precariously below them.

text.Vaan: Let go of me!

text.Balthier: Keep this up and I will!

text.ACTION: The man notices the viera seems to be struggling with the bike.

text.Balthier: What's going on, Fran?

text.Fran: I don't know, it's not heeding me!

text.Balthier: I don't have time for this.

text.Vaan: I – I'm slipping!

text.ACTION: They are obscured by smoke again as the hover bike appears to finally go down.
The scene changes to a dark tunnel, filled with rubble, where the viera kneels beside the apparently ruined hover bike. Vaan and her partner stand behind her.

text.Fran: What happened? Our hover didn't just drop – it disappeared.

text.Balthier: Bah, forget it. Even if we could fly ... the Ifrit's playing with fire, and I'd rather not get burned. We'll go the old-fashioned way.

text.ACTION: The man notices Vaan is staring at the viera.

text.Balthier: Not many viera where you come from, thief

text.Vaan: It's Vaan.

text.ACTION: to the viera

text.Vaan: Sorry.

text.Balthier: Well, Fran is special ... in that she'd deign to partner with a hume.

text.Fran: Oh? Like a sky pirate that chooses to steal through the sewers?

text.Vaan: Pirates? You're sky pirates? So you have an airship?

text.Balthier: It's Balthier. Listen thief – Vaan. If you ever want to see your home again, you'll do exactly as I say. Myself, Fran, and you. We're working together now. Understood?

text.ACTION: Vaan notices Balthier is now eyeing the glowing stone in his hand.

text.Vaan: Don't even think you're going to be getting this.

text.Balthier: The thought never crossed my mind.

text.ACTION: Balthier and Fran join the party!

text.Balthier: Ah, Vaan. There's something I want to check before we set out.
As I thought. You don't know much about gambits yet, do you?

Listen carefully – I don't care to repeat myself. For each gambit, you can combine one action with a target for that action. Example: you can arrange that Cure be cast on an ally whose HP falls below fifty percent. Useful, that. Of course, one error of judgment, and you could well find yourself throwing punches at that same ally. If you've a good head on your shoulders, it should come easily enough. Hmm ... I fear a more detailed explanation is in order.

This is the Gambit Screen. You can reach it from the Party Menu. To create a Gambit, you need only select an action and a target for that action. Here, let me show you. I'll start by changing the action of one of my gambits.

Now whenever an ally gets hurt, I'll toss a potion his way. Charming, eh? Of course, that's a sure way to go through our stock of potions. So let's adjust the target to make sure things don't get out of hand.

Now I'll only ever use potions when an ally's HP drops below seventy percent. That should be a little more bearable. Nothing to it, really. You can set a gambit's action to more or less any ability you have at your disposal.
Targets aren't so simple. You'll have to pick up new ones from gambit shops.
But that isn't all. You can also prioritize your gambits. Allow me.

The gambit in the first slot always takes priority. As it stands now, even if an ally's HP starts to fall, should there be foes near, I'll only attack. For which I could rightly be criticized. In general, it's better to prioritize healing before attacking. Vitality before violence, if you like.

Oh, another thing – you can turn gambits off and on here, from the Gambit Screen, as well as from the Battle Menu. Of course, gambits won't do you much good if they're turned off. Still, discretion is the better part of valor. If you need to beat a hasty retreat, try turning gambits off first. It's hard to fall back when your allies insist on picking a fight.
Well, that's the long and short of it. I'll set my gambits as they were before we started. Feel free to change them later if you like.

We're like to come across new actions and targets, so don't be afraid to experiment with new gambit combinations. But don't put all of your faith in any one combination. With each passing day, the world finds new and exciting ways to kill a man.

Be flexible! If you find yourself up against beasts that don't take well to fire, create a gambit to cast Fire on nearby foes. Likewise, should we face a creature that used Poison, a gambit to cast Poisona on poisoned allies just might come in handy. A bit much to take in? Don't let it worry you – you're in good company. Yes, these sewers are thick with the bones of others who had similar "difficulties".

text.ACTION: Gambits has been added to the Party Menu.
Party has been added to the Party Menu.

text.Balthier: Let's be off then, shall we?

text.ACTION: When you examine the Fallen Soldiers ...

text.Balthier: Insurgents. Most like they thought to take advantage of a lax watch while the fete's on. ... to feed the good consul a length of steel for his supper. I should think Vayne used to such hospitality. Clever. He used himself as the bait to draw them near, and then sent in the air brigade. A fine, bloody banquet. Hmph. I daresay I've soiled my cuffs. If a dungeon's waiting for us at the end of the night, it had best have a change of wardrobe.

text.ACTION: Examine the Fallen Soldiers a second time ...

text.Vaan: I'd take you with us if I could ... but there's just no time. Sorry ...

text.ACTION: An unnamed girl, the same from the earlier scene, is fighting a group of Imperials, who are backing her into a ledge.

text.Imperial: Close ranks! Bring her down!

text.ACTION: running to the base of the ledge

text.Vaan: Jump down!

text.ACTION: The girl considers ...

text.Vaan: Hurry!

text.ACTION: The girl jumps. Vaan catches her. They exchange glances for a moment.

text.Imperial: She's not alone!

text.Fran: Our ranks grow by the hour.

text.Balthier: And our troubles with them.

text.ACTION: After defeating the four Imperials ...

text.Vaan: You all right?
Um, I'm Vaan. And this is Balthier, and –

text.ACTION: notices Balthier and Fran walking away

text.Vaan: Hey!

text.ACTION: turns back to the girl

text.Vaan: What's your name?
Amalia, huh? Nice to meet you.

text.LOCATION: Amalia: There were others with me ...

text.Fran: I'm sorry.

text.ACTION: Suddenly, the Goddess's Magicite in Vaan's hands begins to glow.

text.Vaan: Huh?

text.Balthier: Oh, now, isn't that impressive.

text.Vaan: Don't get any ideas. I said it's mine.

text.Balthier: I'm afraid the jury's still out on that one.

text.Vaan: Yeah!

text.Fran: Have you finished? When the guards don't report in, they'll come looking for us.

text.Balthier: If they aren't already.

text.ACTION: to Amalia

text.Vaan: You should come with us. Better than being by yourself.
What's wrong with her?

text.Balthier: You have a lot to learn before we even get started on your thievery.

text.Vaan: What's that mean?

text.ACTION: Approach Amalia again after the cutscene ...

text.LOCATION: Amalia: The situation requires I accept such help as I find. Though it be from thieves. I shall accompany you until we find my companions. No longer.

text.Balthier: Let's think of her as a "guest", then. Unlike Fran or myself, our "guest" won't be taking orders from anyone anytime soon. And she'll leave when she pleases. So, we keep to our affairs, and she to hers. I doubt we'll find her wanting in valor ... being such an upstanding member of the insurgence.

text.ACTION: Amalia joins the party as a guest!

text.LOCATION: Amalia: Well, what are we waiting for?

text.ACTION: Upon arriving in the central area, three flan emerge from the sewers and corner the party. Feeling a presence, they slowly look up to see a fourth flan on the ceiling above them, which now descends on them.
After defeating the four flan, the party gets the first victory screen in the game, and is then free to move on.
As the group enters the area, steam suddenly begins to rise in great amount from the water. A ball of fire flies in from another part of the waterway, and turns into the Firemane.
After defeating Firemane ...

text.LOCATION: Arrested, and Vaan's Visit with Reks

text.ACTION: The creature turns back into a fireball and shoots down the waterway.

text.Imperial: Stand where you are!

text.ACTION: The party turns to see they have been surrounded by Imperials armed with crossbows. Vayne appears among them, seemingly smugly satisfied having caught them. Amalia looks as if she's about to start something, but Balthier grabs her by the arm.

text.Balthier: Now is not the time.

text.ACTION: Amalia growls, but does nothing. The scene changes to Lowtown, right outside Storehouse 5. The party is now in handcuffs, escorted by Imperials, and Lowtown's citizens are watching and speculating.

text.Random Citizen 1: They're the thieves who stole into the palace.

text.Random Citizen 2: Is that what the commotion was about last night?

text.LOCATION: Amalia: They think me some common thief.

text.ACTION: murmuring, to Amalia

text.Balthier: Better than a common assassin.

text.LOCATION: Amalia: These people have done nothing. Release them.

text.Vaan: What are you doing?

text.LOCATION: Amalia: Don't interrupt me. I'm thinking.

text.Penelo: Wait!

text.ACTION: Vaan turns to see Penelo trying to shove past a bunch of Imperials.

text.Penelo: He didn't know what he was doing! You have to let him go! You have to!

text.Vaan: Penelo!

text.ACTION: she looks up at him

text.Vaan: Sorry. That dinner'll have to wait.

text.Penelo: I told you!

text.Imperial: That's enough!

text.ACTION: cuffs Vaan

text.Penelo: Leave him alone!

text.ACTION: Penelo breaks free of the Imperials and is making a beeline for Vaan. A soldier steps in front of him, hand on his sword ... Then, Balthier steps between the two, facing Penelo with a handkerchief in his hands.

text.Balthier: Hold onto this for me, would you? Just until I bring Vaan back.

text.ACTION: Penelo takes the handkerchief, clutching it to her chest as the three are escorted away by the Imperials.

text.Imperial: On your feet! You, over here!

text.Balthier: All right, all right. Edgy, aren't we?

text.ACTION: Nearby, a triplet of bangaa watches the scene. The one we recognize from a scene earlier in Rabanastre – the fierce-looking green bangaa with piercings.

text.Ba'Gamnan: What does that philanderer think he's doing? I was to kill Balthier, not those addle-pated Imperials!

text.ACTION: The scene changes to a bright white light, coming through a window. It's the sterile white room again, where Reks sits lifeless in a chair before the window. Vaan walks into the room with the Galbana lilies in his hand.

text.Vaan: I brought you some of those flowers you like: Galbana lilies. Remember? You always said how they smelled nice, and how pretty they were. Remember?

text.ACTION: pause

text.Vaan: The King – Did you? Were you really a part of it?

text.ACTION: pause again

text.Vaan: Even if – Even if you were – Captain Basch must have tricked you into it!

text.ACTION: Vaan resignedly places the flowers on Reks's lap. As he does, Reks begins to dissolve into glistening particles of light that then flow out through the window like liquid. Vaan is left alone, with Reks's ring in his hand. The scene fades.
Vaan awakens in a sandy chamber on the ground. Balthier sits nearby.

text.Balthier: You're awake.

text.Vaan: Where are we?

text.Balthier: Prison, where else? More a dungeon, but it's really all the same.

text.ACTION: Vaan walks curiously toward the open doorway. Someone outside screams. He draws away, reviled, and almost trips as he steps backward. He looks around to see the body of a bangaa sprawled in the dirt.

text.Balthier: It's just a corpse. Jump at every little thing down here and you'll wear yourself out.

text.ACTION: yawn

text.Balthier: It's not even a proper dungeon. They just sealed off the bottom level of the fortress. Take a look around. We're not the first they've thrown down here.

text.Vaan: Where's Fran?

text.Balthier: She's off trying to find us a way out.

text.ACTION: Vaan looks cautiously at the doorway again.

text.Balthier: Remember what curiosity killed. Just a friendly word of advice. This is all the water we've got. I'd save your strength if I were you.

text.ACTION: Vaan turns and walks away. Balthier looks vaguely surprised, and then simply smirks.

text.Balthier: Looks as though our belongings were carted off by the Imperials. Ah, perhaps they've brought our things up to our rooms. How kind. No sense strutting about at a time like this. Save your strength, and stay out of trouble.

text.No. 691: Ah, new arrival? Welcome to the famed Nalbina Dungeons, boy. We're all equals here. Stripped of everything by our kind friend the Empire. All we got is our bones, and those'll be theirs soon enough! Har!
You're in with us, which means you're in here for a long, long time. You're lucky. You get to die slow. If they were going to kill you quick, you'd be down in the oubliette.
