Don't even think about going back to see the oubliette, boy. They'd as soon toss you in there as look at you.

text.No. 278: Room back there's the corpse pile. That's where they'll throw me when I pass on. You, too.
I wonder why they say "imprisoned for life," when it's for death we're waitin'.

text.No. 474: My friend and me were just going to the cathedral to pray for Lady Ashe and Lord Rasler, when some Imperials arrested us! Said we were part of some royalist movement! Can you believe it? They had no proof at all! And my friend, he ... (sniff)
What have I done? All I did was pray for Lady Ashe's peaceful repose ...

text.No. 823: Tell me, boy, you still have hope?

CHOICE.No. 823: Eh heh ... good, good! Man can't live without hope. Here's another bit of hope: the Empire's fated to fall, you know. Not too long from now ... Should be any day ...
Eh heh ... I see, I see ... Too bad, 'cause I've got hope. You see ... the Empire's fated to fall. Shouldn't be too long now ... Might be today ... might be tomorrow ...

text.No. 823: The Empire can thrash about all it wants, there's no escaping fate. Eh heh. Eh heh heh heh!

text.No. 381: Ach ... So overjoyed was I to see my lass once again, I went to give 'er a kiss ... ... And got a fresh slap in the face for my affections! I can't be blamed for mistakin' that viera for my bonnie lass ... Been a year since I saw a lady. Should've known one tough enough to survive down here long'd be cast of iron. Grr ... Blasted viera ...
What! If you're fixing to have a staring contest, let's end it right now. There, I lose. You happy?

text.No. 102: W-why bother giving us this brackish swill ... A man can't drink that ...
Please, just a taste ... Cold, clear water ... A taste ...

text.No. 124: You Dalmascan, boy? I once fought at this fortress to save the King of Dalmasca. It's true. Seems an age ago, now, down here.
Listen, boy. No matter how hard it gets, don't forget your pride in Dalmasca, and your hatred of the Empire! They're all we got.
Accursed Captain ... I hope he's burning in the pits of the underworld ...

text.No. 982: Ah, fresh blood! If you want to make it out of this place in one piece, you'll do whatever Daguza tells ya to, got that?
You've the face of one looking to start something. Start all you want, but I guarantee, you won't much like the end.

text.No. 546: The man you came here with had a familiar look to him ... Might be I saw him somewhere? Might be a wanted man ... In fact, I think that's it. He were a bandit ... No, a sky pirate, he was. Seem to remember a hefty sum on his head ...

text.No. 395: Escape? There's plenty of folks down here wanting to do that. Never heard of anyone succeeding, though.
I always heard Nalbina Fortress was impenetrable. Just never thought it worked both ways ...
If you're thinking of trying to escape, better stop thinking. The lucky ones get thrown in the oubliette.

text.No. 643: What did you do to get in here, boy? You don't look none too bright. Throw a stone at some Imperial, or something?

text.No. 502: They don't need a reason, them Imperials toss people in here when they feel like it. Criminals, free-thinkers, bad singers ...

text.No. 643: Keeping from dyin' is a full-time business in here. But if you ain't alive, you'll never get out.
Call it what you will, we're an occupied state. What the Empire wants ain't "shared prosperity," or "self-rule." It's a herd of nannas to milk.

text.No. 502: You've heard about the lower levels? Sounds like all manner of vile nasties are lurkin' down there ... When it gets dark, they get to movin' around ... I'd stay out of there, if I were you.

text.No. 643: When night comes, you hear the voices ... Like demons weeping in the deep ...

text.No. 502: That sound, it's like something from the pits of hell ... or worse.
I'm scared ... I'll admit it, I'm scared ...

text.No. 281: Er ... Annngh ... Damn swine ... ! What's he talking about "spy hunting"? What gives him the right ...
That Daguza ... Swine thinks his manure's made o' gold.

text.ACTION: When you walk through the doorway past 281, if you've talked to him ...

text.No. 281: Look, take my advice, and stay out of there!

text.ACTION: After Vaan enters the arena area, two bodies drop from a balcony about two stories up. One of them is either unconscious or deceased; the other, a red bangaa, feebly looks up from where it landed at Vaan's feet and pleads for help. Before Vaan can do anything, two seeq land on the ground, and the bangaa tries to crawl away. The seeq easily overtake the weak bangaa and proceed to beat him with their clubs. Just as one is about to land a killing blow ...

text.Vaan: No, don't!

text.ACTION: ... the club is swung anyway, and the bangaa falls limp. The seeq now turn to Vaan and look menacingly at him.

text.Vaan: He was defenseless ...

text.ACTION: The leader, a seeq with an absurdly ugly, disarrayed set of teeth, drool dripping from his mouth, approaches Vaan, dragging his club in a Neanderthal fashion behind him; he grumbles something incoherently to Vaan. Vaan doesn't notice until too late the third seeq who jumps down from above, hitting Vaan as he lands. He blacks out.

When he opens his eyes again, he's been dragged into the pen in the center by the seeq. He scrambles up from the ground and tries to run, but the gates on all four sides close on him. He's trapped, and the seeq gang begins to close in on him, but they stop when they hear a voice.

text.Balthier: Something stinks in here all right. I've changed my mind. This is no dungeon, it's a sty.

text.ACTION: The seeq leader begins grumbling incoherently again, this time at the speaker. Balthier appears on the other side of the fence. He spits and cracks his knuckles.

text.Balthier: I said you're the one that stinks, hamshanks. Hear me now?

text.ACTION: Balthier jumps down into the pen next to Vaan.

text.Balthier: You all right, Vaan?

text.ACTION: He proceeds to smirk and wave provocatively at the seeq.
After defeating Daguza, Gwitch, and Galeedo ...

People approach the pen, looking on in admiration at the ones who defeated Daguza. Then they hear the sound of a door opening, and the prisoners all retreat into the shadows with bitter backward glances. Balthier and Vaan take a hint and press up against the wall closest to the approaching party, out of their sight.

text.Balthier: Great. They just don't give up, do they?

text.ACTION: Imperials file in and line the stairs, standing at attention. A hoplite walks in and looks around, followed by the green bangaa from the earlier scene in Lowtown, who scowls and looks around himself.

text.Balthier: Now is looking like a good time for us to leave.

text.ACTION: The two hear a sound. Fran stands at one of the gates, quietly opening it just enough so they can crawl out. As they approach, Fran murmurs to Balthier.

text.Fran: Through the oubliette, there's a way out. Only –

text.Balthier: Only you sense the Mist.

text.ACTION: Fran nods

text.Balthier: Then we'll need magicks.

text.Imperial: What did you call me? Say that again!

text.ACTION: Balthier, Fran, and Vaan's attentions are directed back at the Imperials with bangaa

text.Ba'Gamnan: What, you couldn't hear? I merely said that the lot of you are incompetent fools. If you've the sky pirate in your hands, where is he?

text.Imperial: You'd have done better, Ba'Gamnan? By your own words, it was the Imperial army who caught this sky pirate of yours. We've done your job for you! We don't require the assistance of filthy headhunters. The Empire will restore order here.

text.Ba'Gamnan: Eh? What's that you say now? Maybe I'll whet my blade on you ... before I kill Balthier.

text.ACTION: yet another voice

text.Gabranth: That's enough, Ba'Gamnan.

text.ACTION: From the doorway, another Imperial, this time in an ostentatious horned helm and blue and red cape bearing the insignia of House Solidor, makes his grand entrance.

text.Fran: A Judge.

text.Vaan: Judge?

text.Balthier: Hmph. The self-proclaimed guardians of law and order in Archadia. They're the elite guard of House Solidor. Which effectively makes them the commanders of the Imperial army. If you ask me, they're more executioners than judges. Not a friendly lot, at any rate. What are they doing here?

text.ACTION: to Ba'Gamnan

text.Gabranth: The Emperor is willing to overlook race for his more talented servants. However, those that do not show respect will receive none in kind. You travel freely through our lands because the Emperor wills it. Am I correct?

text.ACTION: Ba'Gamnan grumbles, then says "Bah" and throws his hands up before turning away.
to soldier

text.Gabranth: Where is the Captain?

text.Imperial: We have him in solitary, Your Honor. We're ready to begin our interrogation.

text.Gabranth: This does not concern you, bounty hunter.

text.ACTION: frustrated, to his henchmen

text.Ba'Gamnan: He's in here somewhere! Find him!

text.Balthier: Time for the hare to follow the fox.

text.Fran: The magicks binding the door to the oubliette are quite strong. Too strong even for my talents.

text.Balthier: That's why we'll get them to open it for us.

text.Vaan: How is going deeper into this place –

text.ACTION: cutting off Vaan

text.Balthier: What's wrong? You don't trust her? Viera's noses are sharp. If she says there's a way out, there's a way out.

text.Fran: Look.

text.Balthier: Ah! The prison repository of wrested relics and raiments.

text.Vaan: So our things are in here?

text.Balthier: That's what I said.

text.ACTION: You recover your lost items and equipment!
You obtain a map of the Nalbina Dungeons!
Your location map for this area is complete!

text.Balthier: There are more turnkeys than cutpurses down here. I've had my fill of chains. Let's tread lightly, shall we?

text.ACTION: Balthier, Fran, and Vaan hide in the shadows and watch the following scene unroll. The Judge approaches the chasm in the middle of the room, from which a long thin cage is being hoisted. Inside the cage a very unkempt and scarred blond man is shackled. The Judge takes his helmet off as he begins speaking to the prisoner. The two look remarkably alike, thought the Judge is of course clean-shaven and groomed.

text.Gabranth: You have grown very thin, Basch. Less than a shadow. Less than a man. Sentenced to death and yet you live. Why?

text.Basch: To silence Ondore. How many times must I say it?

text.Gabranth: Is that all?

text.Basch: Why not ask Vayne himself? Is he not one of your masters?

text.Gabranth: We've caught a leader of the insurgence. She is being brought from Rabanastre. The woman Amalia. Who could that be? Such a faithful hound to cling to a fallen kingdom.

text.Basch: Better than throwing it away.

text.ACTION: putting back on his helmet

text.Gabranth: Throwing it away? As you threw away our homeland?

text.ACTION: The Judge and accompanying Imperials leave, and Balthier, Fran, and Vaan emerge. Basch perks up.

text.Basch: Who's there?

text.ACTION: to Balthier and Fran

text.Balthier: This the place?

text.Fran: The Mist is flowing through this room. It must be going somewhere.

text.Basch: You! You're no Imperials. Please, you must get me out –

text.Balthier: It's against my policy to speak with the dead. Especially when they happen to be kingslayers.

text.Basch: I did not kill him.

text.Balthier: Is that so? Glad to hear it.

text.Basch: Please, get me out. For the sake of Dalmasca.

text.ACTION: Vaan scowls at this comment, and leaps onto the cage, enraged, gripping the bars as he screams at Basch.

text.Vaan: Dalmasca!? What do you care about Dalmasca!? Everything that's happened is because of you! Everyone that's died, every single one! Even my brother – You killed my brother!

text.Balthier: Quiet! The guards will hear.

text.ACTION: Too late – Fran is the first to hear the sounds of Imperials coming.

text.Fran: I'm dropping it.

text.ACTION: She kicks the lever that keeps Basch's cage suspended. The chain holding it up loosens ...
shaking his head

text.Balthier: Pirates without a sky.

text.ACTION: Balthier jumps onto the cage along with Fran and Vaan, just as the cage begins to drop full velocity into the abyss below.

The cage is clearly wrecked and busted open, and Balthier, Fran, Vaan, and Basch gather themselves after their descent at the bottom of the chasm. Vaan immediately lunges at Basch, but Balthier grabs him and throws him back.

text.Balthier: Spare us your quiddities.

text.Vaan: Yeah, but – But he's a –

text.Balthier: A traitor. I know. Stay here and fight, if you want.

text.ACTION: to Basch

text.Balthier: If you can walk, let's go.

text.Vaan: You're taking him with us?

text.Balthier: We could use another sword arm.

text.Basch: And you have it.

text.ACTION: Basch joins the party as a guest!
If you talk to Burrogh before examining the Timeworn Device ...

text.Burrogh: Don' get many visitors down here. Come scavengin' fer odds and ends, have you? I don't reckon you saw whatever caused that terrible racket just now, eh? Hrm. Come crashin' down straight on the stairs? That was the only way out! Guess it's time to start lookin' fer a back door outta this place. What about you? You plan on pokin' 'round these tunnels, best go prepared. I piece together what scraps of this, that, and the other I find into all manner of things. It may be I have somethin' you need.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Burrogh: Normally I get supplies I need off'n the caravans come through Nalbina. But Barheim Passage is known to have certain items not easily come by. I knew it weren't safe, but ... well, here I am.
You wanna make it outta here alive, best go prepared. It may be I have somethin' you'd want to, uh, purchase, eh?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Burrogh: Normally I get supplies I need off'n the caravans come through Nalbina. But Barheim Passage is known to have certain items not easily come by. I knew it weren't safe, but ... well, here I am.

text.ACTION: Timeworn Device: It appears to be some sort of switch.

CHOICE.Balthier: Let's have a look. Hm ... the fuse is blown. That would explain why there's no power reaching the switch. If the wiring is any indication, I'd say this is a central power relay of some sort. As it stands, I doubt we'll find much still running down here.

text.ACTION: If you talk to Burrogh again after examining the Timeworn Device/Power Relay ...

text.Burrogh: To smithereens, you say!? Then there's nothin' left but to find some other way out through these tunnels. You'll need to get the power workin' again, 'fore that gate'll budge, though. The fuse in that contraption up the stairs is blown ... but this oughta fix it up.

text.ACTION: You obtain a Tube Fuse!

text.Burrogh: Made that tube fuse from parts I found down in these very tunnels. It's good as any you'll find, and better 'an most, mark my words.

text.ACTION: If you did not talk to Burrogh once before examining the Timeworn Device/Power Relay, his dialogue is slightly different.

text.Burrogh: Don' get many visitors down here. You come scavengin' fer odds and ends, have you? Oh, the way out? It's just back up those stairs -- To smithereens, you say!? Then there's nothin' left but to find some other way out through these tunnels. You'll need to get the power workin' again, 'fore that gate'll budge, though. The fuse in that contraption up the stairs is blown ... but this oughta fix it up.

text.ACTION: You obtain a Tube Fuse!

text.Burrogh: Made that tube fuse from parts I found down in these very tunnels. It's good as any you'll find, and better 'an most, mark my words.
What's that? No power in the Passage, eh? Can't say I'm surprised, tunnels as old as these. This gate ain't workin' one, either. Here we go ... try putting this in that contraption up the stairs.

text.ACTION: You obtain a Tube Fuse!

text.Burrogh: Made that tube fuse from parts I found down in these very tunnels. It's good as any you'll find, and better 'an most, mark my words.

text.ACTION: Power Relay: The fuse seems to have blown.

text.Burrogh: Looks like that fuse did the trick, but that don't change the fact it's dangerous down here. There's anything you want to be buying, be about it.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Burrogh: Normally I get supplies I need off'n the caravans come through Nalbina. But Barheim Passage is known to have certain items not easily come by. I knew it weren't safe, but ... well, here I am.

text.ACTION: Gate Switchboard: The switch is covered with rust.

text.Burrogh: I see you got the gate open. Oughta be able to look fer all manner of ways out, now. While the lights are on, the Passage ain't so bad. But let the charge drop, and some fierce beasts start comin' out in the dark. Openin' this gate probably took the charge down some. That gauge oughta show you how much charge is left. Hrm, 'bout thirty percent to operate somethin' the size of these gates, I'd say. Who knows how many more of these gates they got down here. You look fer these switchboards, you oughta be able to make yer way.

text.ACTION: The party watches a strange mechanical blue creature begin feeding on the current of an open conduit. The lights dim.

text.Vaan: Hey! Who turned out the lights? One of those!?

text.Balthier: I've heard of these: mimics. They disguise themselves as all manner of things, then strike when you're least weary. Some of them have a fondness for energy, I'm told. They gorge themselves on the stuff until there's naught left.

text.Vaan: So ... what happens then?

text.ACTION: A zombie emerges from the shadows.

text.Balthier: Lights out. And it's worse in the dark. Much worse. So, let them get too close one of those conduits and they'll suck it dry. But don't worry: it'll give it back, if you ask it nicely. Sticking it with a sword helps, too. Clock's ticking!

text.Fran: The Mist seethes.

text.Balthier: It reeks. Something's close.

text.ACTION: Basch picks up some armor and a sword from a skeleton lying nearby and makes a few practice swings.

text.Balthier: Nice moves there, Captain.

text.Vaan: You mean "traitor."

text.Balthier: So they say. But I didn't see him kill anyone.

text.Vaan: My brother did.

text.Basch: Reks. He said he had a brother two years younger. I see. He meant you. Your brother. What became –

text.Vaan: He's dead.

text.Basch: I'm sorry.

text.Vaan: It was you who killed him!

text.Basch: I give you my word: that was not the way of it.

text.ACTION: Flashback; we see random images and hear various snatches of dialogue from the night of the treaty signing
Reks: Reks, sir. My name's Reks. He's two years younger than I. Living in Rabanastre.
Vossler: It's time, Basch! Save the discussion for later.
Reks: But if we arrive after he's signed the treaty –
Reks: Sir! We have little time! You must go to the king!
Vossler: It's as I feared. They're slowing us down.
Now we see images of the real Basch, being held by Imperial soldiers out of Reks's line of sight, while a man who looks exactly like Basch is eyeing him smugly.
Reks: Captain, why? Our King ... what have you done?
????: His Majesty was a traitor.
End flashback

text.Balthier: A twin brother? Fancy that. But still, the pieces fit. I'll give you that much. And he did look like you.

text.Vaan: I don't believe you.

text.Basch: Of course not. It was my fault that Reks was there. I am sorry.

text.Vaan: My brother, he trusted you. He trusted you, and he lost everything. How can I believe you?

text.Basch: Not me then. Believe in your brother. He was a fine soldier. He fought to the last to protect his homeland. No. Surely he fought to protect his brother.

text.Vaan: You don't know anything!

text.Balthier: Believe what you want to. Whatever it takes to make you happy. What's done is done.

text.ACTION: The party encounters the Mimic Queen. After defeating her, her death throes induce an explosion that causes the room to cave, and the party escapes as the walls crumble.

text.Basch: To think Dalmascan air could taste so sweet.

text.Vaan: Where are we?

text.Balthier: The Estersand, by the look of it. Let's back to Rabanastre before we shrivel up. By your leave, Captain.

text.Basch: Yes, the hour of my return is already over late. The people may hate me, but that does not free me of my charge.

text.Shifty Seeq: The whole entrance just caved in with a crash. And the boss is still inside! There's another entrance to Barheim 'round here somewhere, but the boss has the key ...

text.LOCATION: Go to the previous chapter (Chapter 2: The Sunstone) | Go to the next chapter (Chapter 4: The Skycity of Bhujerba)
Go to Clan Primer | Go to Side Quests | Go to Intro & Key

text.Basch: I thank you.

text.Balthier: I'd avoid crowds, if I were you. In this town you're still a traitor you know.

text.Basch: The Resistance will surely find me soon. Fates will we meet again. I would pay my respects to your brother.

text.ACTION: Basch leaves them. Balthier turns to Vaan.

text.Balthier: You're a fugitive now, too. Stay low for a while.

text.Vaan: What about the stone?

text.Balthier: Do as you like. That stone's ill-favored.

text.Fran: We feel regret. We sought that stone and found ourselves only worry.

text.Balthier: You offering it?

text.Vaan: It's mine!

text.Balthier: Then why do you ask? Our regards to your girl.

text.Fran: We stay in Rabanastre a while.

text.ACTION: Fran and Balthier leave, and Vaan begins musing to himself (and to Reks?)

text.Vaan: What do you think? Can I trust Basch?

text.ACTION: long pause ...

text.Vaan: I gotta get rid of this thing.

text.ACTION: pause again

text.Vaan: But maybe I should show it to Penelo first. So she knows I got something. She'd be at Migelo's place this time of day.

text.ACTION: Balthier and Fran leave the party.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, pink, and gr: Quite the spectacle at the palace last night. I thought the Rozarrians had decided to invade! Imagine, all that to catch some thieves.

text.Rabanastran (woman in white speaking wit: The Moogling is finally running again, and let me tell you: there's no better way to move about the city! I use it all the time.

text.Hapless Merchant: A good chum got sent to Nalbina just after Dalmasca lost the war – false charges, I guarantee. No matter. Doubt I'll see him again. I've never been in Nalbina myself, but they say that death is the only escape. My gut tells me that's more than just idle talk, too.

text.Moogling Attendant (during this period i: The Moogling is once again open for business, kupo! We'll happily teleport you to any of several select locations throughout Rabanastre. And I've saved the best part for last: it's free, kupo!
Just look for one of our signposts and speak with the friendly moogling moogle who's sure to be close at hand, kupo!

text.Hurdy: Welcome to the Moogling, kupo. This is your first time using the Moogling? Nothing to it! The Moogling lets you teleport to several select locations across Rabanastre. We had to close for the parade earlier, but we're up and running again, kupo! The service is free of charge. Why not give it a try? There's no time like the present, kupo!

text.ACTION: Moogling menu

text.Weather Eye: Sure, the Moogling is handy, but without some old-fashioned walkin', I'll never lose weight. Hard to say no to a free ride, though ...

text.Reluctant Adventurer: It's desert far as the eye can see out west of Rabanastre. Never been farther than the Westersand, myself. A vicious tribe are rumored to live in the wastes beyond.

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with group): I'm so glad all those people from Archadia have finally gone. The aerodrome has reopened, and things are settling back to normal. Only a handful of routes open, though. A sign of the times. Few are willing to risk travel with the world as it is.

text.Bhujerban (man leaning against counter): You have come to book passage on an airship, friend? You can pay your fare at any of the counters you see here. Each counter serves a different destination, so it is as simple as finding the counter of the city you would like to visit, you see. If a given counter is empty, that route is not currently in service, be it due to maintenance or what have you, and you will need to wait.

text.Flights to Nalbina: Good day, sir. This counter serves travelers wishing to book passage to Nalbina. We have ships fitted with shops and amenities, or if you prefer to sleep during your journey, ships with only private cabins. Whichever you choose, the price is the same. We will show you aboard as soon as you've purchased your ticket. Passage is 200 Gil. How would you like to travel?

text.Rabanastran (woman in white pacing): You can book two kinds of passage on the airships. The first lets you take your time shopping and conversing during your journey. The second lets you sleep the whole way, which can be nice when you don't want to deal with any distractions.

text.Son: We have our own airship ... I don't see why we have to travel on a public ship. It's so slow and crowded ...

text.Mother: What's this? We've booked the finest quarters on the ship! Besides, I enjoy the thrill of traveling with the smallfolk. Someday you'll understand.

text.Father: That's right, Mother. Father wouldn't change that about you for the world.

text.Rabanastran (woman embracing man by the: I know you need to go ... just hold me a little longer ... I've never felt more sad, more lonely ... but Nalbina's so far away ... I know you're going there to work, and I don't care ... we could be happy here, just being together ...

text.Bhujerban (man leaning against counter): You wish to ride the airships in safety and comfort, do you not? The docent here can be most helpful in that regard.

text.Aerodrome Docent: Welcome to the aerodrome, sir. The East Ivalice Company proudly offers passage aboard leisure craft on which you might shop and enjoy your flight. For those eager to reach their destination, we also have ships with private cabins in which you can sleep or rest until your arrival. You may book passage from the counters you'll find throughout the aerodrome. Each counter serves a different destination.

text.Merchant (Aerodrome): I'm headed to Bhujerba to lay in some new goods, but I plan to see the sights while I'm there. They have guides at every corner and byroad.

text.Rabanastran (man in blue, green, and red: You see that group of people by the window? They're from Archadia. I wonder what they think of Rabanastre.

text.Traveler (woman with the Archadian group: This is the last time I travel on a whim. I've never been anywhere more boring in my life. I can't wait to go home and relax properly.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Westgat: Hey, Vaan. Have you seen Penelo lately? Sure seems like somethin's botherin' her. Whaddaya think it might be?

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: From Southgate, it's a straight run down to the nomad village on Giza Plains.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Southga: I saw a real weird guy over in the East End. His beard and hair were all long and scruffy ... Wonder what his story is?

text.Bright-eyed Boy: Someday I'm gonna be tough enough to go into the Estersand all by myself. Just you watch!

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: Capturing those insurgents so soon after his arrival ... that new consul is a sharp man. If he can keep peace in the city, I'll be happy.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue and green on so: If people are lookin' to this new consul to make our city a better place, forget it! I have ... other ... expectations for our rich friend.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa in red vest): May not be cheap, but takin' an airship out of the aerodrome's the easiest way to get from city to city. When they aren't in dry dock for repairs ...

text.Cotze: The guards may be watchin' us, but I'm watchin' them. I don't trust 'em any further than I can throw 'em.

text.Lovestruck Man: Did you see? Have you heard? Have you ... touched? You really shouldn't touch, you know. ... Why, the viera, of course! Such style and grace ... everything I've ever wanted in a woman! I wonder if she's attached ...

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants with his: No one hates the Empire more than the people in Lowtown. I can't say that I blame them, but at the same time, the Empire's not all bad, either.

text.Rabanastran (boy with his father in the: Well of course they captured the thieves that tried for the palace. They're thieves! They got what they deserved!

text.Imperial (Southern Plaza): That commotion with the thieves in the palace on the night of the Lord Consul's fete shook people up a fair bit. All's well now, though. The watch did for them, sure enough.

text.Rabanastran (boy squatting down and hugg: People seem to think pretty well of Vayne ... . What I'd like to know is: why?

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa speaking with wo: Hey, did you see that fellow who just passed this way? Had a beard, looked and smelled like he hadn't had a bath in years? There was an unsavory bunch followin' him ... You think he's all right? Not that I'm about to stick my nose where it don't belong.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa chatting with: My friend here says there are 6,387 cobblestones in the Southern Plaza 'round the corner, not including the tiles in the fountain. But even with the stones by the city gates ... 'Course, he could be countin' the flagstones, too. That would be another matter altogether.

text.Imperial: Order's come down to buy new armor, but there's no mention of just what to be buyin'. Mystic armor raises magick potency, heavy armor'll make you stronger, and of course light armor gets you healthy as an aurochs ... Which to choose?

text.Bucco: Hey, Vaan. Where've you been? Feel like it's been forever since I saw you last. Hmm, haven't seen Penelo today, now that you mention it. She wasn't in Migelo's, either.

text.Town Gossip: Just a while ago, a viera came through here. But that's not all ... she was with a man. The sort of man a lady takes note of, if you follow. Hmm, a viera and a dashing young man. Could that have been this Balthier I've heard so much about? Have you seen the bounty on his head? I think he's over by the Sandsea ... maybe I'll go take a look.

text.Rabanastran (man in green shorts near Pa: I was walking past the Sandsea when I noticed the Moogling was up and running again. I feel a fool for walking, heh.

text.Wistful Bangaa: The Consul's set out to "re –" educate the guards ... Hah! He's as like to teach seeq to fly!

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa EE): The Imperials may rule Rabanastre, but that's no reason for the city itself to change. You've heard of Bhujerba, yes? She's ruled by a wise man who's managed to keep her independent to this very day. If only we'd been so lucky ...

text.Rabanastran (woman in green and pink EE): I saw a beautiful viera and a dashing man walk past not long ago. And here I am alone ... there's no justice in this world. Oh, they were headed toward the Sandsea.

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq pacing about): Migelo hasn't seemed hisself lately. Something's been worrying at him ... but what?

text.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): Hey, mister. You wanna hear about the sneak attack on the palace? It won't cost ya much ... What? I gotta eat, too, ya know. Let's see ... 1 gil oughta do it.

CHOICE.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): The night the new consul came, some insurgents waited until the Imperials were off guard 'cause of the fete, and snuck into the palace. So the Imperial army had to come and capture them! You could hear the commotion from here! 'Course, nobody knew what was goin' on then. When all was said and done, the palace was okay, and the Imperials seemed pretty happy that they'd caught the insurgents when they did. Well, at least it ended there. Just think if it had turned out to be the start of another war ...
Aww, and this was a real nail-biter of a story, too. There's just no pleasin' some people.

text.Lonely Boy: I heard they caught them insurgents what snuck into the palace down in Lowtown. Why'd they do something like that in the first place?

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: I saw a really shady bunch of bangaa during the parade. I wonder if they weren't the insurgents that stole into the palace?

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq by bazaar entranc: I'm all for the Moogling, don't misunderstand me. But sometimes I wonder ... what's in it for them?

text.Rabanastran (man in turban and brown sho: I've tried my hand at hunting to make a few spare gil. Between the loot and equipment you find, you can turn quite a profit!

text.Johm: I was, uh, practicing what you showed me, but I kinda slipped up and bumped into this viera ... in a bad sorta way. She didn't get mad or anything, just kept walking like nothin' happened. The man she was with didn't seem too happy about it, though.

text.Kytes: Vaan, is it really you? I heard you got took off to Nalbina!

text.Vaan: The Imperials'll need more than a dungeon to stop me.

text.Kytes: You broke out of a dungeon? Whoa!

text.Vaan: Hey, try and keep it down, wouldya? Penelo isn't around, is she? Out on a delivery, maybe?

text.Kytes: Nope, haven't seen her all day. Not like her to up and skip out on work like that. Migelo's not here either. He went running off somewhere a little while ago.

text.Vaan: So much for my big welcome. Guess everybody's busy.

text.Kytes: I got my hands full watching the shop ... and Old Dalan had something for me to do, but I can't get away.

text.Vaan: Old Dalan, huh? Tell you what. I'll go see him for you.

text.Kytes: Really?

text.Vaan: Well, nothing better to do.

text.Rabanastran (orange seeq): Hrmph. Will we never be rid of these Imperials? They've been on their best behavior, but an Imperial is still an Imperial. The thought of living out my days under Imperial rule is ... an unpleasant one.

text.Rabanastran (man talking to red bangaa): I haven't seen Migelo all day. I can usually count on finding him up to his elbows in something or other at the back of the store, but not this time.

text.Kytes: Thanks for going to see Old Dalan for me. I'm so busy here, I'd never have had time to make it down to Lowtown. I sure hope Migelo shows up soon ...

text.Shop Clerk (Migelo's): That's quite a stone you've got there. If Migelo were here, I'm sure he'd want to take a look, but he hasn't been in today. Ah, but I don't suppose you came here for small talk, did you.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink headscarf): Wouldn't you know it, the one day I have questions about something I'm looking to buy, Migelo isn't here. I'll just have to make do.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, green, and t: The war has really driven up prices. I think it's made me a bit of a pinchpenny, but let's call it "responsibly price-conscious," shall we?

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa in green vest): There hasn't been any official proclamation yet, but apparently some insurgents staged an assault on the palace the night of the fete. You could hear the commotion all over the city. It quieted down soon enough, though. Maybe it was just part of the night's entertainment?

text.Sherral: These weapons inspections may not seem like much, but they're vital to restricting the supply of arms to insurgents and other undesirables. What would happen if powerful weapons should find their way to the insurgents? War, that's what. So must we be ever vigilant.

text.Amal: Say, aren't you the lad that minds Migelo's shop when he's busy? Poor thing ... Oh, sorry. Must've confused you with someone else. No harm meant by it, boy. Now, how may I help you?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (man browsing curio): The news of thieves in the palace had put a little spring in my step, but that was the last interesting thing to happen 'round here. Peace and quiet is all well and good, but it can be rather dull.

text.Lively Bangaa: The Consul may have changed, but you wouldn't know it to look out on the streets. Though I do suppose these things take time.

text.Panamis: We've a fine assortment of armors for the choosing. There's sure to be something to tickle your fancy! Why, that's a most unusual stone you've got there! Don't suppose you'd be interested in sellin'? N-No, what am I saying! If I go off buying odd knickknacks again, me mum will have a fit! Now, where was I? Ah, yes! Armors! Armors for the choosing!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue pants): I'm sure you've heard about the insurgents who stormed the palace. It made me realize just how important it is to be able to defend yourself. All's quiet now, but who can say what the future may bring?

text.Earnest Seeq: Magicks is a fickle mistress ... I can't make no sense of her. But sense or senseless, I done made up me mind to have at her, and let the chips fall where they may.

text.Yugri: Are you sure you shouldn't be helping Migelo today? With him and Penelo out, poor Kytes is minding the shop by himself. Sorry, you came to shop, not to talk.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (man sitting with woman): Those Imperials have finally left the balcony ... I can't remember the last time I sat down to a meal without knowing they were watching. If it feels this food to have them out of the Sandsea, imagine how good it would feel to be rid of them altogether.

text.Tavernmaster: A pair of what looked to be sky pirates came in just now. A viera and a hume ... can you imagine?

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa at bar with To: You remember that hullabaloo the night of the Consul's fete? The explosions, the airships ... Well, they say it was over some thieves that broke into the palace, but I don't fool that easy. They're hidin' somethin', I know it.

text.Barkeep (man standing near foot of stair: You've heard of Bhujerba, the skycity, yes? When I was young, I used to think if I could get to Bhujerba, I could become a sky pirate ... Ignorance can be such bliss. Speaking of sky pirates, you should get a look at the fellow up on the balcony.

text.Balthier: I believe our business is finished, yes? Hadn't you better say hello to all your little friends?

text.Fran: She must worry for you. Balthier's handkerchief may dry her tears, but it cannot console her.

text.Balthier: That's right. I'd prefer to get that back with as few tear stains as possible. Better hurry.

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with moogle): I thought – Tomaj said – Weren't you captured and sent to Nalbina? ... You escaped!? You? I shouldn't have written you off so easily. Have you said hello to Migelo or Penelo yet? Poor Penelo's been inconsolable since you left.

text.Rabanastran (woman talking to red bangaa: The Consul's begun making changes throughout the city. Who knows, there may even be new jobs to be had. I may start looking for one myself.

text.Batahn: Ah, Vaan. You haven't seen Penelo lately, have you? No, no, I don't need her for anything in particular. Usually she's stopped in to see if there are any chores need doing by now, and I was curious why she hadn't is all ... Now, what can I get for you?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Greenhorn: I've managed to pick up quite a lot – I'm even making my own gambit combinations now. Oh, I see I'm not alone. Guess I better keep at it ... Don't want to be one-upped!

text.Adept Adventurer: The Way of the Gambit is long and steep. Any novice may combine gambits, but using them to give form to your every thought is truly an art. Yet the tightest grasp can hold only dust. The most intricate combinations stand upon simple foundations ... gambits are like that.

text.Yamoora: You're one of Migelo's little friends, aren't you? Well, I'm glad he's all right. Some nasty business the night of the fete. There was no serious damage, at least. Good thing the Consul was ready for it. But I'm forgetting ... you're here to shop, aren't you.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (woman in green and pink NE): They've sent the worst of the guards back to Archadia. Removed for running afoul of the Consul ... I shudder to think what happens to them.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, yellow, and: Seems Vayne's ordered the guards to speak to us more proper, like. Trouble is, some of the guards aren't too bright, and it just comes out funny.

text.Rabanastran (man in white turban and bro: I heard the Imperials had caught you for something or other. Glad you gave 'em the slip. I gotta tell ya, I'm surprised you made it out.

text.Riby: Vaan, is that you? I'm surprised to see you here. All I've heard out of Penelo lately is "Vaan's GONE!" She's been miserable. You should really go see her.

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa NE): The consul may change, but how long will it be before we see change on the streets? Though I'll admit, the guards seem more mannerly now.

text.Dispirited Woman: I've heard the kingslayer is back in Rabanastre. If it's true, I have choice word or two for him ... Though I wonder if I'd even recognize him.

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on east sid: Things have finally settled down 'round here. They've even reopened the aerodrome! Not that I'll be flyin' anywhere ...

text.Imperial (North End): Lord Vayne is very particular about the rules he sets out. He's ordered us to treat you commoners proper, like. Of course I would, orders or no!

text.Traveler (North End): Life is easier in Archades, no question. But Lord Vayne is here in Rabanastre ... Should I stay? Should I go? What to do!?

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: The Consul's been quite busy with his civic projects, you know. Perhaps Lowtown's fortunes are on the up?

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on west sid: Did you know there's a mine right in the middle of Bhujerba? Hard work, mining, but the pay's tempting, so it is. Bhujerba's run by one Marquis Ondore. Supposed to be a right generous fellow, so maybe the money's as good as they say.

text.Rabanastran (woman in red, pink, and blu: So, the night of the fete, I tried to sneak into the palace to steal a word or two with Lord Vayne. But the guards mistook me for a thief! It was all straightened out quickly enough, but I was furious. Couldn't have happened at a worse time.

text.ACTION: For dialogue involving Viera/Ktjn, see "Side Quests – Ktjn's Road to Improvement".

text.Troubled Woman: Oh, Vaan! I'm surprised to see you here. I'd heard you'd been taken by the Imperials ... My mistake! What a relief.

text.Swarthy Bangaa: I used to be a sky pirate m'self. I remember this one time I was deep inside a huge cavern lookin' for some treasure ... Just when I thought I'd found me some loot, out jumps the horriblest monster you ever did see! Get the shivers just thinkin' on it ...

text.Patient Bangaa: We was just talkin' about Bhujerba, the skycity. Put my friend here in a foul mood. He can't abide the fact they're free of the Empire, gettin' rich off those magicite mines of theirs.

text.Merchant (tan seeq to side of stairs): Up to your usual "work," boy? May want to lay off for a time. Vayne's really tightening the screws on the watch. To be sure, you can bet the Consul's just trying to keep his men looking all in charge and Imperial, but any pressure on them is pressure on us. Best watch yourself, boy.

text.Trader: Quite an unusual stone you've got there. Don't think it would be worth much, though. Nah, you best hold onto it.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink and tan MB): The Bazaar is one of the few places in Rabanastre where people can go to let off steam. Not literally, of course.

text.Merchant (tan bangaa in blindfold): Sometimes I think I'd enjoy the kind of success Migelo's achieved, but other times I'm not so sure ... Getting jealous looks from the other merchants, worrying about how to keep it all going ... I think I'm happy just the way things are.

text.Traveler (Muthru): Rabanastre seems so much more cultured since Lord Vayne was appointed consul. This city grows more charming by the day!

text.Headhunter: Don't be thinking you can just wait around for new bills to be posted. You want to hunt marks, you have to work for it, boy. Earn a name for yourself in your clan. Then you'll start to see bills for the really notorious marks. Remember that, boy.

text.Busy Messenger: Hey, I heard you met the boss. I wish that meant the end of my errand-running days, but I know better.

text.Rabanastran (man in white, yellow, and b: That Moogling is really something! Now that the service is running again, I finally got to give it a try – it's the way to move about the city! If you haven't used it yet, there's an attendant at the entrance to the Bazaar. I'd sure like to thank the moogle who thought of it!

text.Reks's Friend: If you feel like you've nowhere to turn, talk to your friends. Reks may be gone, but you're not alone, you hear?

text.Rabanastran (green-horned tan seeq): Heard tell there's a huge, powerful wyrm lurking somewhere in the Westersand – a wyrm unlike the others you're liable to find there. Think I heard me the cry of the beast once. Or maybe it was only the raging winds of a sandstorm. Regardless, I can't remember where.

text.Tott: Our fathers have gone stone-digging. That's why the only adults here are all women. Bet you were wondering where all the men went!

text.Dantro: Even a small outpost like ours can mean the difference between life or death in the desert. We see quite an assortment of travelers through here. Keeps things interesting, at least. Not interesting enough for me to want to be here all day, though. Why hasn't the village sent out my replacement?

text.ACTION: Gambitry Banner: Find gambits difficult to grasp? So did I, until I opened this shop. Now I've got a perfect gambit for everyone, even you!

text.Morning Star Gambits: Never shoulda opened my shop in this heat. Buy something, will ya?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Imperial (standing at the door of the ae: You looking for the aerodrome? I'll take you. Citizens are only allowed in sections of the fortress.

CHOICE.Imperial (standing at the door of the ae: If you want to go to the aerodrome, speak with me. You'll need an escort.

text.ACTION: Aerodrome

text.Imperial (at entrance): Headed into town? I'll escort you. Much of the fortress is off-limits.

CHOICE.Imperial (at entrance): Come back should you decide to go into town. You'll need an escort.

text.Imperial (speaking to two men and bangaa: They came here to work and earn a good wage rebuilding the fortress, and now they complain! I've had enough of these people.

text.Itinerant Hand (man in group of two men,: I came here to work on restoring the fortress, but it's soooo hot! I can't work in these conditions! If we're to work out here, we need good coin. That's what my bangaa friend here's negotiating for.

text.Shy Bangaa: Wh-What ... ? I'm just watchin' these goods, like always ... Hey, no stealin', you hear?

text.Homebound Man: I came out here from Rabanastre to earn some gil to make my wife and child happy ... but I can't take this hard labor no more ... Hi, honey. It's me ... the failure. (sigh)

text.Itinerant Hand (black bangaa at window): Far to the east lies a port town where sky pirates gather. I'll be one, someday, and that's where I'll ago. Just need to make some gil first.

text.Chief Steward Chezelle: Ladies and gentleman, allow me to welcome you aboard on behalf of the East Ivalice Company. Your captain for our voyage is Mr. Ranton, with Mr. Nicol his first officer. I am Chief Steward Chezelle. We have cabins available, should you wish to retire for the remainder of our journey. And please, let me know if I may be of any service.

text.Passenger: Kupo! Oh, miss! Miss! I've shopped, taken in the sky, and now I'd like to rest in a cabin, kupo. I'm not having any luck finding one, though. Where are they?

text.Steward: You mean to rest until we arrive? The cabins are right this way through the sky saloon. Give your name to the chief steward, and she'll have a room prepared for you.

text.Passenger: Ah, we never looked in there, kupo! We thought they might be up on the deck. Thanks for the help!

text.Steward: Please feel free to use one of our cabins should you wish to retire until our arrival. Give your name to the chief steward, and she'll have a room prepared for you. You'll find her this way, in the sky saloon.

text.Energetic Boy: My brother's off keeping the peace in Dalmasca. Mum, Dad, and me are going to visit him!

text.Assistant Storekeeper (to the right): Care to purchase something to remember your voyage by?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Traveler (woman in pink, blue, and yello: I bought my parents a trip to Rabanastre. I'm hoping to do some shopping, find some things you just can't get back home in Archades.

text.Assistant Storekeeper (to the left): We've a wide selection of goods for the traveling adventurer. Take a look around.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Traveler (man in turban and blue shorts: Standing here I feel no less than the captain himself! Someday, someday ... My shop in Archades does well, but not well enough to afford a ship. Still, even being able to travel by airship is a luxury I could only dream of when I lived in Rabanastre.

text.Perceptive Boy: I was enjoying a spot of juice over in the saloon, and the barman was tellin' me all sorts of things. Did you know he used to be a sky pirate? Can you imagine?

text.Traveler (man in green hat and vest with: We heard it would be hot in Dalmasca, so we dressed the part. A little chilly out on deck, though.

text.Imperial: That little girl just over there's been staring up at the sky for some time. Not doing anything dangerous, mind you, but something's not right.

text.Paranoid Man: I am not here to enjoy the wind against my face or any such mean pleasure in which these others bask. No, I am here to search the skies! They're out there, yes. Out there, at the edge of vision! Waiting, watching ... Had I the funds, I would buy an airship for their study. (sigh)

text.ACTION: Caution! (signs all around railing on upper and lower decks): For your own and others' safety, please remain behind railing at all times.
Caution! (two signs on upper deck): Authorized personnel only!

text.Troubled Passenger: You have troubles, friend? I went to Archades chasin' dreams, but all I found was trouble. Finally weren't nothin' left but to run away. Out here though, fresh air in my lungs, sky above my head, my troubles don't seem so bad.

text.Innocent Girl: Look how high we are! I can see forever! But what if I fell ... Hey, no pushing!

text.Charming Woman: I'll finish my drink alone, thank you.

text.Migrant Laborer: You from Rabanastre? Same here. Work keeps me away more than I'd like. I was away during the war, too. Heard a friend o' mine got driven out of the city. Plan on payin' him a visit soon.

text.Saloon Steward: Interest you in a frothy mug o' scuttlebutt?

CHOICE.Saloon Steward: One Rabanastre, comin' right up! Last time I was in Rabanastre, let's see ... Right after Princess Ashe was born, musta been. Ninth in the Dalmascan line, and the first girl. The people were overjoyed, that they were. The city bustled with life. Rabanastre's fallen on hard times, but she'll get back that ol' magick of hers, just you watch.

text.Saloon Steward: Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

text.ACTION: For dialogue with the Chief Steward and Rande, see "Side Quests – the Seven Sisters."

text.Steward: This door leads to our guest cabins. If you'd like to retire until we reach port, you should find the cabins quite comfortable. Should you wish to use a cabin, speak with the chief steward at the counter to my left. She'll only be too happy to assist you.

text.Chief Steward Binastre: Ladies and gentleman, allow me to welcome you aboard on behalf of the East Ivalice Company. Your captain for our voyage is Mr. Ranton, with Mr. Nicol his first officer. I am Chief Steward Binastre. We have cabins available, should you wish to retire for the remainder of our journey. And please, let me know if I may be of any service.

text.Roamantics (tan blindfolded bangaa): Easy to let your guard down aboard these airships. But danger is always lurkin', even here. First rule of adventurin' is to keep your eyes open ...

text.Roamantics (moogle with orange pom-pom): We travel the world, seeking adventure. That's our leader standing over by the window. Grim, strong ... just like an adventurer should be, kupo. He's always helping me out, kupo. I hope I can help, too, when we reach the desert. High adventure on the sands ... Gotta pull my own weight!

text.Roamantics (green bangaa at shop counter: I hear there's a huge dungeon in Nalbina that hardly anyone makes it out of ... in one piece, anyway. Makes the blood run cold, it does.

text.Roamantics (black bangaa looking out win: Your greatest enemy is your own carelessness. The world teems with trouble. Never know when it might come knockin'.

text.Wayward Seeq: Can't find me friend anywhere. You don't suppose I got on the wrong airship? That'd be a fine how-do-you-do, wouldn't it?

text.Migrant Laborer (orange seeq on lower de: ... Leave me be! I'm in no mood for talk ... Urph! I've a touch of airsickness ... Please boy, just leave ... me be ... Ooorph!

text.Merchant (Airdeck): Do you think it's because of the reconstruction in Nalbina? All these seeq and bangaa onboard, I mean. It's not helping me relax, I'll say that.

text.Boonswaggled Bookkeeper: I thought I'd contracted to be a keeper of books, but somehow they changed the agreement ... they expected me to do heavy labor at the fortress! I don't know how, but they cheated me. I can't work out under the sun like that ... I won't! What was I to do but run and hide?

text.Bohemian: You've heard of Theodora the Highborn, I presume. The epic tale of romance and intrigue set against the backdrop of Nalbina Fortress. To think, I'll soon walk the halls and byways of the novel! I cannot wait!

text.Migrant Laborer (blue seeq on upper deck: Had the most vivid dream that I was thrown into the dungeons at Nalbina, my body wastin' away to nothin'. Ever since, I've walked the true path, on my mother's soul! Just thinkin' on that dream is enough to keep me honest.

text.Troubled Passenger: No one ever said it would be easy earnin' a livin', but there are limits to what a man can take ... How many times have I left the crews in Nalbina. ... How many times have I gone draggin' myself back. Man can't live without gil in his pocket.

text.Migrant Laborer (green bangaa at back ba: Nalbina may be hot, but heat I can stand. If there's gil to be had. It's this dungeon talk what has me worried. I mean really ... dungeons? Who ever heard of a city with dungeons? Straight out of a mummer's farce, that. Hope I don't regret this ... .

text.Traveling Merchant (Sky Saloon): Friend o' mine was sent off to Nalbina. A petty offense – ought to have been able to pay a fine and be done with it. Turn of ill luck. Luckily he managed to get out, somehow. Saw him toiling away last time I was passin' through Nalbina. Better an' rottin' in a dungeon.

text.Saloon Steward: Interest you in a frothy mug o' scuttlebutt?

CHOICE.Saloon Steward: One Nalbina, comin' right up! Truth be told, I don't have fond memories of that place. I'd just crossed the deserts, not a gil to my name ... barely made it there alive. A pretty girl found me, brought a skin of the finest water I'd ever drunk. Like an oasis on my lips, it was.
Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

text.Chief Steward Binastre: How may I help you, sir? We have cabins available, if you would like to rest until we make port. Would you like me to show you to a cabin?

CHOICE.Chief Steward Binastre: Let's see ... Vaan, was it? You'll be staying in cabin A-31. I hope you've enjoyed your journey.
Don't hesitate to ask again, should you change your mind.

text.ACTION: Lowtown

text.Vexed Father: My daughter won't listen to a word I say. Before I'd say "behave like the knights of the Order," but after what Basch did, that's out of the question. In fact, I was just tellin' another fellow this as he passed – had a tangle of a beard, filthy clothes – he just let out a sigh and kept walkin'.

text.Rabanastran (tan seeq wandering open eas: Licenses aren't just for equippin' new weapons and castin' new magicks, y'know. They can also make you a better warrior. Take the Remedy Lore licenses, for instance. Each one of those you get lets you use a remedy to cure more and more ailments. Not bad, eh? Probably best to strike a balance between licenses for equipment and magicks, and those with more direct, if not subtle, effects.

text.Well-spoken Boy: We live at the whim of the Empire. If the mood takes them, they can force us to do whatever they like. The masters of our destiny.

text.Angry Woman: What's that? I'm a little on edge, at the moment. How can anyone relax, forced to live in a place like this? You heard about the ambush Vayne set for those thieves, I'm sure. If we get on the wrong side of some Imperial, the same will happen to us.

text.Deadbeat: Lowtown ... Yeah, I like Lowtown. You got your South Sprawl in the south, and ... where are we again? Oh, right, the North Sprawl. Saw a man scoldin' his daughter over near the stair to the East End the other day. Don't know why I remember that ...

text.Milha: The poor little guy. What am I going to do?

text.Furious Bangaa: Pah and fie! Blast those Imperials! They may say we're all citizens good and proper, but not all citizens are created equal, apparently. Whenever there's been mischief, "round up the lizards by the tail," they say. Us? Lizards!? Bah!

text.Wandering Woman: Before I realized that the North and South Sprawl met in two places, I ran around in circles for hours. But not today! I have my map. Due south from here and I can take the passage up to Southgate. I think I find my way better with a sky above me ...

text.Northon: I saw a real familiar lookin' man walk past just a while ago, and it's killin' me I can't remember who he is. Had an unkempt beard ... you know him?

text.Impoverished Man: Back before the war, I led a fine life up in the city. (snort) I hate to think of them using my wealth to strengthen the Imperial army.

text.Rabanastran (man in blue sitting against: The Imperials smashed the lock on Migelo's storehouse back when those thieves snuck into the palace. It's been open ever since.

text.Fussbudget: No fair ... She saw Vayne arrest those thieves, and I didn't get to see a thing! She didn't see who they caught, though. All those Imperials kept gettin' in the way.

text.Dalmascan Patriot: People have high hopes for Vayne, but I'd say they're being rather naïve. It takes more than well-meant words to rule a city.

text.Cynical Boy: The people that live up in the city don't care what happened before, so long as they're good and comfortable now. Vayne tells 'em what they wanna hear, and they eat it up. He probably has 'em goin' on about how great he is already.

text.Rabanastran (seeq sitting next to boy): Vayne, Vayne ... Oh, that new consul what just come? The whole lot are the same to me. (snort)

text.Laughing Seeq: What's so funny? Just saw a man with a beard you wouldn't believe! Didn't look half bad on him, neither. (snort) Hah! A refugee, maybe ... who can say? Had a few other people circlin' him in. They disappeared down the halls up north.

text.Balzac: Look, uh, now isn't the best time, okay? Things are a little ... tense. If you need something, come back in a little while, once things have settled down.

text.Well-spoken Girl: Vayne's manner disgusts me. Laying a trap for the anti-Imperials as he did. Who knows who'll be the next person to fall into one of his traps. I know there are many in Lowtown who would like nothing more than to see Rabanastre rid of the Empire. Hope they have an eye for traps ...

text.Resolute Boy: I remember when you could get up to Westgate through that door, but it's broken now ... Bet the Imperials did that, too.

text.Samal: I can't believe he's still alive ... Sorry, just talking to myself. Promise me something, would you? No matter how hard things might get, never give up. So long as you don't give up, there's still hope.

text.Awestruck Girl: See that man squattin' down talkin' over there? They say he used to be a sky pirate! He always seems so calm and in control. But there was this one time he seen someone, and his face went white as a sheet. You'd think he seen a ghost.

text.Traveling Merchant (South Sprawl): One of my regulars had an unexpected guest drop in. Weird fellow, couldn't quite place him ... Anyway, you here to buy somethin', kid?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Guileless Girl: Sometimes I play down in the alley what leads up to Southgate. Yep.

text.Layabout (South Sprawl): So there was this weird man, and this group a tough-lookin' guys came up and took him off somewhere. Smells pretty funny to me.

text.Fidget: Vaan, is that you? It's been so long I hardly reco'nized ya! Did something happen?

text.Filo: Arr, Vaan! Haven't spied you 'round the city in a long time. Kytes and me were startin' to wonder what happened to ya! You seem the same as ever. You here to see Old Dalan? We're tryin' to solve a mystery. There was this suspicious guy – er, bloke – before. We wanna work out who it is.

text.Guileful Boy: I saw some people pushin' this scruffy-looking man around a little while ago. Looked like they didn't want to be seen. What's that all about? I just hope everything's all right ... Maybe Old Dalan knows somethin'.

text.Resigned Boy: If the Empire's protecting us, it must mean they think we're important enough to protect, right? Otherwise why would they bother?

text.Frustrated Man: I barely make enough to get by, but I should count myself lucky. Some of my friends, they can't even find work.

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: After seeing the Imperials capture those thieves, it hit home how easily any of us in Lowtown could be rounded up and taken off, if they wanted to.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, blue and gre: If you ever need to hear a kindly word, Old Dalan, is always willing to give advice to those who ask.

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): Haven't seen you around in a while ... Somethin' happen to ya? Old Dalan sure did seem worried.

text.Old Dalan: Well, well. Look who we have here! Heard you were sent off to Nalbina?

text.Vaan: And I got out of there as fast as I could. But it was all worth it, Dalan. Here, look at this!

text.Old Dalan: My, my, my. Quite a treasure you've got there.

text.Vaan: Well, you know, I couldn't have done it without your help.

text.Old Dalan: So, there is more to this gutter-churl than first meets the eye. Vaan, I've an errand: a simple favor to beg of you. I was going to ask that Kytes to go, but I should think that you ought to do. No – no I think you're just the one. There's a fellow by the name of Azelas, and I need you to bring this sword to him.

text.Vaan: That's – that's a sword of the old Order.

text.Old Dalan: Speak my name when you arrive. That should be enough to get you in to see him. I've made a note on your map showing you where he can be found. Mind you, you are to deliver the sword to him personally.

text.Vaan: I will. Hey, Dalan? Could I get you to do something for me? I need to find out where Penelo is. I wanted to show her what I got from the palace, but I haven't been able to find her anywhere. Can you let me know if you hear anything?

text.Old Dalan: You can just leave that to me.

text.Vaan: Thanks, Dalan.

text.ACTION: Vaan walks away.
aside

text.Old Dalan: And so it is done. But will it be enough to remind him of what the Order once meant?

text.ACTION: You obtain a Sword of the Order!

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): Old Dalan write something on your map? I wanna see!

text.Rabanastran (woman at left): Dalan may be old, but he's no fool. When he asks you to do something, you can be sure he has his reasons.

text.Old Dalan: Well, m'boy? The mark on your map not big enough for you? I should think you know the North Sprawl well enough, no?

text.Vaan: I'm supposed to deliver something to a man, name of Azelas. This is the place, right?

text.Balzac: And who was it told you that?

text.Vaan: Old Dalan. He said I have to give this to him personally.

text.Balzac: Does nothing get past that Dalan? He has ears in every wall. All right, get inside. But not a word of what you see or hear in there, you got that?

text.ACTION: In the room beyond, a group of men in fairly piecemeal armor are having a heated discussion.

text.Man 1: Then what of Ondore's proclamation? Did they fool even the Marquis?

text.Man 2: What if a Judge killed the King, not the Captain? That would explain everything wouldn't it?

text.Man 3: Then the Captain would be brother to a Judge! How are we to trust such a man?

text.ACTION: They are interrupted as Basch emerges from another room, now clean, groomed, and dressed properly.

text.Vossler: Now there is the Basch that I remember.

text.Basch: Then will you fight again at my side?

text.Man 3: His word alone convinces me of nothing!

text.Man 2: I'd take his word over that of a mouthpiece marquis!

text.Man 4: Then you name Reks liar with him.

text.ACTION: Vaan shoves his way into the circle indignantly, silencing the men.

text.Vaan: My brother was no liar!

text.Basch: Just the opposite. Reks was the witness they needed. They had to make it appear as if I'd killed the King – Reks bears no blame. The Fates have willed it.

text.Vossler: So this is Reks's brother.

text.ACTION: Vossler takes the sword from Vaan's hands

text.Vossler: Your words may convince this child, but they weigh too lightly on the scales for my taste. Our paths will remain separate.

text.Basch: Do you not think Amalia worth saving?

text.ACTION: This seems to give Vossler pause.

text.Vossler: I hold men's lives in my hands. I must see foes in every shadow. The night we moved against Vayne, he knew. I will not chance such disadvantage again. I must treat you as I would Ondore – as I would treat any abettor of the Empire.

text.Basch: Then what will you do? Hold me here in chains?

text.ACTION: Vossler and Basch lock eyes menacingly for a moment. Then Vossler tosses the sword to Basch.

text.Basch: Some things never change. Do they.

text.Vossler: Listen to me, Basch. Your cage may have no bars, but it is a cage. The eyes of the Resistance watch unblinking.

text.Basch: Let them watch. I know something of cages.

text.ACTION: The scene fades out, and then fades back in on Vaan and Basch outside the building, in the alley in Lowtown.

text.Vaan: That's right ... Amalia's in the Resistance.

text.Basch: Then you know her.

text.Vaan: Sort of. We met just before we got sent to Nalbina. I've known nicer people.

text.Basch: Our paths keep crossing, yours and mine. It's more than coincidence.

text.Vaan: It's annoying.

text.Basch: I'm sorry. Allow me one last annoyance: a favor to ask. I want you to take me to Balthier. Even caged birds need wings.

text.Vaan: This makes us even.

text.Basch: Even?

text.Vaan: For Nalbina. We couldn't have done it without you.

text.ACTION: Basch joins the party!

text.Balzac: I overheard you and Bas - your friend - talking. Trying to find some transportation, eh? Well, with money or the right connections that would be easy enough. You might try looking up in the city for someone headed the same way as you.

text.Careful Listener: A fancy-lookin' guy and a viera? No, I haven't seen anybody meets that description. You try Old Dalan yet? Seems like if anybody like that walked by, people would remember. Hm ... How about askin' around in the Southern Plaza? Anybody what comes through the city has to go through there ... maybe somebody saw somethin'.

text.Laughing Seeq: A sky pirate, eh? Why would someone who lives up in the clouds want to spend time down in this cellar? (snort) Hah! Maybe you shouldn't be so quick to agree to help find people when you don't know where they are. Might try askin' around the city. (snort)

text.Imperial (by east end entrance): What's that? A viera and a man walking together? ...Ah, yes. Yes, I think I may have seen who you're after. They went into the merchants' district.

text.ACTION: When you approach the Sandsea, a cutscene will trigger.

text.Vaan: A lot of kids lost their parents in the war. Mine – mine had already died before that. The plague took them both.

text.Basch: I'm sorry. I didn't know.

text.Vaan: It's okay. It's been five years now. After that, I lived with my friend Penelo and her family. Then ... Then the war came.

text.Basch: I am sorry.

text.Vaan: You don't have to keep apologizing. Really, it's all right. I know it wasn't your fault. I see that now. You didn't kill my brother. It was the Empire. My brother trusted you. And he was right.

text.ACTION: When you go up to the balcony, another cutscene triggers.

text.Balthier: As I said, a misunderstanding.

text.Migelo: Misunderstanding? What I am understanding is they took Penelo because of you!

text.Vaan: What? What about Penelo?

text.Migelo: Oh, Vaan! They've taken Penelo! And there was a note – a note for this Balthier! Come to the Bhujerba mines, it said.

text.Fran: It's Ba'Gamnan. He was in Nalbina.

text.Migelo: If anything were to happen to that sweet child – why, I've her parents' memory to consider! You're going to go to her aid, and that's that! It's what you sky pirates do, isn't it?

text.Balthier: I don't respond well to orders. You do know that the Imperial fleet is massing at Bhujerba?

text.Vaan: Fine, then I'll go! You at least have an airship, don't you? Just get me there, and I'll find Penelo myself.

text.Basch: I'll join you. I have some business there as well.

text.Balthier: An audience with the Marquis, by chance?

text.Vaan: Balthier, just take us and this is yours.

text.ACTION: Vaan brandishes the glowing stone from the palace.

text.Fran: The gods are toying with us.

text.Balthier: Make yourselves ready. We leave soon.

text.Vaan: Right!

text.ACTION: Balthier and Fran join the party!

text.Balthier: Ba'Gamnan's note can only be referring to the Lhusu Mines in Bhujerba. We'll leave at once. When you're ready, meet me in the aerodrome. I should imagine it's still by the west gate ... We weren't in Nalbina all that long. Do be quick. I'd like to save your girl and be rid of this headache as soon as possible.

text.Bucco: Hey, Vaan? I heard ... I heard Penelo was kidnapped. It's not true ... is it?

text.Kytes: Migelo's finally back, but Penelo still hasn't shown up. I hope everything's okay.

text.Rabanastran (man talking to red bangaa): Migelo's here all right, but is it me, or does he seem a little tired today?

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink headscarf): Migelo showed up, but he paid hardly any attention to my questions. I wonder what's on his mind.

text.Migelo: What a terrible thing to have happened! You've got to see that Penelo gets back home safely, Vaan!

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue and green on so: Oh, Vaan! I heard all about Penelo bein' kidnapped. You're gonna go rescue her, right? I know there's nothin' I can do to help her, but I'm sure you can do it, Vaan. I just know it!

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Westgat: Hey, I just heard that Penelo was kidnapped ... I sure hope it's some kinda joke. But what if it's not? The other day she seemed really down, and now this ... I'm worried.

text.Balzac: Sorry, but I can't let you back inside. Outsiders such as yourselves would only be in the way. You and Captain Ronsenburg would do well to keep from drawing any unwanted attention. Avoid using your real names and you should be safe enough. Few people are like to recognize you by your face alone.

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): Friend of mine ran into a viera out in front of the Sandsea. I dunno what exactly happened, but he sure thinks it's a big deal.

text.Rabanastran (woman at left): A sword of the Order of the Knights of Dalmasca ... Why give this to you now, of all times?

text.Old Dalan: I was just about to look into this Penelo business, and – what? Kidnapped!? So you're off to the Lhusu Mines with this sky pirate then, are you? Why, that's in Bhujerba ... Can he even be trusted? No time to worry over that now ... Listen to me, Vaan. You must hurry to Penelo. And be careful. Careful for both your sakes.

text.Fran: Balthier is waiting inside. If you've made ready, we can leave at once. He feels responsible for what has happened to your friend. Do not think he is in the habit of doing favors.

text.Balthier: Bhujerba's on the sky continent of Dorstonis, and the magicite mine we're looking for is in Bhujerba. If we're going to save the girl, we start there. You ready to leave?

CHOICE.Balthier: You do realize that once we've left, you may not see Rabanastre for a while. Once we leave, there'll be no looking back.
We make for the Lhusu Mines in Bhujerba. Seems I took on more baggage in Rabanastre than I'd planned ... Well, let's save your girl and be done with it. Come on.

CHOICE.Vaan: Let me check one more thing ...

CHOICE.Balthier: Don't take too long. We leave soon.
Don't take too long. We leave soon.

Don't get out of Dalmasca much, do you ... Bhujerba is a small city-state that thrives on the export of particularly fine magicite. It's ruled by Marquis Ondore, who, by staying in the Empire's good graces, has managed to stave off Imperial invasion.

text.ACTION: Balthier, Fran, Basch, and Vaan all walk into an aerodrome hangar. Vaan exclaims, "whoa."

text.Balthier: This is the Strahl.

text.ACTION: We get an overview of the airship.

text.Balthier: She airship enough for you?

text.ACTION: Vaan, still gawking, shoves past Balthier and runs up to get a closer look.

text.Vaan: The Strahl ... you really are a sky pirate!

text.Balthier: Well, the headhunters seem to think so.

text.ACTION: to moogle emerging from airship

text.Balthier: What's the good word? Is she ready?

text.ACTION: The moogle salutes with tool still in hand. He and his crew pass by the gang as they leave.

text.Vaan: So is she armed? How fast is she? Could she take the Ifrit?

text.Balthier: I suppose I could tell you, but wouldn't you rather see for yourself?

text.ACTION: He beckons to Vaan from the doorway before disappearing into the cockpit with Fran and Basch. With alook like he can't believe his luck, Vaan follows them. Balthier and Fran take the pilot and co-pilot's seats and start up the ship with practiced movements.

text.Balthier: Fran, our course.

text.Fran: The shortest way is over Dorstonis.

text.Basch: How flies Bhujerba?

text.Balthier: Oh, she's free as can be – for now. The Empire took notice when they announced the Princess's unfortunate suicide and your untimely execution.

text.Basch: If it becomes known that I am alive, the Marquis will lose their favor.

text.Balthier: I try to steer clear of such things.

text.ACTION: to all, as the engine crescendos

text.Balthier: Right, it's time to fly. And no wagging tongues, or you're like to bite them off.

text.ACTION: Vaan and Basch take their seats.
thinking

text.Vaan: I'm coming, Penelo.

text.ACTION: A hatch opens above them, and the ship lifts into the air. Once clear of the hangar, the back wings spread, and it shoots off into the sky.
In a room somewhere, Penelo sits on the floor, bound. Voices are heard and a couple of bangaa emerge from a trapdoor.

text.Ba'Gamnan: You've seen to her feeding, yes?

text.Rinok: I have, my brother. She eats well.

text.Ba'Gamnan: See that she does. We need her alive. Balthier's bait must be fresh.

text.Penelo: I keep trying to tell you, I barely even know who Balthier is!

text.ACTION: No sooner does she say this than a third bangaa pops up through the trapdoor.

text.Bwagi: My brother! A message come from Rabanastre! The Strahl, she's set sail! She leaves straight for the Skycity of Bhujerba!

text.Ba'Gamnan: Barely know, was it? Yet at a trice, he goes boundin' off for you! Tell me, how could that be?

text.Penelo: That's what I'd like to know! I just met him that one time and that's it!

text.Ba'Gamnan: Does that tongue never stop? What if we ... plucked it from your head? As for you, we need Balthier alive! His corpse fetches but half the bounty!

text.Rinok: There's no fun in it if we can't tease out a scream or two!

text.Penelo: Where are you?

text.ACTION: The scene fades on Penelo looking up at the sky through a small window near the ceiling.

A short cinematic follows showing the Strahl flying through the clouds, and the clouds breaking to reveal a massive floating land, with buildings and spires jutting from the green trees. One building in particular is spectacular with what look like giant feathers billowing from its sides.
The scene changes again to show Vaan, Balthier, Fran, and Basch entering the aerodrome, where Imperial soldiers seem to be in a tizzy.

text.Balthier: Easy.

text.Imperial: No good, he's not here.

text.ACTION: The Imperials run off. Balthier and co. proceed out of the aerodrome.

text.Balthier: You're a dead man. Don't forget it. And no names.

text.Basch: Of course.

text.Street Kid (near window): Haa, that was a shock! I was watching airships fly back and forth, when an Imperial grabbed me from behind! He was looking for someone. Not me!

text.Street Kid (sitting on luggage): Amba and Tatah, they are too worried, I think. Why do we need so much luggage, just to go on a trip to Rabanastre?

text.Bhujerban (moogle with orange pom-pom wa: Bhujerba's airships use a lot of mooglecraft to fly so well. They're a good deal better than those heaps the Empire lurch about in, kupo! Just goes to show, it takes more than gil to make the best ships in the sky, powered by the best magicite to be had anywhere!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom Aer: There're lots of moogles living here in Bhujerba, kupo. After all, it's mooglecraft that's made this place what it is!

text.Imperial (pacing nearest docent's counte: Apologies, but we're having some difficulties. All scheduled airship services are suspended. There is nothing to see here. Move along.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Svagatam, traveler. Welcome to Bhujerba. All of us are here to ensure your safety on the streets. Speak to us should you have any troubles.

text.Bhujerban (man sitting on rail speaking: Why can our civilian craft not fly just because the Empire says so, bhadra? I've filed official complaint, but I fear nothing will come of it.

text.Traveler (blonde man in blue): When exactly is my airship going to take off? It's hours past the scheduled departure time ... Can't these provincials tell the time?

text.Bhujerban (moogle with yellow pom-pom by: Oh noes! I was shopping and I missed the flight for Rabanastre, kupo! Suppose I'll have to wait.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler. Welcome to Bhujerba. We parijanah guides are appointed by the Marquis himself to aid visitors to our fair city. Once you leave the aerodrome, you will find yourself upon Travica Way, the main thoroughfare of Bhujerba. Good journey, bhadra.

text.Imperial (running around entrance/exit a: By order of the Imperial army, all airships are grounded. Passengers are asked to wait until further notice. Understood?

text.Traveler (man in Archadian clothes leani: A generous helping of my countrymen out on the street today. Not such an odd sight in Archadia or our colonies ... but wasn't Bhujerba neutral?

text.Balthier: The Lhusu Mines are just up ahead. Though, I do hear there's not much left there these days.

text.Larsa: You're on your way to the mines?

text.ACTION: The party looks in the direction of the speaker to see a boy perhaps a bit younger than Vaan and Penelo leaning on the wall. He hops down and approaches them.
