text.Bhujerban (moogle with orange pom-pom wa: The Leviathan? Kupo! That's just a showboat. You want real quality, you gotta look at the Bhujerban ships! Moogle-made, kupo!

text.Bhujerban (man sitting on rail speaking: They have given priority to the Imperial fleet, so all of our airships are behind schedule. Kastam ... How can this be permitted?

text.Traveler (blonde man in blue): Now that the Leviathan and her fleet are in dock, they're holding my airship grounded. My lack of luck is astounding. Simply astounding!

text.City Parijanah: Haa ... Master Basch fon Ronsenburg! I would kindly request that you refrain from such reckless displays in the future. One never knows where the Empire's spies are lurking, here in Bhujerba.

text.Traveler (man in Archadian clothes leani: Did you chance to see the Leviathan and her fleet? One look at that'd be sure to send the Rozarrians back where they came from! Hmm? Ah, don't worry, Bhujerba's safe from harm.

text.Bhujerban (man in turban and green short: For hundreds of years, our magicite mines have made Bhujerba very rich indeed. Her history and culture are more than a match for Archadia's!

text.Bhujerban (woman in white pacing up and: The airships often pass beneath this bridge. How often I have seen a great Archadian warship pass and wanted to throw a stone down at it.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Last night, the 8th Fleet of the Imperial army docked here, along with the flagship Leviathan. That many ships ... in one fleet of how many?

text.Bhujerban (man in blue, red, and green w: Is it true that Captain Ronsenburg lives? If that is so ... why, it would mean Marquis Ondore has deceived us! He is in league with the Empire!

text.Bhujerban (woman in white sitting on wal: Did you see the great fleet come from Archadia? My son, he rejoiced to see so many airships at once. But I ... I was frightened.

text.Bhujerban (tan bangaa walking up and dow: That Marquis, he's no fool. So why does he let the Empire station soldiers here? Sure, there's not many of 'em, but you ask me, even one's too much.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: You have the look of a man who loves architecture. You have seen the great wings of magicite that unfold from Marquis Ondore's estate? They are a symbol of our prosperity, made by special means known only to our builders.

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Travica Way): Ondore's residence? It's up these steps here and to the left. Though a commoner such as yourself isn't like to be granted admission. Not when Imperial citizens are being turned away!

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! Welcome! I am a parijanah, a guide. May I be of assistance? Haa ... it is you. You are aware that His Excellency's ties to the organization are not public knowledge. Please, be discreet. Good journey to you, bhadra.

text.Street Kid (Travica Way): Amba, she always says the raksas Diabolos will come and take me away to the mines. When amba and tatah were little like me, the Diabolos came and took away all the children with hats. Now, it sleeps among the stones, they say. It is a silly story.

text.City Parijanah: The armorer just over there is the finest in Bhujerba. I highly recommend a visit, bhadra. You may find something out of the ordinary. Good travels to you. And, young Captain Ronsenburg, please, try to remain as discreet as possible.

text.Bhujerban (woman in white sitting on cra: Is it true that Captain Ronsen-boori-boori – I cannot remember the name – the captain thought dead is, in fact, quite alive? I recall quite clearly at the end of the war the Marquis announcing that this captain had, indeed, been executed. Very odd.

text.Bhujerban (man sitting on crates outside: My wife, she goes often into this shop of weapons. For many hours, she does not come out. We have no need of so many weapons!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: No, it is not a hard life here, bhadra. The guides, the parijanah, they help the travelers find their way. We merely stand and are content with peace.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! I am a parijanah, a sort of guide to our wonderful city. Down this slope lie the Khus Skygrounds, a beautiful vantage point befitting of a skycity. And ... I beg you to remain discreet about our operations here. Good journey to you, bhadra.

text.Bhujerban (tan bangaa pacing boulevard): Sounds like the Imperial fleet's weighed anchor at last. Never seen such an armada as that ... Good thing we're not at war with them.

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: I give the Marquis credit for not bowing to the Empire ... but he should know that if they wanted it, Bhujerba would be theirs or no one's ... just like Nabradia ...

text.Bhujerban (green-pommed moogle sitting o: If we moogles weren't keeping the mining machinery here running, Bhujerba's economy would founder! That's why we're privileged citizens here, kupo.

text.City Parijanah: That magickery has only recently opened its doors, you see, but already it is quite famous. The staff there are all most pleasant. Take care that the girls there do not fill your head with murkha rumor and gossip. Good journey to you, bhadra.

text.Lost Archadian Wayfarer: To tell the truth ... I'm quite lost. I suppose I could speak to one of these guides, but it is quite beneath me to ask provincials for assistance ...

text.City Parijanah: Traveler! May I be of assistance? Haa, it is you! I trust your days of making ... trouble are ended? If you have time, may I suggest seeing the sights of beautiful Bhujerba? For example, down this slope you will find the Khus Skygrounds, a most recommended scenic spot. Good journey to you, bhadra.

Svagatam, traveler. Down the stairs to the west you will find the Khus Skygrounds, scenic pride of our Bhujerba. ... Might I also remind you to keep your knowledge of our organization to yourself. Good journey to you, bhadra.
Svagatam, traveler! This is a shop of armors! This is ... haa! You are the one! The one making all the noise! Please, restrain yourself. Shocking!

text.Shop Clerk (Rithil's): Svagatam ... (yawn) My son, he tells me to ... to leave the work to him. But ... (yawn) I must do my part, yes.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, trav – Ah, it is you. I hear you have spoken with our leader directly. Very bold of you, bhadra, very bold.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in turban and blue shor: I came all the way from Nalbina to make some gil working the mines, but with the closings, and now the monsters, I haven't worked a day!

text.Lhusu Miner (man in brown shorts examini: The depths of Lhusu are a nest of foul raksas. A paling there was to keep the creatures at bay, yet it has fallen, and they run wild, bhadra.

text.Bhujerban (woman talking to seated man): The Lhusu Mines have been closed a long time now. If the sale of magicite stops, will the Archadians not attack in anger?

text.Lhusu Miner (man standing in line at cou: Svagatam, traveler! Welcome to the finest armory in Bhujerba. Kah? No, no, I do not work here. I'm merely enthusiastic, you see.

text.Bhujerban (woman browsing weapons on upp: Haa ... I wonder if there is a weapon that I, too, might use? The Marquis has kept the peace a long time, but it is best to be prepared ...

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler. Or should I call you Captain Ronsenburg? Please, speak to no one of the Marquis's ties to our organization, yes?

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom): Pilika, over on the stairs there, works at Clio's Technicks, kupo! But she's always loafing! Should I tell Clio, kupo? I couldn't! I couldn't!

text.Street Kid (in yellow, with mother kneel: Amba, she is in a most foul mood! She says to me, "My son, do not honor the Marquis, for he abandons his people." I do not understand.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Do not speak of this elsewhere, but in truth the Bhujerban army is quite weak. They are given arms but no training! The Empire fears us not at all.

text.Bhujerban (man in blue leaning on ledge): The Imperial army buys a mountain's worth of supplies, my friends in the markets tell me. Perhaps they prepare for a great battle?

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink, blue, and red: To tell the truth, bhadra, once I sold trinkets and the like here. But I did not care to sell to them, the Imperials. So I closed my stall.

text.Street Kid (in blue, on ledge): One of the Imperials, he played with us. He was a nice man. He said his children, they play in the same way in Archades.

text.Bhujerban (black bangaa walking about): Why does Bhujerba supply the Imperial army? It is simple. We ingratiate ourselves with them, and thereby buy shelter from the storm!

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler. Up the steps here you will find Travica Way, our main boulevard ... And watch what you say!
Svagatam, traveler. Welcome to this fine shop of quality magicks, newly opened. Here shall you find all you need to prepare for your journeys.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: I am a rakis guard of the watch, stationed here. Of late, I, too, desire to study magicks. Due to recent troubles ... not to the lovely staff here, no!

text.Bhujerban (man bent over inspecting shel: Haa ... Can one such as me truly learn magick? And ... does it really matter? I am only here for the lovely staff, you see. Do not interfere.

text.Shop Clerk (woman in pink and blue with: Please, feel free to ask should you have any questions about our magicks, bhadra. Interest in magick is high these days! It is a good thing to see!

text.Bhujerban (man in blue on upper level): Until a short while ago, this shop was, in fact, a tavern, you see. Hungry, I came here to find that now it sells magicks, not food. Haa ... If only they had a magick to make the old tavern reappear!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: There is no anti-Imperial "Resistance" in Bhujerba, bhadra. Not only we guards, but the parijanah guides, too, watch for such activities.

text.Miners' Ender (man in green and brown sh: Have you heard? The mines are closed. They say that raksas run wild within! Strange, since there have always been raksas in the mines ... They have never seen cause to close the mines before. Perhaps a creature most foul has come?

text.City Parijanah: Greetings, I am a parijanah ... I am new to this posting, and I have heard a most curious rumor. They say the Dalmascan captain who died has come back to us, and now he runs through the streets of Bhujerba! Murkha! I believe it not.

text.Bhujerban Guru (Miner's End): Now I hear that those ill-favored bangaa were the headhunter Ba'Gamnan and his crew ... Who were they after, I wonder?

text.Miners' Ender (moogle with orange pom-po: The creatures in the mines, they came through when the mine's paling fell, kupo! We built that paling ... it was strong. Very strong! (gulp)

text.Miners' Ender (man in white turban and d: The Marquis, he trades the best Stones to the Empire, and so avoids their wrath ... Without magicite, Bhujerba would be lost.

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink top and hea: I have received a letter from my friend in Rabanastre. She tells of the new consul. He sounds quite the gentleman!

text.Miners' Ender (guy sitting on ledge next: An intruder in Marquis Ondore's estate? Haa ... . Surely one of the Resistance seeks to kill the Marquis. Too friendly he is with the Empire.

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink, blue, and: I have heard that the Judge who came to our mines was no mere Judge, but a high Judge Magister! Why, there are only a dozen or so of these.

text.Lhusu Miner (Bhorta): Bhadra, have you heard that this Ronsen-boobi, this captain, lives? He is the one who killed the Dalmascan king for bowing to the Empire, no? Now, here is a man with backbone! Bhorta likes!

text.Miners' Ender (green-pommed moogle sitti: When I think of Bhujerba, I think of sloping roads and high, high walls. The walls protect the buildings from the winds, kupo! We would not enjoy the Khus Skygrounds or the Kaff Terrace so much but for the opportunity they afford us to escape the city walls, kupo.

text.City Parijanah: I have heard that the 8th Fleet of Archadia goes now to Dalmasca! Perhaps they think to show their Leviathan off to the Rozarrians, haa?

text.Lhusu Miner (black bangaa yelling at moo: Moogle! You are coming down at once! Yes, you will pay for what you have taken! Moooooogle!!!

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink, blue and y: Even those who dislike the Empire keep their thoughts to themselves after seeing the great Leviathan. It is like an awakening to reality.

text.Lhusu Parivir: Mine's closed, and won't be opening anytime soon. Best return my Site 3 key to the Staras residence 'fore I forget. Mmmmnnrgh.

text.Miners' Ender (moogle in gold with orang: So, so many hills in this town, don't you think, kupo? But, 'tis worth it for our freedom! Maybe. Do, do they have hills in Rabanastre? (pant)

text.Lhusu Miner (man in dark shorts sitting: I do hope the mines will open again soon. I am a miner, you see. We who dig the Stones must be ready for raksas attacks, to fight them as one. That is why we frequent Bashketi's Gambits!

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink leaning aga: The Stones in the market of late are of quite low quality. The best magicite is being bought up before it can reach most buyers, I know it! Hanta ... I do hope this does not tarnish our Lhusu mine's reputation.

text.City Parijanah: Haa, the false captain. If you are to imitate another in the future, I would hope you try a little harder in your imitation.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Haa? The Lhusu Mines? They are closed, bhadra. It was the paling within the mines that fell, I hear. It is too dangerous for entry now.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in green and brown shor: There are those who would tell you that the small amount of Stone taken from the Lhusu Mines is on account of our laziness, but this is a lie, bhadra! The Marquis, he will not permit us to mine, with Imperial inspections, and raksas running wild, you see? That is all.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler. Welcome to Clio's Technicks. This shop is run by the Bhujerban Alliance of Moogles, B.A.M.! For quality, it's B.A.M.!

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Clio's): Did you see the 8th Archadian Fleet, pride of the Empire? My brother rode on the Leviathan, but they left as soon as they came. I could not meet him after all.

text.Shop Clerk (moogle in red with green pom: Oh, if there's anything you need, anything at all, don't hesitate to ask, kupo! Our staff are here to help you help yourself!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Up ahead is Kaff Terrace, famed spot of Bhujerba. You are the one who caused the disturbance in town, yes? You will behave in my jurisdiction!

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! Here on Kaff Terrace, witness the most ... haa. The young Master Ronsenburg. I am glad you live. Please, stay away from the edge.

text.Bhujerban (black bangaa): A traveler, are you, bhadra? If heights frighten you, I recommend you turn to your right and make for the Khus Skygrounds. Your heart will soar!

text.Bhujerban (man in red, green, and blue t: These islands in the sky, they are called "purvama," you see. The purvama upon which Bhujerba rests, Dorstonis, is the largest.

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom wal: Psst. Did you know that the first to live here on Dorstonis were moogles!? Bhujerba grew thanks to our skill at building, kupo!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with yellow pom-pom si: When I'm feeling sad, I come here and gaze out at the big, big, sky. When the clouds clear away, kupo, so do my worries!

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink, green, and tan: Sometimes, the cargo ships come to this terrace. Just now, a ship carrying magicite from Lhusu left, bhadra.

text.Bhujerban (light blue seeq at left of st: Did you see the Imperial fleet!? I've not seen a ship the size o' that Leviathan 'fore now. That were impressive, that.

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: The great edifice you can see ahead is Marquis Ondore's residence. House Ondore traces its ancestry back to the time of Raithwall, you see. Compared to House Solidor ... ayi, it is like comparing a fine Bhujerban Madhu to Archadian swill!

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink and blue top wi: Haa ... There are so many gambits! I wonder if there is one to improve my husband's cooking?

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown in Gam: I know the Empire needs the magicite from Lhusu, but we are a free people, bhadra. I would not have them telling us what to do!

text.Miners' Ender (woman leaning against wal: I overheard the Imperials speaking, and do you know what they have said? They are taking the best magicite to Rabanastre, and from there ... It goes to the laboratories of the Empire! Do you not think it curious, bhadra? Why not take it straight to Archades?

text.City Parijanah: Ahead and to the left you shall find the great Lhusu Mines. But, take care, for it is a place of considerable danger these days. I recommend a stop at Miners' End to outfit yourself before venturing inside.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: With mining halted in Lhusu, so halts the flow of Stones to the Empire. Will they stand and allow this state of affairs to continue? I think not.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in green and brown shor: The mines have stopped. It is because those men from the Empire came, I am sure of it. I can only hope they will reopen in due course.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! Just up these steps is Travica Way, where one can find Mait's Magicks, and some very lovely young – Ah, it is you. I must ask that you refrain from such displays, young Master Ronsenburg. I cannot guarantee that a tavern visit will be the worst that befalls you next time.

text.Cloudborne Resident (woman talking with: Inspectors from the Empire, a Judge no less, and the entire 8th Fleet in port ... Is Bhujerba nothing more than an Imperial colony? I fear a life in seclusion on Bur-Omisace may be the only path left to people like me ...

text.Cloudborne Resident (man sitting on crat: The Leviathan and her fleet came to Bhujerba quite recently. Many goods did they buy. "Out, Empire!" I say, "but by all means leave your gil!"

text.Cloudborne Resident (tan bangaa in green: Some fool thought to trespass upon the Marquis's estate. Such rudeness! He was given to that Judge, I hear. The last we will see of him, no doubt.

text.Bhujerban Guru (Cloudborne Row): Do you know the leader of the parijanah guides, Havharo? Very mysterious, very handsome ... and very friendly with Melisa at the Cloudborne.

text.Cloudborne Resident (moogle in gold with: The Cloudborne ... den of mystery and danger! How thrilling, kupo! Well now ... which door to go in through today? Choices, choices ...

text.Cloudborne Patron (man standing beside c: Witness the fate of one who drinks unwisely. Rivers pass across his tongue, but he tastes not a drop! A waste of good Bhujerban Madhu, that.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Why is it that so many come to our fine city only to drink their sorrows away? Many these days from Rabanastre, there are. The yoke of Empire must make men thirsty.

text.Cloudborne Resident (woman in white lean: If Captain Basch is alive, then does this mean the Lady Ashe, too, still lives? But then, why would the Marquis lie to his own people?

text.Cloudborne Resident (tan seeq with turqu: You say Captain Ronsenburg lives? Pah! Pigswill spread by the Empire. They hope to erode our trust in the Marquis! I wish them luck.

text.Cloudborne Resident (tan bangaa in green: If it is true that this Basch of Dalmasca lives, then the Marquis fed his own people lies! He is nothing but a puppet of the Empire.

text.Cloudborne Resident (man in turban and g: This is but a back alley, yet of late I see many travelers wandering here. Perhaps the parijanah do not do their job well?

text.City Parijanah: Many of our people question the Marquis for working with the Empire, but I know the man. His own people's criticisms are but a shield to blind the Empire's eyes from the truth, you see.

text.City Parijanah (talking to red bangaa): If it is directions which you wish, bhadra, ask another parijanah. I am off duty. I am always off duty, you say? Is this a problem?

text.Cloudborne Patron (man leaning on bar, s: Have you seen it, bhadra, the giant Leviathan? And the Empire has many more like her. Bhujerba could not hope to war against that.

text.City Parijanah (with blue jacket): Do you know the biggest fools in Bhujerba? It is the Imperials, bhadra. You see, many of them are country folk from Valendia. Haa, the prices our vendors charge them! It is quite humorous ... Of course, if they took too much, it would cause problems. This is why we recommend some restraint.

text.Cloudborne Patron (blue seeq at bar): Have you tasted the spirit known as Bhujerban Madhu? It is a local favorite! Only reluctantly do we allow outsiders to drink it. Of course, now the Imperials are here buying it up, there is little left for us! Kastam!

text.Shop Clerk (woman in green, pink, and br: Bhujerban Madhu, you want? Well, keep searching! Those Imperial murkha have taken every last drop, bhadra! And Magu, does he work? No! Hanta ...

text.Shop Clerk (moogle with green pom-pom): We've quite run out of Bhujerban Madhu, kupo ... So very, very sor – Erm ... you're too young to drink anyway, kupo! And there I was apologizing ...

text.Cloudborne Patron (man in white shorts s: If you seek posted bills for hunting marks, you can find them at the far end of the tavern, bhadra. Be warned: there is much competition. Why, I have even heard of camps where hunters gather who think such marks sport! Professionals, they are.

text.City Parijanah (talking to woman at tabl: Though I do not know for certain, the day will doubtlessly soon come when I am to leave here and join our organization's efforts elsewhere. Before that day, I would have an answer of my love ...

text.Chief Steward Chezelle: Ladies and gentlemen, allow me to welcome you aboard on behalf of the East Ivalice Company. Your captain for our voyage is Mr. Erbna, with Mr. Ardinne his first officer. I am Chief Steward Chezelle. We have cabins available, should you wish to retire for the remainder of our journey. And please, let me know if I may be of any service.

text.ACTION: All other dialogue here is the same as the Nalbina to Rabanastre Flight.

text.Chief Steward Chezelle: Ladies and gentlemen, allow me to welcome you aboard on behalf of the East Ivalice Company. Your captain for our voyage is Mr. Erbna, with Mr. Ardinne his first officer. I am Chief Steward Chezelle. We have cabins available, should you wish to retire for the remainder of our journey. And please, let me know if I may be of any service.

text.Excited Bangaa: I ain't never been good with heights. So why is it business always sees me headin' to Bhujerba? The Fates have a sense o' humor, don't they?

text.Machinist: No interruptions! No interruptions! We're discussing plans for our next airship design. We've just come from an inspection of an airship-yard in Archades, kupo. Should it be of Archadian design, built for speed? Or should we place soundness of build first, as we have in the past? No easy choice, kupo.

text.Traveler (Observation Parlour): You killing time, too? My friend's asleep in his cabin. Can you imagine, wasting time sleeping on a voyage like this?

text.Clumsy Bangaa: Get lots of moogles working as airship machinists. I been trying for that myself, but my hands are too big to handle some of the finer parts.

text.Imperial: Don't be gettin' too friendly with the fairer members of the crew, boy. Don't want you gettin' in the way of their work.

text.Deck Swab: We're the cleaning crew, kupo. Been at this job since we were young, and there ain't no one does it better. Just look at that deck, kupo!

text.Machinist: Could I have your frank opinion on something, kupo? What do you think of this airship?

CHOICE.Machinist: Kupo ... Nothing special? Really? Most interesting. We can't beat them for speed, but perhaps that's not the only thing that matters ... Kupo ... I thank you for your time. Kupo!

text.Traveler (guy on stairs): You see that moogle walking around? I think he's an important machinist. He was asking me what I thought of the airship. Rather clever, blending in with the passengers to find out what they really think.

text.Traveler (woman in blue on upper deck): My daughters are women grown now. 'Tis as though I travel with my own sisters! The children grow up so very fast ...

text.Traveler (woman in green and blue on upp: I'm happy to travel with my mother, though I hate having to leave my husband alone at home.

text.Storekeeper: My wife and son will be meeting me at the aerodrome. Business has kept me from home ... too long. It will be good to see them again.

text.Mischievous Boy: Hehe, that oughta do it ... Y-You shouldn't sneak up on people like that! Th-Those could be anybody's initials!

text.Saloon Steward: Interest you in a frothy mug o' scuttlebutt?

CHOICE.Saloon Steward: One Bhujerba, comin' right up! Not many free cities left these days, but the skycity, she's one of 'em. Sky pirates take to her like ducks to water. Those floatin' islands are home to whole flocks of sky pirates. Used to be I was one of 'em. Ha! So long as we didn't cause no trouble, Marquis Ondore was willin' to look the other way.
Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

text.Traveling Merchant (Sky Saloon): Balms and tinctures sell good, but not so good as magicks. And then not half as good as magicite! Off to Bhujerba to lay in a supply of the finest magicite I can get my hands on. There's huge gain to be had sellin' the stuff in Archades.

text.Traveler (Sky Saloon): My sister and I keep a small villa just outside Bhujerba. We're on our way there now. Haven't been on holiday in ages. It'll do us good!

text.Bhujerban (man leaning against counter): Have you come to book passage on an airship, friend? Each counter serves a different destination. Pay your fare there. If a given counter is empty, that route is not currently in service, but give it some time and it should open again.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Westgat: Hey, Vaan. Penelo's with you now, right? Phew! What a relief! I know we can count on you to keep her safe, no matter what happens!

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue and green on so: I was so worried about Penelo, I couldn't even work. But thanks to you, everything's back to normal again! Heh, heh.

text.Rabanastran (boy squatting down and hugg: I heard all about how you saved Penelo, Vaan. You're practically a hero!

text.Bucco: What's that? Penelo's with you? Phew! I guess all that talk about her bein' kidnapped was just talk. I was worried for nothin'.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink headscarf): I've heard the Imperial Fleet was gathering near Bhujerba. Do you think they were spying on Dorstonis?

text.Rabanastran (man talking to red bangaa): Migelo had been sulking about for a while, but he finally seems to have cheered up. Not sure why, but I'm not complaining.

text.Migelo: Ah, Penelo! You're all right! Those sky pirates got you tangled up in some nasty business. What!? Don't tell me you're off running about with those sky pirates, too! Vaan I can understand, but you, Penelo? ... Ah, I see. I suppose I have been a bit over protective of you. It's time you made your own decisions, your own mistakes. Do as you feel you must. Whatever trouble you might get yourselves into will only make you stronger, I'm sure. Yes, yes. When you want to come back, you've only – No, no, you go about your adventures until you decide for yourselves it's time. And until then, don't worry yourselves about the shop or any of your friends. Just leave all that to Migelo, you hear? Now that that's decided, we should get down to business. If you'll be traveling, you'll be needing sundries, yes? Well, sundries we have!

Keeping busy, are you, Vaan? You needn't worry yourself about the store. I won't be closing just because you aren't around. No, there are plenty of other hard-working youths to pick up your slack. Off with you now! We'll be here when you get back.

text.Sotted Imperial: What're you starin' at? Come to have a good laugh, have you? Blast that rumor ... The whole bloomin' town's talkin' about it ... But they've got it all wrong. I was given orders to stand watch at this shop. That's why I don't get over to the Sandsea as much as before, right?

text.Tavernmaster: That Imperial's finally left the place ... and good riddance! Can finally get some peace 'round here. That's what people come to the Sandsea for!

text.Barkeep (woman on balcony): We won't be seeing those Imperials around here anymore. The Consul's implemented a new policy to see the watch behave as they're meant to. I don't think any policy will help that one Imperial, though. I hear he's off hiding somewhere, in his cups as usual.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: His Excellency has given orders that you are to be granted an audience. You are prepared?

CHOICE.Bhujerban Sainikah: Then please come this way, bhadra.
Then, please come back when you are prepared.

text.Ashe: When Vossler learned my father had been killed the night of the treaty-signing, he returned to Rabanastre to aid my escape. There was still time before Vayne's reach extended too far. We thought that you could protect me.

text.Ondore: However, when I made the announcement that you had taken your own life ... I must have seemed a model citizen of the Empire. The announcement, you see, was Vayne's suggestion. At the time, I was reluctant, but I could not perceive his reasons. Now it is clear: he meant to drive a wedge between us.

text.Ashe: Halim, we are past all this. Bhujerba must stand with us. We can stop Vayne.

text.Ondore: I once knew a girl whose only wish ... was to be carried in her uncle's arms. Your Majesty is a woman grown now.

text.Ashe: Then Bhujerba will aid me?

text.Ondore: Suppose for a moment that you were to defeat Vayne ... What then? You cannot simply rebuild your kingdom with the only proof of your birthright stolen. The Gran-Kiltias on Bur-Omisace cannot recognize you as the rightful heir without it. You may yet be a princess, but without proof of your identity, you are powerless. You will remain with me. We will do nothing till the time is right.

text.Ashe: I cannot just wait!

text.Ondore: Then what does Your Majesty propose we do?

text.Ashe: Uncle Halim –

text.Balthier: Incidentally, what is the going rate for rescuing princesses these days? Food would be a good start – the good stuff, mind you.

text.Ondore: This can be arranged, though it will take some time.

text.ACTION: As Balthier lists his demands, Ashe walks away as if in a daze, disappointed. Vaan watches her go.

text.Balthier: Time enough for a bath, I hope. Dirty business, you know. Ah, best bring a change of clothes too.

text.ACTION: The scene fades to black. Fade in again on the Strahl docked in the Marquis's private hangar. The camera switches; we are looking from the point of view of someone seemingly sneaking up on someone else who is sitting at the controls, messing with the buttons.

text.Vaan: What are you doing? This is Balthier's ship.

text.ACTION: Ashe, in the pilot's seat, turns her head in his direction.

text.Ashe: I'm going to retrieve the Dawn Shard. It's the proof that I need. I know where it's hidden. I'll return his airship later.

text.Vaan: Are you crazy?

text.Ashe: This is something that I have to do! For myself and all those who have fallen. I will not be made to hide! I'll fight alone, if I must.

text.Vaan: You still have Basch, right? Besides, you can't just go around stealing people's ships. What are you trying to do?

text.Ashe: I'm trying to concentrate!

text.Balthier: That's quite enough, Your Majesty.

text.ACTION: Ashe and Vaan turn. Balthier stands in the doorway with a device, like a microphone of some sort, held up to his mouth.
still vaguely in Ondore's voice, thanks to the device

text.Balthier: What do you think? A bit over the top? In my line of work, you never know when something like this might come in handy.

text.ACTION: in Ashe's voice, over the device

text.Balthier: I'm trying to concentrate!

text.ACTION: Pause, as Balthier approaches the two.

text.Balthier: I'm leaving you with the Marquis.

text.Ashe: You can't.

text.Balthier: Trust me, you're better off staying here.

text.ACTION: Balthier turns to leave, but Ashe's next words stop him in his tracks.

text.Ashe: Suppose you kidnapped me instead? You're a sky pirate, aren't you? Then steal me. Is that so much to ask?

text.Balthier: What do you have that I would want?

text.Ashe: The Dynast-King's treasure. The Dawn Shard is but one of the riches that lie waiting in King Raithwall's tomb.

text.ACTION: whistles and turns to face Ashe again

text.Balthier: King Raithwall, you say?

text.ACTION: Suddenly Basch enters the bridge.

text.Basch: Kidnapping royalty is a serious offense. It won't do much to lower the bounty on your head.

text.Balthier: How much is the price on your head these days, I wonder?

text.ACTION: to Ashe

text.Basch: Allow me to escort you in Vossler's place.

text.ACTION: Fran and Penelo also appear in the doorway.
to Vaan

text.Fran: Will you be joining us?

text.Vaan: What, are you kidding? I don't wanna stick around this place.

text.ACTION: Penelo runs to take a seat immediately behind Vaan.

text.Penelo: Then I'm coming too.

text.Vaan: Penelo?

text.Penelo: Don't leave me here!

text.ACTION: sighing

text.Vaan: Of course not.

text.ACTION: to all

text.Fran: Then it's settled. We should leave before the Marquis realizes she's missing. Like proper kidnappers.

text.ACTION: The scene fades to black, then fades in again on a grand city.
Archadian Empire – The Imperial City of Archades

A short cinematic shows an overview of the great Imperial City, and the tower, its largest structure, in the center. A carrier craft lands at a port on the tower, and we see Basch's Judge twin departing it and entering the tower.
The view switches to a grand drawing room draped in the colors and insignia of the Empire. Emperor Gramis is having an audience with the same Judge, who has his helm off.

text.Gramis: Doctor Cid does this at Draklor?

text.Gabranth: I have confirmed he receives funds from Lord Vayne. His agency in the fall of Nabudis is also certain ... yet, with Judge Zecht, who led the assault, missing ... the truth remains difficult to ascertain.

text.Gramis: The long, cold years have clouded my eyes. I cannot see my own son's heart.

text.ACTION: Suddenly, Gramis is taken by a coughing fit. The Judge appears concerned.

text.Gabranth: My Lord.

text.ACTION: recovering

text.Gramis: This illness will claim me. So then, who is to be my successor? The Senate fears the capable peregrine Vayne. They prefer a young, fledgling emperor.

text.ACTION: Pause

text.Gramis: Gabranth. Once in the past, I laid siege to your homeland.

text.Gabranth: The Republic of Landis is long since gone. My allegiance lies wholly with the Empire.

text.Gramis: Perhaps, but what of your brother? He did not accept us as you did. He fled to Dalmasca. Did you never think to follow him?

text.Gabranth: I follow his every move. He is an enemy of the Empire. He will be cut down.

text.Gramis: So you would kill even your own brother for the Empire. Be that as it may, Gabranth. Your ruthlessness is not without merit. But it must not become this way with Larsa. You must ensure that it does not.

text.Gabranth: So then, you ask me to be his sword, to strike where he might not?

text.Gramis: Rather be his shield. Gabranth, keep your close watch on Vayne. His is the keenest blade of all.

text.Gabranth: My Lord.

text.Gramis: Do this for me, Gabranth. I could not – I could not bear ... to see my sons war with each other again.

text.ACTION: Scene fades to black.
Open again on the desert, where the Strahl, floating above the party, suddenly becomes invisible. Vaan and Penelo look on with great interest.

text.Ashe: This "come in handy" often?

text.Balthier: It's tough being popular. Wouldn't want admirers dropping in while we're away.

text.ACTION: to all

text.Balthier: Well then, that's as far as she goes. We'll be in jagd from here onwards.

text.Ashe: Across the sandsea, to the Valley of the Dead. And to King Raithwall's tomb below.

text.ACTION: In the background, Vaan is explaining something to Penelo. Balthier, Fran, and Ashe turn their attention to them with some interest.

text.Vaan: So when you're in jagd, skystones don't work at all. That's why we gotta hoof it the rest of the way, ya see?

text.Penelo: Happy you get to teach me something for a change?

text.Vaan: Well, if you wanna be a sky pirate, you have to know your – Hey! What do you mean, "for a change"?

text.ACTION: aside

text.Balthier: At least we thought to bring entertainment.

text.ACTION: Ashe puts her forehead in her hand exasperatedly.

text.Wayward Bangaa: (sigh) I'm about at the end of my rope. I was crossin' the desert makin' for Rabanastre, when a sandstorm hit. Got all turned around. Which way you headed?

CHOICE.Wayward Bangaa: West, eh? Out to the Yensan Sandsea? That ain't this way. Better turn yourself around. For that matter, maybe you oughta rethink headin' west at all. The Sandsea makes the desert look like a sandbox. Easy to lose your way.

If you're goin' east, you must be headed for Rabanastre. I'd love to join you, but I'm too exhausted to think about it right now. I tell ya, I had a time gettin' here. Didn't know where I was or where I was goin'. You get caught in a sandstorm, you be careful.

text.Imabakk: Nearly lost my tail to a trap once. Ever since, I been sure to use Libra to spot any traps good and early. Told that to my pal here, he says, "Oh, you can float right over traps without setting them off." Never thought of that ...

text.Lohen: Don't let the desert sun get the best of you. If you're low on supplies, now's the time to stock up.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Lohen: If you're westward bound, travel lightly, boy. Not all the races you'll meet in the Sandsea are the civilized variety. And mind the weather. Nice, clear days, the elementals come out in droves. Don't want my customers dying ... bad for business!

text.Nono: Don't you worry about the Strahl, kupo. I'll keep an eye on her. No, wait! Both eyes!

text.Arjie: Well, hello! The wary traveler never passes the chance to restock his supplies.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Arjie: We will leave before the Rains come. If there's anything you want to buy, now's the time.

text.Nutsy: Be careful during the Rains, kupo, it draws out the lightning balls. I think they're elementals, but I'd avoid them, whatever they are.

text.Tott: Didya see? The dark crystals out on the plains are all glowin' again. Time to make sunstones! You wanna make sunstones, too? You should talk to my mom. She's over in front of that biiig crystal.

text.Camina: Normally you can go down to Kerwon through Giza, but the Rains washed up a tree what's blockin' the path. Maybe the next Rains what come'll wash it away?

text.Roaklo: Seems like everythin's costin' more these days. I gotta have more money if I'm gonna buy anythin'. Would you, uh, talk to my sister for me?

text.Nanau: I sent my little brother to Rabanastre to buy a few things we needed, but he spent all the change before coming back. Can you believe it?

text.Elder Brunoa: Giza Plains has two seasons, the Dry and the Rains. I don't smell rain on the air ... I'd say the Dry ought last a while longer. You look like you're getting swept up in something big, boy. See it doesn't sweep you away, eh?

text.Lesina: Have you heard? They're saying the Princess is alive! And I'd thought she committed suicide ... I'm not sure what to believe anymore. Those people in the city like nothing more than to gossip, don't they.

text.Jinn: I like goin' out into the plains. That's why I never really think of makin' sunstones as work. Well, I like the plains in the Dry, anyways. The monsters that come out during the Rains are too scary.

text.Masyua: Don't often get visitors in this heat. What is it?

CHOICE.Vaan: Can you tell me about sunstones?

CHOICE.Masyua: Did you notice the dark crystals? They again shine with light. No small thanks to the fine weather we've enjoyed these past days. Are you interested in making some sunstones?
There, now you've the shadestone you need. Fill it with the light of the dark crystals and return when you've made a sunstone. I pay well for stones of high grade!

You've made one before, yes? So the process should be familiar to you. You'll take a shadestone to the shining crystals of the plains and fill it with their light. That's your sunstone. The energy gauge will show you how much light the shadestone has absorbed. When the gauge is full, your work is done. Once you begin, you should stick to the task. If you leave the plains before you finish, any energy the shadestone has stored will be lost. The dark crystals of the plains wax and wane with light — a measure of the sun's own fickle nature. Are you clear on how to make a sunstone?
Well, you seem eager. Ready to make a sunstone?
I pay well for stones of high grade. I wish you luck!
You're always welcome, if you change your mind. We pay well for stones of a high grade, should you need a few extra gil.
You're always welcome, if you change your mind. We pay well for stones of a high grade, should you need a few extra gil.
Jinn and my son have been getting along just fine. A little friendly competition can be a healthy thing, really.

text.Masyua: Don't often get visitors in this heat. What is it?

CHOICE.Vaan: So, how do you make a sunstones?

CHOICE.Masyua: Take the shadestone I gave you to the shining crystals on the plains. When the energy gauge is full, the sunstone is ready. If you have trouble finding the crystals, stop and take a look around. Remember, I pay well for stones of quality.
Jinn and my son have been getting along just fine. A little friendly competition can be a healthy thing, really.

text.ACTION: After making a sunstone ...

text.Masyua: Don't often get visitors in this heat. What is it?

CHOICE.Masyua: I see you've made a sunstone. Interested in parting with it?
This is a sunstone of highest grade! You don't see many of these.
Should you change your mind, do let me know.
Jinn and my son have been getting along just fine. A little friendly competition can be a healthy thing, really.

text.ACTION: The Ogir-Yensa Sandsea

A short cinematic introduces us to the Sandsea; Vaan approaches the shores and reaches into the murky brownish waves, cupping some of the "water"; when he brings his hand back out, grains of sand are sliding off his palm. As he gazes at the sea, Penelo calls his name, and his reluctantly returns to the party,

text.Penelo: So, where exactly is Raithwall's tomb?

text.Basch: Far to the west. We must first cross the Ogir Yensa Sandsea. We must pace ourselves. If you grow tired, we stop and take rest.

text.Penelo: You don't have to worry about me. I'm tougher than I look.

text.ACTION: laughing

text.Basch: You are at that.

text.ACTION: Vaan looks inquiringly at the tanks around whose catwalks the party is navigating.

text.Basch: A construct to draw oil from the ground. Abandoned many years now, it seems.

text.Vaan: Did Dalmascans build this?

text.Basch: No. The Rozarrians. Their empire lies far to the west, ever at war with Archadia. Heedless of the kingdoms caught in their midst. Dalmasca. Nabradia. Landis.

text.Vossler: 'Tis the small craft's fate: to watch the list of the galleons and pray for light winds.

text.Basch: Vossler! Why are you here?

text.Vossler: Imagine my surprise ... when upon my return to Bhujerba, I find both you and the Lady Ashe have vanished. I thought you above consorting with sky pirates.

text.Basch: Balthier is a man worthy of our trust, and it was the Lady Ashe's decision. I am content to lend my arm. As I could not when Rasler died, when her throne was taken. Never again. I will defend her this time.

text.Vossler: You walk the knight's path. The Lady Ashe?

text.ACTION: Basch turns in response. Vossler follows his gaze to Ashe, and approaches her. Meanwhile, Fran and Balthier stand a short distance away, looking out on the Sandsea.

text.Fran: We should leave this place.

text.Balthier: Let me guess: sandstorm?

text.Fran: Something far worse.

text.ACTION: The camera switches to Vossler and Ashe.

text.Vossler: I see ... So the Dawn Shard does lie in King Raithwall's tomb. The Marquis sympathizes with your plight, yet the Empire watches his every move. He can keep whispers of your "abduction" silent for only so long.

text.Ashe: Yes, but tell me, Vossler, what have you accomplished?

text.ACTION: Balthier interrupts their conversation.

text.Balthier: We leave at once! This is Urutan-Yensa territory ... and they are unfond of visitors.

text.ACTION: Fran, noticing something, turns to look out over the sandsea.

Another cinematic shows something in the sea thundering toward the promontories where the party is located. Strange, insect-like humanoids in raggedy cloaks ride large fish like steeds through the sandwaves. One raises its scimitar and whoops, having scented the party. The others echo his battle cry.
The party is now off and running.

text.Balthier: Looks like we've attracted the wrong sort of attention. Let's quit this place while we still can. Move!

text.ACTION: Ashe and Vossler are still standing where they were; Vossler starts forward, but Ashe stops him by calling him.

text.Ashe: Vossler! Have you found the means to restore Dalmasca?

text.Vossler: First, we must claim the Dawn Shard. It all begins with that.

text.ACTION: Vossler joins the party as a guest!

text.Dyce: Oh? Unusual to see people out here ... We're trying to catch us some sandfish, but they're not biting.Dilah: Why have you come to such a place? You seem to be adventurers, yes ... Surely, you did not come to hunt treasure in the Valley of the Dead!Dyce: The Valley of the Dead? Treasure hunter or no, you'd best avoid that place. 'Less you care to tangle with an avion most fell! Speaking of which, you have all the equipment you need? The Yensan Sandsea's a vast place! If you need something, might be I can help you.

text.ACTION: shop menu
Before accepting or completing the Urutan Eater side quest ...

text.Dyce: Hail! You find your treasure? Heh ... no, there's little out there but shifting sand and hot sun ...

text.Dilah: Still, people rarely visit the sandsea ... A bit of sand might make a nice souvenir?

text.Dyce: What I want to know is, are you outfitted for the desert? I'm something of a merchant ... if there's anything you need, let me know!

text.ACTION: shop menu
After completing the Urutan Eater side quest ...

text.Dyce: You still gallivanting about – Eh? You've claimed a treasure of the Urutan-Yensa!?Dilah: Well, adventurer, there may be more to you than I thought. With that, you may just be able to defeat the avion.Dyce: Say, if you do find some treasure in the Valley of the Dead, send some this way, eh? Ha ha ha! Now, care to buy anything?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Sandsea Moogle: Did you see that Urutan-Yensa just now, kupo? They're usually a violent lot ... but this one wanted help. Interested?

CHOICE.Sandsea Moogle: The Urutan-Yensa are all up in a panic about a creature on the Nam-Yensa Sandsea ... their blood enemy, it seems! One of them was asking for help ... an Urutan Yensa asking for help! Whatever it is, it's got to be bad, kupo. You look pretty strong ... maybe you could have a swing at the thing, kupo? It's supposed to be something like a giant tortoise ... He said he'd found some treasure of the sandsea, too. Why, you might be able to claim that as a reward if you're successful, kupo.

text.Sandsea Moogle: If you defeat this beast, you could claim the treasure of the sandsea! Look for the tortoise, kupo!

text.ACTION: When you come back after defeating the Urutan Eater ...

text.Sandsea Moogle: You killed the wild scourge of the Sandsea, kupo!? Amaaaaazing! By the way, that Urutan-Yensa from before ... he just went by, kupo. Maybe he was going to look for that "treasure" for you? Unusually kind of him! He was headed for the Ogir-Yensa Sandsea ...
Were you off looking for a reward, kupo? Did you find the treasure of the Sandsea?
Just where is he going, kupo?

text.LOCATION: The Sandsea Moogle and the Rogue Urutan

text.Sandsea Moogle: Kupo! A gathering of the Urutan-Yensa! A truly rare occurrence, kupo!

text.ACTION: The Urutan who asked for help and a curious-looking Urutan, apparently a superior, appear to exchange words.

text.Sandsea Moogle: ... Kupo? Kupo-po!? Wait, what's happening, kupo!? Wait! No! They're going to execute him!

text.ACTION: The moogle runs through the crowd of Urutan to the Queen.

text.Sandsea Moogle: Don't do this! The creature would still be at large if it weren't for his plea for help, kupo!

text.Queen of the Urutan: You shame us by seeking aid outside the tribe! Urutan-Yensa are lords and masters of the great sea! We seek the aid of none!

text.ACTION: The Urutan appears to say something.

text.Queen of the Urutan: Your words are the howling of the sand to my ears! I condemn you to dust!

text.ACTION: The Urutan dissolves into a ball of orange-ish light.

text.Sandsea Moogle: (gasp) Wh-Wh-What have you done, kupo!? You bring him back!

text.Queen of the Urutan: Those who sully our name will be punished, be they foeman or kin. They must pay the honor-price. There can be no forgiveness! I would destroy you, too ... but I am merciful. Better you live to tell the world that the Urutan are not to be taken lightly. Now, leave!

text.ACTION: The Urutan Queen and the other Urutan with their Yensa mounts scuttle away.

text.Sandsea Moogle: That rogue Urutan ... he wouldn't have been happy back with his clan, I'm sure of it, kupo. That flower ... It's rare to see one blooming in the Sandsea, kupo. Maybe the treasure that he found ... was this?

It's rare to see a flower blooming in the Sandsea, kupo. And not just any flower! There's a particularly dangerous avion known as the "garuda" that's said to be quite unfond of this flower's scent, kupo ... A treasure indeed!

text.ACTION: A bunch of berries hangs from the flower.

CHOICE.ACTION: You obtain a bunch of Eksir berries!
The flower gives off an alluring, ephemeral scent.

text.ACTION: The flower has not yet berried.
If you didn't speak to them in the Yensa Border Tunnel ...

text.Dyce: Oh? Unusual to see people out here ... We're trying to catch us some sandfish, but they're not biting.

text.Dilah: Why have you come to such a place? You seem to be adventurers, yes ... Surely, you did not come to hunt treasure in the Valley of the Dead!

text.Dyce: The Valley of the Dead? Treasure hunter or no, you'd best avoid that place. 'Less you care to tangle with an avion most dire ... What I want to know is, are you outfitted for the desert? I'm something of a merchant ... if there's anything you need, let me know!

text.ACTION: shop menu
If youve completed the Urutan Eater side quest ...

text.Dyce: You still gallivanting about – Eh? You've claimed a treasure of the Urutan-Yensa!?

text.Dilah: Well, adventurer, there may be more to you than I thought. With that, you may just be able to defeat the avion.

text.Dyce: Say, if you do find some treasure in the Valley of the Dead, send some this way, eh? Ha ha ha! Now, care to buy anything?

text.ACTION: shop menu
If you haven't started the Urutan Eater side quest ...

text.Dyce: You still wandering these reaches? Time to give up treasure hunting, I'd say. The shining bird'll peck at your bones, boy ...

text.Dilah: Lo there, adventurer! If you're truly set ongoing to the Valley of the Dead, I'll give you some advice. The avian there is said to be invincible, but it has a weakness. I'm sure the Urutan-Yensa know something ... this Sandsea is theirs, you see.

text.Dyce: You can't just go giving people fool advice like that! What if they actually went out and tried to do it!? That'd be blood on your hands. That said, if anyone knows the way through the Valley of the Dead, it's the Urutan-Yensa. But how to ask ... ? They don't speak our tongue. By the by, you need anything? Take a look at my wares! You might just be surprised at what you find ...

text.ACTION: shop menu

Yet another short cinematic gives us sweeping views of the plateaus and canyons around the Nam-Yensa Sandsea. In one plateau, we see a place where the rock seems to have been perfectly cut out. In here is where the Tomb of Raithwall sits, a grand structure.
As the party approaches the tomb, a giant glowing bird descends from the skies.
After defeating the Garuda ...
The ancient device stirs.
As the group ascends the numerous steps to the entrance to the tomb, Ashe begins explaining the origin of the tomb; as she weaves the tale, we see images of King Raithwall.

text.Ashe: Long ago, the gods granted their favor to King Raithwall ... who would oversee the subjugation of a territory spanning from Ordalia to Valendia. Here he forged the Galtean Alliance. Though he is called the Dynast-King ... upon establishing the Alliance, he showed compassion for his people, and disdain for war. A philosophy passed on to his successors. One that would bring peace and prosperity for hundreds of years to follow. It was during this time of peace that the city-states of Archadia and Rozarria ... each members of Raithwall's Alliance, took root and flourished. Raithwall left three relics signifying descent from the Dynast-King. Of these, the Midlight Shard was given to what would become House Nabradia ... and the Dusk Shard to my ancestors, the founders of Dalmasca. The last of these relics was the Dawn Shard. It remained hidden here, known only to those of royal blood.

text.Vossler: As though the Dynast-King foresaw the very plight before us now.

text.Ashe: Only his descendants are suffered within. If we enter without proof of such lineage –

text.Balthier: There's no guarantee we'll make it out alive. Vicious beasts. Fiendish traps. Something like that?

text.ACTION: nods

text.Ashe: But you must consider the prize. The Dawn Shard lies within, and Raithwall's treasure.

text.Balthier: And there I was thinking this was going to be hard!

text.Dyce: You ... you killed the avion? Amazing! And this – I've never seen such a magnificent structure!

text.Dilah: It looks like some sort of tomb. The wealth it would take to build such a thing ... Think of the treasures it must hold!

text.Dyce: And a hoard of ravenous monsters, I don't doubt. Me, I value life over loot. I go no farther ... But, should you find something, I'm sure I could be persuaded to part with a few gil for it! And if you need aught, of course, I'm your man!

text.ACTION: shop menu
Magicks stir within this device.
The stone in the device glows, and the group disappears into thin air.
Hall of the Destroyer
In a flash of light, the group reappears on the interior of the tomb, dark, stony, and lit by torches.

text.Vaan: What was that thing?

text.Balthier: A contraption you'd find in all but the most rudimentary ancient ruin. One touch, and off you're whisked to you know not where. The finer points of their operation elude me, but they're handy all the same. What more need a sky pirate know?

text.ACTION: Way Stone: The device bears a timeworn inscription.

CHOICE.ACTION: These words have been left by the tomb-watchers: "With godscraft armed, guard we His tomb. Diad stirred, come they, one unto the other."
Nothing happens. There must be a corresponding device elsewhere.

text.ACTION: As the party descends to the corridor, the wall behind them comes alive with claws and starts crawling toward them.

text.Balthier: Fight or run, we better decide fast!

text.ACTION: In this room, the wall far, far to the front of them, at the head of the corridor, comes alive as well.

text.Fran: The wall comes. We must be quick! Together we can bring it down.

text.ACTION: The brazier bears a timeworn inscription.

CHOICE.ACTION: These words have been left by the tomb-watchers: "Wakes it with the flames. Follow it their shadow. Ne'er straying."
if first brazier in set of two
The Demon Wall halts its advance.
if second brazier in set of two
The Demon Wall hastens its advance ...

text.ACTION: Royal Passage

text.LOCATION: The Call of the Dawn Shard

text.ACTION: The party enters the next chamber, where we get a sweeping view of the immense tomb.

text.Penelo: Incredible ...

text.Vossler: It wounds me to look on as they pillage so solemn a place.

text.Ashe: Yet without help, you and I are as nothing. Is this not so?

text.ACTION: pause

text.Ashe: He thinks ever and always on his own profit. Assure him of it, and he shall remain true to our cause.

text.Vossler: I do not share Your Majesty's trust.

text.Ashe: We will continue this later. Now we should concern ourselves with finding the Dawn Shard.

text.ACTION: pause, as Ashe steps forward

text.Ashe: It sleeps, in waiting. Somewhere deep within.

text.Vossler: How can you be certain?

text.Ashe: I can hear its call.

text.ACTION: Examine the urn ...
You obtain a map of the Tomb of Raithwall!
Your location map for this area is complete!
Way Stone: Nothing happens. The device remains asleep.
Southfall Pedestal: A luminous beryline jewel is set in the pedestal.
After activating the pedestal ...
Way Stone: Magicks stir within this device.
Northfall Passage
Way Stone: Nothing happens. The device remains asleep.
Northfall Pedestal: A luminous crimson jewel is set in the pedestal.
After activating the pedestal ...
Way Stone: Magicks stir within this device.
Cloister of Flame
In the next chamber, the air seems to be distorted somehow, almost discolored.

text.Penelo: Fog? Underground?

text.Fran: Not fog – Mist.

text.Penelo: You can see the Mist? With your eyes?

text.Fran: Where it is thick enough, you may. The nether runs deep in this place.

text.Penelo: So, is the Mist dangerous?

text.Fran: Yes, but it is also an aid. A dense Mist allows the workings of powerful magicks.

text.Penelo: I'll keep that in mind.

text.ACTION: looking to Vaan a short distance away with Vossler and Ashe

text.Penelo: Can't count on Vaan to keep track of these things. That's for sure.

text.ACTION: At the bottom of the cloister, what appeared to be a statue, an almost ogre-like creature with a bright red mane, comes alive.
After defeating Belias, the Gigas ...
Belias collapses, then disappears in a whirl of flame. In its place a fiery glyph appears, twirling in the air a moment before dissapearing.
You obtained the Esper Belias, the Gigas

text.Fran: In vainglory they arose, shouting challenges at the gods. But prevail they did not. Their doom it was to walk the Mist until Time's end. A legend of the nu mou.

text.Ashe: My family tells a story of the Dynast-King and an Esper. The story goes that in his youth, the Dynast-King defeated a mighty gigas ... for which the gods took heed of him. Thereafter, it was bound to him in thralldom.

text.Balthier: So all this time it's been here guarding the Dynast-King's treasure.

text.Ashe: Not so. The Esper is the Dynast-King's treasure.

text.ACTION: surprised, and dismayed

text.Balthier: That's your treasure?

text.Ashe: In this Esper we now command rests a power whose worth is beyond any measure.

text.Balthier: Is that so? Call me old-fashioned, but I was hoping for a treasure whose worth we could measure.

text.ACTION: Way Stone: The way stone bears a timeworn inscription.

CHOICE.ACTION: "By this, return ye to the Hall of the Destroyer. By other means, return ye back to this place."

text.ACTION: Vossler appears troubled. Basch takes notice.

text.Basch: What's wrong?

text.ACTION: ignoring Basch

text.Vossler: Your Majesty, we must go.

text.ACTION: Ashe nods and approaches the pedestal slowly.

text.Ashe: What?

text.ACTION: Standing before Ashe is an apparition.

text.Ashe: Rasler ...

text.ACTION: It seems that Ashe and Vaan are the only two people out of the party who can see the apparition of Rasler. Rasler starts forward and descends the steps. As he passes, Ashe reflexively reaches out for his arm, and her hands pass through him. She watches him go with a pained expression, and catches her breath.

text.Ashe: You will be avenged.

text.ACTION: Rasler walks by the still ignorant party, save for Vaan, who looks up at Ashe after Rasler fades away. Ashe finds a purplish, glowing stone in her hand -- the Dawn Shard.
You obtain the Dawn Shard!

In another wordless cinematic, Vaan and co. are exiting the tomb and running out onto the sands of the Valley of the Dead, when they hear the sound. They look up to see the 8th Fleet of the Archadian army looming overhead, the Leviathan at the fore. Smaller ships are deployed and land in a formation surrounding the party.
On the bridge of the Leviathan, Ghis awaits them.

text.Judge Ghis: Such a tremendous honor to again be graced with your presence, Majesty. You left us with such great dispatch upon our last encounter that I must confess ... I had begun to worry that we may have given some cause for offense.

text.Ashe: Such a heartfelt display of remorse. Now what is it you want?

text.Judge Ghis: I want you to give me the nethicite.

text.Penelo: The nethicite?

text.ACTION: Penelo protectively grasps the nethicite from Larsa in her hands, behind her back.

text.Judge Ghis: That is a base imitation! We seek Raithwall's legacy ... the ancient relics of the Dynast-King: deifacted nethicite.

text.ACTION: pause

text.Judge Ghis: Did you not tell them, Captain Azelas?

text.Vossler: Majesty, he speaks of the Dawn Shard. That is the nethicite.

text.Basch: Are you mad, Vossler?

text.Vossler: If we are to save Dalmasca, we must accept the truth. I will fight this profitless battle no more!

text.Judge Ghis: Captain Azelas has struck a wise bargain. In return for the Dawn Shard the Empire will permit Lady Ashe to reclaim her throne, and the Kingdom of Dalmasca will be restored. Think on it. An entire kingdom for a stone. You must admit, 'tis more than a fair exchange.

text.Balthier: And when all is said and done, your master will have another pet.

text.Judge Ghis: Lady Ashe, let us take him for the people of Dalmasca. Your Majesty wallows in indecision on peril of their heads!

text.ACTION: Ghis draws his sword and holds it to Balthier's neck

text.Judge Ghis: And his shall be the first to fall.

text.Balthier: Well, at least your sword is to the point.

text.ACTION: Ashe hesitantly steps forward with the Dawn Shard in hand. Ghis lowers his sword and takes it from her; she sighs frustratedly as she lets it go.

text.Judge Ghis: To think the relics of the Dynast-King were deifacted nethicite. Doctor Cid will be beside himself.

text.Balthier: What did you say?

text.Judge Ghis: Captain Azelas, take them to Shiva. They should have leave to return to Rabanastre soon.

text.ACTION: The party is escorted out. Ghis turns to one of the ship crew with the magicite.

text.Judge Ghis: I want you to assess its power.

text.Male Researcher: Did our orders not specify that we return the stone for testing?

text.Judge Ghis: I will not chance returning with a Stone that is yet unproven.

text.LOCATION: Fran's Frenzy, and A Son of Dalmasca

text.ACTION: Another very brief cinematic shows the party being transported to another ship in the fleet.
The 8th Fleet of the Archadian Imperial Army – Light Cruiser Class Ship Shiva

text.Vossler: When we return to Dalmasca, we can announce that you are alive and well. I will then continue our negotiations with the Empire. I believe Larsa is the key. He'll listen to us. We should trust him.

text.Ashe: Who are you, Vossler, to talk of trust?

text.Vossler: A son of Dalmasca.

text.ACTION: On the Leviathan, the researchers place the Dawn Shard inside a glass capsule; the instant the lid shuts over it, Fran perks up as if she can hear it. The researcher explains to Ghis as the capsule locks into place.

text.Female Researcher: Our equipment here is limited, so we'll be using the ship's drive to make our assessment. Once we've connected the Stone, the reaction should be easily measured –

text.Judge Ghis: Methods do not interest me. Only results.

text.ACTION: On the Shiva, the party hears Fran begin to pant, and turn to her, concerned. She is doubled over, seething

text.Vaan: Fran?

text.Fran: Such heat. The Mist – it's burning!

text.ACTION: Back on the bridge of the Leviathan ...

text.Female Researcher: Sixty-eight hundred, sixty-nine hundred, seven thousand! This must be deifacted nethicite! The count still climbs!

text.Judge Ghis: We've found it at last: true deifacted nethicite. The power of the Dynast-King in my hands. Blood alone does not an emperor make, Vayne.

text.ACTION: A red light starts flashing; alarms go off.

text.Judge Ghis: What is it?

text.ACTION: Back to the prisoners - Vaan and Penelo stand over Fran, who is slumped over on the ground as if in pain.

text.Imperial: You! Stand!

text.ACTION: The Imperial is knocked back. Vaan and Penelo move away. Vossler makes a command to the other Imperials.

text.Vossler: Hold her down!

text.ACTION: Fran scrapes her claws against the floor, then jumps up with a scream and starts taking down the guards. The rest of the party is fiddling with their cuffs while the Imperials fall around them.

text.Penelo: What's wrong with her?

text.Balthier: I always knew Fran didn't take well to being tied up. I just never knew how much.

text.ACTION: to Ashe

text.Balthier: How about you?

text.Ashe: I like Fran's idea. Let's get out of here!

text.Vossler: No farther! Sky pirates! The future of Dalmasca will not be stolen!

text.ACTION: pause, as Vossler raises his sword

text.Vossler: Why do this, Basch? This struggle is futile. You must know where it leads!

text.Basch: I do know. All too well.

text.ACTION: After defeating Vossler ...
Vossler falls before Basch. Ashe looks on sadly from a distance. Back on the bridge of the Leviathan, all hell is breaking loose.

text.Researcher 2: Engine power falling rapidly. It's ... negative? Impossible! We cannot maintain hover!

text.ACTION: Ghis is looking about wildly, lost, while the researchers are abuzz.

text.Judge Ghis: I want to know what's happened!

text.Female Researcher: The nethicite's draining the ship's power!

text.Judge Ghis: Disengage it at once!

text.Male Researcher: It's inflected! She'll reach critical in three hundred! Cascade failure!

text.ACTION: Back to the party, who is scrambling to escape as the ship begins to shudder forebodingly.

text.Vaan: Ashe, let's go.

text.ACTION: Basch and Vossler are left alone.

text.Vossler: All I have done – I've ever thought of Dalmasca first.

text.Basch: I know you do. I would ne'er gainsay your loyalty.

text.Vossler: Look on what my haste has wrought. Did I act too quick? Or was your return too late?

text.ACTION: pause

text.Vossler: I can serve her no more. You must take up my charge.

text.ACTION: Basch finally leaves him. On the Leviathan, flames break out. Vossler, alone, looks up as a bright light erupts.

An implosion comes from the Leviathan, rapidly expanding outward, tendrils of mystic fire consuming all the ships gathered in the 8th Fleet. The party, in a Tonberry, is struggling to fly out of its range.

text.Balthier: This might get a little dicey.
Fran. The Mist. It manifests now.

text.Vaan: Is that what you call this?

text.ACTION: As they finally escape, and look back on the now dissipating fire around where the 8th fleet once was, Penelo sees something emerging from the Mists.

text.Penelo: What's that?

text.Ashe: I think it's the Dawn Shard.

text.Balthier: Then what are we waiting for?

text.ACTION: Balthier veers the ship around to retrieve the Dawn Shard as the scene fades.

text.LOCATION: Go to the previous chapter (Chapter 4: The Skycity of Bhujerba) | Go to the next chapter (Chapter 6: The Garif)
Go to Clan Primer | Go to Side Quests | Go to Intro & Key
Excerpt from Memoirs of Marquis Halim Ondore IV, Chapter 16: Biding Time

text.Ondore: The Dreadnought Leviathan is sunk. The 8th Fleet of the Archadian Imperial Army, lost.
As Word of the Events in the Jagd sounded throughout the Empire, quit I Bhujerba, citing sudden Malady.
My true Motive: to bring the various counter-Imperial Forces scattered throughout Ivalice together in unified Resistance.

By this Time, Lady Ashe had made her Return to Rabanastre. She had not, however, made known her Presence. Rather, she was content with keeping both her Whereabouts, and those of the Dawn Shard, concealed.
Had she chosen to go before her People, my Error in announcing her Suicide would be known, to the great Detriment of my Efforts to assemble a Resistance.
In such Circumstance as the Lady Ashe then found herself, even were she to proclaim Dalmasca restored, it would serve only to invite the Empire's Wrath.
Though Archadia had lost her 8th Fleet, she remained, as ever, a Military Power with which to be reckoned.

text.ACTION: Memoirs of Marquis Halim Ondore IV, Chapter 16: Biding Time
Another cinematic brings us back to the great city of Archades in the middle of the day. Hovering vehicles like cars zip between the gigantic buildings.
The Imperial City of Archades – The Senate
In a darkened room, hooded figures sit around a huge, round table. Emperor Gramis presides over them.

text.Senator 1: The Rozarrian Empire assembles a vast host under guise of martial exercises. It is our belief they wait for the proper pretext ... the sooner to make their strike against Archadia. The loss of Leviathan and her fleet at such a time comes as a most grievous blow. Were Rozarria to invade, the battle would be hard-fought. Had Lord Vayne not deployed the fleet so capriciously ... we would not find ourselves in such perilous circumstance.

text.Senator 2: Lord Vayne shall be made to answer for his actions. It is the will of the Senate. Excellency, though he be your son, justice must be served.

text.Gramis: A convenient thing, justice. And so I must now make a choice ... between my throne, and my son.

text.Senator 2: A most lamentable situation for us all.

text.Senator 3: Oh? For Lord Vayne, perhaps, yet surely Lord Larsa will make for a fine emperor.

text.Gramis: Larsa so adores his brother, and he is yet young.

text.Senator 1: But he will not remain young forever. Already he busies himself unraveling Lord Vayne's tangled skein. Lord Larsa has found his role to play, and pursues it with some enthusiasm.

text.Gramis: Ah, yes ... And who would set him at such tasks?

text.Senator 3: What matter? Lord Vayne himself once saw his elder brothers brought to like justice, did he not? At Your Excellency's behest, as I recall.

text.Senator 2: You may put yourself at ease, Lord Gramis. So long as the Senate watches over her ... Archadia's well-being will ever be ensured.

text.Gramis: By your will. I shall bid Vayne return to Archades.

text.ACTION: The scene changes to a grim, gray landscape, where Ashe stands at the edge of a half-formed wooden bridge, looking out over swampy, foggy waters. Sparse, mossy ruins are around her. When she turns, she sees the apparition of Rasler again, now standing beneath an arch not far from her. She approaches him, and he sets the Dawn Shard into her hands. She watches as he disappears. From beyond, Vaan comes walking toward her, looking at her curiously.
Ashe now sits in a sparsely furnished room, looking at the wedding ring on her finger. In the next shot we see Balthier is also present, as well as Basch, Fran, Penelo, and Vaan.

text.LOCATION: Basch: So it was the Dawn Shard which brought down the Imperial fleet.

text.Balthier: You know your stuff.

text.ACTION: A tag appears in the bottom right corner: The Royal City of Rabanastre – Four Days After the Sinking of Leviathan

text.LOCATION: Basch: Destructive power of such force – I've seen it once before. Lady Ashe, you know of what I speak.

text.Ashe: Nabudis.

text.LOCATION: Basch: The capital of Old Nabradia – Lord Rasler's fatherland. During the invasion, a division of Imperials entered the city – there was a mighty explosion. Friend and foe died alike. Something was there – one of the Dynast-King's relics. The Midlight Shard was in Nabradia.

text.Balthier: More nethicite. Well, no wonder they invaded.

text.ACTION: Ashe picks up the Dawn Shard from the table behind her. It's lost its color and light.

text.Ashe: That ridiculous war, the trap at the treaty-signing – all because Vayne wanted power. He must not be allowed to claim the nethicite. The Empire must never hold it.

text.Balthier: Oh? They already do. The Dusk Shard, most likely the Midlight Shard, too. Besides, can't they manufact nethicite now?

text.Ashe: Very well, then the path set before us is clear. We'll use the Dawn Shard to fight them! Dalmasca does not forget kindness nor ill deed done. With sword in hand she aids her allies. Sword in hand, she lays to rest her foes. This nethicite I hold must be my sword. I will avenge those who have died. And the Empire will know remorse.

text.ACTION: A long pause.

text.Vaan: You even know how to use it?

text.Ashe: I –

text.Fran: The garif may know. The garif people live by the old ways. Magicite lore is a part of their culture. They may hear it. The cry of the nethicite's power. Whispers of the Stone's menace.

text.Ashe: Dangerous though it be, what we need now is power. Should we declare Dalmasca free without the means to defend our claim ... the Empire would crush us. You must take me to meet with the garif.

text.Fran: They live beyond Ozmone Plain.

text.Balthier: Not exactly close.

text.Ashe: Compensation – is that what you want?

text.Balthier: Straight to the point, aren't we. I like that. Compensation?

text.ACTION: He gestures to her wedding ring

text.Balthier: How about the ring.

text.Ashe: This? Isn't there something else?

text.Balthier: No one's forcing you.

text.ACTION: Reluctantly, she takes her ring off, pauses again, and then finally drops it into Balthier's outstretched hand.

text.Balthier: I'll give it back to you. As soon as I find something more valuable.

text.ACTION: Disgusted, Ashe walks away.

text.Vaan: What do you mean "something more valuable"?

text.Balthier: Hard to say. I'll know when I find it. What is it you want, Vaan? What are you looking for?

text.Vaan: Me? What am I looking for? Well, I guess – well, I – you know ...

text.ACTION: Giving up, he follows them out the door.
The party find themselves out in the middle of the Bazaar. A map is overlaid on the screen as they discuss their route.

text.LOCATION: Basch: The garif are said to dwell in Kerwon.

text.Balthier: So they do. We'll need to head south, past the Giza Plains.

text.LOCATION: Basch: It is the Rains now in Giza - the wadis will be swollen with the deluge. Passage may be difficult.

text.Balthier: But those same waters may also lay open new routes to us.

text.Ashe: Regardless, we must go south, yes?

text.Balthier: First things first. You're eager to be on your way, I know ... but we should see that we're prepared before setting out.

text.Ashe: I made my resolve two years ago. I swore to overcome any hardship I may face.

text.Balthier: Man cannot live by resolve alone, princess.

text.Rabanastran (green-horned tan seeq): The guards were running about like mad the other day. I heard a rumor that it had something to do with the sinking of the Imperial Fleet. I haven't heard a word since. What do you suppose happened?

text.Reks's Friend: I couldn't help but overhear – you're leaving to find the garif? Well, I happen to know the way. You first need to pass through Giza Plains. From Giza, continue south, and you should come to the garif village. Whatever your errand there, good luck.

text.Rabanastran (man in white, yellow, and b: The other day I tripped and bumped into an Imperial. Normally I'd count myself lucky to get away with a harsh scolding. But he didn't even stop to look at me! Just ran off like nothing'd happened. I wonder what was going on to make him act like that?

text.Busy Messenger: The Rains have come to Giza. You'd be surprised how the land changes if you aren't expecting it. The boss has me mapping the place out. Hmm, anything useful? Well, the most important thing I found out is that the Rains opened a passage leading to Ozmone Plain.

text.Headhunter: Hey there. Hear about any juicy marks, boy? I'm looking for the parts what you need to make serpentwyne. Don't want to be beaten to the punch ... least of all by the likes o' you!

text.Traveler (Muthru): Vayne was scheduled to make an inspection of the Bazaar, but it was canceled for some reason. I wonder what could have happened?

text.Merchant (tan bangaa in blindfold): I thought about stocking wares from the village on Giza Plains, but then I heard it was the Rains – not a soul to be found there.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink and tan MB): The Bazaar is one of the few places in Rabanastre where people can go to let off steam. Can almost forget the constant watch we're under ... Almost.

text.Merchant (blue seeq at top of steps): Nanna cheese! Nanna cheese! Interest you in a wheel, m'boy?

text.Trader: I set off for the garif village to see about stocking some of their wares. But I got lost on the way and barely made it back. I'm fairly sure I had the right directions – south through the Giza Plains, then southwest across Ozmone Plain – but I didn't get very far.

text.Merchant (tan seeq to side of stairs): Out hunting monsters these days, are you? Better than your old "work" with the Imperials, I suppose, but still dangerous enough. Monsters fight just like me or you – they go after the one they hate the most, first. Like how we might go for a poisonous monster, you know? And there's nothing monsters hate more than healing. You remember that. It just might come in handy.

text.Patient Bangaa: My friend here's in the foulest of moods. "Moogle" this and "sluice gate key" that. He's goin' at it somethin' fierce.

text.Troubled Woman: Vaan? I haven't seen you around the city much these days. What have you been doing? Nothing too dangerous, I hope? I'm sorry ... it's really none of my business. But sometimes I think about Reks, and I get worried for you. Be careful, okay?

text.Rabanastran (woman in red, pink, and blu: Thanks to the work I found in the palace, I can afford to feed my younger brothers, and I even have a few gil left over for myself!

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on west sid: Went off to Giza Plains looking for work, but It turns out it was the Rains. Went all that way and didn't see a soul.

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: The other day I saw a bright flash in the sky off to the west, and a few hours later some wounded Imperials were brought into town. I wonder what happened out there ...

text.Traveler (North End): Apparently Vayne's been summoned back to Archades. I'm sure it will only be temporary, though. If not, what reason have I to remain in Rabanastre? Oh, I do hope he comes back soon.

text.Imperial (North End): I'm on watch. If you have no business here, kindly leave me be. I've enough on my mind with Lord Vayne breathing down our necks ...

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on east sid: I keep well away from trouble – haven't the stomach for it. If that makes me a coward, so be it!

text.Dispirited Woman: Turns out those rumors about the kingslayer being in Rabanastre were no more than that. A friend visiting Bhujerba told me she saw a kid running around saying he was Basch. Needless to say, he wasn't.

text.Rabanastran (dark brown bangaa in black: The city's prospects have taken a real turn for the better since Vayne became consul. I really underestimated that man.
