text.Riby: I had no idea Penelo had been kidnapped ... And to think, you were off rescuing her! I knew we could always count on you, Vaan!

text.Rabanastran (man in white turban and bro: I know that look. Reks used to have that same determined fire in his eyes. Whatever you may be thinking, don't do anything stupid, okay, Vaan? You owe it to your brother.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, yellow, and: Have you noticed the bangaa standing guard in front of the building just to the west of the bridge? I wonder what's inside ...

text.Rabanastran (woman in green and pink NE): I used to think all the guards were bad, but some of them actually care about the people they're protecting.

text.Helpful Man: Such a grand city ... Why, even the locals must need a map to find their way! You surely know your way around by now, though!

text.Greenhorn: When it really counts, nothing can replace giving each and every command without using gambits. Of course, it's nice to not have to worry about giving orders for every little thing. I suppose it really just depends on the situation ...

text.Adept Adventurer: Walking the Way of the Gambit is like climbing a mountain whose peak you cannot see. You climb and climb, but still the summit eludes you. Yet never have I thought to turn back. I seek the ultimate combination of gambits, one capable of accommodating any scenario. Such a thing might not exist, but I will not rest until I have found it.

text.Yamoora: Yamoora, at your service. Please, take all the time you like.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Johm: Ain't got nothin' to do. Ever since the parade, there aren't hardly any people visiting the city. A pickpocket's no good without pockets to pick!

text.Rabanastran (man in turban and brown sho: I haven't found a better way to make money than selling the loot and equipment I get from my hunts. If there is a better way, let me know!

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq pacing about): Migelo's back to his old jolly self again. Though he seems a bit ... wistful, I suppose is the word. Like a father whose children have flown the nest.

text.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): Hey, mister. You wanna hear about the history of Rabanastre? It won't cost ya much ... What? I gotta eat, too, ya know. Let's see ... 1 gil oughta do it.

CHOICE.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): Have you ever heard of King Raithwall? He's an ancestor of the Dalmasca family from a long, long time ago. "He was a leader of unrivaled wisdom, and a warrior of peerless fortitude." At least, that's what my folks told me. They say he even had a powerful gigas that had to do whatever he said, and that the gigas still guards his tomb to this day. I don't know if that part about the gigas is true or not, but it was somethin' mighty strong, anyways.
Well, not everyone's interested in that sorta thing, I suppose. Don't worry none.

text.Lonely Boy: I heard there're some kids down in Lowtown what wanna be sky pirates. Waste of time, if you ask me, dreamin' about something that won't never happen.

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: Hey, Vaan! I heard you're the one who saved Penelo from that lousy bunch of bangaa. You've really come a long way from hunting rats down in the sewers. Nice work!

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, blue, and gr: Have you heard? They say Vayne's being called back to Archades – that he may already have left. Do you suppose he's in some kind of trouble?

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa EE): The Imperial fleet en route to Rabanastre simply ... vanished into thin air. What could have happened?

text.Wistful Bangaa: While back, there was a rumor kickin' around that Basch was alive and in Bhujerba. Turned out to be lies, of course. Who'd start a rumor like that?

text.Rabanastran (man in green shorts near Pa: The other day I saw some wounded Imperials being carried through here. They haven't said what it was all about, though there are rumors aplenty.

text.Town Gossip: It's the Rains in Giza again, but not to worry. The Dry will be back soon enough.

text.Bucco: Hey, Vaan. I haven't seen you around town much lately. And now that I think of it, I haven't seen Penelo around, either ... So ... just what have you two been up to, huh? Heh heh heh.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa chatting with: My friend here says there are 529,412 cobblestones in the Southern Plaza 'round the corner, not including the tiles in the fountain. But even with the stones by the city gates ... 'Course, he could be countin' the flagstones, too. That would be another matter altogether.

text.Rabanastran (man chatting with another m: Technicks are skills that let you do things no magicks can. Stealing treasures from your foes, stanching wounds ... Well, you should know!

text.Rabanastran (woman talking to red bangaa: My friend here was just telling me about the Salikawood, a great forest that lies beyond the desert, even the mountains. It was once part of the Kingdom of Nabradia, but no one has claimed it since Nabradia's fall.

text.Rabanastran (man sitting with woman): The marks from the hunts on the notice board are trouble enough, but I hear there are even tougher hunts out there ... The really difficult hunts don't go up on the boards at all. You can only find out about them through a clan. Huh, they must be some marks ...

text.Tavernmaster: There was a bangaa from the Empire through here, said he was lookin' for help with something ... Can't for the life of me remember what, though. I do remember he said he'd be out at Westgate. If you're curious about what he wanted, you can always go ask him yourself.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa at bar with To: Some paths may only be navigated on a chocobo. Not many, to be sure, but they're there. You need a careful eye to spot 'em.

text.Barkeep (man standing near foot of stair: There was a tremendous explosion in the west, yes? And the Rains have come to Giza, yes? Of course, it had been the Dry for some time ... I suppose the one has nothing to do with the other, yes?

text.Barkeep (woman on balcony): I'm so glad all of our patrons can use the balcony again. Before the war it was such a lively place, but no so since the Imperials had come. If he never does another thing for us, I'll still be grateful to our new consul.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue pants): D'you see that Imperial just there? Word is he was caught ducking his duties in the Sandsea and ordered to stand watch here instead.

text.Earnest Seeq: Wanted to try out me magicks, so I heads down to the Ozmone Plain. Saw me a garif, and bein' as you don't see 'em every day, I a-followed him. Along the way we passes this cave, and curiosity gets the better of me. So I steps in, but the beasts in there ... You best not even know! The garif kept right on past that cave, and he had the right of it.

text.Rabanastran (man browsing curio): Did you ever notice the guard on the second floor of the Sandsea? I think he may have been caught loafing about on the job. Now he's been moved over to Yugri's Magicks, but I doubt that will make any difference.

text.Rabanastran (red bangaa speaking to woma: Rain may fall and sandstorms may whorl, but I've not seen anything to match the coming of the Rains in Giza! The villages empty, and I'd swear the lay of the land itself seems to change! Neither the time nor the place to find yourself lost!

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa in green vest): Can't say as I know for certain it's Lord Vayne's doing, but the guards do seem to be getting on better with people than they used to. You can be sure the guards aren't too pleased by it. I'd hate to be whoever or whatever they're taking their frustrations out on.

text.Sherral: In addition to my inspections, I've been assigned patrols as well. The combat can be trying, I'm not ashamed to admit. I suppose I had let myself grow soft ... Mayhap this is just the proper medicine.

text.Amal: Take the Amal challenge! You'll not find weapons of higher quality!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink headscarf): They lost contact with the Imperial Fleet out west of Rabanastre. They wouldn't have flown into jagd, would they? That would be suicide.

text.Rabanastran (orange seeq): When I was growing up, I heard all manner of stories about the great hume-king Raithwall.

text.Rabanastran (man in green and blue talki: South of Giza Plains? That's the northern tip of Kerwon. You'll find races you've never even seen in Dalmasca down that way.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, green, and t: Relations between Archadia and Rozarria haven't been good. The Rozarrians couldn't have been glad to see Rabanastre fall to Archadia.

text.Migelo: Making trouble with the Imperials, sneaking into the sewers ... never know which way the wind blows with you, m'boy! Now you're traveling the world! I won't try to stop you, though. Just you be sure to look after Penelo while you're at it, eh?

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa speaking with wo: That strange man that came through here – you know, the one with the scar on his forehead and that ratty beard? Wonder what became of him.

text.Rabanastran (boy squatting down and hugg: People still seem to think pretty well of Vayne. If things really start getting better, d'you think we should cut him some slack?

text.Imperial (Southern Plaza): Saw a squad of guards headin' in through the south gate. Soaked to the skin, they were. Must be the Rains down in Giza.

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants with his: There was a great explosion in the west. Some are saying it was the Imperial fleet sinkin' from the sky!

text.Rabanastran (boy with his father in the: Did you hear? Did you hear? My friend down in Lowtown saw a GHOST!

text.Lovestruck Man: Urrr ... I can't get her out of my head ... Who? That viera, that's who. She's all I've ever dreamed of ...

text.Cotze: The Empire dispatched a natural philosopher here to look into something or the other. He tried askin' me some questions, but I won't have any part in it. He's probably still over at Westgate trying to figure out what to do next.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue and green on so: What? Vayne's going back to Archadia? Shucks ... and I never got to run into him even once.

text.Jinn: Hey, been a long time, huh? It's me, Jinn, from Giza Plains. Remember? It's the Rains now, so we've all left the village. Not a soul left there. I thought I saw some people coming up from Ozmone Plain when we was leavin' ... I wonder if they know the village is empty?

text.Bright-eyed Boy: I heard there were some sick people at the village in the Estersand. They can't even leave their homes. Wish I could do somethin' to help ...

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: I wonder if there's any truth to that rumor that Vayne's going back to Archadia?

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Southga: All those roly-polies down in Giza Plains disappear when the Rains come. ... The people? Yeah, they leave, too.

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: It's the Rains down in Giza again. How can I tell? By the puddles the travelers leave.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Westgat: Hey, Vaan! Sure haven't seen you around much lately. Off havin' fun without the rest of us?

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: There's a great sandstorm in the northern part of the Westersand. The winds are so strong you can't even stand, much less walk. You can scarcely see for all the sand, but you can hear. There's a terrible cry riding on that wind. Best to keep well away, if you ask me.

text.Hapless Merchant: Have you been to the village in the Estersand? It's on the banks of the River Nebra, should you fancy a visit.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, pink, and gr: On the far side of the Estersand you'll find Nalbina Fortress. That's where His Majesty was assassinated ... Sometimes I wonder what things would be like now, if only he were still alive.

text.Rabanastran (woman in white speaking wit: Before the war, this place bustled with travelers and merchants going about their business. But look at it now ...

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa SG): The continent of Kerwon lies to the south of Giza, much of it covered in wilderness, and even jagd. It's not as though it's never been explored, but who can say what strange things you might find there?

text.Weather Eye: Just takes one look at the sky to tell if it's the Rains or the Dry down in Giza. Never hurts to take a look afore settin' out. The lay of the land, even the very beasts change from the Rains to the Dry, y'know.

text.Imperial (standing a short distance away: The Rains came sooner than expected. Trudging sodden through empty villages and bogs ... a glorious posting this has turned out to be.

text.Imperial (standing beside chocobo): I've naught to say to you, churl. It's bad enough that I'm soaked to the skin ... No one bothered telling us it'd be the Rains, and don't get me started about that village! This is why I hate these bloody provinces ...

text.Rabanastran (man speaking to woman and s: Why do you suppose they raise cockatrices down in Giza? Can't ride 'em like a chocbo ... Hmm, they're plump, round ... you don't suppose ...

text.Reluctant Adventurer: There's a cavern out there what's filled with fiendishly strong creatures. And I hear someone's found a new way inside, deeper than any've been. I'll wager whoever said "nothin' ventured, nothin' gained" never ventured into a pit like that, eh?

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with group): Desert to the east, desert to the west ... I've heard of people traveling many days before realizing they'd set out in the wrong direction. I use the aerodrome as a marker. If I see that, I know I'm at Westgate.

text.Rimzat: Hha! I've been waiting for some time. You see, I am in need of assistance. Please, hear my words. I have been sent from Archadia to study the sandstorms of the Dalmasca Westersand, but the storms' violence makes such study ... impossible. There is a place in the desert, at the end of a long trail that winds through the north. Mayhap you know it. That is the site of my study. But before the wrath of such a storm, I can do nothing. This is why I seek help. Will you help me?

CHOICE.Rimzat: Thank you, my friend! I have made no progress on my own. I would like you to start by gathering information within Rabanastre. My own inquiries yielded little. There is one man who knows more than he will say. He sits atop the fountain in the plaza. He does not care for the Empire, so he will tell me nothing. Perhaps you will have better luck. I will be waiting to hear what you find.

text.Rimzat: Have you learned aught of the sandstorm in the Westersand? There is a man named Cotze, who sits atop the fountain in the plaza. He knows something of this, but when he learned I was from Archadia, he would say no more. Perhaps you will have better luck.

text.Rabanastran (woman embracing man by the: ... I know you'd never push me away ... as long as I hold you, we'll always be together ...

text.Merchant (Aerodrome): It's the strangest thing ... I was in Bhujerba not long back, and there was someone running around pretending to be Captain Basch. Whatever for?

text.Nono: Terrible news, kupo! When the Imperial fleet exploded over the Westersand, the Strahl was damaged! I'm gathering the parts I need to make repairs as quickly as I can, but it may take some time, kupo.

text.Rabanastran (man in blue, green, and red: You see that group of people by the window? They're from Archadia. They never left after the parade ... Maybe they're thinking of staying.

text.Traveler (woman with the Archadian group: The return ship to Archades still hasn't come. But I've patience enough to go on waiting. It's not as though they could have forgotten me.

text.Rabanastran (woman at left): Something's happened in the west ... Dalan's been behaving oddly ever since.

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): You ever hear of the garif? I heard that after they're born, they put on a mask, and they don't never take it off till they die ... Wonder what they do if they get an itch?

text.Old Dalan: The garif? Let me think ... Yes, I have seen the garif here in Rabanastre, though it was long ago. Hm. I can't remember when the last time was. They live in the southwest of Ozmone Plain, to the south of Giza.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, blue and gre: When I heard Vayne had returned to Archadia, it seemed there must have been some reason for it, but even Dalan doesn't know what's happening.

text.Resigned Boy: The Empire will protect us and keep us safe, I know it. But who will protect us from the Empire if they change their minds?

text.Frustrated Man: Door back here hasn't worked since ... since I don't know when. But those blasted Imperials won't give the word to have it fixed.

text.Somber Woman: When the children born since the war are older, and my daughter sees other kids with parents, I wonder if she'll feel more comfortable with me.

text.Guileful Boy: You know why they sent Vayne back to Archadia? I bet it's because he wasn't treatin' us mean enough. He ain't done nothin' mean, really.

text.Guileless Girl: Sometimes I play down in the alley what leads up to Southgate. Yep. But I don't go up there. And I definitely don't go down to Giza. Nope.

text.Awestruck Girl: See that man squattin' down talkin' over there? They say he used to be a sky pirate! It's kinda exciting, havin' someone mysterious around.

text.Samal: People think being a sky pirate is all riches and adventure, but the reality is far different. Your life is always at risk, you never know peace. You are free, I suppose. But it comes at a steep price. Your fate, succeed or fail, is entirely up to you. So what does it mean to be free? That's the real question. Running to escape your troubles won't make you free. It never can.

text.Well-spoken Girl: I wonder if this is how I'm going to grow up, here in the dark passages of Lowtown. Rather depressing, don't you think? Sometimes I just want to run far, far away from it all ... but that's not easy when you're just a child.

text.Friendly Boy: I don't feel so good. There's somethin' funny been comin' up from under the courtyard. I've always been real sensitive to that kinda thing.

text.Laughing Seeq: Word on the street is Vayne's gone back to Archadia. Word has a way of travelin' fast, but then, words ain't nothin' but wind.

text.Rabanastran (seeq sitting next to boy): Them sluice gates down in the Garamsythe Waterway got some special device what controls 'em. Drain the water off, you can walk the waterway into deep places you couldn't reach otherwise. Couldn't figure out how to work it all, m'self.

text.Dalmascan Patriot: The village in the Estersand is one of the few places we can go to escape the burdens of the city. I find the peace and quiet refreshing.

text.Cynical Boy: Plenty of people out there are happy, so long as there isn't a war. Well, if this is peace, I don't see what's so great about it.

text.Kytes: Hey, Vaan. Haven't seen you around much lately. Workin' on somethin' big? Can't wait to hear more about it! You don't have to worry about me and the others. I'll watch after everybody.

text.Fussbudget: No fair ... She said she had a dream she saw Princess Ashe. How come I never have dreams about the Princess?

text.Rabanastran (man in blue sitting against: I hear there's a stair down to the sewers through Migelo's storehouse, but you shouldn't poke around down there. It's dangerous, boy.

text.Northon: Watchin' Filo and her friends play at pirates reminds me of when I was a kid. We'd run around pretendin' we were real sky pirates – had a secret hideout and everything. Things were so much simpler back then.

text.Watchful Seeq: I can't let my eyes off this poor fellow for one minute. Little while ago he got himself all worked up over his son, went runnin' off into a wall.

text.Impoverished Man: Everything I owned was confiscated after the war. Now I'm forced to live out my miserable days here. Suffering here because of the Empire, I feel I'm more of a Dalmascan than I ever was before. Ironic, don't you think?

text.Rabanastran (woman in white): Look, over there by the door. Do you not see Milha crouched there? What might have happened? That is the house where the man from Nabudis had lived, but it has lain empty for some time now. I have recently heard tales of a ... a ghost sighted not far from here. Might it have something to do with that?

text.ACTION: For Milha and related dialogue, see "" in the Clan Primer section.

text.Deadbeat: Lowtown ... yeah, I like Lowtown. You got your South Sprawl in the ... where's the South Sprawl? Just let me lie here and think ...

text.Angry Woman: Don't you find it strange that the Empire lets us lead such normal lives? With the exception of living in this dungeon, of course. Are they waiting to use us in some sinister plot? Are we tools of the Empire? Are we their hostages? Just who do they think they are?

text.Well-spoken Boy: I've heard a rumor that the Imperial fleet was destroyed, but it's hard to be happy about it. Think of all the poor people who must've died.

text.Vexed Father: I've told her a thousand times not to play outside, that it's dangerous, but she goes anyway ... To be honest, some of the places she's been, I'm a little surprised. She made it to the Salikawood the other day. Said there were moogles there. Heh.

text.Furious Bangaa: Grrah! That son of a cockatrice! Who!? Vayne, that's who! Know of anyone else gone runnin' back to Archades with his tail between his legs? You know why he's left, don't you? Too scared to stay and face us, that's why! Well, what can you expect from these Imperial pretty boys.

text.Wise Elder: Looking for the garif, are you? You may want to go back to Rabanastre and leave for Giza by the south gate. From Giza, head south to reach Jahara.

text.Desert Wayfarer (Archadian woman speakin: Fun? What fun is there in a trip through this sand and heat? I'm going home. And not to the capital ... home for good!

text.Dantro's Wife: There's trouble on the north bank, I'm sure of it. I wish Dantro were here, but I know he can't leave the outpost unwatched.

text.ACTION: See also the "Patient in the Desert" part of the Side Quests chapter.

text.Itinerant Hand (black bangaa with tattoo: A lot of Imperials buy keepsakes here before heading home. The viera crafts are particularly popular. 'Course, the seeq in back makes 'em. Heh.

text.Itinerant Hand (light blue seeq sitting: Come to help fortify the fortress? You shouldn't have it too bad. They save the easy jobs for the humes. Me? I get sent off to do the heavy lifting. Those Imperials think the rest of us are to be used as tools, nothing more. Nice, eh?

text.Merchant (Jajim Bazaar): Nestled as it is on the border of Nabradia and Dalmasca, Nalbina was always bustling with trade between the two. These days it's more fortress than town. At least it's still here, though. Our home of Nabudis was wiped from the land, leaving naught but a necrohol of fiends behind.

text.Itinerant Hand (man in reddish brown pan: Them Archadians were all talking, and they didn't look happy. Heard something about the Leviathan and her 8th Fleet goin' down! Took some important Judge down with it, too, from the sounds of it. Heh. Serves 'em right.

text.Imperial (interrogating man off to the s: You report any shops you see selling stolen goods, son. Can you believe I'm here doing this, every day? There I was part of the Western Armada, glorious! Victorious! This war better start soon. I want to be a shield for the homeland, and a sword, striking down those Rozarrian barbarians!

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him by himself

CHOICE.Stonemason? (seeq): I heard a rumor that someone escaped from the dungeons here, but it weren't my friend. See, I'm not really a stonemason. I came with my buddy to get a friend out of the dungeons ... Maybe if he comes out on forced labor we'll get to see 'im. That'd be nice.

text.Imperial?: Hey, don't be fooled by appearances ... I ain't no Imperial. This armor belongs to this guy next to me. He puts it on me so he can loaf off! It's hot, it's heavy ... Okay, so it's tough being an Imperial, I get it. Come to think of it, those Judges wear armor, too, but they don't complain ... 'Less they're saying it real quiet-like behind those scary masks of theirs.

text.Box Merchant: Sold a box to an Imperial the other day. Heard he took it with 'im on some Leviathingy ... then that up and disappeared! Wonder where it went to.

CHOICE.STATUS: if you catch him by himself

CHOICE.Stonemason? (hume): I came here with my seeq buddy to spring a friend out of the dungeons ... but my stupid buddy got mistaken for a stonemason, so here we are ... 'Course, we started getting good at the work, and now the foreman thinks we're some elite crew ... What're we doing!?

text.Imperial (speaking to two men and bangaa: Here to work on the fortress? A word to the wise: complain overmuch and you'll be thrown in the dungeons, from which there can be no escape! ... Huh? You heard of someone escaping? Bah! Nonsense!

text.Itinerant Hand (hume man with group): We're here working on the fortress walls, but it's torture in this heat ... That's why we're negotiating for better pay! They say that any who complain'll be sent to the dungeons, but that's a bluff. They're in a hurry – they need all the hands they can get!

text.Shy Bangaa: ... I'm here, watchin' these goods. For hours. You know, I just noticed, a lot of these Imperials are armed! Yeah, observant, right? That's my job.

text.Homebound Man: I hear conditions in Rabanastre have improved while I've been here in Nalbina. Must be on account of that new consul.

text.Itinerant Hand (black bangaa at window): I'm headed to that port in the east, where the sky pirates gather. Once I've earned me a 'ship, I'll be a sky pirate, free to go where I will!

text.Lohen: Your errand taking you far abroad, friend? Maybe I have something that you'll be able to use along the way.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Lohen: Bright, sunny days are the deadliest out on the sandsea. That's when the elementals come out. You watch yourself 'round those.

text.Wayward Bangaa: (sigh) I give up ... Tried crossin' the desert again, ended up right back here. I'm thinkin' maybe my sense of direction ain't so good. Maybe I'll talk to that fella over there, see about him takin' me on as an apprentice trader.

text.Bhujerban (man sitting on rail speaking: Bhujerban airspace has been taken over by the Imperial fleet for their maneuvers. Our airships are mostly grounded, bhadra! Haa ... I suppose it does little good to complain to a rank and file guard ...

text.Bhujerban (moogle with yellow pom-pom by: I was only a little late, and they still wouldn't let me on, kupo! That chief steward had the face of a siren, and the heart of a cactoid!

text.Traveler (blonde man in blue): Have you heard the rumors that an Imperial fleet was spotted over the Jagd Yensa? Ha! I'd like to meet the chap who thought up that codswallop. I'd walk up to him, look him straight in the eye, and say "Good day, sir! Did you perchance know that AIRSHIPS CANNOT FLY IN JAGD!?"

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Yes, bhadra. Bhujerba is an island of peace and freedom, but not for those who would break our laws. So are we here to keep watch on the city.

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: The Archadian Senate has power, bhadra. Power enough to drive an emperor from his throne. Thus has House Solidor relied on the favor of the crowd to hold the Senate in check these many years, you see.

text.Street Kid (sitting on luggage): Amba forgot a change of clothes, and we have missed the airship for Rabanastre! Why can we not buy such things there!? Haa ...

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom Aer: Bhujerba values our mooglecraft, and values us the same, kupo! I hope Bhujerba stays the way it is ... No wars for this moogle, kupo!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with orange pom-pom wa: Oh oh oh! I heard a rumor that the Empire has an airship that can fly in jagd, kupo! What is this? New technology!? We're lagging, kupo!

text.Street Kid (near window): When I grow older, bhadra, I will be an airship pilot! A moogle, he is teaching me now, you see. He has just left on the airship for Balfonheim!

text.City Parijanah: Haa ... Master Basch, is it not? I have heard that the Empire's lawkeepers are tracing the Marquis's steps out of Bhujerba. Please, try not to give them any information.

text.Traveler (man in Archadian clothes leani: Have you heard the talk of the Marquis falling ill? Troubling news, that. The Marquis is a wise man who values Bhujerba's peace with the Empire. Here's hoping for his swift recovery!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom sit: The Marquis Ondore's estate is up those steps across the bridge ... but the Marquis isn't there, kupo. They say he's ill and away resting!

text.Bhujerban (woman in white pacing up and: I saw a parijanah here standing. He was counting the Archadian warships that passed beneath. He must be quite a military enthusiast. Ayi ...

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The Marquis is currently unavailable pending recovery from illness. Do not worry, he has posted a minister to govern in his absence.

text.Bhujerban (woman in white sitting on wal: Do all boys love the sky so? I fear that, one day, he will say he wants to be a sky pirate! A pirate! What is his poor mother to do? Hanta ...

text.Bhujerban (woman in green, pink, and bro: Haa ... I have heard that Lhusu's output has dropped most severely of late. Without the mines, our wealth will fade. I worry for Bhujerba.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! Welcome! I am a parijanah, a guide. May I be of assistance? Haa ... it is you. The Marquis has quit Bhujerba, and now prepares his Resistance in the marches. You are aware this knowledge is most privileged. Please, be discreet.

text.Bhujerban (woman in white leaning agains: The Marquis Ondore has taken his leave of the city. I hear he has been taken ill. Without the Marquis here who shall protect Bhujerba?

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Have you heard of the instability in the Empire? It is little surprise. Long have the Imperial House and the Senate been at odds.

text.City Parijanah: Haa, the young Captain Ronsenburg! You are to join Marquis Ondore's Resistance? You will be pleased to know that there are many youths here in Bhujerba who sympathize most greatly with our cause.

text.Bhujerban (woman in white sitting on cra: The dead Captain Ronsen-boori-boori walks again, and his Excellency the Marquis has fallen ill. Bhujerba has gone mad, along with all Ivalice.

text.City Parijanah: So ... Rozarria has awaken her armies. She must have been preparing all along, while Archadia's eyes were pointed elsewhere.

text.Bhujerban (woman leaning against wall in: That magickery, it was quite popular upon its opening. I wonder how it fares these days? Competition in Bhujerba is quite fierce, you see.

text.Bhujerban (tan bangaa pacing boulevard): Ye know that Imperial fleet that was anchored here in Bhujerba? Turns out that's just a fraction of the Imperial armada! Glad we're not at war ...

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: Bhujerba is free today thanks to the Marquis's keen sense of politics. Should something happen to him ... I would fear for Bhujerba's future.

text.City Parijanah: Haa, it is you. At last, the Resistance has begun to move in earnest. All depends on our resolve and our secrecy now. Please be discreet.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The parijanah guides work for the Office of the Marquis ... Have you noticed their numbers are thinning of late? This does not surprise me. It is a difficult and most thankless job.

text.City Parijanah: I am glad to see you are ... behaving yourself. His Excellency the Marquis may not be in the city, but our eyes are ever shining and watchful.

text.Street Kid (Travica Way): Tatah works in the mines, but he has not gone to work in a very long time. He says they are not sending so many stones to the Empire any more.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler. I must not speak too loudly of these things, but allow me to assure you that our organization is in perfect order.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Long have I guarded this shop, yet nothing of note has ever happened here. It is like every day is a holiday. Why, then, must I spend my holiday here?

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! This is a shop of armors! Kah? No, no, I do not dislike this shop. Yet ... I wish there were more important work for me, yes?

text.Rithil: Svagatam ... welcome ... Protectives ... protectives ... Why does Targe get all the business? Am I doing something wrong?

text.Bhujerban (tan seeq browsing on upper le: Me? Rithil's got me standing in here to improve his image. Make things look busy, you see. A lost cause, if you ask me. Maybe I should switch shops.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, trav – Ah, it is you. Kah? Our leader? He is no longer in Bhujerba. He strategizes now elsewhere, you see.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in turban and blue shor: I came all the way from Nalbina to make some gil working the mines, but with all the monsters running amok in there ... (sigh)

text.Lhusu Miner (man standing in line at cou: ... To tell the truth, I am not a customer, bhadra. Targe gives me money so that I might stand here every day, encouraging people to buy, you see.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Every day, more raksas fill the mines. This store benefits from the constant patronage of the miners, yet when no mining may be had ...

text.Bhujerban (woman browsing weapons on upp: Have you heard that the Marquis has fallen ill? Should he leave us, so shall peace, bhadra. We must prepare for the worst.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler ... or should I say "Captain"? The Empire reels with the loss of the 8th Fleet! Some would name Vayne culpable ...

text.Street Kid (in yellow, with mother kneel: Amba, she is always angry at me! I prefer the Imperial soldiers, yes? They are kind.

text.Bhujerban (light blue seeq walking aroun: I haven't seen the Marquis on some time. He used to take walks in the Skygrounds ... Hope he's not fallen ill, eh? (snort)

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: His Excellency, gone missing? This is foolishness! He is only on leave to recover from illness. Please, refrain from repeating every rumor you hear!

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink headscarf leani: Please, bhadra, find someone else to talk to. I wait for my boyfriend ... and what business is it of yours who I choose to spend my time with?

text.Street Kid (in blue, on ledge): Do you know the game of Judges? One is the Judge, and they must run to catch the others! If you are caught, you become a Judge and must chase too!

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler. Welcome to this magickery. Haa ... You are the Captain Ronsenburg of whom I have heard, no? I admire your bravery, bhadra ... Though I find your sense of propriety and restraint ... somewhat lacking.

text.Shop Clerk (woman in pink, red, and blue: Welcome, traveler, to Mait's. Our customers are serious about their magicks. How could we be any less dedicated than they? We could not, no.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Of late, I have been studying magicks, you see. Haa, now I can speak of a mutual interest with the lovely staff here, bhadra. Not bad, eh?

text.Shop Clerk (woman in blue, pink and gree: The supply of magicite in Bhujerba has run dry with the halting of mining in Lhusu. We even thought to import Stones from the mines in Kerwon, for a time. To think, Bhujerbans buying magicite from an Imperial colony! Kastam ...

text.Bhujerban Guru (Mait's): Relations between the Marquis Ondore and the Empire worsen daily. The question is, how will the Marquis move? Whichever way it is, I would think making the first move to be the wisest choice of all.

text.Cloudborne Kid: My sister works at the Cloudborne, though she is no bar-wench, but the taverner. Very busy, very strict. Best not to trouble her, no. Especially now that her man, Havharo, is so busy. Yes, no time for my sister, none at all. We shall see how much time she has for him later, yes?

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: So many travelers, so many draughts of win. Those from Archades fall into their cups the swiftest, I find. Haa ... the burdens of Empire ...

text.Drunken Archadian Wayfarer: How many cups have I drunk? Sweet Bhujerban Madhu, I am yours! Once I thought the world revolved around Archades, but now I know ... It spins around ME! (hic)

text.Cloudborne Patron (light blue seeq): I'm tryin' to get me friend here to join me for a drink. We're one step away from goin' in ... it's just that this step seems to be takin' a while.

text.Bhujerban Guru (Cloudborne Row): I have not seen Havharo for many days now. Does he no longer come to the Cloudborne? I worry for Melisa. She did seem quite fond of him.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in green and brown shor: The Lhusu Mines have been quiet for a time. I hear much talk of raksas running wild, and broken machinery. No talk of the truth.

text.Cloudborne Resident (tan bangaa in green: Even were there a resistance welling in Bhujerba, who would be fool enough to speak of it? Anyone could be a spy for the Empire ... even you!

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Cloudborne Row): I came here to see the Lhusu Mines, yet the locals here speak of some monstrosities running amok ... I had so wanted to see natural magicite! (sigh)

text.City Parijanah: The Marquis prepares the Resistance out in the marches. I ask that you do nothing to interfere with our plans. Are we understood, bhadra?

text.Cloudborne Resident (woman talking with: Marquis Ondore has left his post due to illness ... I pray for his Excellency's swift recovery. He is the only one who might stand against the Empire!

text.Cloudborne Resident (man sitting on crat: My merchant friend tells me arms and munitions sell quite well these days, yet it is not the Empire which buys them. Does another army form?

text.Cloudborne Resident (light blue seeq wal: You take care in the Cloudborne. The folks in there, they'd do anything to keep their little organization a secret. Anything.

text.City Parijanah (talking to woman at tabl: Though I should not say this too loudly, the day I leave to join the Resistance fleet is nigh. I would have an answer of my love before then!

text.Shop Clerk (moogle with green pom-pom): We get customers from all over Ivalice in here, kupo! Oh, the Bhujerban Madhu is a pow'rful draw! And ... our customers get pow'rful drunk.

text.Cloudborne Patron (woman sitting at tabl: The Marquis is gone from Bhujerba, have you heard? They say he is on the mend from some illness, but I believe there is more to it.

text.Cloudborne Patron (moogle with yellow po: Think it strange to see a moogle drinking? Well, I'll have you know that the spirits where I come from are ten times as strong as Bhujerban Madhu! Show me a moogle in his cups from drinking this hume-brew and I'll show you a lightweight! I mean ... a lighter weight, kupo!

text.City Parijanah (talking to red bangaa): Here I sit, pretending to drink off duty, while, in reality, I pass notes to others in the Resistance, you see. The drunken bangaa is my comrade. He, too, merely acts as though he were in his cups. I think.

text.Melisa: Haa. Hello again. Havharo? He's not here. Why, I'd say he's off in the sky with the Marquis by now ...

text.City Parijanah (with blue jacket): Even the poorest man may earn a title for himself in the Imperial army, if he is able. So are the soldiers enthusiastic, and the officers skilled.

text.Cloudborne Patron (man leaning on bar, s: The Leviathan and her fleet destroyed? I cannot believe this, bhadra. Yet, even were it true, the Empire has many more fleets. I have heard their 1st Fleet, in particular, cannot be defeated!

text.Timorous Bangaa: Hrrm? Oh, it's you. Sounds like you've been puttin' it to the Empire, eh? Sorry if I came across a little gruff before.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The Lhusu Mines? Closed, as always, bhadra. The Marquis has fallen ill and left Bhujerba, and without his government, we sit idle.

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink leaning aga: I keep track of the magicite trade, you see. My sources, they tell me the Empire has turned to the Henne mines, now that Lhusu has run dry.

text.Miners' Ender (moogle in gold with orang: T-too many hills, kupo! I once thought of moving to Archades, but there they have Judges! Wait ... I've seen Judges here, too. And hills!

text.Lhusu Parivir: Mmmrrgh? Ehh, the Lhusu Mines are sep'rated into sites ... Nah, you need keys to get into each. They keep 'em all at the Staras residence, see. The master there's the Lady Niray. Eh? Aye, she has a husband ... eh, I'll explain later. The Staras residence's at the south end of Cloudborne Row.

text.Lhusu Miner (black bangaa yelling at moo: My patience is spent, Moogle! Down! Adhuna! You are coming – "Kupo"!? I'll give you kupo!

text.City Parijanah: I hear word of a great Rozarrian fleet gathering, bhadra. Please, you should speak of this to no one. I am not even sure why I have told you.

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink, blue, and: Have you heard, bhadra? The Marquis has fallen ill! I do not know which pundit will take his place. I hope he is firm with the Empire.

text.Miners' Ender (guy sitting on ledge next: Have you noticed less parijanah guides upon the streets? No? Perhaps it is just me.

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink, blue and y: Bhujerba remains independent only because its neutrality affords the Empire certain ... conveniences, yes? Should it become less convenient ... Kastam ...

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The Lhusu Mines are closed on account of raksas, er, creatures. It is at times like these when I am glad to let the clans help.

text.Lhusu Parivir (Lhusu Square): The paling erected within the mines to keep raksas at bay has fallen, and so mining has stopped. Why do they not fix it, I wonder? Haa ...

text.Street Vendor: Raksas are running wild in the mines, and all work has come to a stop. How am I to sell without any customers? Ah, are you looking for something?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.City Parijanah: Yes, traveler, this is Bashketi's Gambits. Our organization, too, uses gambits. We must fight as one if we are to defeat the mighty Empire!

text.Shop Clerk (orange seeq on upper level): This young lady's being followed by a most persistent man, she tells me. (snort) Were she to use a gambit, she'd be rid of him in no time!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The flow of magicite to the Empire has dropped, on account of raksas in the mines, they say. But I suspect there is more to it ... . No, bhadra, on second thought, there is nothing.

text.Bhujerban (man in brown pants and green: My love, she comes by airship, yet no word of her arrival has reached me ... Hanta ... What could be the matter?

text.Bhujerban (moogle with yellow pom-pom si: Have you any worries, kupo? Then, join me! Gaze out at the sky, kupo! Take a deep breath, that's right ... see? No more worries!

text.Bhujerban (woman in red, pink, and blue,: I have dropped a ring near to here, you see. Haa ... By now, it is surely washing up on the Phon Coast ... Kah? Did you not know? It is said that objects dropped from Bhujerba are carried by the currents to wash up on the shores of Phon!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Every once in a while, people do fall from here ... usually travelers, spreading their wings, causing a disturbance. Bhujerbans know better.

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink, green, and tan: Perhaps you have heard that most of Bhujerba's food comes from other lands. If relations with the outside were to sour, we would all starve.

text.Bhujerban (light blue seeq at left of st: Ye've heard the rumor that one o' them Imperial ships went down in the Jagd Yensa? Bah! Skyswill! It couldn't fly there in the first place!

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: The great edifice you see ahead is the residence of his Excellency the Marquis ... whom I have not seen lately. He is a busy man, yes.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler. Lucky for you, the organization deemed you useful. After you spread that rumor ... things could have gotten ugly.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Svagatam, traveler. I have seen many airships from many lands in my day, but none compare to ours. It's the moogles' skill with machines, you see.

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Clio's): My brother works in a laboratory in Archades. He was with the 8th Fleet, but we've lost contact. I hope nothing untoward has befallen him!

text.Shop Clerk (moogle in red with green pom: Oh, if there's anything you need, anything at all, don't hesitate to ask, kupo! Having a pleasant trip? We'll help you make it pleasanter!

text.ACTION: In various areas of the Plains during the Rains is a withered tree that can be struck down to form a bridge.
The tree is dry and brittle.

CHOICE.ACTION: The tree will be cut down and fall into the water. One of the following system messages will appear depending on where you are.

text.ACTION: Throne Road: The tree drifts slowly to the south.
Nomad Village: The tree drifts slowly to the southeast.
Toam Hills: The tree drifts slowly to the southeast.
Starfall Field: The tree drifts slowly to the east.
Giza's North Bank: The tree drifts slowly to the south.
Crystal Glade: The tree drifts slowly to the east.
Tree Stump: The tree that stood here has drifted off to the
direction

text.Sadeen: South of ... Starfall Field ... There. The plain ...

text.Tiny Wayfarer: Well this is perfect. I forgot everyone leaves the village during the Rains. I'm a blundering fool, kupo! What's that? A sad-lookin' man, kupo? Haven't seen anyone matchin' that description 'round here, kupo.

text.Weary Seeq: Phew! Just came from Ozmone Plain. I'm dead tired. Not all that far, no ... Just keep makin' your way south through Giza. Head out the village here and you're on your way. (snort) There's a garif village out on the west end of the plain. Mind yourself if you head out that way, though. The creatures there are murder.

text.Game Hunter: Ah, travelers, are you? We were traveling, too, till the fell creatures of Ozmone Plain got the better of my partner here. We're exhausted. Where are you headed, by the way? Eh? Jahara? Then you're headed the wrong way. Jahara is back the way you came.

text.ACTION: When you speak to one of the warriors guarding the bridge ...

text.Garif Warrior: Who are you? This is garif land. No place for hume-children to play at games.

text.ACTION: Another garif appears from behind you.

text.War-chief Supinelu: They are wayfarers. They bring no harm. I saw them cross the Ozmone Plain. They are warriors of great distinction. The fiends of the plains troubled them not at all.

text.Garif Warrior: You ventured upon the plains alone, War-chief? Again?

text.ACTION: to Vaan

text.War-chief Supinelu: ...What business have you with the garif?

text.ACTION: Vaan appears to say something.

text.War-chief Supinelu: Let them pass. The responsibility will be mine.

text.Garif Warrior: If this is your wish, War-chief.
Then, you may pass. These days see many humes wandering through our lands.

text.ACTION: The garif who let you in is waiting for you across the bridge.

text.War-chief Supinelu: Ah, I have not made introductions. I am Supinelu, War-chief of this village. We garif have been friends to all since long ago, however, lately the hume world is in much turmoil. We must protect our village, and our people. As War-chief, and protector of our village, I ask you: Why have you come to this land?

Hmm ... I see. So you too have come to ask about the nethicite. You must speak with the elders. Though our masks may make it difficult for you to tell us apart, walk through the village and look with your eyes, listen with your ears.

text.Garif Warrior (on riverbank by two sparr: What is this? Another hume visitor to our land? This is most unusual. Have you, too, come to speak with our elder chieftains?

text.Warrior Guromu: Ah, you are the hume the War-chief has spoken of. You have crossed the plains to learn of the Stones, yes? I believe the elders can tell you much.

text.Garif Warrior (talking to another behind: You seem a great warrior, but it is best you avoid Zertinan Caverns. There are many fell creatures there, and of late, worse ... A fiend with strange powers has been seen. Perhaps this is why the other creatures there have grown yet more violent?

text.Old War-chief Kadalu: Ah, you are the humes our War-chief saw on the plains. Welcome to our village, protected by the clear flow of the Sogoht. I am Supinelu's brother, Kadalu. I worry ... for Supinelu often goes to the plains alone. Why, when the others surely wish to train with him? He is stubborn this way. Your pardon. I spoke of a personal matter. Please forget it. You have business with the elders, yes? On you go.

text.Garif Elder (talking to Kadalu): What is it, hume-child? Have you something to ask of this wizened man? Ah, you wish to know of the nethicite? It is a word I hear quite often of late, though I know not why. Nor do I know anything of this Stone. So too did I tell the hume-child who asked me before. I'm sorry. Ask another of the elders. Perhaps they will know.

text.Garif Herder (by the nanna pen): The green creatures you see in my enclosure are nannas, the best livestock in all Ivalice. No part of the nanna goes to waste. Meat, hide, and bones, all have their uses. They are strong against drought, and cold, and - oh yes - easily herded.

text.Garif Elder (by the Nanna pen): You have the look of one who wishes to know something. If it is something that I know, good. Ah, the nethicite ... You are not the only one who has asked me about this. It saddens me to admit that I know nothing of this Stone. Magicite contains within it a great power, thus have we worshipped the Stones from the beginning of time. Yet I had never heard of this nethicite ... Perhaps the High-chief knows something of this? If you have not spoken with him yet, go. He will be with Geomancer Yugelu.

text.Garif Elder: You may ask me three more times, or a hundred, and each time I will tell you, "I do not know." ...Perhaps the High-chief knows something of this? If you have not spoken with him yet, go. He will be with Geomancer Yugelu.

text.Garif Herder (standing in front of shack: Greetings. You are a traveler, yes? Our village is not like a hume village, but you are welcome to find what comfort here as you may.

text.Garif Trader: Do you need anything? Please, take your time, for the world has much of it for the taking.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Garif Trader: Have you heard of the monographs? Merely bearing one of these on your person aids in the retrieval of objects from the foes you defeat. There are different monographs for different persuasions of adventurer. As a merchant, I would love one, if only I knew where it might be found.

text.Warrior Hsemu: Beyond here lies the hill where sits the Great-chief. Those from the outside are not welcome here.

text.War-chief Supinelu: Have you learned of the Stones? Perhaps if you asked the elders, they might have wisdom for you.

text.Garif Herder (one of two, nearest the br: There is a wood to the southeast of here, where the Mist is uncommonly thick. Even its flowers are perilous to Man. If you would pass through that wood, be wary of places where the Mist runs thickest.

Many people come to our village of late ... Perhaps the road to Giza is open? Once again we can bring medicinal herbs and the fine cheese of the nanna to the people of Giza. When the Rains have lifted, I will do this.

text.Geomancer Yugelu: Many hume-children come to our village of late. You, too, have come to learn of this nethicite? We Garif protect the old ways, the old knowledge. Perhaps one of us knows of this Stone. My knowledge, however, is little. I know that nethicite makes the power of magick as nothing, but this is all. But you already knew this, did you not?

text.High-chief Zayalu: Oh? What is this? More humes come to visit us? A little bigger this time, but no matter. You need not tell me anything. I know you have come to our village to learn of the Stones, the nethicite. We garif have knowledge of this, passed down from father to son, mother to daughter. Some of it remains, some has been lost in history's sands ... I ... know nothing of the Stones. You must speak to the Great-chief. He alone holds the deep knowledge of these things. He alone remembers all the tellings. Cross the bridge to the north, and there you will find him. There are watchers at the bridge, so I think it best to speak with War-chief Supinelu.

text.ACTION: Zayalu looks to the garif next to him. They nod to each other. He turns back to Vaan.

text.High-chief Zayalu: ...May I ask of you a favor? Give this to War-chief Supinelu, from me.

text.ACTION: You obtain a jaya stick!

text.High-chief Zayalu: There is no rush. When you next happen to meet him, you may give it to him then. May you find all the answers you seek.

Our Great-chief, he will know of the nethicite. If he tells you he does not know, then you must abandon your search, for no one knows. Ah, also, I must ask you to give the jaya stick to our War-chief. Now, I hope you will find the knowledge you seek.

text.Geomancer Yugelu: Sitting here on the earth, one comes to see many things: the great flow of the world, even the flow of Man's thought ...

text.Garif Elder (talking to Kadalu): You ask about nethicite, yet I know nothing of this Stone, so can I teach you nothing. You would do well to speak to the Great-chief. Go north from here, and you will reach a bridge. The Great-chief may be found beyond.

text.Garif Elder: You must ask the Great-chief about this nethicite. He sits beyond the bridge to the north. He will have something to teach you, I am sure.

CHOICE.STATUS: if you did not speak to him before Zayalu

CHOICE.Garif Elder (by the Nanna pen): Hmmm, nethicite ... Perhaps the Great-chief knows something. He is across the bridge to the north. You would do best to speak to the War-chief before attempting to cross. The warriors guarding the bridge are his.

text.Garif Elder: You may ask me three more times, or a hundred, and each time I will tell you, "I do not know." ...Perhaps the Great-chief knows something of this? He is wise in the knowledge of our people. You would do well to speak with him.

text.War-chief Supinelu: That which you carry, is it a jaya stick?

CHOICE.War-chief Supinelu: The High-chief has given this ... to me? I shall receive it. I thank you for bringing it to me. Now, did you learn what you wished? No, do not tell me. It is written clear upon your face. So, even the High-chief could not help. Then, you must meet with the Great-chief.
Yes, it is true. The Great-chief may know something that would aid you. Yet, arranging an audience may be quite difficult ...

CHOICE.ACTION: Next scene in blue, Without Proof, begins

text.War-chief Supinelu: So you have learned nothing of the Stones? To think that even the High-chief did not know ... Then, you must meet with the Great-chief.

CHOICE.War-chief Supinelu: Yes, it is true. The Great-chief may know something that would aid you. Yet, arranging an audience may be quite difficult ...

CHOICE.ACTION: Next scene in blue , Without Proof, begins

text.Ashe: I must learn more about the nethicite. I cannot turn back now. Please, tell your Great-chief that I am of the royal line of Dalmasca, a direct descendant of Dynast-King Raithwall. If the garif have passed down knowledge of the Stones, they must know of the nethicite that the Dynast-King once held.

text.War-chief Supinelu: Do you have proof of your heritage?

text.Ashe: I ... I do not.

text.War-chief Supinelu: Hrm ... I have looked into your eyes and seen that you speak the truth, hume-child. I give you my trust. The Great-chief is ahead, across this bridge.
The Great-chief is across this bridge, at the meeting place. Walk softly, friend. Ah? You wonder about the stick? If you wish to know more, ask the High-chief. Do not ask me about this matter.

text.Warrior Hsemu: If the War-chief has given you his trust, so shall I. Go, meet with the Great-chief.

text.High-chief Zayalu: The stick you gave to our War-chief, it is a ward against demons, known to our people. I fear he will have need of it soon ...

text.Geomancer Yugelu: All of us, all people have a role. What a sad thing it is that this role is not always what we desire in our life. In this village, too, there is one who rages against the role given him by the heavens ... in vain. None may change their fate.

CHOICE.STATUS: if you haven’t already spoken to him

CHOICE.Garif Elder (by the Nanna pen): Perhaps the Great-chief would know of this nethicite? He is wise in the knowledge of our people.

CHOICE.STATUS: if you haven’t already spoken to him

CHOICE.Garif Elder (talking to Kadalu): Have you met with the Great-chief? He can be found across the bridge to the north.

text.Garif Elder (sitting on ground talking t: There is a rich magicite vein near this village, did you know? It is an important and very holy place to us. Yet, in recent years, humes have spoiled the land. They use machines to mine more and more of the Stones. They steal power from the earth at their own peril, for the earth will surely take it back.

text.Low-chief Sugumu: Ah ... a hume-child. It is unusual for your kind to visit us here on our knoll. Have you come to speak with the Great-chief? He is in the meeting place before the bridge. You will know it by the guards standing at the entrance.

text.Garif Elder (talking to another): Oh? A hume-child? This is most unusual. You seem quite burly for one so young. We are old here, and you may find our village lacks the excitement you crave, but sometimes it is better to move slowly.

text.Garif Youth: Ah, a hume-child. I am surprised to see you here. This hill is called the elderknoll. Here does the Great-chief hold counsel with the other elders. We garif welcome outsiders to our village, but few are they who are allowed here. You must be on important business indeed.

text.Garif Warrior: The Great-chief is ahead. Will you meet with him?

CHOICE.ACTION: move on to next scene in green

text.ACTION: The Great-chief sits at the head of a bonfire, wearing an elaborate horned mask, with a long, braided white beard. By his fire, Ashe and the others wait patiently as he examines the stone.

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: This nethicite - you have used it.

text.Ashe: It was not I who used it. Indeed I had hoped you could show me how. Thus I've come.

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: You do not know the workings of the Stone. Then we are no different.

text.Ashe: What?

text.ACTION: The Great-chief tells her a tale; as he talks, we see images of garif around the fire, and finally King Raithwall with nethicite in hand, before the camera pans back to Ashe.

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: In ages past, the gods made a gift of nethicite to my people. But the manner of its use eluded us. Displeased by our failure, the gods took back their Stones. They chose instead to give them to a hume king. Called the Dynast-King, he used the nethicite's power to bring peace to a troubled time. It is a curious thing. Though the blood of King Raithwall flow through your veins, you cannot wield nethicite.

text.Ashe: Cannot wield it? So then, am I to understand you can't tell me how to use the Stone?

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: Though it shame me so to admit. Here before me stands a descendant of the Dynast-King himself ... and I can accord her no help at all. Still, even if you knew how to use the nethicite, you would find it of small avail. The Mist collected in the Stone over ages past is lost, and with it the Stone's power. It will be your posterity who wield the Stone in ages yet to come.

text.ACTION: Ashe sighs frustratedly.

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: This Stone is devoid of power. Empty, yet full of thirst. A terrible longing to drink the world dry. The power of men, and of magick. Of good, and of evil. It is often those who desire nethicite whom the nethicite itself desires.

text.ACTION: Just then, a familiar face appears at the meeting place.

text.Penelo: Larsa?

text.ACTION: Now nighttime, the scene changes to Ashe standing by the fire. She thinks back to the conversation she had with Larsa, shortly after meeting up in the garif camp.

text.Ashe: To Bur-Omisace?

text.Larsa: I say we ought leave tomorrow. I was going to wait for my escort, but meeting you presents a great opportunity. This terrible war can be stopped, but I will need your help to do so.

text.Ashe: A war?

text.Larsa: You know the Marquis Ondore leads a group of insurgents - your pardon, he leads a large resistance force against the Empire. Lady Ashe, neither of our countries can afford this now. The Rozarrian Empire would stir. They would aid the Resistance and use this aid as a pretext to declare war on Archadia ... and Archadia would have no choice but to answer. Lady Ashe, let us go to Bur-Omisace. With the blessing of his His Grace the Gran Kiltias Anastasis ... you may rightly wear your crown, and declare the restoration of the Kingdom of Dalmasca. As queen, you can call for peace between the Empire and Dalmasca ... and stop Marquis Ondore.

text.Ashe: For peace? How dare you say that! The Empire attacked us, stole all we hold dear ... and you would have me save them from war?

text.Larsa: Dalmasca would be the battlefield! What if nethicite were used on Rabanastre? You know my brother would do this!

text.ACTION: As Larsa continues to speak, we see Ashe, later that night again, walking away from the Great-chief's fire with the useless Dawn Shard in her hand.
Larsa: Forgive me. I presumed overmuch. I could think of no other way to avoid bloodshed. If you cannot trust me, then please, take me as your hostage.
Ashe sees the ghost of Rasler again, this time standing on the bridge before her, looking out over the Sogoht.

text.Ashe: Rasler.

text.ACTION: She starts to run for him. Suddenly, it's not Rasler on the bridge, but Vaan. He turns to her as she approaches.

text.Vaan: You saw him, didn't you. Like at the King's tomb.

text.Ashe: So you did see him, too. But why?

text.Vaan: It's strange. Before, I didn't even know what you looked like. And the Prince - I barely knew there was a prince. Who knows? Maybe the person I saw was my brother.

text.Ashe: Basch told me about him.

text.Vaan: He enlisted, right at the end. But for what? He knew we couldn't win.

text.Ashe: To protect something.

text.Vaan: How can he protect anything when he's dead? Was it different for Prince Rasler? Did that make sense?

text.ACTION: There's a long pause. Ashe looks down.

text.Vaan: Hating the Empire, getting revenge. It's all I ever thought about. But I never did anything about it. I mean, I realized there was nothing I could do. It made me feel hollow, alone. And then I'd miss my brother. I'd say stuff like, "I'm gonna be a sky pirate"... or some other stupid thing. Just anything to keep my mind off it. I was just - I was running away. I needed to get away from his death. That's why I followed you. Know what? I'm through with it. I'm through running. I'm ready to find my purpose. To find some real answers - some reasons. If I stick with you, I think I will.

text.Ashe: I wish I knew.

text.Vaan: I'll find 'em.

text.ACTION: The scene fades out, and then in on Ashe, Larsa, Penelo, and Vaan standing on the bridge near the exit to Ozmone Plain the next day.

text.Ashe: I will accompany you to Mt. Bur-Omisace.

text.Larsa: I had hoped you'd say yes. I am glad.

text.Ashe: My heart is not set. I still have questions. I hope to find answers along the way.

text.Larsa: I had other reason to invite you. There is someone I'd like you to meet waiting on Bur-Omisace.

text.Ashe: Who is that?

text.Larsa: An enemy, and an ally also. You will just have to wait and see for yourself.

text.ACTION: Larsa turns and walks away.

text.Vaan: That Larsa likes his secrets.

text.Ashe: He does not mean ill by it.

text.Vaan: He's not bad. At least for an Imperial.

text.ACTION: In the background, Balthier, Fran, and Basch have a chat.

text.LOCATION: Basch: Holy Mt. Bur-Omisace stands at the northern edge of the Jagd Ramooda. Once we're in jagd, we need not fear pursuit by their airships.

text.Balthier: Don't get your hopes up. You remember the Leviathan sailed straight over the Jagd Yensa, right up to Raithwall's tomb. Skystone that works even in jagd. You know nethicite's behind it. Little wonder they're so keen on the stuff.

text.LOCATION: Basch: And what is it you're after, Balthier? You're a welcome hand, and a great aid, but why?

text.Balthier: Worried I'm out to steal the nethicite, eh? Can't say I'm unaccustomed to people doubting my intentions. Nothing could be further from my mind. Shall I swear by your sword or some such?

text.LOCATION: Basch: Apologies. But I needed to know where you stand. Her Majesty depends on you. And you seem to have an interest in the Stone.

text.Balthier: I'm only here to see how the story unfolds. Any self-respecting leading man would do the same.

text.ACTION: Larsa joins the party as a guest!
Vaan nods.

text.War-chief Supinelu: Take this as a token of our parting.

text.ACTION: You obtain a Bowgun!
You obtain a quiver of Onion Bolts!

text.War-chief Supinelu: If you would ride a chocobo, you may. I have spoken with the moogle. She will not charge you for your first use of the chocobos. Take care on the road ahead. Should it lead back to our land, you are welcome guests. Spirits of the land watch over you.

text.LOCATION: Go to the previous chapter (Chapter 5: The Dawn Shard) | Go to the next chapter (Chapter 7: The Gran Kiltias and the Sword of Kings)
Go to Clan Primer | Go to Side Quests | Go to Intro & Key

text.Garif Warrior (on crystal's side): The War-chief has spoken with the chocobo keeper. He has asked that you be allowed to ride for free. You travel to Mt. Bur-Omisace? Perhaps you will go by chocobo, then! Ah, the holy mountain ... East of Ozmone Plain, through the jungles of Golmore, and across Paramina Rift it lies. I wish you a safe journey.

text.Gurdy: I heard from the War-chief. You ride for free! The offer's only good once, though. Well, care for a ride?

text.ACTION: Lull of the Land

text.Garif Warrior (on riverbank by two sparr: The garif dislike needless use of force, yet when battle comes to us, we face it as warriors must.

text.Asdalu: The Golmore Jungle to the east of Ozmone Plain is an ancient place that suffers no entry by Man. The wood has a mind of its own. It thinks. Often did the Great-chief tell me to avoid its boughs and winding paths when I was young.

text.Warrior Guromu: So the hume-child who came here was your companion. This is why he came to ask the same thing, I see now.

text.Old War-chief Kadalu: Kerwon, by its very nature, does not welcome Man. Your journey, I fear, will be fraught with difficulty. I pray for your good fortune.

text.War-chief Supinelu: Mt. Bur-Omisace lies far to the east. It will be a long journey to its paths. Walk softly, for in foolhardiness lies doom.

text.Garif Herder (standing in front of shack: I am told that you entered our village with permission of the War-chief? This is most unusual, for he does not take to outsiders. Quite stoic, that one! Hoh! It is his strength, and his weakness. I am afraid it is the weak side that shines most brightly of late.

text.Warrior Hsemu: The Great-chief is across this bridge. Walk softly.

text.Garif Herder (one of two, nearest the br: On your way here through the plains, you must have spied the cave entrance? This is the way to Zertinan Caverns, and a place to avoid. Many fell creatures dwell within the caverns. Even our most hale of warriors find it difficult to enter the deepest reaches.

text.Geomancer Yugelu: The stick you gave to our War-chief has the power to ward off evil things. Our War-chief fights against a great monster, possessed of immense power. May that wood grow in his heart and make him strong.

text.Garif Elder: To the garif, magicite is most holy. We have worshipped the Stones since the beginning of time, and their tale is told in our legends. Yet, there is much we still do not know. What is this nethicite? Its very name speaks of dark power, yet it is a mystery to us.

text.Garif Elder (sitting on ground talking t: The jungles of Golmore are ancient, little changed since the earliest times. I have heard that a wyrm lives there, a legendary creature from the time of the gods.

text.Garif Elder (standing and talking to two: There are many foul creatures in the lands around our village. They trample the herbs of the plains, and taint the magicite veins with their presence. It is perhaps more than our warriors can ever hope to handle. Yet we must do something.

text.Garif Elder (talking to another): To the east of here lies Paramina Rift. On days when the snows are heavy, the creatures known as elementals can be seen there. Take care, for they are quite dangerous, and unfond of Man.

text.Garif Youth: Hrm? Do you find my mask odd? You may look upon it all you wish, yet I will not take it off, lend it, or sell it. All garif receive a mask the day they are born, not to be removed until the day they die. This has always been our custom.

text.High-chief Zayalu: I am sorry we could tell you nothing about the nethicite. Still, you are welcome to visit our village again. Our War-chief has warmed to you considerably.

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: You go to Mt. Bur-Omisace, yes? There is one in the village selling provisions. You might speak with him.

text.ACTION: For dialogue with the Wandering Viera, see "Side Quests - Viera Rendezvous."

text.Imperial (Southern Plaza): Hard to believe I've been here two years already. Heh. I remember when the Rains were a big deal. Now it's just same-old, same-old.

text.Patient Bangaa: We couldn't reach the deeper parts of the Garamsythe Waterway and it's put my friend here in the foulest of moods. We weren't able to make it past this one sluice gate. There's a moogle what has the key, but he wouldn't let us use it!

text.Trader: I set off for the garif village to see about stocking some of their wares. But I got lost on the way and barely made it back. I've given up on all that now. Reckon I'll just stick around here for the time being.

text.Merchant (blue seeq at top of steps): Spices! Authentic Bancour spices! Whaddaya say? Care for a pinch or two?

text.Merchant (tan bangaa in blindfold): I may never be a trade baron, but I bring in enough to live as I please. I've no complaints.

text.Traveler (Muthru): Delightful it may be, but Rabanastre is not my home. It is time that I returned. What tales I have to tell!

text.Busy Messenger: You've heard there's a passage connecting the Giza Plains with Ozmone Plain now, right? Boss has me down there surverying for him.

text.Rabanastran (man in white, yellow, and b: When I first moved to Rabanastre I couldn't tell one street from the other. But I think I may finally know my way around now.

text.Reks's Friend: You've made yourself some good friends along the way, Vaan, but you've done it all standin' on your own two feet. Reks would be proud of ya.

text.Rabanastran (green-horned tan seeq): Heard tell there's a huge, powerful wyrm lurking somewhere in the Westersand - a wyrm unlike the others you're liable to find there. Think I heard me the cry of the beast once. Or maybe it was only the raging winds of a sandstorm. Regardless, I can't remember where.

text.Rabanastran (woman in white): Locked himself in the house for fear of a ghost, has he? Hmm ... I might have mentioned before, but that is the houes the man who fled Nabudis lived in ... until he fell ill and passed away. Were it me, I would be more frightened to be alone in there.

CHOICE.Rabanastran (woman in white): The child who'd been hiding in the house has finally come out. I must confess, I am ... relieved. That is the house the man from Nabudis rented. He was a kind man. I ... I do not suppose that he was the sort to return in death to torment the living. No. Did you notice? The seeq landlord - usually so jovial - did not laugh while the child was shut in the house. He sighed sadly all the while.

text.Old Dalan: Mt. Bur-Omisace? Let me think ... What could you possibly need to go there for, m'boy? Well, it's none of my business, I suppose. The Gran Kiltias Anastasis leads the Light from Bur-Omisace. He is a wise man, said to find hidden truths in his dreams.

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): Dalan was tellin' me about this place called Kerwon ... Didn't sound like anywhere I'd wanna go.

text.Rabanastran (woman at left): Most of us in Lowtown are glad to see Vayne gone. That one's too cunning for his own good.

text.Son: Bhujerba's nothing but sky and cloud - it's boring. Are you really going to build a summer home here, Father?

text.Mother: The rustic atmosphere is fashionable, dear. Our neighbors just bought a summer home in Bhujerba. Our residence must be even more grand.

text.Father: You've quite the competitive spirit, Mother. Father wouldn't change that about you for the world.

text.ACTION: Vaan and Penelo chatter as the party enters the area. Basch speaks with Ashe.

text.Basch: An alliance between Dalmasca and the Empire?

text.Ashe: Reason tells me 'tis the only course. We must avoid war with the Empire at all cost. Yet I fear I could not bear the shame. Had I but the strength -

text.Basch: A shame perhaps for me and for you. But for Dalmasca it is hope!

text.Ashe: And you can just accept this, can you?

text.Basch: After Vayne's ruse, I had abandoned hope for honor ... yet never did I forget my knightly vows. If I could protect but one person from war's horror ... then I would bear any shame. I would bear it proudly. I could not defend my home. What is shame to me?

text.Ashe: My people hate the Empire. They will not accept this.

text.Basch: There is hope.

text.ACTION: He looks to Vaan, Penelo, and Larsa all chatting casually.

text.Basch: Hope for a future where we can join hands as brothers.

text.ACTION: The scene changes. Two Judges of Empire stride down a grand corridor.
The Imperial City of Archades - The Imperial Palace

text.Bergan: The Senate may play at intrigue, but Lord Vayne will not be brought down easily. The entire military waits upon his orders, from the War Council to the rank and file. What better blade than he to strike down the enemies of the Empire?

text.ACTION: They pass by another Judge who leans against the corridor wall. They don't notice her till she speaks.

text.Drace: Your Honor reminds me of Zecht two years since. He, too, put his trust in Lord Vayne's strength, and what became of him? Gone without a trace since Nabudis!

text.Bergan: I will not hear you malign Judge Zecht! He was a noble warrior. Or ... do you think his trust in Lord Vayne ill-placed?

text.Drace: Vayne took two of his own brothers' lives. He is ruthless beyond contempt.

text.Bergan: Ruthless, you say? Would he were more so! He gives traitors no quarter, be they of his own blood! How fitting for one who would bear the burden of Empire.

text.ACTION: turning to the other Judge

text.Drace: Zargabaath, what of you? Surely you do not believe his brothers were traitors.

text.Zargabaath: So found His Excellency, Lord Gramis. You would do well to mind your tongue, Drace. That matter is long past.

text.ACTION: The two see Judge Gabranth approaching.

text.Gabranth: Your Honors, a summons! Lord Vayne has arrived at the palace.

text.ACTION: Bergan and Zargabaath leave Gabranth and Drace lagging behind.

text.Drace: Lord Larsa has left for Bur-Omisace. He hopes to enlist the aid of the Gran Kiltias in stopping the insurgents. I doubt this will be enough to deter Ondore ... but even a slight hindrance to his operations would be welcome. This will delay the Rozarrian invasion ... and we will have bought much-needed time to shore up our defenses.

text.Gabranth: Just as His Excellency had hoped.

text.Drace: No matter the result, I am pleased with the young Lord's progress. I can already see the stunned faces of those mud-witted senators. The fools think a child emperor's strings easy to pull from the shadows ... but they will find that Lord Larsa is no puppet.

text.Gabranth: Yes. The senators would be most pleased with a puppet for an emperor. Recall, Drace, how the Senate fears and despises Lord Vayne's ability? When they realize the truth, that Lord Larsa is no docile lamb to be shepherded ... they will bare their teeth and devour him.

text.Drace: You're right. I shall speak on this matter with His Excellency at once. Gabranth. It falls to us to protect Lord Larsa. Are we agreed?

text.Gabranth: Aye.

text.ACTION: They set off down the hall together. Fade out, and back to the party.

text.Game Hunter: We tried passing through Golmore Jungle, but we encountered some sort of barrier and could go no further. There must be a way through ...

text.ACTION: The party stands at the magical blue crest that acts as a barrier that blocks the path.

text.Vaan: What is it?

text.Fran: The jungle denies us our passage.

text.Ashe: What have we done?

text.Fran: We? No. I.

text.ACTION: Fran turns and walk away.

text.Vaan: What's that mean? How're we supposed to get through that?

text.ACTION: Balthier, some distance away, falls into step with her as she passes. You can hear Vaan indignantly shouting in the background.

text.Balthier: Making an appearance?

text.Fran: I am.

text.Balthier: I thought you'd left for good.

text.Fran: Our choices are few. This is as much for you as it is me.

text.ACTION: They stop on the steps. Fran turns to Balthier.

text.Fran: You are ill at ease. The nethicite troubles you?

text.ACTION: Balthier is silent.

text.Fran: You've let your eyes betray your heart.

text.ACTION: Balthier shrugs it off. Fran stands before what seems to be nothingness, tracing the air with her index finger, glowing green with magicks. Vaan, who has followed them, watches.

text.Vaan: What are you doing?

text.ACTION: Fran blows a soft breath with a gesture of her hand, almost as if blowing a kiss.

text.Fran: Soon you will learn.

text.ACTION: A grassy path suddenly opens before them. Vaan looks stunned.

text.Fran: We go to seek aid of the viera who dwell ahead.

text.ACTION: stepping in beside Vaan

text.Penelo: I bet they'll be glad to see you after so long.

text.ACTION: looking down

text.Fran: I am unwelcome. An unsought guest in their wood.

text.Garif Warrior (on crystal's side): Judges, here, in our village. Times have changed.

text.Garif Warrior (on riverbank by two sparr: More humes have come to our village, these in great suits of armor. I hear they have come to escort someone, but I know not who. They speak now with our War-chief.

text.War-chief Supinelu: These men among us, these Judges, came here to protect someone important from Archadia. And now I hear this person will accompany you. The Judges will soon leave us too, and quiet shall return to our village.

text.Judge Hausen: Do not fear, I bear you no enmity. I am Judge Hausen, guard to Lord Larsa. I would accompany my lord to Mt. Bur-Omisace, yet I fear my presence upon the holy mountain would ... excite the followers of the Light. I entrust Lord Larsa to your care. Please, take this. It may help you along your way.

text.ACTION: You obtain 3 Hi-Potions!
You obtain an Ether!

text.Judge Hausen: Normally I would accompany Lord Larsa to Mt. Bur-Omisace, yet I fear my presence would threaten the peace. I entrust Lord Larsa to your care. Please, be safe.

text.Fran: In the village ahead you will find her: Mjrn. Bring her to me. She will know why you call her.
