text.Acolyte (at top of steps): All Bur-Omisace mourns the passing of His Grace Anastasis. Now it falls to us to choose another Gran Kiltias, yet no one steps forward ... I fear the future of the Kiltias is imperiled.

text.Acolyte (slowly wandering the base of th: Hume-child, do you seek greater power? Know, then, the fate of those who have fallen in their search for strength. In the distant past, the great Condemner, too, sought such power, and was stricken down by the gods. Even now, his spirit is bound within the Stilshrine of Miriam ... Take this stone in hand, and walk the paths into darkness.

text.ACTION: You obtain the Stone of the Condemner!

text.Acolyte (slowly wandering the base of th: In the distant past, the great Condemner, too, sought such power, and was stricken down by the gods. Even now, his spirit is bound within the Stilshrine of Miriam. Know the fate of those who have fallen in their search for strength.

text.Kiltias (man standing at base of steps): Should the Archadians come again, what will become of us? We have no strength to resist an attack. Light's mercy on us all. Faram.

text.Ivaness: With the passing of His Grace Anastasis, the future of the Kiltias is shrouded in darkness. I pray the Light will cut through these clouds ...

text.Acolyte (speaking with Kiltias man): You go to the Imperial City of Archades? Hrmm ... It would not do to travel on foot. I recommend chocobo, or perhaps a gate crystal.

text.Kiltias (woman at entrance to temple gro: The holy mountain was greatly damaged in the Archadian attack. It falls to us who remain to rebuild ...

text.Wounded Refugee (woman looking over the: No one here has the strength to douse what remains of the fires. It wish it would all burn away, not smoke and sputter so.

text.Wounded Refugee (man looking over the ca: This rain ... do the gods weep? If they've time to weep, they've time to come down here and start saving us.

text.Relj: I turned my back on my home to see the world of the humes, and what I found was slaughter and despicable weakness.

text.Ieeha: Relj, do not say such things. If you find humes weak, then lend us your strength! Bereft of His Grace Anastasis's protection, Mt. Bur-Omisace is vulnerable. Even now, a terrible wyrm rages near. Many have fallen ...

text.Wounded Refugee (kid crying): No, Mama, no! You musn't die, you can't! Don't leave me! Mama ... !

text.Wounded Refugee (woman in blue dress aga: As soon as I am mended, I shall leave this place. I wouldn't stay here if they made me Gran Kiltias.

text.Wounded Refugee (man speaking with his f: There's an ailment called "disease," very nasty. Once you get that in your system, your wounds ... they won't heal. I've heard of people who fought on, even while diseased, till there weren't nothin' left to heal. It's enough to make you want to stay at home.

text.Wounded Refugee (old man with a crying c: I would leave for Rabanastre, but to pass through the rift, the viera's Wood, Ozmone Plain, and Giza ... I would not survive the trip.

text.Refugee (woman speaking with man): I thought Mt. Bur-Omisace free from the wars of the lands below ... Is there no safe haven left in Ivalice?

text.Refugee (man speaking with woman): I fled when the Imperial army came, yet I had nowhere to run to ... So I've come back.

text.Cartographers' Guild: Who thought that armies would ever come to Mt. Bur-Omisace, kupo? Would you like to buy a map, kupo?

text.Traveling Merchant (hume man at left): Go on, buy somethin'. Folks around here are too sullen to buy anythin'...

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Traveling Merchant (seeq): I've a mind to pack up and leave this place. The Imperials may be gone now, but they'll be back. Why, you may be my last customer.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Kiltias (Sandstrewn Pass): The Kiltias today have no strength to withstand the violence of the world below. The Archadian attack may well have been a divine test.

text.Kiltias (Walk of Mind): The same fleet we saw descend upon Mt. Bur-Omisace not long before you emerged from the shrine. I pray for our brothers and sisters on the mountain...

text.Refugee (blue seeq): They're short of helpers on Mt. Bur-Omisace, so I'm doing my part, guiding the refugees. Somebody's gotta be here to greet 'em, poor souls.

text.Refugee (man talking to seeq): For Mt. Bur-Omisace to be attacked ... I fear the dark times are just beginning! Where will the weak find sanctuary? Where will I go?

text.Garif Warrior (on crystal's side): Ah, it is you. To what far-off land do you travel now? You will have to tell me of your travels someday.

text.Asdalu: You have been to Mt. Bur-Omisace? Where do you go now? I admit, I envy you. I have never been further than the Plains in all my years. I, too, wish to see such wonders as the skycities someday ...

text.Warrior Guromu: our War-Chief is a great warrior, though not so great as his older brother, who served as War-Chief before him. Like a demon-god in battle he was.

text.Old War-chief Kadalu: I believe my brother — he is the War-Chief — wears his responsibility too heavily. He thinks he must do it all himself. Yet there is not one of us who is all-powerful. Thus we rely on our companions to make up for our shortcomings. If only he could see this...

text.War-chief Supinelu: You who walk the paths of Ivalice, I would give you advice. There are caves, called the Zertinan Caverns, near Ozmone Plain. The creatures that dwell in those caves are fell indeed. It is worth your life to venture inside. Be warned.

text.Garif Herder (by the nanna pen): On rare occasions, hume merchants come to our village, asking for us to sell them the cheese of the nanna. Our cheese would fetch a good price in the cities, they say. We Garif have no need of money, so we turn them down.

text.Garif Herder (standing in front of shack: Tell me, what do you think of our War-Chief? He is serious, and ofttimes grim to a fault. Why does he seek to do everything alone?

text.Garif Elder: Supinelu has only been War-Chief a short while. Yet he is too earnest, I think. His enthusiasm is well meant, but wasted. I would aid him...

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: I have been told that the hume armies head toward the land to the east. I had hoped that this conflict would be averted ...

text.Garif Youth: The wisdom of the village is passed down through words. I am still young, and there is much I do not know, so I must listen to what the elders say.

text.Old Dalan: So, you go now to Archades, do you? And afoot, no less ... Let us see ... that would take you first north, through the Mosphoran Highwaste. This will bring you to the Salikawood. There you must pass through a great gate on its eastern border before continuing further east still. I won't even ask what takes you to Archades ... I ask only that you do nothing I would not do, heh heh.

text.Wise Elder: The Imperial City of Archades? Why, that's past the Salikawood. I'd go northeast to Nalbina, and then across the mountains. Yes, that's it.

text.Itinerant Hand (black bangaa by the exit: Mosphoran Highwaste's just a ways down this road. Make your way across the Highwaste and you'll come out in the Salikawood. I'm quite fond of the starfruits you can find there. Now that the blockade is down, I'm hopin' Adair's Caravan will bring some to town.

text.Nalbinite: Many of our young men died defending their homeland in the war two years ago. Right here at Nalbina Fortress. They were slain. Yet now this place is a base for the Archadian armies. They have gathered labor to fortify the town in preparation for Rozarrian attack.

text.Caravaner (man in hat and white shorts): Hello there. Welcome to Adair's Caravan, bringing dreams, and bringing wares to every corner of the land. Crossing the mountains, are you? Rest here a while, it's a long way yet. You need something, you speak with Luccio.

text.Adair: You're a spirited one to walk these mountain roads, boy. Misplaced your airship, perhaps? Ha ha ha! About the only ones traveling on foot these days are those without two coins to rub together, dyed-in-the-wool travelers, or else ... But I don't mean to pry, and I won't. Going to Archadia? You'll want to cross the mountains to the north, then go east through the forest.

text.Luccio: Greetin's there, sonny. Anything you need, you let me know. 'Course, you gotta pay. Heh heh.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Luccio: Well now, you goin' to the capital? It's a long way. Best get what you need now, or you'll regret it later.

text.Va'Kansa: I've walked this way too many times to count, procuring wares in Archadia ... 'cept I never lost my partner before this time.

text.Caravaner (tan bangaa walking about): One of the old shrines up here still gets water. I wonder why none of the others do?

text.Scout: Would you like to buy a map, kupo?

text.ACTION: Mosphoran Highwaste 2400
Cancel

text.Scout: Guess what? I saw a giant bomb deep in the Salikawood, kupo! That's not far from the Nabreus Deadlands ... it probably came from there! If you're headed towards Archadia, don't get bogged down in Nabudis, kupo! Dangerous place, that!

text.Concerned Woman: Oh, are you headed to the capital, too? According to our map, we should go northwest from here ... but my husband, he cavils and stalls. He says he's concerned about the road ahead being blocked, but why don't we just go and see for ourselves?

text.Determined Traveler: My wife and I decided to throw it all away and head to the capital! But we hear that the road is blocked up ahead ... ... Where is she anyway? Last I saw her, she was headed off toward the shrines, saying she was thirsty ...

text.Scout (red bangaa): Hello there! I'm a scout, a guide to this Mosphoran Highwaste. If there's anything you'd like to know, just ask!

CHOICE.Vaan: How do you get to Archadia?

CHOICE.Scout (red bangaa): Huh? If you want to get to Archadia, just head north across the Mosphoran Highwaste, then east through the forest beyond. Only problem is, there's been trouble in the forest lately. Some travelers have turned back. But that's the only way through.
Like I said, we scouts are guides to the mountain. We know more about the Mosphoran Highwaste than anyone, and we're proud of it!

text.Caravaner (man in yellow sitting on low: I've seen some wild chocobos on this mountain, up to the northeast. I hear if you feed 'em good they'll even let you ride 'em. A wild chocobo for a mount could make a hard trip easy ... 'Course, you'd still have boulders to contend with. What to do with those ...

text.Learned Man: I've come from the capital to study the shrines here. They seem to be manufacted springs, in fact, drawing water up from an aquifer. Pity they seem to have dried up some time ago. The odd thing is, when I examined the shrines, the mechanisms seemed functional ... Perhaps the flow of water underground changed? Perhaps it might change again?

text.ACTION: Shrine of the Northwest Wind: A strange scent permeates the air.
Message is the same for South, Southeast, East, and Northeast Shrines.

text.Forest Traveler: There's a community of hunters on the Phon Coast. I came here thinking to join them, but my way is blocked. Should you head east from this forest, well to the east, you will find an old gate. Beyond that, the Phon Coast. Trouble is, the gate's broken. Some moogles were fixing it, but I have some doubt as to their industry in this matter. When will the gate be open? There being nothing to do about it, I returned here. Of course, now I've dropped my map of the wood, too. The Fates spit upon me, surely.

Should you head east from this forest, well to the east, you will find an old gate. Beyond that, the Phon Coast. Trouble is, the gate's broken. Some moogles were fixing it, but I have some doubt as to their industry in this matter. When will the gate be open? There being nothing to do about it, I returned here. Of course, now I've dropped my map of the wood, too. The Fates spit upon me, surely.

text.Layabout: Ooh? A visitor, kupo? We're here working in the gate up ahead. Well, not actually right now. Right now, we're resting.

text.ACTION: Note: Moogles in the bungalows at Trunkwall Road and the Garden of Decay will say the same thing before you talk to their boss at Living Chasm.

text.Overseer: If I don't find those layabouts and get them back on the job soon, the Boss'll have our Pom-poms! I don't think anyone's laying about beyond here, though. With bombs on the road, the next you take could be your last, kupo!

text.ACTION: The King Bomb comes shooting out of the forest, crashing against a couple trees before landing in front of the group.
After defeating the King Bomb, you get a victory fanfare.

text.Overseer: If I don't find those layabouts and get them back on the job soon, the Boss'll have our Pom-poms! I went searching up ahead, but no one was there, kupo. Only scary monsters! I was lucky to escape with singed whiskers!

text.Moogle Boss: Once the gate's fixed, everyone will be able to go to the Phon Coast, kupo. It'll take a little while longer, yet. That is, if my 9 missing apprentices ever come back from the Salikawood! We'll never finish repairs like this, kupo! They're probably loafing in the Salikawood bungalow ... Still 9 missing ...

text.Craftsmoogle (yellow-pommed moogle at le: We're here working on the gate up ahead. Except, right now we're taking a break, actually. What? The Boss wants us? Uh oh, kupo! We'd better go! He's ugly when he gets mad, kupo!

text.Layabout: of us on break out there!

text.ACTION: No one seems to be home ...

text.Craftsmoogle (green-pommed moogle at lef: Oh, we're here working on the gate down the road, kupo! But right now, it's break time, kupo! Kupo? The Boss wants us back on the job? That moogle-driver, kupo! (sigh) Well, let's get back and be done with this ...

text.Layabout: of us on break out there!

text.Craftsmoogle (red-pommed moogle,on the r: What? No, we're working on the gate up ahead ... Okay, we're not actually working on it right now, if you must be literal about it. The Boss wants us, kupo? Break's over, kupo? Ah well ...

text.Layabout: of us on break out there!

text.Craftsmoogle (white-pommed moogle on bot: Kupo? We're here working on the gate up ahead. Well, right now we're on break, actually. Eh? The Boss wants us, kupo? That's no good, he's scary when he gets mad! Okay, break time's over!
That's all of us, kupo! Let's get working!

text.ACTION: You found all of the moogles!

text.Craftsmoogle (white-pommed moogle on bot: Come with us to the gate, kupo?

text.ACTION: Living Chasm
The moogles are all working on various sections of the huge gate.

text.Moogle Boss: Now that my apprentices are all back, the repairs took no time at all, kupo! Witness the power of moogles!

text.ACTION: The gate unlocks and lifts behind him, opening the way.

text.Craftsmoogle (orange-pommed moogle at le: We're off to the Cerobi Steppe next, kupo. Once we're done fixing the windmills there, we'll put one back at the tavern in Balfonheim, kupo!

text.Craftsmoogle (yellow-pommed moogle at ri: Nothing better than a job well done, kupo. I'm headed off to the Cerobi Steppe for a job, and then, it's vacation time!

text.Craftsmoogle (green-pommed moogle at lef: We're off to do some repair work in the Mosphoran Highwaste next, kupo! Repairing what? Better ask the overseer ... wherever he is.

text.Craftsmoogle (white-pommed moogle on bot: Repairs are finished, kupo! We are off to our next job site ... Wish the Cerobi Steppe wasn't so far away, kupo ...

text.Craftsmoogle (yellow-pommed moogle at le: When we put our minds to it, we moogles get things done! Next stop, the Mosphoran Highwaste!

text.Craftsmoogle (white-pommed moogle at lef: It's been a while since the Craftsmoogle's League got together, kupo! We're usually scattered, off to one place or the other. Mosphora's next!

text.Craftsmoogle (red-pommed moogle,on the r: The Craftsmoogles' League will go anywhere in Ivalice we're needed, kupo! ...When we get around to it.

text.Craftsmoogle (red-pommed moogle's on the: Next stop is Nabudis to do repairs on the old palace ... if only those horrible monsters weren't trapped there! Someone should sort 'em out ...

text.Craftsmoogle (white-pommed moogle to upp: I hear we're off to the Necrohol of Nabudis next. But there're monsters there ... big ones! Let's play it safe, kupo.

text.Moogle Boss: Thanks to you, the repairs to the gate are finished, kupo. Here, a token of our gratitude!

text.ACTION: You obtain a Sash!

text.Moogle Boss: The Phon Coast is up ahead, kupo. Pretty views there, but the locals ... not so pretty.

text.Forest Traveler: What's this? The repairs to the gate are finished? Then I'm off to the Phon Coast ... once I find my map.

text.Overseer: I'm lost, kupo ... where is everybody, kupo? They didn't leave me behind, did they!? Just my luck ...

text.Basch: This is all that remains of Nabudis. Two years ago it was destroyed utterly by a mysterious force. The work of the Midlight Shard.

text.Vaan: This? In just 2 years? How?

text.Basch: As the Dawn Shard brought down the Leviathan and her fleet, a fell Mist spilled forth. It is like the same thing happened here. The nethicite's Mist has corrupted the life of this place. It is a necrohol overrun with beasts. We tread here on a fool's errand. We had best turn back.

text.Scout (red bangaa): Hello there! I'm a scout, a guide to this Mosphoran Highwaste. If there's anything you'd like to know, just ask!

CHOICE.Scout (red bangaa): The Mosphoran Highwaste is known for its oddly shaped rock formations. Some form roofs over the paths, or spires, or any number of other things. Also, right where you're standing is a spring, and resting place for travelers. The spring shrines antedate the Galtean Alliance! There is a lot we don't know about the shrines, even what their names mean. Some think they're shrines to wyrms, or water gods. All this and more awaits you in the Mosphoran Highwaste!

The Mosphoran Highwaste is a mountainous divide with Dalmasca to the south and Nabradia to the north, a different climate on each side. Incidentally, Archadia lies to the east, on the far side of the Salikawood. The gate that way was recently fixed, so you should get through fine.
Like I said, we scouts are guides to the mountain. We know more about the Mosphoran Highwaste than anyone, and we're proud of it!

text.Determined Traveler: My wife and I decided to throw it all away and head to the capital! The blocked road is open again, and our new life awaits! What is she doing, anyway? She's been staring at that rock forever!

text.Concerned Woman: Doesn't this giant boulder look like it's about to topple? If one were to push it from the other side ... avalanche!

text.Scout: Guess what? I saw a giant bomb deep in the Salikawood, kupo! That's not far from the Nabreus Deadlands ... it probably came from there! I'm sure the one I saw was the Bomb King! I wouldn't want a forest fire to break out, so I'd avoid exciting it, were I you, kupo ...

text.Learned Man: Behold, water has returned to the parched shrines! I still don't know how the flow came back, but this clears up a few mysteries. Would you care to hear my theory?

CHOICE.Learned Man: Previously, I believed these shrines were a sort of artificial spring, meant to deliver water to these mountains. How wrong I was! In fact, when water is flowing to the shrines, touching a shrine just so causes the temperature of the water to rise quite dramatically. The stream from this ... that's what lifts up the floatweed around the shrines! Floating up like balloons ... floating on the air itself ... It's a characteristic of the floatweed that makes it react to the steam so. In fact, I believe the shrines were made for no other purpose. With me so far?

Then allow me to continue. I ask: for what purpose might we want to float floatweed? Floatweed is a sturdy sort of shrub. When floating, several people can stand on it quite securely. Now, a book I read back in Archades said that floatweed was sometimes used to bridge gaps between rocks and such on mountain paths. I believe that here, in Mosphora, someone attempted to do the very same thing! Fascinating, don't you think? In documents on the Mosphoran Highwaste, one often hears of a place whose name translates roughly to the "wind-blown wyrm-god path." I had always wondered what it meant, and now I think it means the path's made of floatweed! And at the end of the path of the gods ... heaven! In other words, this was all a way to make a path to the summit ... that's my theory, at least. So, did you follow all that?

Unfortunately, I still can't find the route to the summit. Perhaps there's a trick to using the floatweed, or perhaps something else is needed ... One thing's for sure, I shall get to the bottom of this! ... A-And then the top. Obviously.
I see, that's... too bad. It really is quite interesting, you know.

text.Learned Man: There's a deep connection between the floatweed and the shrines ... Would you like to hear about it?

CHOICE.Learned Man: Touch a shrine, and steam comes out of the spring. In response, the surrounding floatweed rises, creating a path between cliffs and rocks. However, only three shrines may emit steam at one time. When a fourth is activated, the floatweed goes back down. I assume this is due to some limit on the amount of steam the shrines may produce. Line the floatweed up just so, and you could create a new road into the mountains. Myself, I'm aiming for the summit!
Very well. Just tap me on the shoulder should you change your mind.

text.Caravaner (tan bangaa walking about): One of the old shrines up here always had water. So I started wondering why none of the others did ... No sooner did I have the thought than water starts bubbling from the rest of the shrines! Weren't I surprised! This fellow here says the shrine waters have something to do with a road to a hidden place in the Mosphoran Highwaste ... Intriguing, eh?

text.Adair: I'll admit, when the water started flowing from the shrine, I was quite surprised. Take a look, boy, it's quite beautiful. That one over there, he's come all the way from Archades to visit this shrine and learn its secrets.

text.Va'Kansa: I got a baaaaad feeling about this ... Might be time to post a bill for one of them — what were they called? Marks? Eh? Sorry, don't mind me.

text.Luccio: Greetin's there, sonny. Anything you need, you let me know. 'Course, you gotta pay. Heh heh.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Luccio: With the Salika gate fixed, we should see more travel to Mosphora. If there's one thing I know, it's roads bring people.

text.Craftsmoogle (white-pommed moogle on bot: Kupo, you're the one I met by the Salikawood gate! Remember me, the craftsmoogle, kupo? I've come to check the shrines of Mosphora! Maintaining the ancient buildings of this land is a very important task for us League moogles.

text.Craftsmoogle (yellow-pommed moogle at le: Kupo-po-po ... I came to fix the shrines, but they're not broken, kupo! I guess I'll just rest here a while.

text.Craftsmoogle (green-pommed moogle at lef: I heard the shrines were broken, and the springs dried up. But look at all this water, kupo! I came all the way out here for nothing.

text.Caravaner (man in hat and white shorts): Hello there, traveler. Listen close, and I'll let you in on a secret: there's a path on this mountain you need a chocobo to access. Quite handy, too. Ach, sorry, but I can't hand you one of mine. These are for the caravan. Can't move wares if you can't move, eh? If you've some gysahl greens on you, you might try riding a wild chocobo. I saw one just northeast up the mountain.

text.Caravaner (man in yellow sitting on low: Now that's just the thing. Caravan life ain't easy, but you take in a view like this, and it's all worth it.

text.ACTION: Shrine of the South Wind: A strange scent rises from the running water.

CHOICE.ACTION: Steam pours out from the shrine and the floatweed at its top is released.
The surrounding floatweed is lofted into the air by the steam coming from the shrine.

text.ACTION: Nalbina Town

text.Pilgrim: It's my dream to work for the Craftsmoogles' League, kupo. But I lack the skill ... That's why I'm helping to rebuild here at Nalbina. The League's next project is the old palace in the Deadlands! B-But you know what I heard? I heard that a group of nu mou used magicked medallions to trap some evil creatures there!

text.ACTION: Imperial ships fly overhead.

text.Balthier: It would seem we made the right choice. If we'd taken the easy way and come by airship ... one of those patrols would no doubt have been quick to roll out the red carpet. We're on the Empire's doorstep now, so we shouldn't have to worry quite so much ... but that's no excuse to get sloppy. It is still a long road to the capital.

text.LOCATION: Balthier's Warning, and the Unforgettable Past

text.ACTION: The party enters the camp, with Vaan and Penelo at the front. The two take off running for the beach after Vaan says "Race you to the water!" Ashe trips in the sand, and Balthier catches her. She looks up at him before walking on. They're now behind everyone else.

text.Balthier: Why the capital?

text.ACTION: she stops

text.Ashe: The nethicite. I must destroy it.

text.Balthier: Are you sure? You don't want it for yourself? Use its power to restore Dalmasca — something like that? The best intentions invite the worst kind of trouble.

text.Ashe: Lusting for ever greater power, blinded by the nethicite.

text.ACTION: turning to him

text.Ashe: Is that how you see me?

text.Balthier: That does sound like someone I know.

text.ACTION: as he talks, we see Penelo and Vaan playing in the sand while Basch and Fran stand by watching

text.Balthier: He was obsessed with nethicite. It was all he cared about. He'd babble nonsense, blind to aught but the Stone's power. He'd talk about some 'Eynah,' or was it 'Venat'? No matter. Everything he did, he did to get closer to the nethicite, to understand it. He made airships, weapons ... He even made me a Judge.

text.ACTION: Balthier walks ahead, his back to Ashe. She stops short.

text.Ashe: You were a ... a Judge!?

text.ACTION: Balthier stops at the water's edge.

text.Balthier: Part of a past I'd rather forget. It didn't last long. I ran. I left the Judges ... and him.

text.ACTION: pause

text.Balthier: Cidolfus Demen Bunansa. Draklor Laboratory's very own Dr. Cid. That's when he lost his heart to nethicite, lost himself. And I suppose that's when I lost my father.

text.ACTION: Ashe, realizing the meaning behind his words, sighs in surprise and sympathy. Balthier turns his head and looks her in the eyes.

text.Balthier: Don't follow in his footsteps.

text.ACTION: These words received by Ashe, he turns back to the water.

text.Balthier: I ran away. I couldn't stand seeing him like that, a slave to the Stone. So I ran. Free at last. Funny I went for the Dusk Shard. How could I have known that it was nethicite? And then, of course, I met you. All that running, and I got nowhere. It's time to end this — cut my ties to the past.

text.ACTION: Ashe steps up beside him.

text.Ashe: It's hard to leave the past behind. I know.

text.ACTION: Fade out, and then in on a scene from the past ...
At the Rabanastran Royal Palace, Prince Rasler stands at the edge of a balcony, looking out over the sun-bathed city. Ashe appears from behind him. Though he doesn't look, he hears her approach.

text.Rasler: A marriage of convenience. A symbol of the alliance between Nabradia and Dalmasca. This is how they see our match.

text.Ashe: They do, do they?

text.Rasler: These roles we play... I must admit I find it wearying.

text.ACTION: Ashe put her hand on his.

text.Ashe: I will play mine.

text.ACTION: He turns to her and smiles.
The scene changes back to the beach on the Phon Coast. Ashe is gazing down at the wedding ring on her finger.

text.Balthier: The choice is yours to make. But don't give your heart to a stone. You're too strong for that, Princess.

text.Ashe: I pray you're right, Balthier.

text.Atak: What's that, boy? This here's a club for hunters, not children. Run along, now.

text.Huntmaster: You've the look of a hunter about you, true, but you're a bit wet behind the ears. We're looking for sharp-taloned birds of prey, here, son, not spring chickens. Run along now.

text.Blok: What's your business here, boy? You don't look much like a hunter. Pah. This ain't no pleasure dome, boy. Keep faring, wayfarer.

text.Stok: Listen good, boy. I don't hate your kind, I just hate you. See? So do us a favor and leave us be, eh?

text.Shifty-eyed Man: There's nothing for you here, boy. Shopping the Outfitters is a privilege, see.

text.Hawker: I was supposed to meet my partner here, but honestly, I don't think he's coming.

text.Realistic Man: I worry about the sorry state of our hunters here sometimes. I mean, falling to a fiend is one thing, but falling to a heat wave?

text.Game Hunter: We just come out here for the first time ... What a place! The shore seems to stretch on forever ... In fact, I woulda been lost if it weren't for that moogle straight up the hill there. He sold me a map, set me straight.

text.Fallen Bhujerban: Svagat ... er, welcome to the Hunter Camp, traveler. I ... am not a hunter myself, I do not think. I fell from a skycity, you see, and have forgotten everything from before the fall ... I do not even know my own name, bhadra!

text.Cartographers' Guild: Good day, hunter! How may I help you, kupo?

CHOICE.Cartographers' Guild: Would you like to buy a map, kupo?

Leave it to me, kupo! I'll soon point you the right way! That's my job! First thing, there are five ways in and out of camp here. But worry not, they only go to two places: the Tchita Uplands and the Salikawood. Which way were you headed, kupo?

There are two ways out to the Tchita Uplands, kupo. One runs along the coast, and one cuts up through the hills. If you plan on following the coast, you'll want to leave from the east side of the camp. To go the other way, you'll want to head off to my left, kupo. That way leads to the hills! Don't worry, no matter which way you take, you'll end up in the Tchita Uplands, kupo, guaranteed! Got that, kupo? You just come to me anytime you're feeling lost! This camp can be a confusing place, kupo!

There are three ways to the Salikawood, kupo! Two of them go by the sea, and one goes through the hills. To go the first way, head over to the southeast side of camp and follow the road up that rocky slope, kupo. That leads to the coast road! The other two ways are to my right, kupo. Go down the hill, and you'll soon be on the coast road. Stay higher up, and you'll reach the hills. Don't worry, no matter which way you take, you'll end up at the Salikawood, kupo! That said, the hill road is a touch shorter.

text.Concerned Hunter: I hear some hunters have gone up Sochen way to do battle with some nasties that think they own the place ... I wish 'em luck! If what I've heard is true, they're going to need their fair share of it!

text.Game Hunter (man in brown shorts speakin: I hear the moneyed folk up in Archades have taken to boastin' about hunters ... and wagerin' on 'em. Each of 'em tries to pick the best hunter to sponsor ... How can that possibly be fun? What are we, racin' chocobos?

text.Enthusiastic Streetear: What kind of information have I? Information what's beneficial to hunters, of course. Not that you'd have much need of that now, eh? Heh heh ...

text.Game Hunter (bangaa with the group inclu: You know that "bad breath" of the malboros? One whiff of that stuff and you'll be reeling with ailments. Nasty, that. There you are, totally in control, whole fight's going your way, and wham! You get hit with an ailment and everything goes to pot. Take care! It happened to me, it can happen to you.

text.Game Hunter (man in hat and blue shorts): Those red bangaa over there are talking about going to Archades on foot, I hear. Now, if you go from the Tchita Uplands through Sochen Cave Palace, you can reach Archades, all right. But the fiends in Sochen are a nasty lot. A group of hunters left to do something about that I hear ... I wish em' luck!

text.Nice Hunter: You're awful young-lookin' to be a hunter ... or are you just travelin', maybe? This coast may look pretty, but the men who come here, they're here for the hunt. If it is huntin' you're after, you might talk to some of 'em. Might learn somethin' of value, you never know.

text.Unmotivated Hunter: I've got a fancy to get up to Archades, make my fortune there. That's why I'm travelin' by foot. Got to save money ... 'Course, now I hear that the place right before you get to the capital, some ruin by the name of "Sochen-something-or-other's" rife with fiends! How'm I supposed to make it through that? I heard a group of hunters gone up that way, so I figure I'll wait for them to get back. Maybe they'll clear a path for me, eh?

text.Phon Camper: Are you traveling by foot, perchance? Take heed of the weather is my advice. Around here, when it rains, that's when the elementals come out.

text.Vendor of Goods: Hello there! If it's marks you'll be hunting, best go prepared.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Vendor of Goods: I know what you're thinking: why should I buy cures from this girl when all it takes is a good knock to the head to make all that ails me go away, right? Fact is, some ailments don't just go away. A blinded man goes down and comes back up just as blind as he went. Need an item to purge that lot!

text.Well-informed Bangaa: Hey, did you know that there's a sprawling ruin that comes up right under Archades? It's called the "Sochen Cave Palace." Fascinating place, that. Just head out of Phon and north across the Tchita Uplands ... that's where you'll find the entrance!

text.Aspiring Writer: I came here to hear the hunters' tales ... for I'm writing a novel based on the stories they tell me. Please, if you've aught to share ...

text.Laid-back Seeq: You know, I was up in Archades a while — a streetear on every corner. Knowledge is the lifeblood of that city, it is. My time there prepared me for just about anything. Yessir, I can sniff out rotten informations like a rat after cheese! (sniff sniff)

text.Proud Hunter: You seem like the adventurous sort, so I'll tell you something interesting: to the north of Tchita Uplands, there is an ancient ruin ... Everyone's talking about the fiends there ... rather dangerous, by the sound of it. I say, if they're so concerned, shouldn't they go and hunt the fiends themselves!? I mean, they are hunters, aren't they!

text.Cheery Hunter: When I first heard of a camp filled with hunters, well, I imagined the worst. How surprised I was to find it quite pleasant!

text.Helpful Hunter: Perhaps you weren't aware, but should you leave this camp to the northeast, you'll find yourself shortly in the Tchita Uplands. We'll soon be traveling that way ourselves, then east on to Balfonheim.

text.Game Hunter (man talking with two bangaa: Yours is a face I've not seen around these parts. You seem a bit young to be one of us ... but you don't have the look of a wayfarer, either! All right, all right, enough being nosey ... I'll keep to my own business. Heh.

text.Game Hunter (bangaa talking with same gr: Ah, you got to love this place. Blue sky, white sand, and all the news your ears could hope to hear from the other hunters. The perfect stop!

text.Phon Camper (tan bangaa standing on beac: Many things wash up here on the beach, you know. Mostly crates off merchant galleys, but every so often, something drops down from the sky. That is, from the skycities. A while back, a man came washing up ... from Bhujerba, if I had to guess. He's in the camp now. Amazing, eh?

text.Rimzat: Hello there! You are looking well! It is me! The one sent to study the sandstorms in the Westersand ... do you not remember? As you can see, I am on holiday at the moment. Nothing came of my commission, but thankfully my other work has kept me busy ... Aah? The sandstorm has died down, you say? When you defeated the Earth Tyrant? Well, that deserves a hearty round of congratulations! I knew you would make it far! After all, you had me to guide you, yes? But you should have told me sooner! Mayhap there is a bonus in this for me ...

text.ACTION: Rimzat will disappear from the area after this.

text.Neophyte Hunter: We've come all the way here, and now our leader doesn't want to go into camp! Says he doesn't like crowds ... but I think he's scared. Not that I don't understand. Hunters are a fearsome lot, even when you're one of 'em!

text.Little Hunter: I came all the way through the Salikawood to be here, kupo! But ... I don't think the Club is for me. I was born to ride alone, kupo!

text.Viera Wayfarer: Where do you go, wayfarer? To the east lie the Tchita Uplands. To the north, across the plains, lies the seat of empire, Archades. Myself, I shall go east, to the port town of Balfonheim. I have heard it is a place where men and women value freedom above all else.

text.ACTION: If you speak to the Viera Wayfarer with Fran as party leader, you'll get this dialogue...

text.Viera Wayfarer: What's this? To meet another viera, here ... You, too, have left the Wood? I have left, for I desired freedom. Had I remained, I would have surely perished. You see, freedom to me is like the air itself. Yet, I did not think my little sister would follow. She would not listen to me, and now I fear I may have erred in allowing her to come.

There is good beyond the Wood, yet all is not so. Still, I feel I was right to leave. I shall go east from here, to the port town of Balfonheim. I have heard it is a place where men and women value freedom above all else.

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Boy): This weak-kneed bangaa is worthless, utterly worthless. Just like every other hunter my father employs. You wouldn't happen to be a hunter, would you? I'd like to hire you to deal with a terrible menace in the Sochen Cave Palace!

text.Bill?: A terrible menace plagues the Sochen Cave Palace. Calling hale hunters of all ages and races to deal with this scourge upon us.

text.ACTION: WARNING

text.Bill?: This is not an official bill, and it will not be listed in the clan primer.

CHOICE.Archadian Wayfarer (Boy): East of here you come to the Highlands. North of there lie the Fields of Eternity, wherein can be found the entrance to Sochen. The foul scourge I wish you to defeat lurks within the cave palace. Many hunters have been sent, and all have come running home. Incidentally, I have no idea what this scourge is or looks like. No one that returns will speak of it. ...Intriguing, no? My father, wanting to know the identity of this fell creature, thought to post a bill for the mark ... but was refused! Having no other choice, he employed two hunters from the Hunter's Camp on the Phon Coast, and sent them into Sochen Cave Palace! A pity they were worthless ... I waited with my father at the entrance to the caves and they came running back out mere moments later. They ran right past my father, their employer. Unbelievable! Enraged, I gave chase ... and was separated from my father. Anyway, I'm glad we've met. Were ito hire better hunters than my father, and defeat this monstrosity, oh, the respect I'd earn back in Archades! So, you're hired. Use this key to get into the cavern where you'll find the creature! And no coming back until you've slain it!

CHOICE.ACTION: You obtain the Soul Ward Key!

CHOICE.Archadian Wayfarer (Boy): Are you ... scared? You are, aren't you. Coward. Yet another mewling puss. (sigh)

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Boy): What are you mumbling about? Hmm? You want to see my bill again? Fine, be my guest.

text.Bill?: A terrible menace plagues the Sochen Cave Palace. Calling hale hunters of all ages and races to deal with this scourge upon us.

text.ACTION: WARNING

text.Bill?: This is not an official bill, and it will not be listed in the clan primer.
Confirm the location of the petitioner?

CHOICE.Archadian Wayfarer (Boy): The petitioner is me, right here before you. If you've time to waste chatting with me, get on with the hunt! Go to the Highlands to the east, then to the Fields of Eternity north of there to find the entrance. Got it? Good!
Go to the Highlands to the east, then to the Fields of Eternity north of there to find the entrance. Got it? Good!

text.ACTION: The Nameless Spring

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Father): You're one of those Phon Coast hunters, aren't you? Good, I've work for you. In a hurry, you see. Have to find my son ... wherever he is.

text.Bill?: A terrible menace plagues the Sochen Cave Palace. Calling hale hunters of all ages and races to deal with this scourge upon us.

text.ACTION: WARNING

text.Bill?: This is not an official bill, and it will not be listed in the clan primer.

CHOICE.Archadian Wayfarer (Father): Head to a place known as the Highlands. From there, go north into the Fields of Eternity where you'll find the entrance to Sochen. The menace you must defeat is within. Many are the hunters that have attempted to slay it ... all have come running back out, defeated. The exact nature of the beast is unknown. Nor have any of the hunters that ran said as much as a word ... To put an end to this scourge, I thought to post a bill for its hunting ... Those clansmen refused my expertly written wanted bill, saying it was "crude and ingenuous in its execution." They wanted me to rewrite it! Wounded, I withdrew my posting. I thereupon hired two hunters from the Phon Coast and sent them into the cave ... the craven curs! As my son and I waited by the entrance, these two so-called "hunters" came running out and past us, completely ignoring me, their employer! Enraged, I gave chase, managing to catch one of the two, lying upon the ground, utterly useless. Worse, I was separated from my son. So went all until now. Understood? Very well! Now I will call my servants from Archades to search for my son, while you enter the caves! Use this key to access the chamber where this menace may be found. Off with you!

CHOICE.ACTION: You obtain the Soul Ward Key!

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Father): Do you plan on waiting here all day? Eh? You wish to see my bill again? Is your memory as poor as your sense of industry?

text.Bill?: A terrible menace plagues the Sochen Cave Palace. Calling hale hunters of all ages and races to deal with this scourge upon us.

text.ACTION: WARNING

text.Bill?: This is not an official bill, and it will not be listed in the clan primer.
Confirm the location of the petitioner?

CHOICE.Archadian Wayfarer (Father): Are you as witless as you are craven? I'm the petitioner! Me! East to the Highlands, north into the Fields of Eternity, and into the caves! Got it? You're quite sure? Shall I repeat it again!?
Are you as witless as you are craven? I'm the petitioner! Me! East to the Highlands, north into the Fields of Eternity, and into the caves! Got it? You're quite sure? Shall I beat it into your pate!?

CHOICE.STATUS: if you’ve accepted the hunt from his son

CHOICE.Archadian Wayfarer (Father): I hired hunter after hunter to defeat the mysterious menace within the Sochen Cave Palace, yet all returned empty-handed. Craven curs to a man! And I was separated from my son. Oh, most foul of days!

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Father): Going to Sochen Cave Palace? Then go to the Highlands to the east, then to the Fields of Eternity north of there to find the entrance. You may encounter a well-dressed, clever-looking boy along the way ... my son. Please tell him his father waits for him here.

text.Game Hunter (Tchita): I'm a hunter, out of the Phon Coast ... contracted to defeat this menace in the Sochen Cave Palace, but I can't find my employer! Where is he ... ? We were supposed to meet in the Tchita Uplands ... but this is the road to Cerobi Steppe! Must've taken a wrong turn somewhere ...

text.ACTION: The party walks into a vast cavern; the bright sun from the Tchita Uplands bleeds in through the entryway behind them, but we see darkness ahead.

text.Vaan: Hey, you sure this rabbit hole's really the way into Archades?

text.Balthier: Better a hare unseen than a rat in a trap. Then again, if you'd prefer to go knocking on the front gates of the city, be my guest.

text.Penelo: But what about once we're inside? Won't the city watch find us?

text.Ashe: We'll do what we can to blend into the crowd. Our names may be notorious, but our faces are not far-known.

text.Vaan: True, true. You're our princess, and we didn't even recognize you.

text.Ashe: I noticed.

text.ACTION: Gate of the Soul Ward: The door is locked.

CHOICE.ACTION: You use the soul ward key.

text.ACTION: Hall of Lambent Darkness

Enter a large chamber, where first one, then another, and another mandragora appear til there are four total. A fifth pumpkin headed one comes running in and trips so that its head goes flying off and bonks the other four one after the other. When they finally collect themselves, you face off against them.
After defeating the Mandragoras ...
A bell tolls as the five Mandragoras lie dead. After a few tolls, their ghosts rise from their bodies and float up through a hole in the cavern ceiling.
You get a victory screen with "Mandragoras Vanquished" message.
If you accepted the hunt from the son ...

text.Archadian Wayfarer (father): Walking to Archades, are we? I pity your feet! I shall be going home soon, too. In our private airship, of course.

text.Archadian Wayfarer (son): So you defeated the menace of Sochen Cave Palace? Not bad at all! Hone your skills, and we might have a place for you on our house staff. Here, your reward. This is the going rate. Go on, take it.

text.ACTION: You obtain 1000 gil!
You obtain 3 Remedies!

text.Archadian Wayfarer (son): I cant wait to go back to Archades to tell my friends! My hunter defeated a horrible menace! My hunter!

text.ACTION: If you accepted the hunt from the father ...

text.Archadian Wayfarer (son): Huh. So you defeated the menace of Sochen Cave Palace? I suppose even my father can pick a winner ... given an infinite number of chances.

text.Archadian Wayfarer (father): So you've defeated the menace of Sochen? Well done! You're in danger of showing signs of promise! I may even use you again one day! Here, your reward, richly deserved. I always respect a job well done. And I've found my son, to boot!

text.ACTION: You obtain 1000 gil!
You obtain 3 Remedies!

text.Archadian Wayfarer (father): Walking to Archades, are we? I pity your feet! We shall be going home soon, too. In our private airship, of course.

text.ACTION: After you collect your reward, they will disappear from the area when you leave.

text.Game Hunter: This here's the end of Tchita Uplands. East is Cerobi Steppe, but a landslide's made the road unkind to travelers on foot.

text.Enthusiastic Streetear: When it comes to the hunt, results are everything. Age and species don't matter; if you slay your mark, you're a hunter. It's a tough life, but worth every moment!

text.Game Hunter (man in hat and blue shorts): I heard them nasties up in Sochen got what was coming to them. Guess some hunter was worth his salt, eh?

text.Nice Hunter: Lo, there! I heard the news! They're saying you took down the scourge of Sochen! A whippersnapper like you! That's something to be proud of.

text.Unmotivated Hunter: I hear the worst of the nasties in Sochen've been taken care of. It might be time for us to make our way up there ... ...And wouldn't you know that my travelin' companion picks now to up 'n' collapse! Can't take a little exercise ... Pah!

text.Laid-back Seeq: Better a reward in the hand than a treasure you'll never grasp. See, hunters aren't like sky pirates. They're realists, not dreamers.

text.Well-informed Bangaa: All right, there's been some confusion on this point, so I want to get it straight now, for the record. "Headhunters" are fellows who capture criminals for bounty. "Hunters" are them what hunt marks — them being creatures and the like — for rewards. Now, there was talk once of this headhunter, a bangaa, and a cruel, evil fellow who'd do anything for a little coin. They said he was working in secret for one of them Judges up in Archades! Justice ... heh. I haven't heard much talk of him lately, but headhunters that mean don't die easy. He's probably laying low somewhere, most like.

text.Concerned Hunter: I hear the nasties up Sochen way have been dealt with ... but it weren't no hunter from this camp that did 'em in! Speaking of which, the hunting sortie that went up there never came back, did they. Hope they didn't get lost ... or worse.

text.Realistic Man: So, friend, what's it going to be this time? Some great wyrm? A feral cockatrice, perhaps? Or will you do battle with authority ... or destiny?

text.Hawker: I'm setting up the next trade deal, here. The folks 'round here want all kinds of bizarre things, I tell you.

text.Game Hunter (bangaa talking with same gr: There're all sorts of creatures out there ... only a small sampling ever get put up as marks, see. Now hunting marks is the hunter's job ... but there are plenty other nasties out there needing a good hunting, too, if you ask me.

text.Stok: So it was you what bagged the mandragoras up Sochen way? Hah! Never woulda guessed it. Go talk to the Huntmaster.

text.Blok: I hear you did a piece of hunting off in Sochen? The Huntmaster said you were ready for testing ... Eh? What kind of testing? Now that's for me to know, and for you to find out after you've taken care of your business in Archades. Later, boy.

text.Atak: Boy ... you did some huntin' in Sochen, I hear? Guess that game was easier pickin's than the rumors'd have it, eh? Bah. You did for it, so that's that, I suppose. The Huntmaster was sayin' we could start ... ah, but I'm gettin' ahead o' meself. You've business in the capital, no? You get that attended to, then you come back here, and we'll see what you're really made of, boy.

text.Huntmaster: Ah! You're the one who took down the mandragoras in Sochen, eh? You might have the makings of hunter yet! I'm looking for the best of the best here. You ... and your friends ... you may have some potential, and I'm willing to give you a chance. You've business in Archades, right? You come back here once that's settled, and we'll have a look at you.

text.Moogle Boss: I'd like to try restoring the old palace of Nabudis ... but they don't call it a Necrohol for nothing! Nasty creatures said to be in there ... The good news is, some Nu mou managed to bind the nastiest within. The bad news is, no one knows when the bonds will break, kupo...

text.ACTION: An adventurer bound for the capital. It would seem he didn't make it.
Pilgrim's Door: The door bears an inscription.

CHOICE.ACTION: "Wayfarer travelling the road to Archades, the Pilgrim's Door holds naught for you. That way lie trouble and confusion. You who are yet drawn toward the Pilgrim's Door, the heart of Time and the deeds you must accomplish share their place midst the falls. From the heart look north to Heaven. From the heart step south to Earth. Walk in Time's footfalls to open the way."
Some unknown mechanism holds it fast.

text.ACTION: Falls of Time
The course of the waterfalls seems to have changed.
Mark of Counsel: The wall bears a mysterious inscription.

CHOICE.ACTION: "Wayfarer travelling the road to Archades, the Pilgrim's Door holds naught for you. That way lie trouble and confusion. You who are yet drawn toward the Pilgrim's Door, journey Heaven and Earth in search of the heart, and you will surely reach it.

text.ACTION: You hear a door open in the distance.
Mark of Counsel: There are words inscribed on the wall.

CHOICE.ACTION: "Wayfarer travelling the road to Archades, the Ascetic's Door holds naught for you. That way lie trouble and confusion. You who are yet drawn toward the Ascetic's Door, in circles travel from land of Sun's birth. Stray but once, another day you must return.

text.ACTION: Ascetic's Door: The door bears an inscription.

CHOICE.ACTION: "Wayfarer travelling the road to Archades, the Ascetic's Door holds naught for you. That way lie trouble and confusion. You who are yet drawn toward the Ascetic's Door, count out your steps tracing Sun's round. At journey's end, the Door embrace you."
Some unknown mechanism holds it fast.

text.ACTION: Hall of Shadowlight
A ghoul emerges from the floor.
After you defeat the Ahriman ...
The Ahriman disappears into the floor and you get a victory screen.

text.ACTION: The party emerges from Sochen into a dingy alleyway. Balthier stretches.

text.Vaan: Smells less like a capital and more like a sewer.

text.Balthier: Even empires have need of sewers. The runoff from Archades proper pools here; those who lack papers to live in the city itself. The mighty who have fallen, and the fallen who would be mighty. Their eyes never leave Archades.

text.Vaan: I guess it must be a lot nicer than this place.

text.Balthier: Oh, to be sure. Archades reeks of a different filth. Let's be off! We can follow our noses to Draklor.

text.Man at the Gate: Hrm? Now this is new. Plenty o' worms come up out o' the ground 'ere, but not many of 'em are the sort wi' two legs. Come to make your fortune in th' capital? A word of advice, worms: turn back while ye've still some gil to yer name.

text.Precocious Girl: Come to buy information, or, perhaps, to sell? Information is what makes this town work. Why, if I had gil or a chop to spare, I'd make an offer for what ye know right now ...

text.Stranded Merchant: Meh! Lost all my money ... Can't even afford an airship back home to Rabanastre! Aye, I thought of going back through Sochen, but I hear some ancient wyrm lurks down there, and I don't much care to run into one of those. You think I could get away on these legs!? Bah! I'm stuck here for life. Look, wouldya buy something to help a fellow out? (snort)
I'm saving gil to get back home to Rabanastre. Buy something to help a fellow out?

text.Wary Woman: Welcome to Archades ... Old Archades, that is. The people 'ere, they all took their dreams up to the City, 'ad 'em stripped away, an' fell back down.

text.Stairbottom Elder: Yours is an unfamiliar face. If you're here hoping to go up to the City, best find yourself information that's like to interest the ardents and gentry. Word travels fast in this town. New information is born, grows old, and dies in a day. The Emperor's assassination? Ancient history, my friend.

text.Hating Man: Now that's a face I dislike. It's the eyes ... Beady, shinin'... Eyes that see but ne'er show. You know the sort. Eh, whom do I speak of? Vayne, or course! Only a man like that could do what he's done, killin' his own two brothers in cold blood for opposin' the Emperor ...

text.Cautious Woman: Headed to the City, are ye? Going to be a soldier like the rest of 'em? I wish ye luck. Ye go up there, you die a little inside. Aye, a part of ye goes cold an' black. Just like them senators ... I'd stay down here, if I were you.

text.Loiterer: I tire of swapping tidbits of information in the street ... though there's naught else I fancy doin', truth be told. That's the problem with success ...

text.Archadian Fisherman: What can ye catch here? Well, lots o' things, I s'pose. Depends on what yer fishin' for. Me? I'm fishin' fer ma past ... fer the fire o' ma youth. What? No, ye cannae feed a family with the past. But ye can keep yerself warm at night.

text.Braggart: Me dad's the 'ead of one o' them big entry-prizes up in the City!

text.Defiant Lad: Ye mean 'e was the 'ead. 'E ain't the 'ead no more. There's lots o' them 'round 'ere. Them as used be 'ead, I mean.

text.Resting Man: D'ye wonder why I sit here, doin' naught day-come, day-go? I've done me bit for the Empire, that's why. I've earned me rest. Don't you ever fancy a rest, young 'un?

text.Frank Woman: Do you have business with us? I'll tell you straight out, we've no money, so don't even bother trying to relieve us of it.

text.Ex-Broker: I played many a man false in the City, so I did. 'Course, I was bein' played just the same, though I didn't know it. I've ruined so many men ... 'Tis all I can do now to hide meself here 'n' hope I don't run into any former "clients."

text.Busy Girl: Wot am I doin'? Gatherin' tidbits o' knowledge, that's wot! Think I got bags o' time like you oldies? 'Cos I ain't!

text.Dreaming Man: Brother, brother mine! If we'd only bought them cockatrices when we 'ad the chance, why, we'd be rich men today, so we would.

text.Sensible Man: Brother, brother mine. Cockatrice meat's not 'alf as tasty as they'd 'ave you believe. This recent int'rest in 'em's a fad, you mark my words. Nah, cockatrices or no, our fate's the same.

text.Cockatrice: Me? I've lived here for a good while, now, but I had a jolly hard time when I first arrived. The City was a far cry from my native Giza, you see. But I've seen much in this town. People of all walks of life ... Life ... now there's a fascinating thing. I've seen plenty of men who've failed at it. Lost their hope and then their happiness ... . Most sad. Why, hope's the most important thing of all ... We cockatrices, we must hold on to hope even when our days in this world seem to be numbered. Me? I hope to see my homeland once more ...

text.Fresh Ardent: Who am I? Ain't it plain to see? I'm one o' the many wot tried to make it up in the City 'n' fell back down 'ere. If only I 'adn't signed that paper ... Yeah, I was an ardent with the rest of 'em. All it took was one broker, one bindin' agreement, and nary a scruple in sight. If I find 'im, I'll ... Eh? Did ya want somethin'? Oh, 'ow to get to the City? Up these stairs, then off to the west. Entrance's up there. Better be prepared, mate.

text.Sighing Boy: Once she gets goin', she don't half go on! I only hope her grandad sets her straight. Ain't my place to worry about it, I s'pose. (sigh)

text.Perplexed Grandpa: Me granddaughter claims she's seen a great airship. 'Course, I thought it was the Alexander, that being the biggest I know of. But her description ... Mayhap they've made a new, bigger airship now?

text.Leaving Man: I'm off tomorrow ... to destiny! Mark my words: I'll be the richest man in Archades soon, and I'll bring you a diamond big enough to prove it!

text.Waiting Woman: So soon? Ah, no, 'twould come in time. Spare me the diamond. Just ... stay true. I'll be waiting.

text.Shady Seeq: Oi, you there. Ya look like someone who knows a good deal when 'e sees it. So ... 'ows about some moogles then, eh? I've got eight of 'em. Discount if ya take the lot. It's a bargain! They're cute, they dance ...

text.Suspicious Woman: That seeq over there seems a bit dodgy. Says he's a merchant of some sort, but I haven't seen him peddling any wares.

text.Indecisive Man: I've been told that joining the Watch is a good way to get on in the world ... yet others tell me it's a hard life ... full of hard choices. What to do ... ? What to be ... ? That's the problem with having too much information: ''tis difficult to make up your mind!

text.Wall Child: See that bridge up there? On the far side o' that is the Imperial City of Archades. When I get a bit bigger, I'm gonna be a soldier there.

text.The Moogles Eight: A seeq there was, he sought to play,
Said he, "I'll take you far away."
A gourmet tour, he promised us.
But all we've 'ad is curds and whey.

text.Proud Brother: Me little brother's back! The pride an' joy of the clan's come back with tales from the City!
So 'ow was it? Don't tell me: you made a mint, didn't ya? Nuff for all of us, I'll bet!

text.Weary Brother: Well, I, er, did set up a shop. But the competition ... Let yer guard down for a moment, and the next store over'll slip a knife in yer ribs ... How I've wanted to come home!

text.Distinguished Elder: Wot? We're ain't here for yer viewin' pleasure, nor are we beggin', nor are we blockin' up yer precious gutter. Not yet, at least. So get lost.

text.Granddaughter: Away! Away! My grandad was a right important man up in the City, don't ye know!

text.Distinguished Elder: Hush with ye, sweetheart. Beggin' yer pardon, sir. Pay no one to her. She talks about things she knows little of. Aye, I've a lot in me past, but today I'm just one o' the proud wretches of Oldtown, clingin' onto the underbelly o' the Empire. Now leave us be.

text.Hungry Child: I'm bloomin' 'ungry. Me mum and me gran keep tellin' me that sittin's best when yer 'ungry, but it don't seem to be workin' for me. Maybe if I 'ave a chat with me mum I'll forget about me empty belly ... Or maybe not. ...I'm bloomin' 'ungry!

text.Returnee: 'Tis good to be home ... Those who went up to the City and ne'er came back, they either made it, or fell by the wayside, forgotten. But not me.

text.Quiet Talker: This geezer? Nah, 'e ain't dead, not by a stretch. 'E was a soldier once. Made it pretty far, it seems. 'E's lived a full life, if ya ask me.

text.Little Sister: 'Ello there. Mmm? Oh, don't bother tryin' to talk to 'er. Me sister's not stopped lookin' off into the distance since 'er fella went up to the City ...

text.Indefatigable Granny: Eh, me? I'm ready t' begin a new life up in the City, that's for sure. I been tricked out of all I owned before, but this time, I'll go prepared.

text.Shifty-eyed Man: Know where the Alley of Muted Sighs got 'er name? See, there's two kinds o' people 'ere: them as want to go up to the City ... An' them as want to keep those people down 'ere where they belong, tellin' 'em lies, an' spreadin' misinformation to confuse 'em. Them poor ones wot never made it up ... they're the ones wot are sighin', see? You ... weren't 'eaded up to the City, were ya?

text.Lucky Man: Psst. I'll tell ye a secret, but it stays between us two, right? I spied summary in-credible jus' now. What? Wouldn't ye like to know! ''Twas a bag o' coin! Jus' thrown in a barrel, it was. With a hoard like that, the City'll be me oyster! Now don't go tellin' anyone, ye hear?

text.Disparaging Woman: Trying to go up to Archades, perchance? I know the type. All hopes an' dreams, but never any knowledge. Ye wouldn't venture into battle without a blade, am I right? To go to the City without the proper knowledge, why, 'tis the same thing. And I'll tell ya summat else: it was knowledge what brought them Senators to their knees, an' that's the truth. Still want to go to the City?

text.Worried Grandson: Me gran's got me worried. She keeps on talkin' about goin' to the City, an' makin' 'er fortune. Makin' 'er fortune!? She's old!

text.Beasley: Don't think ye can look down on me. I'm savin' me gil to get out of here and up there. Why, I've got a bag full o' coin put aside already ... That is, I had a bag full o' coin, till someone came along and stole it! Grr ... I was sure it'd be safe as houses in that barrel, too ...

text.Nay-Sayer: You going on from 'ere? On from 'ere's Archades. You go there, you'd best watch yerself. People there, they'd pluck the feathers from a livin' chocobo if they thought they could make a profit on 'em. I'd turn back if I was you.

text.Otto: You think you might ... . not stare at me? I'm in the midst of a very important conversation.

text.Fermon: Come to hear a tale, perhaps? There's a lot to be learned from the stories of the past ... a lot you youngsters seem to have forgotten. To your peril. You should show a little more respect ... for faerie tales.

text.Jules: Might a boy be in the market for some ... information? Sorry, I've none worth selling. Such a boy would be wise to pass on anything he heard to me, though ... I'll pay a good price for word of goings-on in the Ministry of Law and the Senate. A boy could stand to make a profit ...

text.Frustrated Woman: I've plans to go up to the City with my beau ... But he's kept me waiting for hours! I expect he's lost. (sigh) He's so provincial.

text.Broken Man: I spent some time in the City, once ... gatherin' up all the information I could lay me 'ands on. But it turns out some of it weren't true ... an' before long I ended up back down 'ere.

text.Nervous Seeq: The City's just up these stairs ... Me head says all I've gotta do is walk up 'em, but me feet are tremblin', what with the assassination an' all.

text.Trembling Woman: People 'round 'ere? They're the ones wot didn't make it up there. Dregs. Dropouts. Ah, 'ow I tire o' the vulgar life ... But I'll get out.

text.Fallen Man: Best not speak to me, lest my ill luck rub off on you. I lost everything ... Everything! Ah, if I'd only had the right information ...

text.Imperial (Guarding Archades Entrance): Entering the capital? You have credentials?

CHOICE.Imperial (Guarding Archades Entrance): Hm? Well I don't see any! We can't just throw open our gates to you vulgars, you know. Especially not the lying kind! Away with you!
No credentials!? We can't just throw open our gates to any old riff-raff who happen to be passing by. Be off with you, commoner!

text.ACTION: After being turned away by the Imperial, the party hears a strange voice.

text.Jules: Well, well, well ... there's a sight for sore eyes. Didn't think I'd be seeing you again. Not here.

text.ACTION: A man in raggedy street clothes leans against a wall nearby.

text.Balthier: Oh wonderful. Enter the streetear.

text.Jules: A pirate would do well to smile. Wouldn't want to sour his reputation.

text.Vaan: You know this guy?

text.Balthier: An old ... friend. He's a streetear — a peddler of rumor and hearsay, by the name of Jules. He'd bite a gil given him by his own mother, and shave it by half to pay for her funeral.

text.Jules: Sometimes an ear with tight purse strings's the order of the day. Like when a pirate decides he fancies going up in the world.

text.Vaan: To the city? You know a way?

text.Jules: In Archades, knowledge is power. And power has a way of opening doors, boy. Now, a fool will buy a sack of feathers for his pillow, but a wise man ... He'll buy the whole stinking cockatrice and get his fill of meat into the bargain. So, wise man, how does 1500 gil sound?

CHOICE.Jules: Bright boy. You learn fast. I call this meeting to order. Tell me, boy, heard any rumors in town?

CHOICE.Vaan: Actually, I did hear about a man who picked a bag of coins out of a barrel.

CHOICE.Jules: Bags in barrels, eh ... ? A boy would do well to bring that morsel to a man named Beasley near here. Tell him what you've heard.
You would do well to learn the ways of the world, boy, lest the world have its way with you.

text.Jules: So, wise man, how does 1500 gil sound?

CHOICE.Jules: Bright boy. You learn fast. I call this meeting to order. Tell me, boy, heard any rumors in town?

CHOICE.Vaan: Actually, I did hear about a man who picked a bag of coins out of a barrel.

CHOICE.Jules: Bags in barrels, eh ... ? A boy would do well to bring that morsel to a man named Beasley near here. Tell him what you've heard.
You would do well to learn the ways of the world, boy, lest the world have its way with you.

text.Jules: Boy. There's a man near here who goes by the name of "Beasley." Tell him what you just learned.

text.Beasley: Whaaat!? Yer tellin' me that ye know the bloke what's taken me coin!? Oh, it was him, was it?

text.ACTION: Balthier and Vaan stand before Jules as he sits perched on a crate.

text.Jules: You told him just as I told you? Good boy!

text.Vaan: I'm not sure what any of this has to do with going up in the world.

text.Jules: Oh? Witness the power of knowledge, m'boy. See? It begins.

text.ACTION: One of the residents of Oldtown runs up, shouting to the others.
People run toward the scene -- including the Imperials.

text.Vaan: Now's our chance! Thanks, Jules.

text.ACTION: Vaan runs off, but Balthier hangs back.

text.Balthier: Never thought you'd go for such a meager price.

text.Jules: A pirate should know that words are worth gil uncountable. Here's some words for you: The prodigal Bunansa son's come back to the Imperial roost. See? Words of much value, these.

text.Balthier: Bah.

text.ACTION: Balthier takes off.
Now the group arrives in the city proper, with towering buildings and small airships flying overhead. Vaan checks it out.

text.Penelo: You're gaping like a fish out of water.

text.Vaan: I'm just checking out the city. Even if it is the Empire.

text.Penelo: You've changed, Vaan. You were always marching to your own beat ... almost like you were impatient, even. In a good way.

text.Vaan: Maybe it's because I've seen more now. Never imagined I'd ever come this far away from home. Hey, Larsa's here in the city, isn't he? He's a tough one. I wonder how he's doing.

text.Penelo: You always were a soft touch, Vaan. You know what's amazing? I thought I'd go my whole life without meeting people like the Princess, or Lord Larsa. And here we are in the capital!

text.Vaan: I know! It's a little over my head sometimes.

text.ACTION: Basch comes up behind him and claps a hand on his shoulder.

text.Basch: Good, Vaan. You've come to understand the difficulties of serving royalty.

text.Vaan: Hey, I'm just along for the ride.

text.Penelo: That wasn't a complaint, was it, Basch?

text.ACTION: Basch clears his throat.

text.Basch: Right. Let's get moving.

text.Penelo: Hey, don't change the subject!

text.Basch: Right.

text.ACTION: Ashe smiles, watching them fondly in the background.

text.Imperial: There's word of trouble in Old Archades. I'd steer clear of the area. Not that anyone in their right mind would want to go there in the first place.

text.Music Appreciator: I've an elderly friend, a court musician by trade. To hear him play the lute, you would think it sang!

text.Balthier: We go our separate ways here, Vaan. I've some business to attend to. We'll meet again later.

text.ACTION: He walks away.

text.Vaan: Huh? Hey —

text.Farce-goer: I do hope that girl found us tickets to the mummer's farce. And the right number, on the right day ... She can't be trusted with such things.

text.Boutiquere: It's been five years since I finally quit my lodgings in Old Archades, yet I still lack the gil to open a boutique of my own.

text.Smitten Man: I've worked so hard, and so long. All for money. And indeed, I've accumulated some wealth. Yet, I feel there is something lacking in life ...

text.Artisan Architect: How many years have I trained ... and still they mock my designs. Tradition, tradition! Fie! What good building aught that is already built?

text.Lutenist: There are those who make crafts and sell them at market. I make not crafts, but music. By my lute's soothing voice do I earn my daily bread. There was a time when I did quite well by it, too. Sadly, people nowadays seem to enjoy cacophonous marches. Few have an ear for the lute's quiet song.

text.Perceptive Man: We live in an Empire, but 'twas not always so. How did it come to be? Military might? Wise rule? No, it must take more than these things. How can we hope to carry the Empire's glory into the future if we know not her past? Yet our akademies teach us little of her true history.

text.Builder: The population of this great city continues to soar. And buildings sprout like toadstools after the rain in this unruly garden of Archades!

text.Girl on an Errand: I was asked by my mother to buy tickets to the farce, yet I bought one too many! Oh, my mother despises waste. I shall be punished for sure!

text.ACTION: Yes, the above was formatted like that in-game.

text.Smitten Woman: I'm having trouble putting a man I met — a business associate of my father — from my mind. He was so dashing, so ... mysterious. Of course, I'm certain a gentleman of his means would be affianced at the very least. Of course he would.

text.Historian: I was born of Empire, raised by Empire, and within her walls did I grow old. Yet, this city was not always grand, nor the Empire always prosperous. Youths today, they know only of her glory, and nothing of her history. How little they think on the sacrifices of the past. It ... troubles me.

text.Moneyed Gentleman: Money is like a seed, do you not agree? Keep it locked away, it is as something dead. Yet use it poorly, and 'twill never live. There must be someone with use for my money, for I would have it live, and if I could but find the hands to tend it, I would gladly share its fruit.

text.Avid Traveler: I much enjoy traveling ... seeing flora and fauna of faraway places ... except for those flora and fauna with teeth! Perhaps some armor is in order?

text.Poor Wife: It will soon be my wedding anniversary! Whatever shall I give my dearest? That reminds me, I found the oddest thing: a fine necklace at the back of the wardrobe! If only I could remember when I bought it ... But no matter, I've sold the thing now. We live well enough, but it's hard to save ... I needed the gil to buy my dearest what he deserves!

text.Tutor: A tutor by trade am I, yet of late, unemployed. Why? My pupil's transferred to Bhujerba, leaving me to seek out a new charge. It's grown harder in recent years to pass the examinations, yet I have utmost confidence in my ability to prepare any student.

text.Proud Mother: Oh? Oh ho ho ho! My Reginald is quite the brightest child, I assure you! I blush to confess he has his mother's wit!

text.Ardent Woman: My beau and I have been working together of late. We've got quite a stack of chops to show for our troubles, too!

text.Charlotte's Magickery Banner: With a lineage longer than most grimoires, we are the only Magickery recognized by the illustrious Archadian Akademy of Magick. Welcome!

text.Judge's Wife: My husband was a Judge, a fine one at that. Filled with righteousness, and justice. Our house's pride. The pride, too, of our borough ... It was his very own sense of justice that brought his end. To die attempting to save a child's life, and the child of a foeman, no less. How like him!

text.Look-alike (lower level): Seen a swindler about? Not that you'd know if you did: he's a master of disguise. Why, he dressed like me and walked off with my earnings! If I don't find him quick, I'm ruined! Finished! End of story! Ah, I can't go back to scratchin' for gil in the old town. How'd he imitate me so well?

text.Poor Husband: My anniversary's comin' up, see. Haven't got a lot of gil, but I still bought the missus somethin' special. Can you guess what it is? A necklace!

text.Talented Woman: You know, I'm oft told I have a knack for magicks. Of course, I've little coin to buy such things ... I should be handling magicks, not turnips. (sigh)

text.Family-minded Girl: Did you see the mummer? Did you? I truly despise his kind. Who would want to watch such rubbish? Can he possibly hope to glean enough gil by his prancing to survive or raise a family? After all those years of training, to end up impoverished!

text.Ardent Man: Here in the capital, if you take pride in your work, and do right by your customers, anyone can make a decent living. Now, your regular chops are made of pine, but the nobles use chops of sandal — sweet-smelling things, those. My girlfriend and I will get 'em someday!

text.Look-alike (lower level): Seen a swindler about? Not that you'd know if you did: he's a master of disguise. Why, he dressed like me and walked off with my earnings!

text.Mummer: A travelin' mummer taught me this one. Used to live 'ere in the city, so 'e said.

text.Daughter-in-Law: My dear husband's mother has asked for a trinket from Giza Plains. She's ever so particular, though, so I'm having a Giza craftsman come here.

text.Bulward's Technicks: Best selection of technicks in the Empire! Why, 'tis the same as saying "best in Ivalice"! Need technicks? You've come to the right shop!

text.Akademician: I am chancellor at the Akademy of Magick. Sadly, there is little need for our art in this age of ready convenience. Applicant numbers are down. Indeed, the Akademy itself may be to blame for placing profit above the pursuit of quality in instruction. If not quality, what have we, I ask?

text.Would-be Judge: O, to be a Judge! To bring order and peace to the world ... and that just in a morning's work! O, to be — How does one become a Judge, anyway?

text.Man from Giza: I came here all the way from Giza Plains to make some trinket, but I got separated from my guide on the road and couldn't find the client! There's no way I'll make it back home on my own. Here I thought my fortunes were looking up ... Ach, is my woman going to steam about this.

text.Traveling Gentleman: Travel? My work has taken me far and wide. Why, I'm on the road for six months a year. Danger? Near misses? Daily affairs! Of course, I take care to wear the proper protectives, and my sword arm is good enough to hold off your average fell beast.

text.Reminiscing Lady: Did you see the mummer at his act? Oh, it was truly splendid! It made me feel like a maiden in the spring of her youth once more! How I would love to share this with my daughter.

text.Foppish Man: Sweetling, had you heard? My good friend Otto's gone missing.

text.Sultry Woman: Oh, I heard, I heard. Fell in love with a — pardon me — tart down in Old Archades, they say? He always was a character.

text.ACTION: For dialogue with July, see the "July the Streetear" section on the side quests page.

text.Longing Man: Bah! You must think me foolish. I doubt it not. I am a fool. I should never have left her behind in Old Archades to come here ... She always dreamed of a place where we could be happy together ... and it made her sad. She would spend hours gazing into the distance ... Me? I gazed up at the City, so sure it held the answer ... that I was destined for greatness ... But that was the most foolish dream of all.

text.Chopmaster: Hello, I'm the Chopmaster. Help you with aught?

CHOICE.Chopmaster: Looks like you've nary a chop to your name. Are you sure you belong here in the City?

CHOICE.Vaan: What are pine and sandalwood chops?

CHOICE.Chopmaster: Here in Archades, people spend their whole lives trying to get their hands on pine chops and, if they're lucky, a chop of fine sandalwood. Gil, they're only good for the buying and selling of goods. You can have all the gil in the world and it won't buy you respect. Only chops of pine, or a chop of sandal will win you that. You see, the chops represent your contribution to the greater good of the Empire. Common citizens might come by pinewood chops enough during their daily lives, but it takes a soldier, or some great deed to earn sandalwood.

text.Magickery Proprietor: Welcome, welcome. I'm sure you'll find our selection of magicks befitting of the Empire's finest magickal emporium.

text.Hesitant Man: That book I found last time is gone! It's just plain not here! Could it have been sold ... ? I knew I should've bought it when I had the chance.

text.Eager Learner: I stumbled upon a rather good book of technicks the other day. Good as it was, it still missed out some of the best, so the search continues!

text.ACTION: Tchita Uplands 3300
Archades 230
Cancel

text.Hopeful Writer: I'm researching the many varieties of technicks. When I know everything there is to know, I'll write a book — a guaranteed bestseller!

text.Insecure Seeq: Bah! Tryin' to learn some more technicks — impresses the ladies — but there are too many big words in these books ... hardly any pictures!

text.Technicks Seller: Good day to you, sir. We've technicks from far and wide, both new and old. Take a look around. I guarantee you shan't be disappointed. Shop menu

text.Lucky Man: Hello there! You ... haven't dropped a letter, have you? You see ... I found on in the street and I couldn't help but, um, read it. It said: "This is an epistle to Love. Freely have I released it. Should it return to me, then shall my love be made true." ...And that was all. Odd, wouldn't you agree?
