text.Man of the Quay: Eh? Giruvegan? Never heard of the place. South of Golmore Jungle? What's Golmore? Farthest I ever been is the end of the docks.

text.Quay Rat: Going to get a mark? Good for you! Pa always says having those things running wild is bad for business!

text.Resting Pirate: Me mates and I just got back from a voyage. Aye, it's a long haul from here to Rabanastre, when your hull's loaded down with goods.

text.Whitecap Sister: We're watching the store while our mother's away!
Sorry, good sir, but we can't really cook ...

text.Bangaa in His Cups: That Reddas used to drop in and throw a cup back with the boys. Haven't seen him around of late, though! He too good to drink with us?

text.Viera Wayfarer: You have the look of one accustomed to travel. Tell me ... when humes are attacked by monsters, do you stand and fight, or do you flee?

text.Relaxed Man: That tall one sitting at the window ... with the ears ... that a viera? I saw one once, down south. Never expected to see one here.

text.World-weary Woman: People talk about drunken pirates like they were a dying breed, but I've seen enough in my day to last a lifetime, I have! Heh.

text.Horizon-watcher: What would a traveler be wanting here? This is where the honest, hard-working people of the port live, lad.

text.Muscled Pirate: We may look a bit rough in Balfonheim, but we're hard-working folk, and proud of it! Reddas, he's the roughest, hardest pirate of all!

text.Dubious Sky Pirate: Reddas is a sky pirate, and no one will tell you different. But who is he, really? What exactly does he do in that manse of his? Well?

text.Watchwoman: Men in this town love an argument, and when it comes to Reddas, you're either for him or against him. I say "for"... what about you, sailor?

text.Quayhag: I know some youths what meet in a house back here, during the night, to talk about how to get Reddas out. What have they got against him?

text.Blunt Woman: If not for Reddas, the Empire would've ground this town beneath its boot. Still, many pirates, sea and sky both, don't appreciate what he's done.

text.Garrulous Pirate: I know that Reddas is in league with the Empire! You expect me to believe they leave this port alone for a little gil?

text.Fishmonger: Fishermen in other ports might complain of steep taxes, but here, port levy and trade keep the town rich, so there's no need to bleed us.

text.Worried Pirate: Reddas doesn't come to town so much these days ... Shame, 'cause those folks what don't like him are getting bolder. Pretty soon the fights'll start back up, and things'll be just like what they used to be ... (sigh)

text.Old Fisherman: Giruvegan? Never heard of the place. Yet, the path to anywhere starts with a single step. Why, even this canal here leads to Giruvegan! Heh.

text.Reddas Freeman: I've a mind to ask them against Reddas what they hope for our town? They like everyone fighting each other? That's just what the Empire wants!

text.Reddas Freewoman: As far as I'm concerned, you either welcome what Reddas has done for us, or you're welcome to leave town. Some people can't leave soon enough.

text.Teller of Tales: Sure Balfonheim's free. But only because the Empire says it is! Why, we're no better than a colony!

text.Seahand: Somewhere out there blows a free wind, and I'm going to find it 'n' catch it! I'm sick o' workin' here, linin' the Empire's pockets!

text.Strident Bangaa: I hear Reddas has been out of town lately! Time for us to take back the streets! I haven't had meself a good brawl in ages!

text.Feeble Bangaa: B-But what if the Imperials see us? Won't they come bargin' in and take over?

text.Kind Pirate: What is it that pirates do, you ask? Well, not all pirates are created equal! Most here are in the shipping business, though. Exciting, eh?

text.Born Sky Pirate: Everyone you meet's got an opinion of Reddas. Personally, long as he lets me fly the skies freely, he's welcome to do as he pleases.

text.The Leapin' Bangaa: Welcome! See anything you need? Better yet, see anything you don't need? I didn't think so!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Fisherman: Something wrong with a man fishing on holiday? I didn't think so.

text.Waterfront Gambits: This here's a gambitry. Have a look around. See anything you like?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Quayside Magickery: Magicks! Magicks! Get your flamin' hot magicks! Buy, and be happy!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Lazy Man: You there, you're not from this town. Finish your business and leave. There's talk of Imperial spies about, you know. Either you're here to buy something, or you're on your way out, understand?

text.Bangaa Runner: What? I'm headin' out on a trip, that's what! Got to buy some foodstuffs, 'fore I go ... and ye've distracted me. If I forget anything it's your fault!

text.Well-informed Man: If you're looking for the aerodrome, it's just up ahead. Reddas's manse, that's past the bazaar. North? That's the way to Cerobi Steppe.

text.Hawker: Here looking for liftin' work? Sorry, son, but I only needed me one man, and that's this fellow right here. Maybe next time, eh!

text.Bazaar-goer: Pickings are awfully slim these days. Perhaps something to do with these rumors of war! It's the port towns that suffer first, I tell you.

text.Beldame: The men in this town, they may look rough, but each one of them's got a heart of gold. Ah, I sure did some "mining" in my day, ooh hoo!

text.Jolly Pirate: Aye, 'tis the happiest day of my life! For I invited this bonnie lass on a seafaring voyage, and she agreed, she did! Ah ha!

text.Fishing Enthusiast: I'm a shipwright by trade, but of late, the ships of Archades and Bhujerba are more popular, and business is ... What? Those are airships? Oh.
What? Have you some business with me?

CHOICE.Fishing Enthusiast: Ah, you noticed! This here rod was made specially for catching Balfon-catfish. It's a rare work of art, this is. Harder to get hold of one of these than it is a masterwork blade, to hear some tell it. Perhaps you are wanting a rod such as this? Sorry to disappoint you, but there's little chance of that.
Oh? Shall I tell you a story then?

text.Fishing Enthusiast: Nothing like fishing to work up an appetite...

text.Man of Hope: I sent a ship out to fetch some cargo, but it's not come back for some time. I fear 'tis the work of some sea-fiend! Perhaps it's time to stop pinching my gil and hire some Balfonheim pirates for protection?

text.Airship Pilot: On me latest voyage I ran into a dragon the likes of which I've ne'er seen! Grr ... Need to outfit me ship and crew a bit better.

text.Disciplined Pirate: This fellow here says he wants to be a pirate! I told him, what he needs is a strong back. Courage and wits are good, but they don't help lift cargo.

text.Man of Reason: Ah, so you cross Golmore Jungle, brave the Feywood, and so go to Giruvegan? A very long journey, that. Yet, should you use airships and gate crystals wisely, I think it not so difficult. A chocobo might be in order ... but you already knew this.

text.Troubadour: Forget not ... the necklace, needing form ... What left to tell ... foal's fancy fast faded ... An unhealing scar in wetland abyss ... Pass hence, and return, in darkness ... Hrm ... ? Ah, it is nothing. Forgive my ramblings.

text.Sleepy Man: Ach, 'twas a long voyage. I'm weary down to me bones ... You mind? Eh? Giruvegan ... ? What all's that? (yawn)

text.Nono: I've almost finished repairing the Strahl, kupo! I'm working morning, noon, and night ... shouldn't be much longer!

text.Sky Pirate: There's a lot to be said for leisurely journeys. With airships, gate crystals, and chocobos, you're practically there the moment you leave.

text.Glassy-eyed Man: Eh, me? No, I'm not going anywhere. I just enjoy watching the airships come and go. I wanted to be a sky pirate once ... but that was long ago. Eh? Now? Now I'm a fisherman ...

text.Troubled Pirate: I'm busy here handling some deals on Reddas's behalf. You need something, speak with the docent.

text.Welcoming Party: With all the pirates in this town, both sea and sky, the aerodrome saw little use ... At least not until Reddas invited all those traders to town. Now it's livelier than ever!

text.Angry Woman: Can you believe it? My brother says he's off to Archades to find work! Archades! Well, that might be one way to line your pockets, but if a sky pirate's to make his fortune, he should make it at sky pirating!

text.Weeping Woman: My love, my love ... He's flown away on silver wings, and I've not heard a word from him since ... Why, it seems like only yesterday he left me ... (sob)

text.Wingless Sky Pirate: There's an airshipwright's hangar off to the side of this aerodrome. We're here waiting for our repairs to get finished.

text.Hardy Pirate: Arrrrrrrr ... ... you talkin' to me? What? Goin' to Giruvegan? Where's that? Me, I prefer workin' to ramblin'. And after a day of workin', a night of drinkin'!

text.Laboring Bangaa: What's with you? You lookin' for work!? Sorry, boy, but the loads we gotta carry are too heavy for a hume! Now, outta the way!

text.Port Wench: Ah, now that's a fresh face! Here to work the docks? Then you'd do well to speak to Reddas. He's a busy man, though. If you get a chance, take it.

text.Lofty Sky Pirate: Me and me mates are off to make us a pretty gil. What? Now, don't get me wrong ... All we do is ship cargo, you see. That pirate moniker is more of a tradition than a description.

text.Cartographers' Guild: Would you like to buy a map, kupo?

text.ACTION: Cerobi Steppe 4100
Balfonheim Port 80
Cancel

text.Miffed Moogle: I thought to journey by chocobo, kupo! But the price is far too high ... Gurdy's a moogle! We're supposed to stick together, kupo!

text.ACTION: For more dialogue with the Miffed Moogle, Chocobo Wrangler, and Moomer, see Side Quests.

text.Dyce: Hello there! Well, did you find your kingly treasure? It's good to see you again!

text.Dilah: I'd have thought you lucky to 'scape that flying fiend's attentions with your life, but to best it!? That's more than luck!

text.Dyce: Ah hah! True, true! Guess there's more to you than meets the eye, boy! Ah, a friendly word of advice: if you're going to the Cerobi Steppe, heed the weather! On days when it rains, the elementals come out to play, and take my word for it, there's little fun to be had in their games. Of course, you'll want to go prepared. Care to buy anything?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Neophyte Hunter: I'm scouting for word of marks for my hunting party ... but I have to wonder, exactly what sort of mark should we be going for? Anything too strong and we'll be picking the dirt out of our teeth ...

text.Game Hunter (man in hat and blue shorts): Look, just because you think you know something about a mark doesn't mean you can rest easy. You have to keep your ears open and your eyes wide. Get as much information as you can, put it all together, then make your move.

text.Game Hunter (man in blue, red, and green: If it's word on game you seek, this camp can't be beat. The folks here, they've hunted the world over, you see.

text.Concerned Hunter: Used to the camp yet? If you still can't find your way around, go and talk to the moogle on the hill. When it comes to cartography, he's your man ... er, moogle.

text.Game Hunter (green bangaa talking to two: I've got all the information I came here to get ... figure it's about time I headed out and started hunting. Good luck to you, too, Lord Slayer of Sochen! Hah!

text.Nice Hunter: You want to live a long life as a hunter, you've got to know your limits. Sure, fleeing ain't exactly glamorous ... but neither is dying.

text.Game Hunter (man in green, blue, and red: This fellow here, he fell down from Bhujerba! Reckon it's true what they say, that even if you fall from a skycity, you won't die ... Though, just between you and me, I'm not eager to test that theory out for meself, if you take my meanin'.

text.Fallen Bhujerban: I fell from a skycity, you see, and have forgotten everything from before the fall ... I do not even know my own name, bhadra! Slowly, slowly, I am saving up my coin. Even should my memory not return, I will go back to Bhujerba some day. This, I swear.

text.Game Hunter (tan bangaa talking to seeq: Look, this camp's pretty big. You get lost, you do what I did and talk to that moogle up the hill. He'll sell you a map, see. By the by, that way leads to the road to the Salikawood. See? Nothing like a good map.

text.Aspiring Writer: I overheard something the other day ... quite an interesting something. It seems that there are hunters after something other than marks. Apparently, it's some moneyed gentry in Archades funding them, too. Ah, details, details, I can't write anything without more details!

text.Hawker: I'm setting up the next trade deal, here. The folks 'round here want all kinds of bizarre things, I tell you.

text.Phon Camper (tan bangaa standing on beac: Talk to that fellow who fell from Bhujerba? Funny thing, he gets all queer when you show 'im a key ... maybe he was a keysmith or something?

text.Game Hunter (woman in white talking to w: So this is the Hunter Camp! At last ... How long I've dreamt of seeing this place!

text.Game Hunter (man talking to red bangaa): To make her happy, that's why I've come here ... Happy! While I waste away my days as what? A hunter!? Here, in this place? (sigh)

text.Little Hunter: I've got my friends all out looking for word of marks, kupo ... but there's so many out there, I don't know where to start! I may be small, but don't underestimate me, kupo! We moogles have our own way of fighting, you know. Call it ... moogle style! Kupo!

text.ACTION: The following dialogue and further Hunt Club dialogue will also be listed under Side Quests -- Hunt Club.

text.Atak: Ah, yer back. Talk to the Huntmaster.

text.Stok: If yer here to hunt, then get yerself over to the Huntmaster!

text.Blok: Done what you needed to do in the capital, boy? The Huntmaster was saying he had some words for you.

text.Huntmaster: Ah, it's you. I think I told you before, but we're looking for sharp-taloned birds of prey, not spring chickens. The best of the best! Now, I hear you brought down the mandragoras in Sochen, and I've been considering you for ... future opportunities with us. You can hear all the tall tales you like about a fellow, but the true test of a hunter comes here, in the bush. That's right, a test. If you can accomplish the task I shall lay before you, I'll let you into our little Hunt Club. Venture out into the bush, hunt down the game that I assign you, come back, and I'll tell you more. So, are you a bird of prey? Or a chicken?

CHOICE.Huntmaster: Right! Now the game I want you to hunt is called a thalassinon. Normally, I'd have you out in the bush, searching for yourself ... But since this is your first time out, and we happen to know where one is, I'll make it easy for you. He's close, on the Vaddu Strand. Now, your game is what we call rare. You can't expect to just walk out and find 'em all over. No, you've got to know how to flush 'em out, and that isn't always easy. Listen now: the thalassinon can only be spotted from a good elevation. Even if you don't see him at first, you pick your spot, and keep looking. Dispatch him, and he'll drop a Shelled Trophy. You bring that to me. Now, I've gone a bit out of my way to explain things for you, but the hard part's up to you: the hunt! Find your game, hunt him well, and bring back that Shelled Trophy. Me? I'll be here, awaiting the good word. Good hunting!
Suit yourself. Some people can live their lives never knowing the thrill of the hunt, and they're content with that ... poor sods.

text.Huntmaster: Dispatch the thalassinon you'll find out on the Vaddu Strand of the Phon Coast, and he'll drop a Shelled Trophy, which you'll bring to me. Remember, you'll need to choose a vantage point with good elevation if you want to find him. Pick your spot and stay there till he shows himself.

text.Atak: So, yer on the hunt, boy? Do good. The Huntmaster don't carry no baggage.

text.Blok: Ah, being tested, are you? I did that some time ago, myself ... Ach, those were the days!

text.Stok: Feh! A boy like you takin' the test? Huntmaster's gone soft, he has. Pah!

text.ACTION: You obtain a Shelled Trophy!

text.Huntmaster: Ah, I was waiting! Good, good. I believe you've passed the test. Welcome to the Hunt Club! Now, for your next task ... I know! Why don't you have a word with the three bangaa brothers over there. Good hunting!
If you're ready for more, go and talk to the three bangaa brothers over there. They're a bit shifty in a pinch, but they won't lead you astray.

text.Atak: So, you passed yer test. If the Huntmaster says yer good enough, then I suppose I might as well put you to work for me. Heh heh. Now listen, this is what I want you to do. There're rare game out there what have mutated. They're a sight meaner than the usual fare. Your usual marks, they get posted after damage has been done, but we want you to find these rare game before lives are lost, see? These rare game, they aren't going to make it easy for you. You have to find 'em and bring 'em down before you know they're rare for sure ... if they drop a trophy when they fall, congratulations, you've just felled yourself rare game. Now, you bring them trophies back here when you get 'em. We won't pay you direct, like with them usual marks, but you'll get yours. See, if you bring in enough trophies, we'll put things out at the Outfitters for you to buy. Give 'em to me, and I'll stock up weapons. ...You could give 'em to my brothers, too, but I don't see why you'd want to do that, really. So, how 'bout it? You want to join the hunt? Say yes, and I'll send you on your way ... and you can turn them trophies in to whom you please. 'Course, that's me, right? Well? You ready?

CHOICE.Atak: Right, then have at it, boy, and bring yer trophies back to me! You get lost, or aren't sure what to do, you talk to the Huntmaster. He's been at this since I was still crawling. He'll learn you right.

text.Blok: So, you passed your test, boy. Suppose it falls to me to tell you what to do next! Now listen, this is what I want you to do. There're rare game out there that've mutated. They're a meaner bunch than the usual fare out there. Your usual marks, they get posted after damage has been done, but we want you to find these rare game before lives are lost, see? These rare game, they aren't going to make it easy for you. You have to find 'em and bring 'em down before you'll know they're rare for sure ... if they drop a trophy when they fall, congratulations, you've just found yourself rare game. Now, you bring them trophies back here when you get 'em. We won't pay you directly, as with usual marks, but there is a reward. See, if you bring in enough trophies, we'll put things out at the Outfitters for you to buy. Give them to me, and I'll stock up on protectives. ...You could give 'em to my brothers, too, but I don't see why you'd care to do that. So, what say you? Will you join the hunt? Say yes, and I'll send you on your way ... and you can turn the trophies in to whom you please. Of course, it pleases you to give them to me, right? Well? Are you ready?

CHOICE.Blok: Right, then have at it, boy, and bring yer trophies back to me! You get lost, or aren't sure what to do, you talk to the Huntmaster. He's been at this since I was still crawling. He'll learn you right.
That so? Suppose there's naught to be done about it then.

text.Stok: So ye passed yer test. What of it? Bah. Suppose I'll have to tell ye a bit 'bout what it is we do here at the Hunt Club. Now listen up, this is what I want of ye. There're rare game out there what've mutated. They're a meaner 'n' nastier than even me. Yer usual marks, people want 'em dead after damage has been done, but we want ye to find these rare game 'fore lives are lost, see? These rare game, they aren't going to make it easy for you. Ye have to find 'em and bring 'em down before you know they're rare for sure ... if they drop a trophy when they fall, congratulations, ye've just found yerself rare game. Now, you bring them trophies back here when you get 'em. We won't pay you straight, like with them usual hunts, but you'll get yours. See, if ye bring in enough trophies, we'll put things out at the Outfitters for ye to buy. Give 'em to me, and I'll stock up on sundries. ...Ye could give 'em to my brothers, too, but that's be a sure sign o' poor taste. So, how 'bout it? Ye want to join the hunt? Say yes, and I'll send you on your way ... and you can turn them trophies in to whom ye please. 'Course, ye'd better please me. Well? Ye ready?

CHOICE.Stok: So yer goin' to do it, after all? Pah. Waste o' time, I'd say, but in the unlikely event you do get a trophy, you bring it here to me. Anything you don't understand, you ask the Huntmaster. Don't bother me with your whining.
Right. I didn't figure you had it in you.

text.Atak: Hrrm? You don't got a trophy, do you? Try a little harder out there, boy.

text.Blok: Eh? If you have any questions, you talk to the Huntmaster. I'm just here for the trophies, see?

text.Stok: Harrumph? I don't see no trophy. Don't waste my precious time, boy.

text.Huntmaster: How goes the hunt? Ah, yes, I've been keeping track of the trophies you've handed in to the bangaa brothers three. Let's see ...
0 to Atak,
0 to Blok,
and 0 to Stok
Anything else you'd like to know about?

CHOICE.Huntmaster: Rare game are a tricky lot indeed! They're not just lying around waiting to be found, you see ... More oft than not, you won't even know where to start looking! That's when your fellow hunters come in handy. Most of the lot here're just looking for regular marks, but some of them might have heard reports of rare game on their travels. Ask around.

CHOICE.Vaan: Tell me about the Hunt Club.

CHOICE.Huntmaster: The Hunt Club isn't just for sport, you know. When rare game is spotted on a rampage, we're the only thing between it and its next victim. While your average mark is posted after the damage has been done, we like to hunt down game before lives are lost. Thankless work, but it matters. Luckily for us, we've found patrons in Archades with an eye for what we do, and the interest to support it. In fact, they wager on our hunts. The wager is simple: they pick a favorite hunter, and should he fell the most game, they win. You're a guest here, so they'll not wager on you. For you, we have a different contest in store. Now, when you hunt rare game, be sure to bring a trophy back to us. The question is, which of the bangaa brothers three will you give it? That's our little wager. Give the bangaa of your choice some trophies, and you'll be duly rewarded. Well put some things in the Outfitters for you. You follow? The more rare game you fell, and the more trophies you bring back, the more goodies you'll find at the Outfitters. Ah, I suppose I should tell you, we've worked out a system to avoid getting too much of one thing in the Outfitters. See, we split things up ... Atak is in charge of stocking weapons, Blok is in charge of armor and the like, and Stok handles everything else. Think well before turning in your trophies: what's available at the Outfitters depends on how many you bring in, and who you give them to.

text.Outfitters: Hrrm? What are you looking at? Ah, so the Huntmaster's given you the nod, has he? Well, anyone that's right by him is right by me. Listen good, and I'll explain how the Outfitters works. When you bring trophies back for the bangaa brothers here, it pleases their patrons. The patrons send cash, doubtless a portion of their winnings from wagering, and the Huntmaster uses that to bring in goods to sell here. But, not everyone may buy. Only those to whom the Huntmaster has given permission. See, this here's an exclusive shop. Hunt Club only. That said, it sounds like you're here with his blessing, so, how may I help you? Care to see my wares?

CHOICE.Outfitters: Ach, I'm sorry, friend. We've nothing to sell.

text.Outfitters: Greetings. How may I help you today?

CHOICE.Outfitters: Ach, I'm sorry, friend. We've nothing to sell.

text.Enthusiastic Streetear: They say a bat-like fiend has been spotted in a darkened ruin somewhere ... they say he's rare game.

text.Laid-back Seeq: I ain't fond of ghost stories, but I heard a real good one the other day. Barheim Passage is haunted, they say, though the ghost only shows up once in a while.

text.Well-informed Bangaa: Come to me if you want to hear about big game. And about little game, too. Like that thing that might have been seen in a swamp rife with dangers ...

text.Realistic Man: Word is rare game has been spotted on the sandsea. Reports are vague, but it sounds like some kind of giant bird...

text.Nalbinite: You here to help 'em shore up the walls, too? Or maybe to find work with the watch? Been a steady stream since they upped the wages. Tch. Is this our fate as Dalmascans? Working to rebuild our own fortress for the Archadians ...

text.Itinerant Hand (black bangaa with tattoo: I'm tired of bricklaying, thought I'd join the army. 'Course, they only take humes. Everyone else gets used for works, or cannon fodder.

text.Itinerant Hand (light blue seeq sitting: Some days they say the Rozarrians are coming, others, the Resistance. They keep fortifying their walls to be ready. Day and night, day and night. 'Cept the humes! They get rest days! Tch. Those Imperials think the rest of us are to be used as tools, nothing more. Nice, eh?

text.Merchant (Jajim Bazaar): The Imperial army's gearing up for something big. Airships full to overflowing with soldiers fly in, and work on the fortress never stops. Sure, merchants are happy. War is good business. Our shop, too, does well ... yet I look upon our success with a troubled heart.

text.Popol: When will I ever get to sleep ... It's the same voice ... Always the same ...

text.Itinerant Hand (man in reddish brown pan: My home, the Republic of Landis ... you wont find it on any map. The Empire's to thank for that. I ran from Landis to Nabradia, and when Nabradia was attacked I fled here, to Nalbina ... and war followed me again. Where next!?

text.Burrogh: Ain't life funny? When I ran into you down in the Barheim Passage, I'd never seen you before, and reckoned I'd never see you again..
Now here we are! Well, you keep up yer scavengin' and I'll keep up mine, heh heh.

text.Imperial (interrogating man off to the s: My predecessor was transferred, leaving me to patrol the stalls, looking for stolen goods ... quite a task, I assure you! Hard times have driven shopkeepers to desperate measure out here in the provinces.

text.Imperial?: Hey, don't be fooled by appearances ... I ain't no Imperial. This armor belongs to this guy next to me. He puts it on me so he can loaf off ... At least he used to. Now that war's a-comin' he doesn't get to relax quite so much. It's hard being an Imperial, I guess ...

text.Box Merchant: My boxes're selling like popular boxes to them Imperials! Wait, you think they're usin' em to fight with? Are they usin' 'em for ... evil?

text.Stonemason? (seeq): I'm not really a stonemason, see. I'm just here pretending to work, waiting for my chance to get a friend out of the dungeons. Not that I'd be much help if a chance did come along ... this work's exhausting!

text.Stonemason? (hume): I came here with my seeq buddy to spring a friend out of the dungeons ... but my stupid buddy got us trapped here workin' as stonemasons. Anyhow, now that it seems like Rozarria's going to invade, I figure it's time to be off ... 'cept we can't just leave our friend in the dungeon! Tch.

text.Homebound Man: I finally got used to the work, and they even raised our wages, but I think I'll go home to my family, to Rabanastre. If war's coming like they say it will, I should be with my wife and child ... or I'll die out here alone. A failure to the end. (sigh)

text.Itinerant Hand (man in group of two men,: They raises the amount they give to us laborers, but the work's gotten that much more difficult. War's got them all in a rush to build. Even if we get twice the coin, what good's it do us if we have to do three times the work!?

text.Imperial (speaking to two men and bangaa: We pay good wages, and still they complain! Can't anyone work in silence anymore?

text.Shy Bangaa: I've been watching these goods for hours. The one what owns 'em hasn't come back from wherever he went. How long do I got to wait here?

text.Villager (man in brown and green leaning: A traveling merchant made the crossing not long ago. Told of a Great War brewing ... The world's stirring out there, beyond the sands.

text.Villager (man in green pants and hat by: A steady flow of people from Rabanastre, lately. And not your common travelers. Men of strong build, jaws set with determination.

text.Villager (woman in white by fire): I overheard some travelers talking about Rozarria attacking. Is there truth in this? Will they come through here?

text.Sassan: I wanna see Torrie, but I ain't goin' nowhere near that bleedin' Nathyl. I ain't thick!

text.ACTION: For more dialogue with Sassan, Tchigri, and Torrie, see Side Quests.

text.Wise Elder: Giruvegan? Can't say as I've heard of that before.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, pink, and gr: Lately, I find myself thinking about Nabudis. About how close Rabanastre came to ending up like it did. About how we still could ... Nabudis stood far to the north of Dalmasca. The Imperials who destroyed it — what must it feel like to do such a thing?

text.Rabanastran (woman in white speaking wit: I've been thinking often about life as it once was in Rabanastre. A friendly place, where families might live out their days in peace. It's been two years now since that life was taken from us. And here I thought I'd finally gotten used to it ...

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa): I was just passin' through the west gate, and I saw somethin' I ain't never seen before: a feathered tumbleweed rollin' through as the gates closed. Don't see cockatrices visitin' the city much, that's for sure! But, I suppose if it doesn't cause any trouble, people won't pay it much mind.

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa SG): You traveled afoot to Bur-Omisace? Passing through Golmore must've set a fright about you. What's that? You've walked to Archades, too? Sounds as though you're on a walking tour of Ivalice! Where you heading next?

text.Rabanastran (man in blue talking with se: I saw a group of people down in Lowtown I haven't seen before. I think they may have come from Bur-Omisace. They looked exhausted. Everyone's saying it was the Empire who attacked Bur-Omisace, but I just don't see what they'd hope to gain by it.

text.Adventurer: A cockatrice come runnin' through here just fine as you please. I chased after it, but it was too fast for me. Lost it when it went into the city. Sell it? What are you goin' on about? I was gonna eat it!

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with group): I hear they've finally reopened all of the airship routes again. Ah, how I'd love to travel by airship, even just once ...

text.Rabanastran (woman embracing man by the: ...after what happened in Bur-Omisace ... how could I let you leave now? ...what if Nalbina is next? ...I'll never let you go ...

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: A chance encounter with an Imperial patrol could bring unwelcome trouble. I am checking to be sure such is not likely. Better safe than sorry.

text.Merchant (Aerodrome): When I'd heard what had happened, I left for Bur-Omisace as soon as I could. What I saw there left me speechless ... What could the Empire possibly hope to gain by making an enemy of the Light?

text.Rabanastran (man in blue, green, and red: With all that's happening in the Empire, even the Archadians are worried. Let's just hope we don't see a repeat of what happened at Nabudis ...

text.Traveler (woman with the Archadian group: Lord Vayne May be the acting emperor right now, but it's obvious he will be our actual emperor before long.

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: Who can say what will become of the Empire? All I can do is hope and pray that we don't see another war ... There are enough poor orphans.

text.Bright-eyed Boy: I hear there's monsters that run away if you don't kill 'em quick enough. You think they get tired of fightin', or are they just in a hurry?

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: I once went on a journey to the south — just to see what could be seen. I walked, and walked, and finally came to a foreboding fog-shrouded wood. But inside this wood, I came to a place where no matter how much I walked, I'd always end up right back where I started ... There wasn't much to do then but turn and go home. The Mist there ... I've never seen a Mist so dense! Why, it nearly knocked me out cold.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Southga: I was pokin' around outside Southgate, just inside Giza Plains ... I can't believe how different it is between the Rains and the Dry.

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants down by: The great sandstorm in the Westersand has finally died down. Good news for wayfarers, though the sunsets won't be half as pretty any more.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue down by Westgat: Hey, Vaan! Sure haven't seen you around much lately. If you're off havin' fun, how 'bout lettin' me in on it? Unless it's that dangerous and scary type o' fun. You can count me out of that!

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa in red vest): Saw me a chubby little cockatrice rollin' off to the north o' here. Lookin' a mite bedraggled at that! 'Twere domesticated, if I had to guess. Needs to toughen up some or he'll never make it out in the wild.

text.Rabanastran (boy in blue and green on so: I can't stop thinkin' about Vayne ... There must've been some way to get at his coin, but search me if I know what it was. At first, I thought it was 'cause of all the guards, but now I think it's the way he is. It's like ... there's somethin' lurkin' under the surface.

text.Imperial (Southern Plaza): Seems like Rozarria's on the move. Only no one's quite sure what they're up to. I just hope the higher ups don't do nothin' foolish. One wrong move and all Dalmasca could go up in flames, and I'd just as soon not see that happen.

text.Rabanastran (boy squatting down and hugg: I saw a bunch of people I ain't seen before down in Old Dalan's place. They looked all tired and worn out. I'm not sure, but I think they might've come from Bur-Omisace. Whaddaya think happened?

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa speaking with wo: First Vayne returns to Archades, then the Emperor dies, and now these rumors about an attack on Bur-Omisace ... could it all tie together somehow?

text.Rabanastran (boy with his father in the: This big oil' roly-poly up and jumped right off that ledge. Then it just kept on rollin' on to the North End. Maybe I'll go chase after it!
People are sayin' there's a war about to start. I don't get why grown-ups are always havin' wars and stuff. Why can't they just be nice?

text.Rabanastran (man in brown pants with his: I've noticed refugees from Bur-Omisace around the city. They're welcome as far as I'm concerned, of course, but Rabanastre is part of the Empire ... If the rumors about the Empire being behind the attack on Bur-Omisace are true, you wouldn't think Rabanastre would take in its refugees.

text.Rabanastran (black bangaa chatting with: My friend here says that o'er 430 revelers came through the Southern Plaza during the big fete! But even if you count the bards ... 'Course, he could be countin' the spoony bards, too. That would be another matter altogether.

text.Bucco: Hey, Vaan. You and Penelo off traveling on your honeymoon? Heh, I'm just teasin' ya. It's just I don't see you two much anymore is all. I know you've got stuff to do that's over my head, and that's okay. Just make sure you come back safe, all right? My mom and dad said they'd come back, but they never did ... I don't want that to happen again, okay?

text.Town Gossip: A friend of mine — a seeq up in the North End — used his savings to travel to Archades. I wonder if he's made it safely back? It's hard to imagine that the Imperial capital would be a safe place following the Emperor's assassination. I do hope he's all right ...

text.Rabanastran (man in brown and green shor: I heard the Empire launched an attack on Bur-Omisace ... how horrible. It just doesn't make sense. What could they hope to gain by such an act?

text.Wistful Bangaa: There's a rumor filterin' through the streets that Princess Ashe is still alive. Bah ... this'll turn out the same as that Basch hooey, you watch.

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa EE): The Rozarrian Empire stirs, Marquis Ondore plots ... There are more rumors than even I can keep straight. I wish I knew what it all meant. I'm not so much scared as ... worried. Whatever happens, it's always the small folk who get caught up in the middle.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, blue, and gr: I just heard what happened on Bur-Omisace ... But why? They're only refugees ... what could they have done to deserve this? What kind of world is it where such things can happen? The mighty rule, and the meek are crushed underfoot ...

text.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): Hey, mister. You wanna hear some old legends from Rabanastre's folklore? It won't cost ya much. What? I gotta eat, too, ya know. Let's see ... 1 gil oughta do it.

CHOICE.Rabanastran (boy in brown near bridge): There's a strange place that lies deep within the Mist that only someone with a great power can reach. King Raithwall went there, once. But where it is, and what great power you need to get there, nobody knows. It's all a riddle wrapped in an enigma. Hmm ... If it's so mysterious, how come people know about it? You think someone made it up? I can't charge people to hear this ... Uh, pretend I didn't say that. I'm sure it's all true, every last word! Heh.
Hmm, okay. Well, all I have to talk about are legends, so I guess that's that.

text.Lonely Boy: So if Vayne's back in Archades, who's in charge of Rabanastre? You think he still gives orders and such from there?

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: Hey, Vaan, how've you been? You're planning something big, I can see it in your eyes. I wish Reks could see you now. The little brother he laid down his life to protect ... He'd be real proud of you.

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq by bazaar entranc: D'ja know the moogles what run the Mooglin' at the gates are related, with three more siblin's to boot? A litter o' six ... if moogles have litters.

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq pacing about): That Migelo does seem a mite lonely at times — like a father whose children have flown the nest. I don't suppose I could be 5e son he never had ...

text.Johm: With you being gone so much lately, I think Kytes is really missin' you. You're like a big brother to him.

text.Rabanastran (blue seeq outside Sandsea): Innocently walkin' last the Sandsea I was, when a sudden thirst seized me. I couldn't deny m'self any longer. (hic!) I only had a couple o' drinks. (hic!) Just enough t' wash away my resolve...

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink headscarf): I was thinking of going to the Mosphoran Highwaste ... but there're just so many ways to get there! Let's see, I can go through Nalbina Fortress, or take the ferry in the Estersand across the Nebra ... Then again, I could also cross into the Estersand from the Westersand and then cut north. Which is the most scenic route, do you think?

text.Rabanastran (man in green and blue talki: You ever heard of Zertinan Caverns? It's a huge maze of tunnels connecting a number of different places near and far. I suppose you could even use the caverns as a shortcut, but the creatures within are rumored to be a frightful sort.

text.Rabanastran (orange seeq): With the power the Dynast-King once held, even the Empire would be no match for Dalmasca. Of course, then there wouldn't be anything to keep Dalmasca from becoming the next Archadia, would there.

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, green, and t: I saw Old Dalan in the shop the other day talking about something or other with Migelo. I tried to catch what they were going on about, but I couldn't make anything out.

text.Migelo: Old Dalan came by the shop for a friendly chat the other day. Why, I can't remember the last time he'd been in for a visit. He had a few things he wanted to get off his chest: Marquis Ondore's plotting and what not. You know I would never try to stop you from doing something you'd set your mind to, but do be careful, m'boy. You do what you think is right. Then, when it suits you, you come back home to Rabanastre. Rabanastre is your home.

text.Rabanastran (tan bangaa in green vest): If you'd been following the Empire's moves recently, you'd be worried for Rabanastre, too. 'Twixt them and the Resistance, who can say what's a-brewin'...

text.Sherral: We've received orders to stockpile weaponry, but the Empire's got enough trouble maintaining order as it is. People trust us little enough already. We'd only be throwing fuel on the fire. That's why I've decided not to purchase a single thing. Duty or no, I must answer to my conscience.

text.Amal: You never know what tomorrow may bring ... So you best bring a sturdy weapon!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Rabanastran (man browsing curio): Did you ever notice the guard on the second floor of the Sandsea? I think he may have been caught loafing about on the job. Now he's been moved over to Yugri's Magicks, but I doubt that will make any difference.

text.Panamis: War is in the air. Best buy what you need while there's aught left to buy!

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Lively Bangaa: You see more and more viera around these days. There was always one over in the clan hall, but now I'm seeing 'em here, there ... everywhere! Of course you know what that means, don't you? When viera leave their homes, they leave for good. No such worries for us bangaa, though!

text.Earnest Seeq: New bazaar goods mostly come in after you've done some shoppin'... mostly. But I herd there are some what don't have nothin' to do with buyin' or sellin', but just how many times you've paid visit to the shop.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue pants): I've heard a group of nu mou have been seen in the Nabreus Deadlands. But Nabudis has long since fallen into ruin! What could they be doing there?

text.Barkeep (woman leaning against wall by d: Have you been good about checking the notice board? You've probably hunted all kinds of marks by now. Your clan rank must be impressive. You can always raise your clan rank by fighting monsters, and it doesn't hurt to see what hunts are available.

text.Rabanastran (man sitting with woman): I'm sure you heard about the Emperor? Well, they say it was an assassination. I don't know who did it, but it can only mean trouble for us all.

text.Tavernmaster: Hear all sorts of things working a job like this. Some good, some bad. Lately the bad outnumber the good by about nine to one, I'm afraid. How about you, Vaan? Fly where you please, but look after yourself, eh?

text.Barkeep (man standing near foot of stair: There are rumors about a strange band of nu mou in the Nabreus Deadlands. Considering the state of the place, I find it hard to believe.

text.Barkeep (woman on balcony): When Vayne returned to Archades, I was worried the Imperials would come back to the Sandsea, but so far, so good. Maybe they've had a change of heart. Or maybe this is no time to be frequenting taverns. Who knows what the future holds ...

text.Rabanastran (man chatting with another m: Technicks are skills that let you do things no Magicks can. Stealing treasures from your foes, stanching wounds ... In dark days like these, even a technick you thought was worthless could make the difference between life and death.

text.Rabanastran (woman talking to red bangaa: The city of Nabudis was destroyed in a tremendous explosion two years past. Nothing remains of the city. I went there once, long ago. Now its grand boulevards and beautiful white-walled palace live on only in memory.

text.Rabanastran (woman speaking with moogle): I'm sure you want to make Tomaj proud by becoming a great hunter, but know your limits. A truly great hunter always comes back alive.

text.Rabanastran (woman in blue, yellow, and: The Imperials have been buying up a lot of provisions lately. I hope they've left enough for the rest of us.

text.Rabanastran (woman in green and pink NE): The Imperials seem restless. Do you think another war could be on the way?

text.Rabanastran (man in white turban and bro: There's a storm coming, Vaan. Can you feel it? The Empire's on the move ...

text.Riby: Seems like you've been keeping pretty busy lately. Penelo's been with you, right? Just make sure you two be careful. We don't want anything to happen to you, okay?

text.Rabanastran (blindfolded tan bangaa NE): Vayne is a talented man. I hope that in his absence from Rabanastre he applies those talents toward peaceful ends ...

text.Dispirited Woman: Now people are saying they've seen Princess Ashe alive. But after that Basch impersonator's antics in Bhujerba, I'm not falling for it. I wish she were alive, though ... I'm sure she'd be able to help us.

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on east sid: Word on the street is that Marquis Ondore has set something big into motion. I wonder what he has hidden up his sleeve?

text.Imperial (North End): Leave me be, would you? I'm trying to focus on my duties. I've no time for idle gossip.

text.ACTION: For dialogue related to the cockatrice, Renn, see Side Quests.

text.Traveler (North End): Our Emperor is dead, and Vayne rules as autocrat in his stead. How terrible! If I'd known this was going to happen, I would never have moved to this city! O cruel fate!

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: You've heard of the Rozarrian Empire? You don't suppose they'd take advantage of the Emperor's death to attack us, do you?

text.Rabanastran (light blue seeq on west sid: I treated myself to a trip to Archades the other day, but something big must've been happening. The entire city was in a frenzy.

text.Rabanastran (woman in red, pink, and blu: Things have finally started coming together for me since I began working in the palace. I'll keep at it until my brothers can take care of themselves.

text.Greenhorn: The Emperor is dead, Vayne has taken charge of the Empire, Rabanastre faces enemies in every side ... and here I am in the gambit shop! I've lost all touch with the outside world. Maybe this isn't the time to be studying gambits.

text.Adept Adventurer: The journey has been long, but I have finally reached the end of the Way of the Gambit. My eyes ... are open. I know now that I can never master any gambit. I will never know their true worth. Why, you ask? Because gambits have little use in a party of one ...

text.Troubled Woman: You're the spitting image of Reks when he decided to join the Dalmascan army. You have that same look — you're ready to fight for something. Telling you it's too dangerous, you shouldn't go — I know it wouldn't stop you. It didn't stop him ... Just promise me you'll give it all you have.

text.Patient Bangaa: Trouble's a-brewin', and it's put my friend here in a foul mood. People pilin' tragedy upon tragedy, all for greed's sake. If they'd learn to appreciate what they've got, that'd be the end on it. Or so he tells me ...

text.Merchant (green bangaa): Welcome! Welcome to the Muthru Bazaar! Finest goods in all Rabanastre! Hearing much dark talk of late, but it casts no shadow on the Bazaar!

text.Trader: Thinking about selling goods over in Archades, but between the death of the Emperor and stirrings in Rozarria, I'm having second thoughts. It may be best to wait and see how the winds blow before deciding. There may be more profit in selling to Rozarria, if you get my meaning.

text.Merchant (tan bangaa in blindfold): For a merchant, war spells opportunity. Goods are hard to come by, and you have only to name your price. But me, I'll choose peace over getting rich that way any day. Ha ha! Maybe I'm not cut out for this business after all!

text.Traveler (Muthru): I worry about what is to come. For Rabanastre, the Empire ... I fear even to return to my home.

text.Headhunter: Got a lead on a mark you wouldn't believe. Kept gettin' beat to the appetizers, so I'm changin' my whole approach — straight for the main course! So this mark ... Clan Centurio's been after it for years. If I can bring it down ... ha ha!

text.Busy Messenger: The boss is going after something big. 'Course, I'll be the last one to find out what it is ...

text.Rabanastran (man in white, yellow, and b: I know this town like the back of my hand. It's hard to believe I ever got lost here.

text.Reks's Friend: Look at you, Vaan! You're growing into a fine young man. Just like your brother. Do him proud, boy.

text.Koqmihn: We barely escaped with our lives. If we hadn't been away from the temple when they attacked ... The Empire will answer for this.

text.Refugee: Why? Why have they done such a thing ...

text.Rabanastran (woman at left): I'm not sure what's gotten into Dalan. He seems ... restless. Like something's about to happen ...

text.Rabanastran (boy sitting at right): Old Dalan's stories have been a little off, lately. I don't think his heart's in it anymore.

text.Old Dalan: Giruvegan, you say!? Sadly, even I have little to share with you about such a place. I know it lies deep within a forest ... and nothing more. Vaan, tell me ... what exactly are you up to?

text.Rabanastran (woman in pink, green, and b: I've been thinking back to how things used to be ... When I had work, when I had a family ... No matter how much time passes, I'll never be able to just leave these things in the past. Even though I know that's where they'll always be ...

text.Rabanastran (man in green and brown shor: I can't find work, so I was thinkin' about joining the Resistance. Thing is, I'm not sure I've got what it takes to be a warrior. No money, no work, no courage ... I don't have much goin' for myself, do I?

text.Resigned Boy: Do you know why the Empire's protecting us? I do, but I'm too scared to say the reason. Scared that saying it might make it true ...

text.Frustrated Man: You think those Imperials will ever leave Rabanastre? I sure do miss the way things used to be ...

text.Somber Woman: In a way I'm proud my daughter thinks about her friends' feelings, tries to avoid talking to me near them. But it shouldn't have to be like this ... The way the Empire's headed now, I worry things are only going to get worse, though.

text.Guileful Boy: This is all how Vayne planned it. Keeping things nice and quiet in Rabanastre so we let our guard down. Then ... BAM! Those people sayin' they wish Vayne was back ... when he finally shows up, we'll see what they say then. Hmph.

text.Guileless Girl: I saw some people what escaped from Bur-Omisace or something down in Old Dalan's place. They looked dead on their feet ... I heard they had to walk through Mist and everything to get here ... I wonder where they've been?

text.Well-spoken Girl: I saw some rather serious-looking people pass by not all that long ago. I'm not sure where they've gone off to now. I think they were the ones talking about taking the kingdom back ... I suppose that would make them members of the Resistance?

text.Resolute Boy: I remember when you could get up to Westgate through that door, but it's been broken a long time — probably stay that way. Imperials ... meh.

text.Laughing Seeq: Word on the street is Emperor Gramis is dead. Half tempted to say he got what was comin' to him, but it ain't right to float over the dead. What's more, they say he was assassinated. I just hope the Rozarrians don't get it in their heads to take advantage of the turmoil and attack.

text.Dalmascan Patriot: At night, I find myself wishing I could sleep forever. I'm just so tired ...

text.Cynical Boy: The watch has been pretty lax lately. Probably distracted by the death of the Emperor. Ya ask me, this is the chance we been waitin' for.

text.Fussbudget: She said she had a dream that Rabanastre was in another war. I, sure glad I'm not her! But ever since hearin' that, I can't stop thinkin' about the real war ... Now I'm all depressed.

text.Watchful Seeq: This poor fellow over here blamed the Emperor for his son's death, but he still weren't too happy when the Emperor died. Can't imagine how he must feel.

text.Impoverished Man: Seems Marquis Ondore is finally on the move. Had I known what he was planning, I'd have given my money to him, rather than see the Empire take it. If he really is leading a resistance, maybe there's still hope we might someday be free of these Archadians.

text.Deadbeat: I don't feel like doin' anything. Not even talkin'. I think I know why, too. I can't shake this feeling something bad is gonna happen. So what's the point of doin' anything at all?

text.Angry Woman: I just don't understand what Vayne or the Empire want from us! And not knowing makes it worse!

text.Well-spoken Boy: The tragedy on Bur-Omisace, the Emperor's death, and now rumors of a resistance on the move ... The world is rife with dangers, but Rabanastre has remained safe. I find it ... disturbing.

text.Vexed Father: I still haven't figured out just how my daughter managed to get herself to the Salikawood. Well, that's kids for ya. They live in their own little world, and sometimes they really surprise you with what they can pull off.

text.Furious Bangaa: All of Ivalice is in turmoil, and those Imperials ... who knows what they're doin' about it! And where does that leave honest Dalmascans such as ourselves, eh? That's what we're talkin' on now. Somewhat animatedly, I'll confess.

text.Nutsy: Have you ever seen an elemental, kupo? They come out during the Rains, all a-crackle. Whatever you do, don't touch one! Kupo!

text.Arjie: Well, hello! The wary traveler never passes the chance to restock his supplies.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Arjie: The skies are clear, the food and drink fresh and delicious. The people are good, hard working folk. I've never regretted coming to Giza.

text.Camina: The charms we use to ward off monsters need carynath root, but I can't find any. I can't remember where I put anything these days. I thought I had everything in order, but if I don't find it soon, I'm gonna have to go out and collect some more.

text.Tott: I asked Jinn what his secret for makin' sunstones is. No matter what I try, his always turn out better. Turns out he wanted to know how come I can make mine so fast. Kinda funny, huh?

text.Roaklo: I really wanna travel. See strange places, talk to all sorts of people ... But before I can do that, I gotta convince my sister I can take care of myself. Whaddaya think? Does she trust me?

text.Nanau: Sometimes I fly off the handle when I'm talking to my little brother. But he's probably old enough not to be treated like a kid anymore. Then again, the way he's been acting, I can't rely on him for much of anything. Oh, what am I going to do with him?

text.Jinn: You ever been to Giza during the Rains? I hear huuuge frogs and turtles come out! I wanna be a natural philosopher when I grow up. I told Brunoa I wanted to go study in Archades, but she just laughed. Wonder what's so funny?

text.Lesina: Things in Rabanastre finally start to settle down, and now I hear a new storm's brewin'? You take care of yourself, okay? Remember, where there's life, there's hope.

text.Elder Brunoa: Whatever comes to the world beyond the plains, Giza will always be Giza. The sun, the earth, the winds ... if we have these, we have our home.

text.Terra: Dania asked me to help her tend the cockatrices. Everything was goin' along fine, then all of a sudden they darted out of the pen ... Now they're gone, and it's all my fault! What am I gonna do? If I'd only had one of them magick feathers that Dania uses to talk to 'em, this wouldn't have happened.

text.Dania: Would you look at this ... All our cockatrices, gone! I'd always left the pen open, and they never tried to escape before. What do you think got into them? There's nothin' to do but head out lookin' for 'em, but I don't even know where to start. I can't blame Terra for this ... It's my fault. She wasn't ready for the responsibility.

text.ACTION: For more dialogue with Terra and Dania and the cockatrices, see Side Quests.

text.Viera Wayfarer (Giza): Much calm and peace fills these plains. It is a special place, loved and treasured. Though unlike the quiet Wood I knew, in me still it wakes Her memory ... so bittersweet.

text.ACTION: If you speak to her as Fran ...

text.Viera Wayfarer (Giza): How long has it been since I left the Wood? Already Her voice is faint ... when I can hear it at all. At first it frightened me, but I have grown accustomed to it. Can you still hear the voice of the Wood?
People fear power, until they have it. Then it consumes them. How can they let this happen? Power not shown respect returns none in kind, only ruin.

text.ACTION: If you speak to her as Fran ...

text.Viera Wayfarer (Giza): The world shudders. It fears the wounds that are to come. Do you feel it, too?

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Svagatam, traveler. Welcome to Bhujerba. Word of war travels on the winds, yet do not fear, we shall keep our city safe. Good journey to you.

text.Bhujerban (man sitting on rail speaking: If there is war between Archadia and Rozarria, will Bhujerba be attacked? It will, won't it? Haa ... Little point in asking a rank and file guard.

text.Bhujerban (moogle with yellow pom-pom by: I came here first thing in the morning to make sure I wouldn't be late, kupo! But the airship still hasn't arrived! Troubled times, these ...

text.Traveler (blonde man in blue): I'm sure that once all this unpleasant business is settled, they'll choose a new emperor in Archades. I, of course, am in full support of Lord Vayne. Our empire needs strong leadership, and he's the man for the job, if I do say so myself.

text.Street Kid (sitting on luggage): I thought at last we were to leave for Rabanastre, when our airship was forced to turn back with engine trouble! I am tired of this family holiday, and it has not yet begun! Haa ...

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: With the coup in Archadia, I hear that the young Larsa has also disappeared. Perhaps he was "removed" along with the Senate, bhadra?

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom Aer: Bhujerba values our mooglecraft, and values us the same, kupo! I hope Bhujerba stays the way it is ... We moogles will do our part, kupo!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with orange pom-pom wa: Archadia's military technology is pretty good, but we moogles won't give up without a fight! We'll build a ship to beat the Alexander!

text.Street Kid (near window): Haa, I am quite concerned, for the aerodrome is filled with Imperial army ships! Will the regular airships be allowed to fly?

text.City Parijanah: Haa! Master Basch, is it not? You will be pleased to know that morale within the Resistance grows by the day! We are ready!

text.Traveler (man in Archadian clothes leani: I thought the people of Bhujerba a wiser lot than the sort who'd support this "Resistance" I've been hearing about. If you ask me, they must be in a hurry to become the next Dalmasca, eh?

text.Bhujerban (man in brown and green shorts: Kastam! Should Rozarria launch a full invasion of the East, not even Bhujerba will be safe. Rozarria ... they will want our magicite!

text.Bhujerban (woman in white pacing up and: I see many warships passing by of late. Could it be true that war is soon upon us? Hanta!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom sit: I fear we won't be able to avoid war this time. I'm worried for my friends in Archades, kupo!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Do you know why the Marquis Ondore announced he was ill? It was only to divert the Empire's attention, while he prepared the Resistance army.

text.Bhujerban (man in blue, red, and green w: Let Rozarria invade, I say. We'll ally ourselves with Archadia and send them off with their tails between their legs, you see if we don't!

text.Bhujerban (woman in white sitting on wal: Many warships pass by these days. I fear that war is not far off. I am sure that Bhujerba will be safe, and yet ... I a, afraid.

text.Bhujerban (woman in green, pink, and bro: Kastam ... I have heard that many in the Imperial City welcomed Vayne's installation as dictator. He is a hero to them, you see.

text.Bhujerban (tan bangaa walking up and dow: Now's our chance, with Rozarria and Archadia staring each other down! We throw out the Imperials and never let 'em back!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: I would not care to see the beauty that is the Ondore residence scarred by the flames of war. It is a symbol of peace, you see.

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Travica Way): We can't afford to throw Vayne out ... not yet. I'd use his brother, the child, to get the Senate back its power ... with Ondore's help of course.

text.City Parijanah: Haa ... it is you. I must warn you, the Empire has released spies into our Bhujerba. Do not speak of the Resistance to any strangers, bhadra.

text.Bhujerban (woman in white leaning agains: The Marquis has left Bhujerba to recover from illness ... or so they are saying. I hear otherwise. I hear he prepares to war with the Empire.

text.Bhujerban (man in brown and green shorts: Along this road you may find arms, armor, and Magicks of all kinds, bhadra. Business is good. Perhaps rumors of war are true?

text.Street Kid (Travica Way): Amba, she always says the raksas Diabolos will come and take me away to the mines. This is a ghost story meant to frighten me, yes? Indeed, a friend of mine has gone missing ... But the Diabolos did not do this ... right?

text.Bhujerban (woman in white sitting on cra: I hear we are to be annexed by Archadia, or perhaps annihilated by Rozarrian attack. I believe it is wise to run. ...Balfonheim is nice this time of year.

text.City Parijanah: Haa, the young Captain Ronsenburg! You must take great caution not to reveal us until our business with the Empire is settled.

text.Bhujerban (man in blue, red, and green s: My wife, she has gone into this weapons shop, and does not come out. What could be so exciting about weapons? Does she think to join the army!?

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: I have heard that the parijanah were involved with secret doings. Once again, I am thankful to be left out, to stand here, enjoying peace.

text.City Parijanah: Haa, it is you! You know that the Resistance has assembled at last a force capable of facing the Empire? How long we have awaited this day.

text.Bhujerban (woman leaning against wall in: This magickery, I do not think it will last long. They cannot see worth when it is right under their noses! ...I was turned down for a job.

text.Bhujerban (tan bangaa pacing boulevard): If it comes to war, the Empire'll win, hands down. Aye, I've heard rumors of the Leviathan sinking, but she's just one in a fleet of many! Many!

text.Bhujerban (green-pommed moogle sitting o: Kupo! If war breaks out between Archadia and Rozarria, Bhujerba will get attacked for sure! I don't want our machines to be used for war ...

text.Shop Clerk (outside Mait's): Need magicks, just in case? Mait's Magicks is just the place. Come in, bhadra, come in!

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: I was a soldier of Nabradia, a defender. Aye, the Resistance came to me. They offered me a position. I hate the Empire, yes, but I hate war more. I did not accept.

text.City Parijanah: His Excellency Ondore's Resistance forces have begun to move. Yet, I fear against the military genius of Vayne, they stand little chance ...

text.Lost Archadian Wayfarer: With the passing of Emperor Gramis, the Empire is in chaos. Chaos! I cannot go home like this ...

text.Bhujerban (woman in white leaning agains: The Khus Skygrounds are to the west, and to the east is Miners' End. Enjoy them, while they are still to be enjoyed. War is coming, you see.

text.City Parijanah: It appears that those in Dalmasca who share our dislike for the Empire have joined Marquis Ondore's Resistance. All that is left now is victory.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: I am startled to learn that the parijanah were, in fact, part of the resistance organized by the Marquis to prepare for war against the Empire!

text.Street Kid (Travica Way): Tatah works in the mines, but he has not gone to work in a very long time. He says they are not sending so many stones to the Empire any more.

text.City Parijanah: It is only a short time before the Resistance sounds a general attack. A poisoner deceived by his own draught, the Empire shall fall to its knees.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Long have I guarded this shop, yet nothing of note has ever happened here. I think that, even should there be war, nothing would change. Hanta ...

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! This is a shop of armors! Haa! I am to join the crew of the Resistance army flagship, bhadra! At last, my just reward, yes!

text.Bhujerban (tan seeq browsing on upper le: Me? Rithil's got me standing here to improve his image. Now, Targe hires these, er, "promotional patrons" just the same, but for him, it works.

text.Shop Clerk (Rithil's): Svagatam ... (yawn) There is talk for a war ... about to begin. Still ... (yawn) I wonder why business is so slow.

text.Rithil: Svagatam ... welcome ... Protectives, bhadra? 'Tis a dangerous world ... armor is what you need. (sigh) But you'll probably buy weapons first ...

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, trav— Ah, it is you. Kah? Our leader? He is above the marches. He leads our troops at the Marquis's side, you see.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in green and blue): I've come all the way from Nalbina to work the magicite mines, but it seems there's no work to be had ... I've not done a stitch.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in brown and green): You are stepping upon Bhujerban freedom? Then I care not who you are, Archadian, Rozarrian ... I kill you! I kill you all!

text.Bhujerban (woman talking to seated man): Marquis Ondore cannot be trusted! How could he leave us when Bhujerba is on the brink of war!? He is irresponsible! Like a child he is. Kastam!

text.Bhujerban (woman browsing weapons on upp: Hanta! My husband, he is useless. Should war come, it falls to me to protect us. You, you are young. Do not become a man like him, bhadra!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: I'm eager to do battle with raksas. But fighting other men ... it is not something I care for. Yet, if there is war, I will go.

text.Lhusu Miner (man standing in line at cou: The master here pays me to stand in the queue, encouraging people to buy, you see. With the war, though, encouragement is hardly necessary.

text.City Parijanah: The strength of the Empire is impossible to know, bhadra. We can only prepare ourselves with what magicks we might buy, and hope for the best.

text.Shop Clerk (woman in pink, red, and blue: Welcome, traveler, to Mait's. Our shop was just coming into its own, and now there is war! After all our hard work ... Kastam!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: I was speaking with the staff here, and studying magicks ... and before I knew it, I became quite learned! Life is good, and it only gets better.

text.Bhujerban Guru (Mait's): I do not know how the Imperial fleet stands, yet it is clear that, against the entire fleet, we would stand little chance, bhadra. I believe that the Marquis sees this too. He will seek a peaceful resolution through words before he raises the sword.

text.Bhujerban (man in blue on upper level): The people say that there will soon be war between Archadia and Rozarria, bhadra. Should we aid one, we would only make an enemy of the other. Bhujerba should remain, as always, neutral.

text.Shop Clerk (woman in blue, pink and gree: The closing of the Lhusu Mines has made it difficult to find magicite in Bhujerba, so we thought to import Stones from the Henne Mines ... Yet now I hear that the Empire has closed these as well! Kastam ...

text.Shop Clerk (woman in pink and blue with: Please, feel free to ask should you have any questions about our Magicks, bhadra. Interest in magick is high these days! It is a good thing to see!

text.Bhujerban (man in beige, yellow, and bro: Magicks are much simpler than I had thought, bhadra. I simply asked questions of the staff here and they gave me much assistance, you see.

text.City Parijanah: Soon, we will go to join the Resistance forces. Yes, of course I am frightened. This is why I drink the sweet madhu ... to prepare.

text.Cloudborne Resident (man in turban and g: To think the parijanah were, in fact, working for the Resistance! O-Of course, I knew this from the start. I was just ... wondering if you did.

text.Cloudborne Kid: My sister, she works in the Cloudborne ... but, hear this, she is a member of the "Organization"! Is this not incredible!? It means she is organized! Amazing!

text.Cloudborne Resident (tan bangaa in green: The Judge who came to our mines? I hear that his ship was sunk, and he aboard! Hah! Justice has been served!

text.Cloudborne Resident (tan seeq with turqu: Marquis Ondore has feigned illness to draw wool over the eyes of the Empire! What a man!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The songs they sing of Bhujerba and her freedom are drowned in cups of spirits. Then, must I care for them. This is freedom, bhadra?

text.Cloudborne Resident (woman in white lean: No, I have thought on this much, and it is true what we were told: the Lady Ashe and Captain Ronsenburg died two years past. If they lived, why would they not show their faces to the world?

text.Drunken Archadian Wayfarer: Must ... return ... Archades ... nnngh. O, sweet madhu ... you have been a mistress most cruel. How can I hope to leave your embrace? (hic)

text.Cloudborne Patron (light blue seeq): Wouldn't you just know that this friendly little pub was a base for the Resistance? Hrrm? What Resistance? Where have you been!?

text.Cloudborne Resident (moogle in gold with: The Cloudborne always seemed a dangerous, mysterious place, kupo! Then I learned it was a base for the Resistance. It was dangerous, kupo!

text.Cloudborne Patron (man standing beside c: My friend here, he says "war is coming, we must drink!" I am begging to differ. How can we run if we are sprawling upon the ground so?

text.Bhujerban Guru (Cloudborne Row): I have heard that Havharo is off to war with the Marquis! I hope that he comes home whole, for Melisa's sake and ... and for mine.

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! Yes, most of my compatriots have gone to join the Resistance army. I too bring recruits to join them shortly.

text.Cloudborne Resident (tan bangaa in green: There are many who now know the true nature of Bhujerba's parijanah guides. I thought it odd from the moment I learned the Marquis paid them.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in green and brown shor: I have heard now, the order to stop the mines came from above. They send fewer Stones to the Empire, you see.

text.City Parijanah: The movements of the Archadian 1st Fleet weighed on all our minds, but now it appears they go home. The time of the Resistance's triumph is nigh!

text.Cloudborne Resident (woman talking with: Have you heard? Marquis Ondore's illness was but a ruse! He wouldn't run off and abandon Bhujerba ... would he?

text.Cloudborne Resident (man sitting on crat: Should war break out between Archadia and Rozarria, I say we should sell weapons to both sides. They may beat each other to the ground.

text.Cloudborne Resident (light blue seeq wal: To tell the truth, I'm scared of this Resistance. They'd do anything to keep their little group a secret ... in fact, they have.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: I am told that the suspension of mining in Lhusu was a part of Marquis Ondore's plan to starve the Empire of Stones. Could it be?

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Cloudborne Row): I will see natural magicite before I go home to Archades. They'll have solved the unpleasantness in the mines by now, I should think.

text.City Parijanah: The Resistance? Haa ... They train in the marches, it is true. But they are young ... so young. I fear all their training will be of little avail.

text.City Parijanah (talking to woman at tabl: I will soon go to join my comrades upon a patrol vessel in the Resistance fleet! Should I live to return, I will be married!

text.Cloudborne Patron (man in white shorts s: With Rozarria and Archadia breathing down each other's necks, few hunters think about marks, bhadra. Perhaps now is your chance?

text.Shop Clerk (moogle with green pom-pom): Finally, we've our Bhujerban Madhu back in stock, kupo! More than enough for a celebratory toast for all when the war is won, kupo!!!

text.Cloudborne Patron (woman sitting at tabl: To think that this was a hotbed of resistance activity, bhadra! Myself? I was merely drinking.

text.Cloudborne Patron (man sitting at table: Me, I'm one of the Resistance out of Rabanastre, to tell the truth. I used to sit here, pretending to drink, talking to our Bhujerban allies. Eh he he ... Pretty good act I put on, eh? Well, I wasn't exactly pretending to drink ...

text.Shop Clerk (woman in green, pink, and br: To think that Melisa and so many of her regulars were members of the Resistance! But even more surprising, that Magu, too, was one of them!

text.Cloudborne Patron (blue seeq at bar): Should the Resistance prevail in this struggle, then we will toast them with sweet madhu, and life will be good!

text.Magu: Harrum? Melisa call for me? Guess my time's come at last ... Time ta pound some Imperials inta cloudspit! (snort)

text.Cloudborne Patron (moogle with yellow po: I haven't told many people, but I used to be a combat pilot, kupo. I'm joining the Resistance to lead an attack squadron! Can't wait to sink a few of them Imperial ships good, kupo!

text.Melisa: Haa ... We have lost much money this month. Men cannot drink if they are away at war. And should they win, we will shower them with fine Bhujerban Madhu ... and we'll lose even more money. As much as it pains me, that's money I hope to lose.

text.City Parijanah (with blue jacket): The Imperial soldier fights for advancement and glory, but the Resistance soldier fights for his freedom. How can we lose? We cannot.

text.City Parijanah (talking to red bangaa): Should the Resistance in Bhujerba move, all our comrades in other lands are set to join us. I am glad to have played my part.

text.Cloudborne Patron (man leaning on bar, s: And so war has come at last ... The Resistance, they are filled with hope, but before the might of the Empire, they will surely lose.

text.City Parijanah (leaning against counter): I thought you a bother after the Ronsenburg unpleasantness, but perhaps it was your unthinking brashness that prompted the Marquis to act.

text.Timorous Bangaa: Ah, it's you! The Resistance's time has come at last, eh? Time to feed the Empire a bit o' their own medicine!

text.Bhujerban (light blue seeq walking aroun: The Empire has attacked Bur-Omisace! The holiest of mountains! What is Ivalice come to? Hanta ...

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler ... or should I say "Captain"? Have you heard of the coup within the Rozarrian military? The hardliners have been deposed!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom): When moogles get a mind to do something, they do it, kupo! I even have friends in the army! Don't judge a pom-pom by its fluffiness, kupo!

text.Street Kid (in yellow, with mother kneel: I do not like Amba, for always she is so angry! But the nice Imperial soldier, he says, "Love your mother, for she is the only one you have." Haa ...

text.Bhujerban (man in blue leaning on ledge): When I was a child, only rarely did I see warships flying here. Today, I can barely see the sky for the birds of war. As if this were a battlefield!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: His Excellency the Marquis is a truly great statesman, but Lord Vayne is a truly great General. To fight Archades ... is to lose, I fear.

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink headscarf leani: I ... I am seeing an Imperial soldier, it is true. His troop, they are in Rabanastre now. I wonder if we shall meet again ...

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink, blue, and red: I have heard that the Emperor in Archades has been killed! A truth: no matter how powerful the man, someday, he dies. You see, bhadra?

text.Bhujerban (black bangaa walking about): Even should Archadia lose this struggle and leave our city, it would change nothing. It would not be long before Rozarria came to take their place.

text.Street Kid (in blue, on ledge): I am tired of playing pirates and Judges. We must think of a new game, yes.

text.City Parijanah: I had to keep the parijanah's involvement with the Resistance a secret from my family for months. Haa ... My wife believed I was unfaithful!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The Lhusu Mines are closed, bhadra. Who knows when they might reopen, with war on the wind. Still, I am sure the Marquis will have a solution.

text.City Parijanah: I am new to this post, you see. The former parijanah, they have joined the Marquis's fleet and ... No. Forget what I have just said, yes?

text.Miners' Ender (man in green and brown sh: The buildings in this part of town exist from the time of the Galtean Alliance, bhadra. Our history is longer than that of Archadia! Of course, should we all be destroyed in war, this will mean little.

text.Bhujerban Guru (Miner's End): Listen, bhadra. You know the board where bills for marks are posted in the Cloudborne? Who puts them there? No one knows. Mysterious!

text.Miners' Ender (moogle with orange pom-po: As Bhujerba floats through the sky, so does she float between empire and kingdom, kupo, never settling on one shore, so to speak. I can't see how any war would involve us, kupo.

text.Miners' Ender (man in white turban and d: Did you know that Bhujerba depends on trade for its food? That is why we must never go to war. We would starve without the ships! Kastam ...

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink top and hea: I have work to do in Rabanastre, but I will not go now. Should Rozarria invade, it would certainly be the battlefield, yes? Another Nabudis ...

text.Miners' Ender (guy sitting on ledge next: Has anyone noticed that the Archadian embassy to Bhujerba has closed? The ambassador has returned to the Empire! Could this mean war? Kastam ...

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink, blue, and: First we head that the Marquis is ill, now we head it was all a lie. He cannot be trusted, bhadra. In public he defies the Empire, but in private ...

text.Lhusu Miner (Bhorta): Bhorta doubts the Marquis will fight the Empire, in truth. His words are sweet like madhu, but in secret he wags his tail for the Judges. Haa!

text.Miners' Ender (green-pommed moogle sitti: Bhujerba has high walls, but these will not hide us forever if there is an invasion, kupo ... I say, strike first! Kupo-kupo-kupo!!!

text.City Parijanah: If we are to fight with the great army of Archadia, we must ally ourselves with Rozarria, or all is for naught. A choice of two damnations! Hanta ...

text.Miners' Ender Kid: They say many maha airships like the Leviathan will soon come! I cannot wait! I wish they would come sooner, yes!

text.Lhusu Miner (black bangaa yelling at moo: Moogle! I will never forget this, Moogle! Silence! No excuses! I smell the truth on your breath! Oh ... my sweet Bhujerban Madhu ... Why? Why!?

text.Lhusu Parivir: Mmmrrgh? Ehh, the Lhusu Mines are sep'rated into sites ... Nah, you need keys to get into each. They keep 'em all at the Staras residence, see. The master there's the Lady Niray.
