Eh? Aye, she has a husband ... eh, I'll explain later. The Staras residence's at the south end of Cloudborne Row.

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink, blue and y: House Ondore has ruled in Bhujerba for many centuries, bhadra, no different from House Solidor of Archades. Neither truly love the people.

text.Lhusu Miner (man in dark shorts sitting: Many of the young workers at the magicite mines, they have joined the Resistance! I bought them all parting gifts at Bashketi's Gambits ... I only hope I will see them again.

text.Miners' Ender (moogle in gold with orang: T-Too many hills, kupo! I once thought of moving to Balfonheim, but there they have pirates! Wait ... I've seen pirates here, too. And hills!

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink leaning aga: I keep track of the magicite trade, you see. My sources, they tell me the Empire has turned to the Henne mines, now that Lhusu has run dry.

text.City Parijanah: Haa, it is you, the false captain. Tell me, "Captain," have you imitated anyone else? Perhaps you could not participate till the war is over.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The Lhusu Mines? Closed, as always, bhadra. It is far too dangerous within for travelers. Don't become another statistick, yes?

text.Lhusu Miner (man in green and brown shor: The mines have been closed a good time now by order of the Marquis. We miners have received a good pension, however. I do not complain.

text.City Parijanah: His Excellency is a practical man, bhadra. To secure Bhujerba's safety in war, he would use any means available to him, you see. Be it the Resistance, Rozarria ... or you.

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: Svagatam, traveler. I have seen many airships from many lands in my day, but none compare to ours. It's the moogles' skill with machines, you see.

text.Archadian Wayfarer (Clio's): My brother, he is a researcher at Draklor Laboratory, you see. He said he would one day like to learn mooglecraft, but his ship ... went down. I know he is lost to me, but still, I come to this shop. You see ... I was to meet him here.

text.City Parijanah: Yes, traveler, this is Bashketi's Gambits. Our organization, too, uses gambits. Many of us lack proper training, you see. Leadership is vital!

text.Bhujerban (man in green and blue browsin: Why must there be war, bhadra? For Bhujerba to become the next Rabanastre would be sad, but to become the next Nabudis ... This would be tragic.

text.Shop Clerk (orange seeq on upper level): I gave this young lady many gambits! (snort) Now we are the best of friends! I get to do her cleaning, and cooking, and carrying ... (snort)

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: The decrease in Stones from Lhusu was all according to the Marquis's plan, bhadra! A fine stratagem! The Empire would never suspect!
To tell the truth ... I am not so good with heights. For 5ree years have I stood guard at Kaff Terrace, and still, I am terrified. Hanta ...

text.City Parijanah: Svagatam, traveler! Welcome to Kaff Terrace! It has been decided. I will join the Resistance fleet. I am enjoying the view while I still may.

text.Bhujerban (black bangaa): Be they Archadian or Rozarrian, if an army should be so bold as to step upon Bhujerban soil, bhadra, we will push them off. Ksudra!

text.Bhujerban Sainikah: These days, I often look to the sky, and my heart suspects a storm of invaders will come.

text.Bhujerban (man in red, green, and blue t: Bhujerbans are born in the free skies. We cherish freedom above all else, you see. We're Bhujerba invaded, all would take up arms in her defense!

text.Bhujerban (moogle with green pom-pom wal: If Bhujerba should become a battlefield, I will spread these little wings of mine and fly far, far away, kupo! Just ... I've never really flown.

text.Bhujerban (man in brown pants and green: My love was to arrive by airship, but her ship has been delayed, I hear. What could be keeping her in Rabanastre ... ?

text.Bhujerban (moogle with yellow pom-pom si: When I stand here, looking out on the sky, I remember my youth. I once was a pirate of some renown, you see ... Alas, those days of free skies and freer love are long past. Kastam, as they say, kastam ...

text.Bhujerban (green-pommed moogle walking a: Wait, wait, wait, the Lhusu Mines aren't closed because they ran out of magicite, are they, kupo? We'll fall out of the sky!

text.Bhujerban (woman in pink, green, and tan: An airship carrying arms and munitions has left the terrace for Balfonheim. Balfonheim? Who there could have bought so much? It is odd ...

text.Bhujerban (man in green and brown shorts: The great edifice you see ahead is the residence of His Excellency the Marquis ... who is away from Bhujerba, I hear. I wonder what he is doing?

text.Bhujerban (light blue seeq at left of st: They're saying 'twere the Leviathan what went down in the Jagd Yensa ... Airships that can fly in jagd!? The whole world's doomed, I tell ye!

text.Miners' Ender (woman in pink top and hea: Yes, Bhujerba has supplied the Empire with their Stones, yet I suspect the very best magicite has been kept in secret by the Marquis!

text.Lhusu Parivir (Lhusu Square): Should war come upon us, we have only to go into the mines. Yes, there are raksas within, but, to be honest, an army frightens me more, bhadra.

text.Street Vendor: Raksas are running wild in the mines, and all work has come to a stop. How am I to sell without any customers? Unless you can help me out, haa?

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Aekom: They say that those who lost their jobs when the mines closed are to receive a pension. What about we parivir? Do those who guard the workers not deserve the same treatment?

text.Entrepreneur: Enterprise!? Why, the time is as ripe as ever! To suffer the markets, lose your gil, and tumble into the gutter. Speak not to me of enterprise.

text.Ruined Woman: I sold my sandalwood chop to pay off a debt, but now I've managed to buy it back! I wagered my coin on some information, and Fortune smiled!

text.Haughty Boy: Naught to do ... (sigh) Though doing naught's a fair shade better than consorting with the likes of you ardents.

text.Imperious Man: Ah, just look at the city sprawled beneath us. That's the joy of Empire: being on top.

text.Quiet Woman: I do wish they'd leave the running about to the children. Grown men shouldn't go dashing to and fro. It's unseemly!

text.Curious Boy: What could fluster a Judge, I wonder. Well, everything seems to be back to normal now in any case. (sigh) How dull.

text.Docent: I see you've a sandalwood chop. Would you care to go to Central now, sir?

CHOICE.ACTION: The Docent presses a button, opening the elevator doors up for you, and bows, and you take the elevator up to the Grand Arcade.

text.ACTION: Grand Arcade

text.Imperial (Dealing with Cockatrice 1): (huff) Whod have thought something so (pant) big and ungainly could move so (wheeze) fast!?

text.Imperial (Dealing with Cockatrice 2): If only there was a way to communicate with cockatrices ... maybe I could talk him down.

text.Imperial (Dealing with Cockatrice 3): Clear the area! This cockatrice is dangerous! I'd tackle it myself, but it's big as well as nasty!

text.ACTION: Until you remove Agytha (the cockatrice) by completing her portion of the quest and reenter the area, the three Imperials and Agytha will be the only NPCs in this area. For more of their dialogue, see Side Quests. Once you do reenter the area, you will get the NPC dialogue below.

text.Perfumed Lady: My, such outlandish clothes! Are you from out of town, perchance? You don't look like gentry ...

text.Hesitant Traveler: Travelers, are you? I'd been contemplating going on holiday myself, but what with the unsettling rumors ... Better go soon, or not at all.

text.Lady of Means: Our combine has begun a glorious new enterprise! If only the goings-on with the Senate would sort themselves out, real progress could be made ...

text.Cab Guide: If you're waiting on a cab, it's like to be a long wait, mate. There's been some trouble — watch ordered us to stop service throughout the city.

text.Researcher (first in line, reading a new: How long are we to be made to wait? 'Tis unjust that philosophers alone have private transport! Ahh, the humble cab: lot of the lowly researcher.

text.Researcher (at the back of the line): You've heard of the intruders at Draklor? The place is an iron-walled fortress! Why anyone would invite such peril ...

text.Proper Gentleman: You've no doubt heard that the prodigal son of House Bunansa has returned to the City at last? Well, I daresay I'm not the only one wondering what precisely he's been doing for all this time, nor where precisely he's been doing it!

text.Gentle Gentleman: Vayne has certainly gone up in the world. Why, we often played as children, he and I. Perhaps I was the one being played, now I think on it.

text.Imperial: Look, you're not the first to ask me which way the Senate lists. Best ask a Judge. They don't tell us such things.

text.Cheeky Child: Hey! Who are you? What makes you think you can walk up 'n' be friends just like that?

text.Pleasant Woman: Peaceful ... So very peaceful up here. Hmm? Something going on below, you say? Whatever it is, I assure you it will have small effect on our little circle. I daresay peace will last as long as the Empire's glory — forever.

text.Proud Horticulturist: Look, even at this height, greenery abounds! Shrubbery in the skies! And you're looking at the bloke who made it happen ... and a few gil!

text.Bristly Mother: I'd appreciate a bit more quiet, thank you very much. If she wakes, I'll have you to thank.

text.Idle Gentleman: Always a rat-race down there. Brokers crying for morsels of knowledge, such-and-such a lord vying for power ... Nothing of the sort up here! Yet, I do feel I've a bit of time on my hands of late. I find myself wanting ... more. If you've anything of import to share, out with it!

text.Hunt Club Owner: Travelers, are you? You've been by Phon Coast?

CHOICE.Hunt Club Owner: Eh, what's that? You mean to say it was you who did for the mark and not the Hunt Club!?

CHOICE.ACTION: He turns back to the other three in the group.

CHOICE.Hunt Club Owner: Friends, listen! This gentleman claims he did for the mark we requested of the Club! Perhaps we put the wrong men in Phon, eh? Hah!

Then, allow me to propose a deal. When you've hunted down a fair share of marks, come back here and regale is with your tales of conquest! What? No, no, we'll make it worth the trip. Keep us apprised of your exploits, and we'll see you're suitably recompensed.
Ah. do excuse me, I thought perhaps ... never mind.

text.Hunt Club Owner: Ah, 'Tis you. So you've already laid to rest a formidable foe? We await news of your further exploits!

text.Weary Man: I tire of these dull, drearisome days. And you? Are your days filled with excitement, hrmm?

text.Nervous Seeq: You ... you went to the City, did you? That's quite somethin', that is. I thought to go up there meself, but me feet went all of a tingle ...

text.Broken Man: I was played false by false information up in the City ... Then it occurred to me, I should be the one doing the playin'. That's the way to do it ...

text.Frustrated Woman: I've plans to go up to the City with my beau ... But he's kept me waiting for hours! Mayhap I'll go on ahead by myself.

text.Jules: With your help, I've made myself a pretty bit o' coin of late. Many thanks, boy. Hope to do business with you again soon. Heh heh.

text.Fermon: I was just telling these youngsters a story about the ruins in the Tchita Uplands. How many years I've spent in their study. How many more to come ...

text.Nay-Sayer: Oh, it's you ... I 'eard you'd been gettin' into all sorts of places you shouldn't, up in the City. Surprised you've come back from 'em.

text.Disparaging Woman: Ye've been to the City, I hear ... How was it? I've a mind to go meself. Someday.

text.Beasley: Hey, er, thanks mate. Got me bag o' coins back. I'm just preparin' meself for the journey up to the City, now. How about you? Are you prepared? Deep down? Really? Oh. All right, well, best o' luck then.

text.Worried Grandson: Me gran's given up on the City for good, it seems. I just 'ope she doesn't get any other barmy ideas into 'er 'ead.

text.Lucky Man: Oi! Ye couldn't keep yer gob shut, could ye? Ye went an' told someone what was meant to stay between us. A right rotten thing to do, was that.

text.Indefatigable Granny: I was all ready t' begin a new life up in the City, but me grandson, he convinced me otherwise. I suppose I belong here ... sad as that makes me.

text.Imperial (Guarding Archades Entrance): Bah, we see nothing but brawling and loutishness down here. If you start something, don't expect to be let off lightly!

text.Shifty-eyed Man: Its important time grab wotever information comes yer way ... but just as important to know Wot ya can and can't trust. Who, me? Heh heh! Oh, you can trust me, son! You can trust me...

text.Little Sister: Me sister's had a letter from 'er fella. What's it say? She ain't even told me that ... But she seems well 'appy, an' that's wot matters, innit?

text.The Moogles Eight: A band of moogles eight are we,

text.Proud Brother: Did you 'ear that!? Me brother says 'e ain't goin' back!? 'Ow can 'e say such a thing, when the 'ole clan's 'ere eggin' 'im on!?
So yer've changed yer mind? Yer goin' back! ...Right?

text.Weary Brother: I made a few gil, but I didn't have no fun doin' it. I need time to think on things, here. The moment I go back into that hell ... I'm too busy to think.

text.Distinguished Elder: Somethin' the matter, is it? Somethin' ye don't like about us, is there?

text.Granddaughter: My grandad was a Judge in 'is day, just so's ye know! Best get lost 'fore 'e gets all judgmental on ye!

text.Distinguished Elder: Hush with ye, sweetheart. Beggin' yer pardon, sir. Pay no mind to her. She talks about things she knows little of. Aye, I've a lot in me past, but today I'm just one more tired old man in Oldtown. For pity, sir, leave us be.

text.Hungry Child: I'm bloomin' 'ungry. I get lots o' tasty tidbits of information down 'ere, ye know ... I just wish I got some tasty tidbits o' food, as well!

text.Quiet Talker: This geezer? Nah, 'e ain't dead, not by a stretch. Funny ya should mention it, though. Turns out, 'e was known for a particular peculiar talent ... 'E was a genius at playin' dead! That's 'ow 'e made it to such a ripe old age. Soon as a battle went sour, there 'e'd be, flat on 'is back. "The Stone Warrior," they called 'im. Heh heh!

text.Sighing Boy: Accordin' to what she's been sayin', this airship she saw weren't wide across, but stacked up high! A bloomin' thundercloud, that's what she saw!

text.Shady Seeq: Them moogles beat me to within an inch o' me life! I'll never look at a pom-pom the same way again ...

text.Suspicious Woman: I knew that seeq was up to no good! He was selling moogles! Can you believe that? He led 'em right up the garden path, he did. Poor little fellas.

text.Indecisive Man: Should I go to the City? Should I not? Is there no way to get ahead, other than the soldiering life? Hmm ... I hear that fellow sitting in the corner over there used to be a Judge. Mayhap he'll be able to advise me.

text.Fresh Ardent: When I sleep, I sometimes dream these dreams. I'm in the City again, meetin' folk. Makin' deals. S'pose I ain't used to life down 'ere yet.

text.Loiterer: You seem to be keeping herself busy. Busy's good. Busy's profitable. Tell me a tale of home someday, will ya? Of Rabanastre, I mean. See? There ain't much I don't know!

text.Frank Woman: Have you got business with us? If it's love you seek, why I had plenty. But I've gone and given it all to my husband. I'm afraid you're out of luck.

text.Ex-Broker: I've given up o' late. No good comes of tryin', so why try? I'm startin' to think the best thing to do is live 'n' die here ... in peace 'n' quiet.

text.Busy Girl: Wot am I doin'? There's knowledge with needs gatherin', an' I plan on gatherin' it! Think I got bags o' time like you oldies? 'Cos I ain't! Ido 'ave a question though ... Er ... This knowledge ... wot's it all about?

text.Dreaming Man: This big ol' lady cockatrice came galumphin' out o' nowhere, jus' now. There was this other cockatrice here, see, and the two of 'em went off somewhere together. If I didn't know any better, I'd say it was love.

text.Sensible Man: It seemed to me they was cryin'. Or maybe it was laughin'? It's hard to tell with cockatrices.

text.Dreaming Man: That reminds me. We plucked that cockatrice out o' Giza, didn't we. I suppose it was lonely, out here in the big city all alone. Poor thing.

text.Archadian Fisherman: What can ye catch here? Well, I'm not sure what ye'd be able t' catch. Me? I'm hopin' t' catch ma supper!

text.Cautious Woman: Headed to the City, are ye? Going to be a soldier like the rest of 'em? I wish ye luck. Just ... think on what ye'll lose 'well as what ye stand to gain.

text.Hating Man: Now that's a face I dislike. It's the nose ... Pointy, probin'. A nose that smells but ne'er tells. You know the sort. Eh, whom do I speak of? His name was Daguza ... and he was the stinkin'est, foulest cretin I ever knew!

text.Stairbottom Elder: And there I was thinking you'd come here without a scrap of information to your name ... Imagine my surprise when I found out you'd got a lot more than a scrap ... that you were very well informed indeed ...

text.Wary Woman: Welcome to Archades ... If you want to see yer dreams come true, be a soldier. The people down 'ere, they're the ones what refused. They wouldn't take up the sword, and look what 'appened: spent n' shriveled, the lot of 'em. You want somethin', you pay the price.

text.Precocious Girl: Yer the prodigal Bunansa, eh? Hrm ... Yer shorter than I imagined ye.

text.Man at the Gate: I've 'eard o' ye. Yer the lad o' seven-and-ten what's come from Rabanastre. Talk is that ye've the prodigal Bunansa in yer party, what's more.

text.Garif Warrior (on riverbank by two sparr: A cockatrice has wandered into the village, and we are all quite concerned. Well, not that concerned, to tell the truth.

text.Geomancer Yugelu: A great power lies sleeping deep within the Henne Mines. Yet ... as you are now, you lack the strength to master such a thing.

text.Warrior Guromu: Our War-chief speaks little and smiles less, but he is a kind person. He is stubborn, yes, but all in the village know of his prowess.Yet, to watch him now, it is sadness. He is in pain, unable to forget a past mistake.

text.War-chief Supinelu: There are many in the village who think me not fit to be War-chief. Of course, this is so. I am not like my brother before me, who was skilled in the ways of leading warriors. Yet ... the Catoblepas I shall slay! It is my duty to the village.

text.Garif Elder: That cockatrice ... Why do I feel I have seen it somewhere before?

text.Asdalu: I have heard that the nomads of Giza herd cockatrices much as we herd nannas. I wonder ... do they eat them? I wonder ... do they taste like chicken?

text.Garif Warrior: Geomancer Yugelu once told me that, in an ancient tongue, "Zertinan" means "the underworld." I believe this name most fitting, for the Catoblepas and this new creature of strange powers seen there are truly hellish.

text.Garif Herder (to the right): You ... can speak with the cockatrice? How amazing! Why did you not say this sooner?

text.Garif Herder (on far left): A cockatrice has wandered into our village. From its manner, I do not think it is wild. Who is raising cockatrices near here ... ?

text.Garif Herder (right next to cockatrice): You can speak the tongue of the cockatrice? Then, ask this one why it has come here!

text.ACTION: For more of the dialogue pertaining to Shurry, see Side Quests. Once you have completed Shurry's portion of this side quest and the cockatrice has gone, some of the villagers will revert to the following normal dialogue.

text.Garif Herder (standing in front of shack: I knew the War-chief in his childhood, and I know him well now. When his elder brother, Kadalu, became War-Chief, he strove to become strong. Yet, after what the Catoblepas did ... I'm sorry, it is a personal matter. Please forget it.

text.Garif Herder (by the nanna pen): The other day, as I was milking one of the nanna in my enclosure, a nanna nearby bleated noisily. Oh, how startled I was! Nanna bleat only rarely, you see. And ... we have a saying, that when the nanna bleats, evil will come.

text.Garif Herder (one of two, nearest the br: Of late, our nannas are very restless. I fear it is a sign of something bad to come.

text.Asdalu: There is to be a war among the humes? At our gathering, so did the Great-Chief and the High-chief say. I fear that it may be true ...

text.Garif Warrior (on riverbank by two sparr: Many garif warriors dream of the day when they shall face and defeat the Catoblepas. The War-chief is one such who dreams ... Yet he dreams of folly, for he would face the creature on his own! Folly!

text.High-chief Zayalu: The garif have ever walked in history's shadow. Soon, even the humes will forget us, and we will remain only in legend. No, do not pity us, for this is how it should be.

text.Great Chief Uball-Ka: In our village, time passes slowly. If you should tire on your journey, come and rest here. The Land will renew you, body and spirit. The burden you carry, it is heavier than most. Rest when you can.

text.Low-chief Sugumu: There is a creature wandering about the Zertinan Caverns that is surely to be posted as a mark ... if it is indeed not already being hunted.

text.Garif Youth: You have traveled to many places, I hear. Have you seen snow? It is like silk to the eye, yet cold to the touch, is it not? I have heard that snow falls in the forest to the southeast of our village, but the elders warn against going there. They say this forest is a place of twisting paths that addle the senses. I do not think I shall go.

text.Fran: The time given viera is long. Carefully must Mjrn consider her choice, for herself decide whether she will remain. She may choose the same path Jote walks, but it is her choice to make. Strength it takes to live by viera laws. Strength I may have lacked ...

text.Lulucce: There was a commotion not long ago. Something fell from one of the trees. I get dizzy just thinking about it, kupo. I saw the wood-warders helping what looked to me like a cockatrice. Yes, definitely a cockatrice, kupo.

text.ACTION: shop menu

text.Tetran: It feels as though time stands still here, but when I go into town to restock my wares ... how much has happened while I've been away, kupo! Want to hear something scary, kupo? I have it on good authority there are monsters which mimic crystals, and pounce when you touch them!

text.Wood-dweller (long-haired viera looking: If in our reclusion we are forgotten, then that, too, is as it must be. As countless spirits and uncountable visions before, the viera will fade to eldritch shadow, an echo of the Wood's voice on the wind.

text.Wood-warder (at bottom of steps): Visitors are not welcome in this place. Leave the Wood. Your way shall not be barred.

text.Wood-dweller (viera sitting in center ar: You persist in visiting us. I did not think our welcome so ... inviting. What do you think to find here? Or do you think not at all? Is it this sluggish wit that gives you humes such resilience? Intriguing ...

text.Wood-dweller (long-haired viera staring: Our paths are of our own choosing. Should two paths diverge, we might look back upon the time they were one, but never can they be untrod.

text.Wood-dweller (viera staring down at flow: At what do I look? I would know this answer myself. Water is like the soul: ever-changing, constant only in its inconstancy. It flows, and freezes. It joins the air, and rains down upon the Wood.

text.Nera: The Green Word, the laws of our village, a future filled with ruin ... if we dwell on such weighty matters, we are like to collapse under the burden. There is no end that is not also a beginning. The sun will rise and fall as it always has ... this is enough for me.

text.Wood-dweller (long haired viera walking: The wooden screens about the village interest you? If our village is attacked, we welcome our guests with arrows from behind those screens. It is a grave matter, never to be spoken of idly.

text.Wood-warder (near warders' den): The Green Word before all other things must we protect. In this we cannot look to others for aid.

text.Kjrs: Yes? What is it? We discuss our sentinel of the Wood. I do not share Rael's tolerance for your interruptions. If your errand concerns not me, speak with me not.

text.Rael: There are those who blame Jote for the deeds of her sisters. As elder, she must always defend the village. Until now, diligently she has. But she is not alone. We wood-warders stand at her side. Together we defend the Wood.

text.Rena: Betrayal begins with but a thought of the world beyond the Wood. This is why we fear its call. What found Mjrn in that beyond? Please, visit us no more. For Mjrn's sake, if no other.

text.Wood-dweller (sitting and talking to ano: The reagents we gather in the Wood — plant seeds and roots, tree sap, animal eggs, feathers — all are stored in the house behind me. The Wood is the world to us, and the world the Wood. As we are part of the Wood, so are we part of the world. In this is there balance, and bliss.

text.Alja: Would you know more of the Wood? The life that burgeons in Her must be shown the proper respect. Beauty seldom comes without danger. To one who walks in ignorance, the Wood can seem dark, Her life promising naught but death.

text.Wood-dweller (long-haired viera): When will you learn your trespass here is not welcome? Do not think all Ivalice yours to wander as you please.

text.Wood-dweller (viera with pixie cut behin: Do you still not see? There is nothing here for you. Here we live out our time. Your time and ours are not meant to cross. So has it ever been, and so shall it ever be.

text.Wood-dweller (viera with pixie cut near: Always must Jote remain with the village, her thoughts on us and the Wood. She is our leader, our guide. Some think her too severe, yet the path the viera walk is long. Missteps early on, however slight, can lead us far astray.

text.Hala: We choose this hidden place, secluded from the world beyond, to live as we have always lived. This is what it is to be viera. If you understand our ways even a little, you will not set foot again within our village.

text.Jote: Seed is carried furthest on rough winds. Where it lands matter little, so long as it finds fertile soil in which to take root.

text.Mjrn: Whence has this cockatrice come? These beasts, too, know loneliness ...

text.ACTION: For dialogue with Mjrn and Chit, the cockatrice, see Side Quests. After Chit has left the village and you exit and reenter Eruyt, the following dialogue will happen.

text.Mjrn: The will to quell my thoughts of the world outside the Wood ... the courage to live beyond Her ... Neither do I possess. Will I never share in the strength of my sisters?

text.Lulucce: A cockatrice just darted past at tremendous speed, kupo. If it's not careful, it's like to have another spill, kupo. Oh, bother.

text.Wood-warder: I have sensed a strong Mist in the south these past days. It is as though it ... it calls for someone.

text.Kiltias (at entrance): The Archadian attack has left our whole mountain, nay, all Kiltias, vulnerable. Many of the refugees who sought haven here has scattered to the winds. May the Light Guide their paths. Faram.

text.Traveling Merchant (seeq): I fear this mountain is doomed to fade. I'll be packing up my shop soon, too. You might be my last customer, come to think of it.

text.Traveling Merchant (hume man at left): What with the Empire invadin', and the Gran Kiltias dyin', this place's gotten drearier than ever. Go on, buy somethin', please?

text.Cartographers' Guild: Sure is lonely here these days, kupo ... Would you like to buy a map?

text.Refugee (woman in orange dress): The Imperial army will soon be here to claim this holy place as its own, I fear ...

text.Refugee (man in gray pants): Ever since that day, I can't help but glance at the sky in fear. Every cloud seems an airship, every thunderclap the peal of cannon.

text.Acolyte (speaking with Kiltias man): In the depths of a forest enshrouded by Mist and snowstorm lies the legendary city of the ancient gods. I have not seen it, mind you.

text.Kiltias (Walk of Mind): I fear a dreadful thing has happened. Yet in your eyes I see a glimmer of hope. May the graceful and merciful Father watch over you. Faram.

text.ACTION: If you try to exit southward, you will be turned back by raging Mist and a system message will show.
A dense Mist prevents you from advancing.

The party looks on the swirling Mist in consternation. Ashe puts her chin to her hand, thinking. Then she looks up and sees Rasler's apparition, standing in the Mist. She begins to walk toward him, and suddenly the Mist surges forward and pours out. The way now cleared, Rasler turns, as if beckoning her to follow.
A giant, sentient plant emerges.
After defeating the Rafflesia ...
You get a victory screen.
Feywood Glyph: A strange pattern is etched in the ground.

CHOICE.ACTION: Voiceless words chime within your head: "In this sanctum shall the pilgrim find truth and illusion both. Illusion betokens the true way."

text.ACTION: The Edge of Reason

text.Gate Gigas: The colossal gate bears a timeworn inscription.

CHOICE.Gate Gigas: "Gigas summoner, gate's Power is yours to claim. Beyond the One gate lies sacred Giruvegan. Over the One gate the Gigas holds sway."
Strong Magicks bind the gate. It will not open.

text.ACTION: If you summon Belias before the Gate Gigas ...
Belias claps the hands of its forearms together, then points them outward to the gate. A series of locks light and open.

text.LOCATION: On the Farthest Shores of the River of Time

text.ACTION: The group emerges on the other side of the gate in what appears to be another dimension or location; no sign of the Feywood is seen on the opposite side of the gate, the side they came from. A grand city is laid out before them, buildings and promenades separated by mirror-like water.

text.Ashe: On the farthest shores of the river of time, shrouded deep in the roiling Mist.

text.Penelo: What is it, Fran?

text.Fran: The Mist runs thick here.

text.Vaan: Like on the Leviathan?

text.Fran: Do not worry. I will behave myself. The Mist here is cooled. I sense something like the shadow here.

text.Balthier: Venat.

text.ACTION: he turns to Fran and Penelo

text.Balthier: It appears Cid has yet to arrive. We'll lie in wait for him here.

text.Penelo: So we're not going inside?

text.Balthier: Not unless you want to end up twisted. Like the old man.

text.ACTION: he notices Ashe looking intently ahead

text.Balthier: Something there?

text.ACTION: The camera shifts over to her, panning from one side of her to the other; we see now, in her vision, Rasler's apparition standing before her. He turns and walks away again. Ashe follows.

text.Penelo: What is it?

text.Vaan: She can see him. Let's follow her.

text.ACTION: A statue of a headless giant with a massive sword waits on the path ahead, and suddenly comes to life.
After defeating Daedalus...
The giant staggers backward, slumps over leaning heavily on its sword, and turns back to stone. You get a victory screen.
Ancient beyond reckoning, the device still functions.
A barrier of powerful Magicks prevents passage. There might be a mechanism to lower the barrier elsewhere.
Chthes Gate
Paron Gate
Parelthon Gate
Tychi Gate
The party walks along the path of green glyphs suspended in the air. The massive, glowing crystal is suspended to their right, always well visible. Penelo stops, and Vaan stops with her.

text.Penelo: I can't shake the feeling we're somewhere we're not meant to be.

text.Vaan: Yeah, it's exciting.

text.Penelo: Exciting?

text.Basch: You are not troubled by the unknown? Who can say what lies ahead? We may encounter the very creators of nethicite.

text.Vaan: Yeah, I don't know what we'll find. I like it better that way.

text.Basch: You're sounding more the sky pirate every day.

text.ACTION: A great aevis lands on the path behind them; as it runs toward them, the path disappears in its wake.
After defeating the Tyrant...
The aevis falls over the edge into the abyss, and bursts into particles of light. A way stone appears in the center. You get a victory screen.
Scorpio Gate Stone: The device does not respond, but voiceless words chime within your head: "For my master's chosen, and no other, the way will I lay open."
What appears to be a great sphere of nethicite hovers before them. It scorches with light and Mist.

text.Penelo: I've never seen this much Mist. Are you all right?

text.Fran: I am fine. Thank you.

text.Ashe: Is that nethicite?

text.Fran: I wonder.

text.Ashe: With that much nethicite in one's grasp —

text.Fran: You could destroy all of Ivalice. If you wished it.

text.ACTION: she looks to Ashe
An Esper lands before them, a demon-like woman with red skin and hooved feet.
After defeating Shemhazai ...
The Esper is sealed into a purple crystal. You obtain the Esper Shemhazai, the Whisperer.
Empyrean Way Stone: Magicks stir within this device.

CHOICE.ACTION: "By this path, and no other, reach ye the Round of the Undying, walk of the Chosen."

text.ACTION: The Round of the Undying, suspended in the sky. Click image for video.
High in the clouds above Giruvegan, on a circular platform edged in statues of strange gargoyle-like figures, a beam of light opens, a column from the complex floating above it to the center.
When the light clears, Ashe is standing there in the center of the platform, alone. She looks around.

text.Ashe: Where is everyone?

text.ACTION: An eerie voice is heard.

text.Occuria: Fear not, Princess of Dalmasca. We Occuria have chosen you, and you alone.

text.ACTION: She looks at the strange statues. Some sort of blue magick begins swirling outward from them. In front of Ashe, it forms the shape of a being that looks very much like Venat, with glowing eyes.

text.Occuria: Ashelia B'nargin Dalmasca. We see your heart desires power, and power most holy shall we grant. Seek you the Sun-cryst, slumb'ring star. In tower on distant shore it dreams. The mother of all nethicite, the source of its unending power. The Dynast-King, his fallow shards, coarse trinkets cut from Sun-cryst's light.

text.Ashe: Such Power exists?

text.Occuria: In times that are long passed away, we thought to save this Ivalice ... and chose Raithwall the Dynast-King. He took the sword and cut the Cryst. Three shards he took from its gilt grasp, and so became the Dynast-King. His words and deeds run through your veins.

text.Ashe: That's why I was given it — the Sword of Kings.

text.Occuria: The treaty held with kings of old is but a mem'ry, cold and still. With you, we now shall treat anew, to cut a run for hist'ry's flow.

text.ACTION: A glowing blue greatsword materializes in front of the shadow being. It continues to speak to Ashe as the sword floats down to her, losing the glow and becoming silver.

text.Occuria: Now take this sword, this Treaty-Blade. Occurian seal, mark of your worth. Cut deep the Cryst and seize your shards. Wield Dynast-King's power! Destroy Venat!

text.Ashe: But Venat — Venat is an Occurian. A being like you.

text.ACTION: enraged
As if these angry words have spawned a soundwave, Ashe's hair is blown back and she puts her hands in front of her face as a shield. Other Occuria appear before the statues in the circle.

text.Occuria: The nethicite is ours to give, to chosen bearer or to none. The heretic trespassed and set the rose of knowledge in Man's hand. With imitations they profane, it is anathema to us. We give you now the Stone and task. Administer judgment: destroy them all!

text.Ashe: Judgment?

text.ACTION: Rasler appears on the other side of the sword, facing her. Ashe looks to them. Her lip trembles.

text.Ashe: Destroy them all? The Empire?

text.Occuria: The humes ever skew hist'ry's weave. With haste they move through too-short lives. Driven to err by base desires, t'ward waste and wasting on they run. Undying, we Occuria light the path for wayward sons of Man. Oft did we pass judgment on them so that Ivalice might endure. Eternal, we are hist'ry's stewards, to set the course and keep it true. The chosen is our hand, our fist, to let live some and crush the rest. Princess, you have been chosen. Take revenge against those who stole your kingdom. Fulfil your role as savior.

text.ACTION: Rasler reaches out and grasps the sword's hilt with one hand. Ashe also reaches out, as if to put her hand over his, but hesitates.

As her hand comes to rest with Rasler's on the hilt, he disappears, and so do the Occuria. The magick that held the sword aloft dissipates; her hand keeps it balanced on its point. For a moment, she stands in silence. Then, the rest of the party appears, and runs toward her.

text.Vaan: Ashe!

text.ACTION: stopping beside her

text.Vaan: What's with these Occuria? What gives them the right to tell you what to do?

text.ACTION: Fran appears at her other side.

text.Fran: Will you take revenge, as they ask?

text.Basch: We could not see them, but we heard the Occuria speak. They may be gods, but we are the arbiters of our destiny. Your Highness, I am against this. The Empire must pay, but destruction?

text.ACTION: Penelo also approaches.

text.Penelo: Um ... Does anyone know what happened to Dr. Cid? Wasn't he saying he'd be here?

text.Basch: He should've arrived by now.

text.Balthier: And I should've realized by now.

text.ACTION: everyone looks to him

text.Balthier: He's not coming. He laid out the bait, and we bit. Remember what he said? He wanted Ashe to get the Stone. He wanted that all along. That's why he flaunted his nethicite, and reeled us in with his stories about Giruvegan. All to bring Ashe to the Occuria.

text.Penelo: But wait — if we got a hold of the nethicite, wouldn't that be bad for the Empire?

text.Balthier: Maybe he wants to see what happens when foes with nethicite collide? That'd be just like Doctor Cid.

text.Ashe: I will search out the Sun-Cryst.

text.ACTION: Quiet with acceptance, the party walks away. Balthier and Ashe remain.

text.Balthier: "History is built by our hands." That's his favorite line. He'd never stand by and watch the Occuria's Stones shape things. So ... he was talking to Venat all along. He wasn't mad at all then, was he.

text.ACTION: With that, he turns and walks away. Ashe follows.
You obtain the Treaty-Blade!
Fade to black, then back in on Vayne in his office at night, with Larsa beside him as he sits at his desk, and Gabranth standing before him.

text.Larsa: Restore Dalmasca's sovereignty, and make our amends with Lady Ashe. It is the only way to avert war!

text.Vayne: It is a war of necessity. Your Lady Ashe herself is bent on it. She desires it above all else. She will not rest until her revenge is full-wrought.

text.Larsa: I fear you misread her intent. She would sooner shun war than embrace it.

text.Vayne: You are young, Larsa.

text.Larsa: And you presume beyond your ken!

text.Vayne: Then let us look closer. Judge Gabranth! I would have you seek after the Lady Ashe ... and adjudge whether she makes overtures of peace, or war. Yours shall be the eyes of the Empire.

text.Gabranth: And should I espy war, I am to put her to the sword. Is that your wish, Excellency?

text.Larsa: It will not come to that, I am sure. I have faith in her — faith in you both. On you, Gabranth, shall I wager all our fortunes.

text.Gabranth: As you will.

text.ACTION: Gabranth leaves. Larsa follows not far behind, but with a last withering glance at Vayne. Cid appears at Vayne's side, apparently having been at the window.

text.Cid: That so sweet a child could be your brother is hard to believe.

text.Vayne: Larsa is as he should be.

text.ACTION: looking beside him

text.Cid: What's that, Venat? Ah, taken the bait already, have they? Splendid.

text.ACTION: to Vayne

text.Cid: The Occuria have given the Princess her Treaty-Blade.

text.ACTION: He stands from his chair, and turns away with hands behind his back.

text.Vayne: The gods have chosen their scribe, to write history as they deem fit. Yes, and she with fresh nethicite to aid her.

text.Cid: To hell with the Occuria and their stones!

text.ACTION: Vayne turns to face him

text.Cid: What good a power that cannot be harnessed? Baubles best-suited for study, no more.

text.Vayne: We conquered two kingdoms, that you might study these "baubles."

text.Cid: Oh, I am grateful for the sacrifice. Without it, manufactured nethicite would have eluded us — an unrivaled weapon, I warrant you.

text.ACTION: addressing the air beside him again

text.Cid: Tell me, Venat. Have I not been an apt pupil?

text.ACTION: Venat appears, and speaks aloud.

text.Venat: My council did but guide your able hand. Through power of Man, the Stones did you perfect. Yes. So much accomplished in six fleeting years. Man's fervor o'er all obstacles prevailing.

text.Cid: Our lives are much too short. You undying might waste long centuries away, but we, I fear, cannot.

text.Vayne: Just so. Had we more time, we might have availed ourselves of more "prudent" measures.

text.Cid: Your greatest work still lies before you. Not lightly will the Occuria allow you to wrest the reins of History from their grasp, back into the hands of Man.

text.Venat: Indeed. What claim does Gerun have on history's reins ... seated on throne immortal, rent from time? For your ascendance, Vayne, I offer prayer. May you attain all that which is your due.

text.Vayne: Attain it I shall.

text.ACTION: Fade to black.

text.Vayne: For too long have my deeds gone unrewarded.

text.ACTION: Fade back in on the party, back at the Gate of Wind in Giruvegan.

text.Basch: In tower on distant shore dreams the Sun-cryst.

text.ACTION: to Fran

text.Basch: Do these words mean aught to you?

text.ACTION: She shakes her head.

text.Vaan: Didn't Reddas say he was going to follow some "other course"? Maybe he found out something that can help.

text.Balthier: I'd rather stay out of that sky pirate's debt, thank you.

text.Vaan: What's wrong with Reddas? If you can't trust your own kind, who can you trust?

text.Balthier: You're an expert on pirating now, are you?

text.Tellurian Way Stone: The words inscribed on the device are changing.

CHOICE.Tellurian Way Stone: "By this, return ye to the Gate of Earth. By other means, return ye back to this place."

text.Dantro's Wife: Shh! Quiet. We've a sick traveler sleeping just inside - collapsed not far from the village. I worry it may already be too late ... Dantro bade you bring this cactus flower? This should help, yes. Thank you. Take this for your trouble.

text.ACTION: You obtain a Bundle of Needles!

Dantro's Wife will return to her normal chapter dialogue after this. You must exit and reenter the villager for the next part. This may mean completing the "Cactuar Family" sidequest If you haven't already.

text.Dantro's Wife: Keep your voice low, please. Our guest is still sleeping inside. The cactus flower you brought should help with the fever, but not the pain. If I had some semclam shells I could make something to ease the pain ... Do you think I could ask you to bring me some? Semclams live in the shallows along the banks of the river. The more you can bring me, the better.
If I had some semclam shells I could make something to ease the traveler's pain. The more you can bring me, the better.

You've brought the semclam shells! Yes, yes, this should do nicely. Unfortunately our guest's wounds continue to bleed. Nebralim can stanch the wound, but we seem to be out. I think Dantro took some with him when he left for the outpost. Would you mind bringing some back to the village?
We'll need some nebralim if we're to stop the bleeding. I think Dantro took some with him when he left for the outpost. Fetch it, would you?

text.Dantro: Running errands for my wife, eh? Nebralim? There should be some over by those crates. Help yourself.

text.Dantro's Wife: You have the nebralim! Wonderful! A little of this spread over the wound should stanch the bleeding. Now to do something about the poison ... Some valeblossom dew would quickly neutralize it ... I hate to ask for your help yet again, but do you think you could gather some for me? You should find some blooming along the cliffs in the Broken Sands.
Valeblossom dew contains a potent anti-toxin. You should find some blooming along the cliffs in the Broken Sands.

text.ACTION: At this point, you must have complete the "Cactuar Family" sidequest to continue this quest.

text.Dantro's Wife: You found the Valeblossom dew? Wonderful! This should flush the poison from the body. Now we have only to wait, and hope.

text.ACTION: If you have already completed the Nidhogg hunt and obtained the great serpentskin ...

text.Dantro's Wife: Is that ... is that a great serpentskin by any chance? Boiled and distilled it makes a potent restorative drought. It may speed our guest's recovery. This great serpentskin... would you give it to me?

CHOICE.Dantro's Wife: Thank you. I shall prepare the drought at once. I'm sure it will be of help.
I see. A pity. But it is yours to do with as you will. I'm sure it will fetch a good price at market.

text.Dantro's Wife: You've helped me more than I could have hoped. The traveler rests now, and I expect a full recovery before long.
Our guest is fully recovered now — should be just around back. Wanted to give you a word of thanks, if I'm not mistaken.

text.Recovering Traveler: you're the one who brought medicine while I was unconscious? Thank you, kupo. I am a treasure hunter by trade. I learned of a great treasure deep in the Barheim Passage, kupo. I posted two sentries to watch while I went in. But I was tricked ... I found a creature waiting for me, kupo. No treasure! I got out of there as quickly as my feet would carry me! The next thing I remember is waking up here, being nursed back to health. The key I used is yours, if you want it, kupo. I've had enough.

text.ACTION: You obtain the Barheim Key!

text.Recovering Traveler: There's more than one way into the Barheim Passage, you know. I hear there's another entrance somewhere in the Estersand, kupo! Well, I'd best be off. Those fool brothers will be wondering where I've gone. Thank you for your help! Farewell, kupo!

text.ACTION: You obtain a Golden Amulet!

text.Dantro's Wife: I'm glad our traveler's recovered. Said some terrible things in the throes of that fever. Things I'd sooner forget.

text.Bandit Chief: Here's the entrance to Barheim, kupo. Look down past Terminus No. 7 if you want to find that treasure. Watch yourself down there, kupo.

text.ACTION: Weather-beaten Door: The door is locked.
Jovy the Hero
After escaping Nalbina & the Barheim Passage, you will unlock this side story. Talk to the viera sitting in an alcove on a stairway in the Muthru Bazaar to begin this side quest.

Ktjn will form a question or comment to which you can give one of two answers. According to the strategy guide, "her questions are given once per scenario block", until you've received the Treaty-Blade, in which case, if you haven't already answered all her questions, she will ask a new one every fifteen minutes. If you've already answered a question and it's not time for her to ask a new one yet, then she will simply repeat the last thing said every time you talk to her, until the time comes for the new question.

Ktjn will appear in the Muthru Bazaar the first time only: after this, she will randomly appear in any one of four locations; leaving Rabanastre or loading or reloading your game will reset her location.
You will be prompted to respond to her on a total of four occasions: how you answer her questions will influence how this side story ends. There are five possible end scenarios.
Dialogue
First Visit

text.Ktjn: H-Hello. I am called Ktjn. I left my home and came to Rabanastre only quite recently. I have yet to learn my way around. I had been hoping to find someone I might speak with. Should you like to talk again, it would please me greatly.
Is the city not wonderful? I still lose my way on occasion, but I have come to know some of her walks and alleyways. But the land, I cannot hear it ... Should this not trouble me as a viera?

CHOICE.Ktjn: I see. Then perhaps it was a mistake to leave the Wood ... Pay no mind to my mutterings. Pray, speak with me again soon.

text.Ktjn: I sometimes lose my way, but for the most part, I can find what I must. Not that I've any place to be, particularly ...

text.ACTION: Second Visit

text.Ktjn: It is good to see you again. I have had so little opportunity to speak with humes. My people keep to themselves. The number of visitors to our village could be counted out on a single hand. So did I long to come to a great city such as Rabanastre. That wish is now come true, but this is not how I had hoped it would be. I knew my choice would bring hardship, yet ...

CHOICE.Ktjn: Perhaps I should have. Strength of will alone could not make up for my ignorance of the wider world. I do not wish to admit it, but I know it now to be true ... Feel not sorrowful. It is no easy thing to speak unwelcome truths to another. Yet these are the most valuable truths to hear.

text.Ktjn: I left the Wood to learn the ways of the world beyond. But nothing here is as it seems ... Perhaps I will begin to understand in time.

text.ACTION: Third Visit

text.Ktjn: Hello. Have you come for another visit? Little has changed for me. I have seen much of the city, though I still have made few friends, and am no closer to realizing my goal. I have not spoken of this to you before, but I came to Rabanastre to become ... more like my sister. She had grown tired of our life of isolation ... Long ago she left. Only later did I hear rumors she had come here. All this time my sister has been making her way through the world, while I lived in the sheltered peace of the Wood. I would be as she is. Do you think it possible?

CHOICE.Vaan: Sure, if you put your mind to it.

CHOICE.Ktjn: ... I see. So you think me too naïve to follow in my sister's footsteps. Though you may speak the truth, I am not yet beaten.

text.Ktjn: I followed my sister's example and left the Wood, but it has not been an easy path for me to walk. I have much to think on ...

text.ACTION: Pilika's Errand

text.Ada: I was walking along the riverbank when I saw it - a boat set adrift from the north bank. Of course I told everyone as soon as I could. No good can come of this ...

text.Village Elder: Yes, it's Ruksel's boat. There's no mistakin' it. What in the name of the gods is happening over there?

text.Dantro's Wife: There's trouble on the north bank, I'm sure of it. I wish Dantro were here, but I know he can't leave the outpost unwatched.

text.Tchigri: This is definitely my dad's boat. But where's my dad? Something bad must have happened ... I'm crossin' to the north bank to see what's going on. I know how to pilot the boat, and there's no point in waitin' around here worryin'.

text.Village Elder: Nonsense! Watching your father pilot the boat and doing it yourself are two different things. The river's dangerous, boy.

text.Tchigri: But what if my dad's in trouble? After him, there's no one that even knows how to pilot the boat 'cept me.

text.Village Elder: Yes ... But even if you make it across the river, who knows what you'll find once you're there? I'm sorry, but it's simply too dangerous!

text.Tchigri: But ... my dad ...

text.Dantro's Wife: What if he went with Tchigri?
He hunted the flowering cactoid for Dantro ... he must know how to defend himself.

text.Village Elder: That is true ... What do you say, boy? Will you do this for our village? Will you go with Tchigri to see what's happened on the north bank?

text.Tchigri: You just gotta! I'll pilot the boat. Whaddaya say?

CHOICE.Tchigri: Thanks! What are we waitin' for!

CHOICE.Village Elder: Thank you, boy. Look after Tchigri for us. And you, Tchigri! You be careful. The river will swallow the lot of you if you're not.

text.Tchigri: Look! Over there! Are those ... cactoids?
They must've attacked the north bank! What're we gonna do?
Wait, there's my dad! And everyone else, too!
I don't like the look of this one bit. Seems like they're holding 'em hostage. But what would cactoids want with hostages? I don't believe it!

text.ACTION: The cactoids all run away.

text.Tchigri: The cactoids all up and left! Now's our chance to go help my dad!

text.Villager (man in brown and green with ha: The cactoids have been running us ragged ever since they took us captive. One point, some malboros had us cornered in the Salikawood. I closed my eyes, knowin' it was the end, and all I could see was the face of my mother, rest her soul. Damn those cactoids! What do they want with us? Maybe I should go ask Ruksel. He's the one been taking orders from their leader.

text.Villager (old man in green and gray): I wonder where those cactoids have got off to. If we were smart, we'd turn tail and run before they got back. But where would we go?

text.Villager (man in different brown and gre: Those cactoids marched us all over the place. They had us running for our lives from malboros in the Salikawood ... I was sure we were done for.

text.Tchigri: I'm so glad you're all right! We didn't know what'd happened to you.

text.Ruksel: Quite a tale, that one. And you've some tales of your own, piloting the boat all by yourself! I knew you'd got the river in your blood!

text.Tchigri: The others said it was too dangerous, but I knew I could handle it. But what about the cactoids? They ran off for good ... right?

text.Ruksel: We can only hope so. Still, they're a prickly lot. Can't imagine they'd give up that easily. (hearing a noise) Whoa, what's that!?
That is the leader of the cactoids.

text.ACTION: Ruksel and the cactoid leader now stand across from Vaan and Tchigri. The cactoid leader is taller than Ruksel by a couple heads.

text.Tchigri: Hey, prickle-pants! Who do you think you are, kidnapping my dad!?

text.Ruksel: Stay back, Tchigri! They're just trying to find their son.

text.Tchigri: Find their son? You mean ... they're related?

text.Ruksel: That's right, they're a cactoid family. The eldest son, Dran, went missing, and they set out to find him. They came to our village along the way. Nothing but bad news, this Dran. He's part of a cactoid clan terrorizing the desert. There's even a bounty on his head. This one here's the matriarch of the family. She's been searching high and low for him. Wants to bring him back home and set him straight. But they couldn't find Dran anywhere in Dalmasca. That's why they needed us. She forced us to guide them to the lands beyond the desert. The Mosphoran Highwaste, the Salikawood ... even the Necrohol of Nabudis. I'd given up hope of ever making it back. And after all that, we still couldn't find him! So they brought us back here - for now. But who knows when they'll drag us off again?

text.Tchigri: So there's a bounty on this Dran, huh? (to Vaan) You have any idea where he might be?

text.Ruksel: I don't think he's to the north of the river. We must've looked under every stone between here and Archadia. As for the south bank, well ... We weren't about to lead the cactoids there and get you and the others mixed up in this, too.

text.Tchigri: So that's why you set the boat adrift - keep 'em from crossing!

text.Ruksel: I never figured on you coming to rescue me ... But there's no time for that now! We'll keep 'em busy while you search the south bank for Dran.

text.Tchigri: Right! Just leave it to us! Let's get going!

text.Dantro's Wife: I don't understand. Why would The cactoids invade the village? They're usually harmless enough. Their son, you say? Then we must find him. But the desert is huge ... where would we even begin? Wait! If this cactoid's been causing as much trouble as they say, someone might've posted a bill for him! Unless - The bill Dantro posted ... you hunted that cactoid, didn't you? You don't think - Of course ... The cactoid you hunted must have been their son! Hunted and made into medicine ... We'll never be able to return him now! What? The flower? Why, I boiled it, and threw it away behind the house ...

The cactoid you hunted must have been this son they're looking for. Made into medicine ... We'll never be able to return him now! What? The flower? Why, I boiled it, and threw it away behind the house ...

text.Ada: I can't believe the cactoids would attack the village. I've never seen anything like it.

text.ACTION: Approach the flower in the sand behind the hut ...

text.Dantro's Wife: What? The flower had budded into ... another cactoid? They're a strange lot, aren't they? Supposing you take it over to the north bank ... do you think they'd accept it as their son?

text.Tchigri: You found the cactoid! What ... you didn't? You hunted the other one, but this one looks just like that one ... huh? Well, none of this makes much sense to me, but I guess we don't have much choice, huh. His family is waiting! Let's get him over to the north bank!

text.Rimzat: Hha! I have been waiting for some time. You see, I am in need of assistance. Please, hear my words. I have been sent from Archadia to study the sandstorms of the Dalmasca Westersand, but the storms' violence makes such study ... impossible. There is a place in the desert, at the end of a long trail that winds through the north. Mayhap you know it. That is the site of my study. But before the wrath of such a storm, I can do nothing. This is why I seek help. Will you help me?

CHOICE.Rimzat: Thank you, my friend! I have made no progress on my own. I would like you to start by gathering information within Rabanastre. My own inquiries have yielded little. I will be waiting to hear what you find.

text.Rimzat: Aah, have you reconsidered my request? I'm still looking for help. There is a place in the desert, at the end of a long trail that winds through the north, where a sandstorm rages.
